The green fox swiftly dodged to the side, but a shadowy figure struck again; it was a black stone the size of a bowl.
This time, the fox couldn't dodge, and its head was struck by the black stone.
With a "bang," the stone burst apart, and all went dark before the green fox's eyes, leaving it somewhat stunned.
Yuan Ming looked at his left hand, a bit dazed.
The instant after he had thrown the first stone, his left hand had subconsciously thrown a second one, with virtually no interval between the two.
This seemed to be some kind of throwing martial arts technique he had instinctively used, which even the agile green fox couldn't evade.
Yuan Ming quickly came back to his senses, his figure dove down, and his hands reached for the green fox's neck.
The green fox's vision had not yet recovered, but it sensed danger and leaped to the side, dodging Yuan Ming's dive and then biting towards Yuan Ming's arm in retaliation.
Yuan Ming's initial grab was a feint, and seeing the situation turn dire, he quickly retracted his arm, narrowly avoiding the fox's bite.
"An uninjured green fox really is tough to handle," he muttered to himself and turned to flee into the distance.
The green fox shook its head, quickly regaining its composure.
As expected, it became enraged by Yuan Ming, bloodthirsty ferocity gleaming in its green eyes. With a low roar, it immediately gave chase.
The White Ape, transformed by Yuan Ming, moved much slower on its legs than the green fox, and the distance between them quickly diminished to less than ten yards.
Seeing that he was about to be caught, Yuan Ming leaped onto a large tree beside him, quickly climbing upward. After pounding his chest with one fist toward the green fox below, he started to leap forward through the trees.
The green fox hesitated for a moment, but driven to rage by Yuan Ming's taunting actions, it relentlessly continued the pursuit.
Yuan Ming advanced at a measured pace, occasionally using stones to attack the green fox to prevent it from turning back.
Naturally, the provoked green fox responded with ongoing roars.
In a pursuit of each other, they quickly arrived near the den of the yellow armadillo.
The yellow armadillo was inside its cave feeding its young when it heard the commotion outside and immediately sprang out.
From afar, Yuan Ming had been watching the area around the armadillo's den closely. As the bushes stirred, he swiftly hid behind a dense clump of leaves.
In the midst of the forest, only the incessantly howling green fox remained.
With its territory invaded by green foxes time and again, and now one daring to approach its den, flames seemed to spark from the eyes of the yellow armadillo. Its body surged with a yellow glow as it charged toward the green fox.Help us out by reading on *.
Only then did the green fox realize something was amiss, and without a word, it turned to flee.
However, the yellow armadillo was thoroughly enraged. In its full wrath, it caught up to the green fox in a few breaths' time. Its iron-hooks-like sharp claws became two black afterimages as they viciously descended.
The green fox found no way to dodge and turned to fight.
The two fierce beasts clashed in an instant, their roars echoing in the woods, stirring up clouds of dust.
From behind the dense leaves, a flicker of excitement crossed Yuan Ming's eyes.
His plan was already half successful. All he had to do now was wait for the green fox to be defeated and flee, and he could once again reap the benefits.
"Wait, there were two green foxes yesterday, and only then could they escape. Now there is only one. Might it be killed outright by the yellow armadillo?" Yuan Ming suddenly remembered something, his mind racing.
Just then, he heard a subtle sound, distinct from the clash of the two beasts, like the cry of a small creature.
"The yellow armadillo is so furious, could it be..." Yuan Ming had a thought and stealthily approached the yellow armadillo's den, soon reaching a large tree in front of the den.
Peering through the gaps in the leaves, his face lit up with joy.
From this angle, he could just make out the interior of the yellow armadillo's den where several young armadillos huddled together, emitting whimpers.
"Just as I thought," Yuan Ming murmured to himself and took a black stone out of the pouch he carried on his back.
The battle in the forest ended quickly, just as Yuan Ming had anticipated. The Green Fox didn't last long before it was utterly defeated, covered in wounds and one of its eyes gouged out. It howled miserably as it fled.
The yellow armadillo naturally wouldn't let it escape and was about to give chase.
A shrill whistle came from behind, and a dark shadow shot straight toward the armadillo's den.
The yellow armadillo was a mix of shock and rage, and immediately abandoned the pursuit of the Green Fox. With a powerful push of its sturdy legs against the ground, it turned into a yellow blur rushing back to its den.
The dark shadow didn't hit the armadillo's den; instead, it struck a large tree nearby with a "bang," revealing itself to be a black stone.
The yellow armadillo was stunned, its large body sliding forward due to inertia, crushing a large swath of shrubs and undergrowth.
Yuan Ming cracked a slight smile as he leapt out from his hiding spot and pursued the injured Green Fox.
The yellow armadillo, concerned for its young in the den, roared a few threatening roars at Yuan Ming and the Green Fox, then turned and burrowed into its cave.
...
Yuan Ming soon caught up with the injured Green Fox, timed his distance perfectly, and leaped down from a tree like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
The sounds of struggle and roars echoed once more in the forest, dust billowed, and quiet soon returned.
Yuan Ming stood up, dusting off his body, the corner of his mouth involuntarily curling up.
Multiple cuts marred his arm, inflicted by the Green Fox in a final desperate counterattack.
But that already heavily injured Green Fox had also turned into a corpse, its neck bent oddly as it lay on the ground, its neck bone broken.
Yuan Ming looked at his hands, staring absently.
He had used the same technique as the day before, strangling the Green Fox with his arms.
This throat-lock capture martial arts technique, which he executed quite skillfully, came out instinctively during the fight, as did the stone-throwing technique he had used before.
Although both martial arts techniques were simple, they were exceedingly compatible with his transformed White Ape form.
Yuan Ming took out the Beast Skin Pouch used for storing blood, activated his Mana to suck dry the Green Fox Blood, and after turning it into a glittering ball of Essence Blood, he didn't continue hunting but withdrew with the Green Fox's body toward the direction of the canyon.
For the next three days, he practiced his breath control and cultivation at night, while during the day he lured Green Foxes to the yellow armadillo's territory using the same tactics, causing the two to fight and then taking the opportunity to hunt.
Yuan Ming was fairly lucky, successfully hunting a Green Fox each day, and by the fifth day, he had collected five portions of Fierce Beast Essence Blood.
He weighed the Beast Skin Pouch in his hand and exhaled a long breath before sitting down on the ground.
Though the process had been somewhat harrowing these past few days, he had finally completed the task by the deadline.
The most difficult times were behind him, and with the profound mysteries of the Nine Elements Technique, his strength would steadily increase. He believed it wouldn't be long before he could hunt those Green Foxes alone and perhaps even challenge the armadillo without it being entirely hopeless.
After a brief rest, Yuan Ming stood up and returned to the canyon's opposite bank, making for the Giant Stone Boundary.
When he arrived at the stone, he discovered Wulu was already waiting there, while Lage, who had traveled with them before, was still nowhere to be seen.
"Who knows what kind of 'safe place with promise of success' that guy was talking about. Lage still hasn't shown up by now, most likely it's more bad luck than good," Yuan Ming mused as he glanced at Wulu, who was meditating with closed eyes, and didn't bother to greet him, choosing to sit and meditate by the stone as well.
With a stranger present, he didn't circulate the Nine Elements Technique but only used his Mana to examine his internal condition.
A month had passed, and the toxin from the Corrosive Heart Pill had gradually spread, infiltrating his heart meridian. An area the size of a bowl around his heart felt chilly and numb, devoid of sensation.
Yuan Ming had also tried to force out the toxin with his Mana in the past few days, but to no avail.
This was to be expected, as Biluo Cave was a Cultivation Sect, and their use of poison was naturally beyond the capabilities of someone like him who had just started cultivating a few days ago.
"I hope Elder Hu Huo keeps his word and provides the antidote," Yuan Ming thought to himself.
Before long, a grey shadow appeared in the distance, swiftly approaching.
Yuan Ming was familiar with this figure, and he promptly stood up, as did Wulu, who opened his eyes and sprung to his feet.
The grey shadow swiftly reached their vicinity. It was Elder Hu Huo's grey bird, circling slightly in mid-air before it landed atop the stone, and Elder Hu Huo's figure lightly descended from its back.
"Elder Hu Huo!" Yuan Ming and Wulu bowed in unison.
"Hand over the Blood Storage Bag for me to see," demanded Elder Hu Huo straightforwardly.
Yuan Ming was about to speak when Wulu stepped forward and presented his Blood Storage Bag.
Elder Hu Huo glanced into the bag, nodded, and tossed a Jade Bottle to Wulu.
"Here's your monthly Detoxification Pill. Take it."
"Thank you, Elder Hu Huo!" Wulu was overjoyed, pulled out the stopper of the Jade Bottle, poured out a pale-red pill, and swallowed it, the tension on his face loosening.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming also handed over his Blood Storage Bag. Elder Hu Huo took a quick look and, without saying much, similarly bestowed upon him a Detoxification Pill.
Yuan Ming swallowed the pill and immediately felt a surge of warmth rising from his lower abdomen, neutralizing much of the chilly poison, returning him to the state he was in a month ago, right after taking the Corrosive Heart Pill; his heart meridian also returned to normal.
This secretly relieved him; it seemed that Elder Hu Huo was trustworthy after all. As long as the Beast Blood was delivered on time each month, he didn't have to worry about the deadly toxin of the Corrosive Heart Pill.
Elder Hu Huo took out a slightly bulging Blood Storage Bag without uttering a word, collected the Essence Blood from Yuan Ming and Wulu's bags, and before the two could say anything more, he took off on the bird once again, seeming somewhat hurried.

chapters.title: Chapter 35 - 17: Decisive Intentions
chapters.content:
"Hehe, congratulations, Brother Yuan Ming, on mastering the Fur Cloak Skill and surviving the first month," Wulu said with a smile as he looked at Yuan Ming and didn't immediately leave.
"Likewise. By the way, Brother Wulu, why is Lage absent?" Yuan Ming shifted the conversation completely.
"Brother Lage went hunting by himself a few days ago but, unfortunately, perished at the claws of a beast," Wulu said indifferently.
"That's truly a pity." Yuan Ming nodded, said no more, and turned away.
Wulu watched as Yuan Ming walked away, his gaze flickering uncertainly, his thoughts unknown.
Yuan Ming did not continue his hunt on the other side of the gorge but returned to his hidden cave instead.
Hunting fierce beasts could wait; what he needed most now was to enhance his strength.
He sealed the entrance of the cave and sat cross-legged on the ground, circulating the Nine Elements Technique as nature's spiritual energy rapidly gathered around him.
...
Time flew swiftly, and twenty days passed in the blink of an eye.
Atop a centuries-old giant tree outside the Green Fox den stood a tall White Ape, none other than Yuan Ming, who had utilized the Fur Cloak Skill.
Compared to twenty days ago, the White Ape was significantly taller, with muscles more robust and imposing.
Before long, five or six Green Foxes ran out of their den in the mountain recess and quickly dispersed.
Having lured and hunted them before, Yuan Ming was well aware of their habits— they were spreading out to forage.
With ease borne of familiarity, he followed one of the Green Foxes to a Black Pine Forest.
This place was four or five miles from the mountain recesses' den, far enough to make noise without it carrying back to the den.
Yuan Ming quickened his pace, and within a few breaths had overtaken the Green Fox, leaping down from a tree to block its path.
The Green Fox was first startled, but on seeing only a White Ape, its eyes relaxed, and it viciously pounced.
This Green Fox was slightly larger and faster than those Yuan Ming had previously hunted, a blurry flash of green speeding toward him, its deep green claws reaching out!
However, Yuan Ming's body lightly swayed and he vanished on the spot, causing the Green Fox to lunge at thin air.
The Green Fox was shocked and quickly stabilized itself.
But before it could completely recover, Yuan Ming descended from above, his right leg carrying a terrifying gust, and fiercely kicked the Green Fox's back.
A horrifying force surged into the Green Fox's body, and with a "crack," its spine instantly broke.
Its body collapsed onto the ground, blood gushing from its mouth.
Before it could struggle to rise, Yuan Ming's other foot descended from the sky, stomping on the Green Fox's head.
Amidst the crisp sound of bone shattering, the Green Fox's head was crushed, white brain matter spilling out, ending its life.
Yuan Ming withdrew his foot, staring blankly at the dead Green Fox.
This copy comes from content on *.
His choice to continue hunting Green Foxes was partly because he was familiar with their habits, feeling that they posed no danger even if not easily defeated, but more importantly, to test his own strength.
Twenty days ago, the Green Foxes had been formidable beasts he could hardly contend with. But now, twenty days later, they couldn't withstand even two moves against him.
Unknowingly, his strength had already increased to such an extent!
Suppressing the excitement in his eyes, Yuan Ming took out the Blood Storage Bag to collect the Green Fox Blood, then returned near the Green Fox den to watch for the others.
A day passed, and he successfully hunted three Green Foxes.
The next day, he continued to the area outside the mountain recess, and with little effort, hunted another two Green Foxes.
The task that had almost killed him last month, he now accomplished with ease.
"If I haven't even completed the first layer of the Nine Elements Technique and can already wield such power with the Fur Cloak Skill, if I continue to train in this technique, and perhaps even break through to the second layer, might I be able to walk sideways through this forest?"
Yuan Ming touched the Ape Skin on his body, his thoughts racing with excitement, foreseeing a shortcut to continually growing stronger.
But suddenly, another thought occurred to him, and a contemplative look appeared in his eyes.
Though he was just a beginner on the path of cultivation, he still found it odd— the Fur Cloak Skill seemed too useful, easily enhancing power as long as one had mana.
Of course, the Nine Elements Technique played a significant role, but he still felt uneasy.
Moreover, this was quite different from the kind of cultivation that could move mountains and summon storms, the kind he had imagined. Was cultivating tremendous mana just to display strength by transforming into a half-human, half-beast creature too suffocating for an Immortal?
This thought took root in his mind, and the more Yuan Ming pondered, the more he felt something was off, though he couldn't pinpoint what exactly.
He tried to suppress these thoughts and reconsidered them carefully, eventually deciding that he couldn't figure it out at the moment and simply put it aside, heading back toward his cave and soon arriving near the gorge.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to descend, he suddenly heard a low moan.
Surprise crossed his face— why would someone be here?
Following the sound, he found a figure in a Black Robe lying in the bushes, body trembling non-stop, with skin exposed outside showing a blood-red color.
Yuan Ming didn't approach rashly but observed the man a few moments then, with a light exclamation, snapped a small tree nearby and turned the robed figure over.
The man's face thus revealed was Wulu.
Yuan Ming had already noticed some clues from the figure's silhouette and was not surprised.
Wulu's face was also crimson as blood, his lips trembling, eyes rolled back, his consciousness long gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 36 - 17: Heart's Decision 2
chapters.content:
"Is this some kind of illness?" Yuan Ming wondered to himself.
At this moment, blood flowed from the nostrils, ears, and eyes of Wu Lu, and his breathing suddenly became rapid while his breath rapidly weakened.
Yuan Ming hesitated briefly but then squatted down to check Wu Lu's condition and quickly discovered, "It seems there is a problem with the heart meridian."
Wu Lu's heart was beating violently, ten times faster than that of an ordinary person, and the meridians near his chest were in disarray, his muscles spasmed and the circulation of his Qi-Blood faced great obstruction.
Yuan Ming invoked his mana, pressed his fingers rapidly over a dozen times on Wu Lu's chest, and finally placed his palm on it, where his mana surged out, unblocking the meridians.
A quarter of an hour later, he withdrew his hand with a slight sweat on his forehead.
There were no medicinal herbs or tools in this place, and that was all he could do. Whether Wu Lu lived or died was entirely up to his own fate.
Perhaps it wasn't Wu Lu's time to die, as the circulation of his Qi-Blood slowly recovered, the blood color on his cheeks faded considerably, and he regained consciousness.
"Yuan Ming... is it you?" Wu Lu spoke with difficulty.Chaptersource:MyVirtualLibraryEmpire(*).
"Your condition is very serious. The Qi-Blood in your body is reversing flow toward your heart. How did this happen?" Yuan Ming asked.
Wu Lu opened his mouth, hesitating to speak.
"It doesn't matter if you don't want to talk. But your condition is very severe. I was only able to alleviate it a little, there is no permanent cure, and it will recur soon. Do you have any medicine that suits your condition?" Yuan Ming waved his hand and asked.
Wu Lu's face showed hesitation, but soon he became resolute and looked towards his waist.
"Do you have medicine there?" Yuan Ming asked.
"Yes... Can Brother Yuan Ming... get it for me..." Wu Lu struggled to speak.
Yuan Ming did not hesitate and took a cloth bag from there, which contained many items, including four sealed bamboo tubes, two dark red stones, one white jade pendant, and a black jade bottle.
"Is it this jade bottle?" He picked up the black jade bottle.
Wu Lu's face showed relief, and he immediately nodded.
Yuan Ming opened the jade bottle and poured out a dark red medicine pill, which had no particular medicinal scent, making it impossible to discern what kind of elixir it was.
He didn't bother to investigate further and placed the medicine pill into Wu Lu's mouth.
Wu Lu swallowed the elixir with difficulty, his complexion quickly turned even redder than before, the veins on his forehead bulged out as if they were alive, and a suppressed low growl emitted from his throat, suggesting he was enduring extreme pain.
Yuan Ming frowned as he watched Wu Lu, thinking that this didn't seem like an illness.
It took the time it would take to finish a meal before Wu Lu's condition began to improve, the blood color on his face gradually faded, and the bulging veins slowly returned to normal.
He looked extremely fatigued, forcibly adopting a meditative posture and cultivating to regulate his breathing.
Yuan Ming leaped onto a nearby large tree and sat down on a thick trunk several meters off the ground to recover the mana he had just expended.
After a good while, Wu Lu's complexion had completely recovered, a flash of red light passed over his body, and the tiger skin on his waist rolled up, clinging to his form. In the blink of an eye, he completed the Fur Cloak Skill transformation, turning into a spotted tiger over three meters tall.
Yuan Ming's pupils contracted slightly. Wu Lu's body had grown by almost half since the last time he saw him by the creek.
As Yuan Ming's cultivation improved, the size of his White Ape Transformation also grew, but it seemed that Wu Lu's growth rate was somewhat faster than his.
Wu Lu looked up at Yuan Ming in the tree, his eyes flashing coldly.
"I just saved your life. Why do you look at me that way, Brother Wu Lu? Is this how the Southern Border People treat their saviors?" Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"Why did you save me?" Wu Lu asked in a deep voice.
"We both entered Biluo Cave at the same time. Whether the relationship is good or bad, you can be considered a companion. Helping you was a trivial effort for me, so why not save you?" Yuan Ming spoke indifferently.
Upon hearing this, Wu Lu's expression eased a bit, although the cold light in his eyes did not fade.
"It seems I have been nosy. Rest assured, I will not tell anyone about this matter. We'll meet again." Yuan Ming stood up, patted his rear, and prepared to leave.
"Wait a moment." Wu Lu suddenly called out to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming stopped his steps and looked down.
"Anyhow, I'm indebted to you, Brother Yuan Ming, for saving me this time. A big favor can't be thanked enough. Take this piece of Fire Pattern Iron as my recompense," Wu Lu said as he took out a piece of dark red stone from the cloth bag and threw it up to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming raised his eyebrows. He had noticed when he opened Wu Lu's bag that these two stones were not ordinary items and emitted slight fluctuations of spiritual power, clearly items required by cultivators.
However, he did not catch the Fire Pattern Iron, but instead deflected it back down with his hand.
"I didn't save you out of greed for your belongings," Yuan Ming said calmly.
Wu Lu caught the Fire Pattern Iron, paused for a moment, and then said, "If Brother Yuan Ming refuses to accept this Fire Pattern Iron, then consider it a favor I owe you. If you need help in the future, as long as it is within my power, I will not shirk."
"You're too polite. We'll meet again." Yuan Ming smiled faintly, leaped away, and vanished into the forest within a few breaths.
Wu Lu stood silently on the spot, his expression indeterminate and rather desolate.
A short while later, he turned and descended from the valley, his figure quickly disappearing into the mist at the bottom of the valley.
Yuan Ming had not gone far, hiding in a large tree on the edge of a cliff ten-some meters away, keeping an eye on Wu Lu's departure.
He wasn't a pushover. The reason he had stepped in to save Wu Lu was partly because they were companions of sorts. Since it was a simple matter to save Wu Lu, he wouldn't be so heartless as to sit by and watch Wu Lu die.
On the other hand, Yuan Ming was also curious about the speed of Wu Lu's cultivation advancement and wanted to use this opportunity to close the gap between them and learn more about Wu Lu's circumstances.

chapters.title: Chapter 37 - 17: Decisive Intentions_3
chapters.content:
Wulu's reaction was somewhat surprising to him; it seemed that this person was very concerned about others knowing about his illness.
"There indeed was a problem with that attack," Yuan Ming muttered to himself.
However, he did not delve deeper, leaped down from the tree, quickly crossed the ravine, and returned to the cave to continue his secluded cultivation.
The matter with Wulu was but a minor episode. For Yuan Ming, enhancing his strength as soon as possible was his only chance to return to the Central Plains.
In any case, his intuition told him that practicing the Nine Elements Technique was always the right choice.
Three months had swiftly passed.
During this period, aside from taking a day or two each month to hunt Green Foxes to fulfill the Biluo Cave tasks and resupply his food, Yuan Ming did not take a single step outside, dedicating his full attention to the arduous practice of the Nine Elements Technique.
Thanks to this intensive cultivation and the mystical nature of the Nine Elements Technique, his mana rapidly increased.
One day, as Yuan Ming was meditating, his increasingly robust mana suddenly began to roil like boiling water, spontaneously flowing out of his Dantian and surging through the meridians throughout his body.
His body trembled, and suddenly, sounds of bones clashing echoed from within, and he couldn't help but spit out of his mouth.
A stream of blue light sprayed out, transforming into a swarm of blue halo that encircled and rotated around his body.
A series of spell sounds emanated from within the halo, and as the swirling blue light quickly dissipated, Yuan Ming had already stood up.
"I have finally cultivated the first layer of the Nine Elements Technique!" Yuan Ming looked at his hands and muttered to himself.
Now, he was equivalent to a cultivator at the first layer of the Qi Refinement Realm and had officially entered the ranks of cultivators.
Yuan Ming's mana had increased several times compared to three months ago, and he couldn't wait to see what level his Fur Cloak Skill had reached. He stood up and walked outside the cave, forming a spell with his fingers.
The White Ape Skin around his waist swept up and wrapped around his body, with countless blood threads emerging from the inner side of the Ape Skin, burrowing into the depths of his body.
Yuan Ming had grown accustomed to this pain and clenched his teeth to endure it.
The heart-piercing pain soon passed, and an ape about ten feet tall materialized.
"The height is still about the same as before; it seems I have reached the limit," he said, comparing himself to a large tree nearby and muttering.Spоt аn еrrоr? Visit thе оriginаl pоst оn М&VLЕМРY&R.
In the past few months, as Yuan Ming's mana continued to increase, the size of the transformed White Ape had been growing, reaching the current height of about ten feet two months ago.
Since then, no matter how much his mana grew, the height and size of the White Ape remained unchanged, clearly reaching the limit of the Fur Cloak Skill.
Though the height did not increase, the muscle density on the White Ape grew significantly, with large and solid muscles bulging, displaying the immense power contained within, far surpassing any previous condition.
He clenched his fist in his right hand and threw a punch, emitting a dull and startling sound, and struck a large tree.
Crack!
The tree trunk, as thick as a water barrel, was directly split in half; the broken part smashed onto the ground, sending dust flying and alarming birds and animals!
Yuan Ming withdrew his fist, a satisfied look appearing on his face.
With his current strength, dealing with a Green Fox was naturally not a problem, and even the defensively strong Yellow Armadillo would likely dare not face his full-force strike.
"With this strength, I wonder if I can cross the Ten Thousand Mountains and return to the Central Plains?" he thought excitedly, unable to suppress the urge to escape.
But remembering the deadly toxin of the Corrosive Heart Pill inside him, his boiling blood turned ice-cold again.
"Staying in this forest filled with nothing but Fierce Beasts and Fur Beast Slaves, what good is strength if I'm trapped? No, I must find a way to truly escape this place!" Yuan Ming clenched his fist.
His current identity was as a Fur Beast Slave of the Biluo Cave, without any chance to contact the outside world, the only link being Elder Hu Huo, who would certainly not provide the real antidote for the Corrosive Heart Pill.
"Right, it has been several months now, I wonder if that incense burner can be lit again? Perhaps I can make contact with the outside world through the incense burner?" Yuan Ming slapped his forehead, remembering the treasure.
He immediately stopped using the Fur Cloak Skill, returning inside the stone cave, and summoned the incense burner with his mana.
Yuan Ming held the incense burner in both hands, feeling a warm flow seeping through his palms into his mind, instantly invigorating his spirit.
However, at that moment, he could not afford to indulge in the pleasant sensation of invigoration, his eyes fixed intently on the green incense burner before him.
Compared to before, the incense burner seemed to have undergone a significant change, a very small part of the Tai Chi Pattern on it had become shiny while the rest remained dull.
"It seems that over time, the Tai Chi Pattern will automatically restore its brightness; I wonder if it will allow traversing again once it is fully bright?" he speculated silently.
But considering the pace at which the Tai Chi Pattern was regaining its brightness, it would take quite some time before it was fully illuminated.

chapters.title: Chapter 38 - 18 Ascending Passage
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming sighed, casually placing the green incense burner down, which just happened to touch the White Ape Skin wrapped around his waist.
A flash of blue light on the surface of the incense burner, and a warm current of air escaped from it, quickly merging into the White Ape Skin.
Shuddering, the White Ape Skin surface began to glow with a pale golden light, then unfolded with a "whoosh" and draped itself over Yuan Ming.
Before Yuan Ming could comprehend what was happening, the mana within his Dantian surged violently and started to flow outward, continuously pouring into the White Ape Skin, which began fusing with his body.
The sensation was like the first time Elder Hu Huo had activated the Fur Cloak Skill, covering his body with fur.
The White Ape Skin writhed as if alive, its surface bulging with protuberances, as if countless mice were burrowing underneath.
Shocked, Yuan Ming hastily tried to control the mana within his Dantian, to stop it from gushing out, but to no avail.
It was not only the mana within him, but even the spiritual energy in the air around him seemed to be drawn by some invisible force, converging towards the White Ape Skin.
What shocked Yuan Ming left him dumbfounded.
As the spiritual energy flowed endlessly into the White Ape Skin, the previously somewhat gray and dried fur visibly regained its luster and softness at a speed visible to the naked eye. Sparse patches regrew white fuzz, which rapidly thickened and elongated.
At the same time, a phantom image of a White Ape emerged within the White Ape Skin, enveloping his body.
"What is this?" Yuan Ming exclaimed in shock, scratching his head and cheeks uncontrollably as if he heard the squealing of monkeys echoing around him.
Before he could react, a cold sensation rose in his mind, causing a sudden intense pain in the center of his forehead, as if a dagger had been thrust into it, piercing through his skull!
Yuan Ming opened his mouth wide but couldn't make a sound, feeling the world spin around him, nearly losing consciousness.
Despite his usually steadfast mind, enduring the inhuman torment by sheer force of will, his consciousness was on the verge of collapse. He could hear nothing and saw not a glimmer of light.
In a daze, Yuan Ming's mind conjured the image of a tall and mighty White Ape standing defiantly atop a giant peak, beating its chest with clenched fists amid roaring winds and lashing rain, howling furiously towards the sky.
Then everything before his eyes went dark, and he lost consciousness.
After an unknown period, Yuan Ming's consciousness slowly returned, and his senses gradually came back.
He shook his somewhat swollen head and felt that the Ape Skin had stopped writhing and was no longer absorbing his mana. However, there was a feeling of emptiness within his Dantian; his mana had been completely drained.
The originally grayish-white Ape Skin was now completely white and lustrous, its surface sleek and shiny, as if freshly peeled, with faint strands of golden light shimmering on it.
Content sourced from * – My Virtual Library Empire.
"What exactly happened just now? Why does this White Ape Skin seem like it's about to come alive? And that White Ape, could it possibly be…" Yuan Ming furrowed his brow, silently pondering.
Although he had no evidence, he instinctively felt that the White Ape that appeared in his mind was the owner of the Ape Skin on his body.
"Bang" "Bang" "Bang"
A series of vigorous heartbeats suddenly echoed in his ears, startling Yuan Ming and awakening him from his scattered thoughts.
"Ah!"
The next moment, he felt an excruciating pain as sharp, bloodied claws burst through the skin at the tips of his fingers, making his body tremble and fall to the ground, clutching his hands in agony.
It took a quarter of an hour before the claws stopped growing, and the piercing pain finally subsided.
Yuan Ming caught his breath, his body almost soaked in sweat, his head thundering, on the verge of passing out.
However, he had made quite a commotion, and he didn't know if any wild animals had heard and would come over, so he forced himself to sit up cross-legged and began cultivating the Nine Elements Technique to regulate his breath.
After half an hour, Yuan Ming opened his eyes, his complexion slightly recovered, and some mana had returned to his body.
He looked at his hands, noticing claws half a foot long on his fingertips, curved like dragon claws, as if cast from steel, seemingly indestructible.
"Although I don't know what exactly happened, it seems that because of the Mysterious Incense Burner, the White Ape Skin underwent some kind of evolution? This incense burner truly is a rare treasure!" Yuan Ming thought to himself.
He cast a spell to collect the incense burner and, with a movement of his arm, casually scratched the wall of the cave.
The wall was easily marked with five deep scratches, the solid earthen wall as easy to cut as tofu under the sharp claws, barely resisting at all.
"How sharp!" Yuan Ming praised aloud.
The original White Ape was known for its arm strength and the ability to move freely through the forests. Compared to jackals, tigers, and leopards, it had no significant advantage in attack. However, now with these sharp claws, things were naturally different.
Take, for example, the armadillo-like fierce beast that wasn't afraid to face the Green Fox's pincer attack. With its incredibly tough armor, it often emerged unbeaten from battles. With my current strength, I could win through brute force, but it would be very strenuous. If I had these sharp claws to assist, it would naturally be easy to break through the opponent's defense and accomplish twice the result with half the effort.
"No matter how much my strength improves, as long as I don't obtain the real antidote to the Corrosive Heart Pill, I cannot leave this area, let alone return to the Central Plains," Yuan Ming thought about the deadly poison inflicted by Biluo Cave and couldn't help feeling disheartened.
"Since the incense burner cannot be lit for the time being, maybe I could try getting some information from that place?" His thoughts shifted, and he looked towards the south.
Over the past few months, he used every opportunity of submitting Fierce Beast Essence Blood to have some exchanges with Elder Hu Huo.
Although the elder was always quick to come and go and reluctant to say much, in one of the exchanges, whether intentionally or unintentionally, he mentioned that Biluo Cave had a large number of Fur Beast Slaves, dispatched to various regions of the Ten Thousand Mountains under the management of different elders, and he was responsible for as many as twenty to thirty of them.
Yuan Ming believed that these Beast Slaves, in relation to him, could all be considered "seniors." They must know more about Biluo Cave and the Ten Thousand Mountains than he did. Perhaps seeking them out and making contact might yield some information he needed.
After settling on this plan in his mind, Yuan Ming did not set out immediately to find other Beast Slaves. With only two days left until the next Essence Blood submission, it wouldn't be too late to embark on his mission after submitting this month's Fierce Beast Essence Blood.
Two days later, Yuan Ming came to the Giant Stone Boundary with the Essence Blood he had prepared in advance.
This time, Elder Hu Huo was already waiting there, but Wulu was nowhere to be seen.
"Elder Hu Huo, here is this month's Fierce Beast Essence Blood, please check it," Yuan Ming said as he took out the Blood Storage Bag and handed it over.
"The color and scent of these five batches of Essence Blood are similar; were they collected in one day?" Elder Hu Huo took the Blood Storage Bag, glanced at it, raised an eyebrow slightly, and looked up at Yuan Ming before asking.
"Elder's insight is indeed sharp! Disciple happened upon a nest of Green Fox Fierce Beasts and was fortunate to collect five batches of Essence Blood in one day," Yuan Ming did not understand the intent behind Elder Hu Huo's question but did not try to deceive him with a false story.
"To slaughter five Green Foxes in one day is not bad. Has your cultivation made any breakthroughs beyond the Qi Refining First Level?" Elder Hu Huo appraised Yuan Ming before asking.
"I had an epiphany a few days ago and was fortunate enough to make a breakthrough," Yuan Ming replied, hesitating slightly.
"A breakthrough in the Qi Refining First Level within half a year is not bad, and it barely qualifies you," Elder Hu Huo nodded and said.
"I'm not sure what you mean by that," Yuan Ming asked, his face showing a hint of surprise.
"Most of you Fur Beast Slaves have Four Spirit Roots, which according to the standards of the Cultivation World are regarded as 'Fake Spirit Roots.' Without special opportunities or exceptional resolve, it's generally hard to achieve great things. Our Biluo Cave cherishes talent, and setting up the Fur Beast Slaves is a trial in itself. Those who break through the Qi Refining first level within half a year may be given a path to ascend, but whether one succeeds depends on their willpower," Elder Hu Huo stated, his face showing a pleasant demeanor.
"Please, Elder, elucidate further," Yuan Ming guessed something and a flash of excitement crossed his face.
"As long as you submit a certain number of Fierce Beast Essence Blood within three years, you can shed the identity of a Fur Beast Slave and be accepted as a Registered Disciple of Biluo Cave where you can learn real Immortal Techniques," Elder Hu Huo seemed pleased with Yuan Ming's reaction and continued.
"To be accepted into Biluo Cave! Are these words true?" Yuan Ming asked excitedly.
"I, Hu Huo, hold some standing in Biluo Cave, when have I ever spoken falsely?" Elder Hu Huo's expression darkened slightly.
"Forgive me, Elder, for my momentary excitement and inappropriate words. May I ask how much Essence Blood needs to be submitted within these three years?" Yuan Ming hurriedly apologized and adeptly changed the subject.
"One thousand portions."
At these words, Yuan Ming's eyes widened as he seemed unable to believe what he had heard.
"If you can't even gather a mere one thousand portions of Essence Blood, then you might as well give up on the idea of cultivation. I see you as somewhat agreeable, so here's a tip: you'd better hunt higher-ranking Fierce Beasts. According to regulations, one portion of Mid-level Fierce Beast Essence Blood is equivalent to ten portions of Lower Stage Fierce Beast Essence Blood, and an Upper Stage Fierce Beast Essence Blood is even worth a hundred portions of the Lower Stage," Elder Hu Huo glanced at Yuan Ming and said.
"Thank you for your guidance, Elder. I understand," Yuan Ming replied solemnly.
Last month, Elder Hu Huo mentioned this matter when collecting Essence Blood, elaborating that First Level Lower Stage is the classification for the power of a Level 1 Fierce Beast, and that there are two more rankings above it: First Level Middle Stage and First Level Upper Stage.
Previously, Yuan Ming had encountered Green Foxes and armadillos, all First Level Lower Stage Fierce Beasts, with power roughly equivalent to Cultivators at the Qi Refining first to fourth layers. Mid-level Fierce Beasts lurking deeper in the Ten Thousand Mountains are equivalent to Qi Refining Fifth to Eighth Level Cultivators, their strength obviously far greater.
Upper Stage Fierce Beasts, even more formidable than the Mid-level, would mean instant death if encountered by someone not strong enough.
Of course, because Fierce Beasts have low spiritual intelligence, an ordinary cultivator, even with a lesser true cultivation, could attempt to kill beyond their level with some techniques, though this cannot be overstated.
In essence, with his current cultivation at the Qi Refining First Level, Yuan Ming had no confidence that he could emerge unscathed from an encounter with a Mid-level Fierce Beast.
That is to say, to accumulate one thousand portions of Fierce Beast Essence Blood, unless he could further improve his cultivation, he would have to continue hunting a thousand First Level Lower Stage Fierce Beasts in earnest.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to ask Elder Hu Huo for the antidote and to take his leave, a rustle came from the nearby jungle, not far behind him, accompanied by the sound of approaching footsteps.
Yuan Ming turned his head toward the sound and saw Wulu hobbling towards them.

chapters.title: Chapter 39 - 19: Testing the Waters
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming looked at Wulu approaching and unconsciously furrowed his brow, which soon relaxed again.
Wulu's shoulders, chest, and arms all bore injuries, and a few places were still oozing blood, as if he had recently been through a fierce battle, and he looked quite bedraggled.
Speaking of which, Wulu seemed to have had some special opportunity. Although he was still some distance away from the Qi Refining First Level, his overall cultivation speed didn't seem to be inferior to Yuan Ming's.
And the beast skin of his primary form, the striped tiger, was far stronger than the White Ape in terms of overall combat power. He should have been able to handle ordinary First Level Lower Stage fierce beasts with ease, so it was unclear what he had encountered.
"Elder Hu Huo, I have arrived late. Here is this month's share of fierce beast essence blood," said Wulu, stopping in front of Elder Hu Huo and handing over a blood storage bag.
Elder Hu Huo didn't seem to notice Wulu's pitiful state, and, expressionless, took his five portions of essence blood. After tossing two antidotes to him, he called forth a large bird and left.
After taking the antidote, Yuan Ming didn't linger and planned to turn and leave as well.
"Brother Yuan, wait a moment. Do you still have some of that healing ointment?" Wulu suddenly called out to Yuan Ming.
"I have one more tube." Yuan Ming stopped in his tracks.
"That's great. Could you sell it to me? I'll exchange this tube of soft bone poison liquid for it," Wulu said, his face lighting up with joy as he produced a bamboo tube, the top securely sealed with beast skin.
"Agreed," Yuan Ming said, taking one out from his chest and tossing it over.
"Thank you very much," Wulu quickly caught it and handed his bamboo tube to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming opened the tube to find it nearly full of a dark purple, viscous liquid.
Since the last time they helped each other out, the two men had grown closer and exchanged a few words more.
Wulu claimed to come from a small clan in the Southern Border, knowledgeable in refining various deadly poisons. This soft bone poison could make a person's limbs weak and was quite effective against fierce beasts. Yuan Ming had used his self-mixed healing ointment to trade with him twice before, finding the results satisfactory.
"Just now, I overheard Elder Hu Huo talking. Do you know what he said?" Wulu, glancing in the direction where Elder Hu Huo had departed, asked with curiosity.
"I was consulting with Elder Hu Huo about some matters concerning fierce beasts," Yuan Ming replied.
Since Elder Hu Huo had not told Wulu about the opportunity to become a registered disciple of Biluo Cave, Yuan Ming naturally wouldn't speak out of turn.
After a brief chat, the two parted ways and left the spot.
Yuan Ming returned to his cave dwelling and began to plot his next steps.
He had originally planned to head to other regions of the Ten Thousand Mountains to find some Fur Beast Slaves and inquire about Biluo Cave and the Corrosive Heart Pill, to see if there was a chance he could escape this place; after all, he had no desire to remain an oppressed, futureless Beast Slave forever.
Now that Elder Hu Huo had pointed out a clear path to joining Biluo Cave, it didn't seem necessary to go through all that trouble.
A thousand portions of fierce beast essence blood might seem a lot, but if he reduced his cultivation time, Yuan Ming was confident he could gather them within a year.
"Something's not right, though. Biluo Cave doesn't seem like a lenient sect at first glance. Why set such a relaxed condition? Any Fur Beast Slave with a modicum of strength should be able to complete this task if they're a bit careful, right?" Yuan Ming pondered, stroking his chin.
Could there be some unknown catch?
Unable to penetrate the mystery for the time being, he decided not to waste more time dwelling on it. At least by collecting essence blood and practicing the Nine Elements Technique as much as possible to increase his cultivation, he could somewhat enhance his ability to protect himself in the future.
With that thought in mind, Yuan Ming started to tidy up his cave dwelling.
The cave was a bit far from the canyon, and each trip took a significant amount of time, so he needed to find a new place to live.
Yuan Ming wrapped his belongings in a beast skin, got up from the cave he had resided in for half a year, and blocked the cave entrance with a large stone before leaving.
This spot was quite concealed, so it might come in handy in the future.
Carrying the beast skin bundle, Yuan Ming headed south and quickly arrived near the canyon.
"Crossing the canyon won't take much time; I should settle down on this side of the canyon."
Yuan Ming looked around and, without proceeding further, began searching for a suitable place to live.
Soon, he found a winding cave at the base of a small hill, seemingly dug out by a ground-dwelling creature like an armadillo.
The cave was long, stretching all the way to the other side of the hill. Besides the main entrance, there was a smaller back exit on the shaded side of the hill.
However, the back exit was too small for a person to pass through.
Yuan Ming blocked the back exit with large stones and then transformed into a White Ape. He used his sharp claws to enlarge the space near the main entrance by double, forming a crude earthen house.Catch the formatted version at *.
Fortunately, the hill had more dirt than rocks, saving him a lot of effort. Otherwise, even with his sharp claws, expanding the cave this much wouldn't have been possible in just a day or two.
Yuan Ming brought a large stone nearby to block the cave door and gathered plenty of dead branches and dry grass to make a simple bed in the cave, thus easily constructing a rudimentary dwelling.
Lying on the dry grass bed, he relaxed completely and couldn't help but yawn.
His previous cave had been a bare-bones dwelling, and he had been too busy with cultivation and hunting to care about his personal living conditions. Now, lying on a soft bed of grass and feeling his accumulated fatigue drain away, he started to feel sleepy.
This time, Yuan Ming didn't fight the drowsiness and collapsed onto the bed of dry grass, falling into a deep sleep soon after.
He had slept very well, waking up refreshed and energized at noon the next day. After hastily eating some dried meat, he left the cave and headed to the forest on the opposite side of the gorge.
Yuan Ming glanced at the hollow where the Green Fox den was located and quickly withdrew his gaze.
The group of Green Foxes had been mostly hunted by him. Since he killed their leader last month, the remaining foxes had scattered, causing a significant decrease in his consistent hunting spot.
Yuan Ming shook his head and stepped further into the depths of the forest.
He had been circling the edge of this forest for the past few months but had never ventured deep inside until now.
As he delved deeper, he found that the trees around him became exceptionally tall. Centuries-old towering trees were everywhere, and the ground was covered with a thick layer of dead branches and leaves, giving a soft feeling underfoot. The dense bushes and vines made the forest much more lush than the one on the opposite side of the gorge, blocking his line of sight.
After some thought, Yuan Ming transformed into a White Ape, leaped onto a tree, and began to jump forward.
The journey was peaceful for a full quarter of an hour, and he encountered no Fierce Beasts along the way.
This did not surprise him. Although this part of the forest was only the outer edge of the Ten Thousand Mountains with Fierce Beasts dwelling in it, they were actually not very numerous. Wulu had once complained that finding Fierce Beasts took much longer than the time needed to hunt them.
The reason Yuan Ming could find a large den of Green Foxes was purely out of good luck, which had made it easy for him to complete his monthly task. The whereabouts of that yellow armadillo were unknown, so he would need to venture further in to fulfill his target of one thousand units of Essence Blood.
Of course, Yuan Ming had no intention of being reckless or overly ambitious; safety was always his priority.
After traveling a distance of about a mile, the sound of rustling water reached his ears. A small waterfall fell from a cliff, pouring its water into a clear pond, bringing a refreshing cool breeze in his direction.
Yuan Ming lay on a tree and peered through the gaps in the leaves, looking ahead.
He saw a Fierce Beast resembling a large wild boar drinking at the edge of the pond. Its whole body was fiery red, with bulging muscles on its spine and hooves that clearly revealed its formidable strength.
The wild boar Fierce Beast also had a sharp unicorn on its forehead, which looked particularly lethal, and two sword-like gleaming tusks at the corners of its mouth, sending chills down one's spine with their icy shine.
Yuan Ming eyed the "prey" before him, his lips curling into a smile as he surveyed the surrounding environment near the pond to check for potential dangers.
Just then, the wild boar Fierce Beast twitched its ears and abruptly lifted its head from the pond, scanning around as if it had heard something.
Upon seeing this, Yuan Ming quickly hid behind the trunk of a tree, staying motionless.
The ears of the wild boar Fierce Beast flickered; it seemed to be listening intently to the noises around it. After a few breaths, it resumed drinking.
Yuan Ming breathed a sigh of relief and carefully peeked out again, observing the beast in detail.
"Looking at this guy's size, it's much stronger than the Green Foxes and armadillo I faced before. Let's start with you for the thousand units of Essence Blood," he thought to himself, moving quietly closer until he was nearby.
At this moment, the wild boar Fierce Beast stood up, shook the water off its body, and snorted contentedly. It was about to turn around and leave the pond.
Seizing the opportunity, Yuan Ming pounced down from the tree, landing squarely on the beast's broad back. Without giving the wild boar Fierce Beast a chance to react, he plunged his claws deep into its neck and forcefully made a slash.
"Sscht"
Two deep, bone-exposing, fearsome wounds appeared on the neck of the wild boar Fierce Beast, from which blood gushed out.
It let out a piercing, agonizing scream, its massive body charged forward, breaking two large trees in its path, sending broken branches and leaves flying.
Yuan Ming didn't have time to stabilize himself and was thrown off immediately.
"Roar!" The eyes of the wild boar Fierce Beast had turned blood red, and it wheeled around to pounce furiously at Yuan Ming.
Its head lowered, aiming the fiery red horn like a giant spear at Yuan Ming's chest, its huge body stirring up a torrent of air that made the trees several meters away rustle fiercely.
Yuan Ming had just steadied himself and it was already too late to dodge. He stretched out both hands in a hurry, grabbing hold of the fiery red horn.
Ssst...
His feet skidded across the ground as he was dragged backward.
After retreating about twenty meters, Yuan Ming's feet sunk half a foot into the earth, stabilizing his body. No matter how hard the wild boar Fierce Beast tried, it could not budge him.
"Get up!" Yuan Ming shouted, his arm muscles bulging as he heaved upward.
He lifted the massive body of the wild boar Fierce Beast into the air. It turned half a circle in mid-air and crashed down on a nearby large tree.
The tree, thick enough that it required a person to wrap their arms around it to fully encircle, snapped on impact. The Fierce Beast's body continued to crash to the ground with a "bang," causing the ground within several meters to tremble slightly.
Before the beast could recover, a grim, pale claw descended from the sky and impaled its head, piercing through the hard skull.
The wild boar Fierce Beast let out a despairing cry as its enormous body convulsed a few times before falling silent.
Yuan Ming nodded, the wild boar Fierce Beast was not weak. If he had encountered it three months earlier, he probably would have lost more often than won. But now facing him, it was as helpless as a kitten or puppy.
He had abandoned the Blood Qi Skill and switched to cultivating the Nine Elements Technique, a decision that had indeed been correct.
Yuan Ming took out a Blood Storage Bag and collected the blood of the wild boar. Just as he was about to leave, a low growling sound suddenly came from ahead, followed by a rumble that shook the ground, stirring up a cloud of dust and turbulent air!

chapters.title: Chapter 40 - 20 The Desire to Kill
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming's heart went cold, and he hurriedly looked in the direction of the sound.
Amidst the flying dust, a towering figure emerged, glaringly a brown bear covered in yellow fur. It stood even taller than the black bear he had killed earlier, nearly as high as a one-story building.
Under the creature's gaze, Yuan Ming felt as though he had been targeted by a terrifying monster, causing his hairs to stand on end. Although he appeared calm, his heart was deeply unsettled!
"This Fierce Beast is far more formidable than the wild boar just now. Could it be my bad luck to encounter a Level 1 Middle Stage being?" His heart sank with worry.
Not to mention he had just been through a battle. Although he had managed with ease, his mana had been significantly depleted. Even at his prime, he wouldn't dare to confront a Level 1 Intermediate-stage Fierce Beast head-on.
Thoughts raced through Yuan Ming's mind. Suddenly, he let out a thunderous roar, his muscles bulging as he feigned a pounce.
The brown bear halted its steps, wary eyes reflecting caution.
At that moment, Yuan Ming sprung backward and agilely climbed up a nearby large tree, scrambling upwards with remarkable speed.
"Ao!"
Only then did the brown bear realize it had been tricked. It charged with surprising speed, reaching the base of the tree where Yuan Ming was climbing in almost an instant, and attacked fiercely with its thick bear paws.
With a "bang," the thick tree, the girth of a water bucket, was forcefully snapped. Yuan Ming, having just reached halfway up the tree, was sent plummeting down with it.
Though shocked, he wasn't disordered. He kicked against the tree to propel himself toward another one.
The brown bear raised its head and let out a horrifying roar that felt as if metal was striking stone, piercing through everything.
The roar caused Yuan Ming's ears to buzz, his head to slightly sink, and his limbs to momentarily stiffen, sending his body tumbling down like a solid rock.
Before he hit the ground, the Nine Elements Technique within Yuan Ming instinctively activated. A surge of pure mana burst forth from his Dantian, swiftly coursing through his body, reviving his Qi-Blood and dispelling the numbness.
As soon as he regained feeling in his arms, he outstretched them forward, his claws piercing into the bark of another tree.
With a "hiss," his claws sank deep into the wood, and his body hung suspended in mid-air.
The brown bear paused below, then once again charged at the tree Yuan Ming was on, its hefty paw striking down.
Find the source of this chapter at *.
"Boom"
This tree, too, was struck and started to collapse with a crash.
However, Yuan Ming had already leapt ahead to another giant tree nearby, ensuring his mana enveloped him as a defense against any further roaring attacks from the brown bear.
Contrary to his expectations, the roar didn't come.
A flicker of surprise crossed Yuan Ming's face. He quickly climbed higher into the giant tree.
From his position, about thirty feet above ground, he was safe from the bear's roar.
The brown bear, refusing to let Yuan Ming escape, pounced to the front of the giant tree, its paws pounding in succession, violently attacking the trunk.
The tree shook tremendously, its bark cracked, and a shower of leaves fell. Apart from a few claw marks left on the trunk, the tree showed no signs of falling.
"Such a massive tree can be shaken; this brown bear must be a Level 1 Middle-level Fierce Beast. Too bad its brain is not as big as its body," mumbled Yuan Ming, taking a rock from his pocket and tossing it down from high above.
The stone turned into a streak of gray light and harshly struck the brown bear on the head.
With a muffled "bang," the rock shattered. Although it didn't do much damage to the brown bear, it enraged the beast even more, driving it to attack the giant tree more ferociously.
The tree's shaking became even more violent, yet being so large, it was unlikely to fall anytime soon.
Yuan Ming, the corner of his mouth lifted in a smile, watched from above like a spectator at a monkey show, occasionally dropping rocks to provoke the brown bear below.
As time passed little by little, the brown bear's ferocity diminished. Its chest heaved with heavy breathing, the fiery rage in its eyes mostly gone.
After a long while, the brown bear let out a disgruntled low growl at Yuan Ming, bowed its body, and turned to leave.
Yuan Ming took one more stone and tossed it down, striking the bear squarely on the back of its head.
However, the brown bear seemed to have learned its lesson, ignoring Yuan Ming's taunt completely and continued to run away without looking back.
"Not too dumb after all, but now it's too late to run away!" Yuan Ming didn't stay put any longer. With a few leaps, he was over the bear, plunging down from above. His ape claws turned into two gleaming cold lights, viciously aiming for the bear's back.
The brown bear sensed something wrong with the wind behind it, rolled away to the side, but still got grazed by the claws.
The tough bear skin was torn open, revealing a shallow half-foot-long wound. Not much blood flowed out, but the wound was tinged with a faint purple hue.
It was Soft Bone Poison that Yuan Ming had quietly smeared on his claws, acquired earlier from Wulu.
The brown bear grew infuriated again, its paw striking down violently toward Yuan Ming's head.
But the bear's movements had grown much slower due to previous exertions, and Yuan Ming, now in his White Ape form, dodged under its paw with ease.
As they crossed paths, the white ape's right claw reached out and made another shallow cut along the bear's flank.
"Roar..." The brown bear grew increasingly angry, its paws flailing as it lunged forward.
Yuan Ming had no intention of clashing head-on. He used the nearby trees to dodge and weave, occasionally leaving minor wounds on the bear with his claws.
Though the brown bear was stronger than Yuan Ming, it had futilely expended too much strength on that giant tree. Combined with its inherently sluggish speed, it now found itself at a disadvantage, with small cuts accumulating and blood covering its body.
Moreover, with the effects of the Soft Bone Poison slowly taking hold, its movements became more and more sluggish.
The brown bear seemed to know that the situation was dire and completely gave up all resistance and evasive actions, charging directly at Yuan Ming in a desperate last stand!
The bear's final desperate attack was significantly faster than usual.
However, Yuan Ming was well-prepared. He moved towards a large tree big enough for two people to embrace, using it as a shield.
"Roar..."
The fierce brown bear charged forward undeterred, its eyes suddenly turning blood-red as it let out a deafening roar.
"I knew you would use this move." Yuan Ming was ready. Dan Tian Power surged out, spreading throughout his body.
He barely shook, and the movement of his feet was not much affected. At the moment before the brown bear charged, he dodged away.
"Bang"
The fierce brown bear failed to stop in time and slammed straight into the tree, its massive body bouncing back and sitting down on the ground, dazed.
The entire tree crashed down, stirring up a large cloud of dust.
The fierce brown bear struggled to get up and tried to flee, but after only a few steps, it collapsed onto the ground.
Yuan Ming's figure emerged from the dust, instantly arriving beside the brown bear, his right hand grabbing fiercely downward.
The sharp ape claws pierced into the brown bear's neck bone with a "puchi," as he slashed downward powerfully.
The brown bear's neck bone was severed, half of its neck cut through, and blood surged out, its huge body convulsing a couple of times before going still.
Yuan Ming took out a Blood Storage Bag and drained the brown bear's blood, then, without bothering to refine it, he slumped to the ground, gasping for air in big gulps. The intense battle had indeed taken his very last bit of strength.
This brown bear indeed possessed terrifying physical strength, and its hide was astonishingly defensive. Had it not been for Yuan Ming's ruse to exhaust most of the bear's energy and the addition of Soft Bone Poison Liquid, he would definitely not have been a match for the beast.
At this moment, Yuan Ming felt his entire skeleton aching, and even moving a bit seemed difficult.
But the area was reeking of blood and was by no means a place to stay for long.
Yuan Ming bit the tip of his tongue sharply, using the pain to stimulate his spirit, and stood up with the support of a nearby tree before heading back the way he came.
Yet, he hadn't gone far when an unexpected change occurred.
His entire body suddenly felt as if struck by lightning; the White Ape Skin that covered him began to wriggle, and an agitated aura permeated out.
The lingering Mana in his body suddenly became restless; his eyes showed traces of Blood Light, and a surge of killing intent rose in his heart.
"Not again." Yuan Ming's heart chilled. He quickly sat down cross-legged and started the Nine Elements Technique.
After three complete rounds of Grand Circulation, the desire to kill was barely suppressed somewhat.
Concentrating Mana in his left hand, he touched the Incense Burner Mark on his right arm.
A flash of aquamarine light passed over the mark, revealing the Mysterious Incense Burner in his palm.
With a surge of warmth from the incense burner blending into his body and mind,
Yuan Ming felt his whole body as if soaked in a hot spring, his head especially so, and the Blood Light in his eyes slowly dissipated along with the killing intent.
A quarter of an hour later, the disturbance caused by the White Ape Skin completely vanished.
Yuan Ming's eyes softened, and he dispelled the Fur Cloak Skill, silent as he gazed at the incense burner in his hand.
This kind of incident had occurred twice in the past three months, always after a fierce fight when his Mana and strength were nearly depleted.
Now the thirst for blood and killing was extremely intense, and the Nine Elements Technique could only resist it, not diminish it. He was clueless about how to deal with it the first time it happened, but then he recalled the warmth from the incense burner had the effect of nourishing the Divine Soul. In his urgency, he retrieved the incense burner, and that was how he suppressed the urge.
"Could it be that being transformed into the White Ape for an extended period in these mountains, I've unwittingly absorbed some of its malevolent aura? Fortunately, I have the incense burner." Yuan Ming privately celebrated but was also worried that this desire might grow stronger with each passing day.
He had intended to ask Hu Huochang about the White Ape Skin's transformation, but unfortunately, he had never found a good opportunity.
Yuan Ming shook his head, put away the incense burner, and quickly left, climbing up a nearby large tree.
Even without transforming into a White Ape, his tree climbing was much faster than before, and he quickly found a relatively flat spot halfway up to sit cross-legged and circulate the Nine Elements Technique, recovering his Mana.
A moment later, he took out the Blood Storage Bag and activated it with Mana to refine the bear's blood, which swiftly diminished and soon turned into a ball of Essence Blood.
But this ball of Essence Blood was a whole circle larger than that of the Green Fox and other Fierce Beasts, and the pulse of Mana within was much stronger.
"It seems this brown bear is very likely a Level 1 Intermediate-stage Fierce Beast." Yuan Ming gripped the Blood Storage Bag tightly.
After this battle, he had gained a preliminary understanding of the true strength of Level 1 Middle Stage Fierce Beasts. Although formidable, they were not entirely unbeatable.
He put away the Blood Storage Bag and once again cast the Fur Cloak Skill to transform into a White Ape and continued deeper into the forest.
An hour later, a fairly wide stream appeared in front of him, meandering out from a gully not far away. The stream was very clear, and a refreshing cool moisture hit him.
After traveling for so long, Yuan Ming was somewhat thirsty. He bent down to drink a few mouthfuls of the stream water and was about to continue forward when he suddenly paused, looking at the ground beside him.
There lay a few fresh green fruit shells, obviously just peeled.
Yuan Ming recognized these fruits, sour mixed with sweet, a rare tasty fruit of the forest, which he had also eaten a few times before.
Dropping fruit shells in the forest was normal enough, as many monkeys also picked fruit to eat. But monkeys eating wild fruits wouldn't peel them so thoroughly, would they?

chapters.title: Chapter 41 - 21: Stimulating
chapters.content:
"Could these husks have been left by other Fur Beast Slaves?" Yuan Ming looked around, but didn't spot anything else of note.
Suddenly, his gaze sharpened as he looked towards a large tree not far away.
A silver cat, about half a foot tall and resembling an ordinary house cat in size, was sitting on a slender branch of the tree.
The cat was completely covered in silver-white fur without a single blemish, looking extremely beautiful. One of its eyes was golden while the other was amber, like two gleaming gems, and it was staring right at Yuan Ming.
As their gazes met, the silver cat immediately turned and darted away, jumping agilely from tree to tree and vanishing in an instant.
"Why run? I'm not going to eat you! That silver cat sure is skittish," Yuan Ming said, not particularly concerned, and continued searching the area.
After a moment, he let out a light "hmm," fixating on some grass on the ground not far away and halting his steps.
There on the ground was a shallow human footprint that looked quite fresh.
Yuan Ming pondered briefly, then moved in the direction of the footprint.
The owner of the footprint didn't seem to be trying to hide their tracks, making it easy to follow.
About a quarter of an hour later, a region of hard mountain rock appeared ahead, where the trail of footprints abruptly ended.
Yuan Ming frowned and stood silently for a while, then continued onward.
Upon emerging from the rocky area, his view lightened to reveal a vast, dusky lake.
The lake wasn't very large, roughly ten acres or so, calm and undisturbed. It was surrounded by weeds as tall as a person. Even though it was clearly summer, the temperature near the lake was notably lower than in the woods.
Yuan Ming squatted by the edge of the lake and touched the water with his hand, a chilling cold seeping through.
At that moment, the nearby grass "whooshed," and a silver shadow sprang out.
Yuan Ming braced for a confrontation, but when he got a clear look, he was slightly surprised.
The silver figure wasn't anything else but the silver cat he had encountered earlier; it had a black object in its mouth and its tail was cocked high.
Upon seeing Yuan Ming, the cat appeared startled and immediately turned back, diving into the grass, dropping the black object from its mouth.
"There's that silver cat again." Yuan Ming quickly moved forward a few steps, but the tall weeds swallowed up the cat the moment it entered them, erasing any trace of it.
He let out a sigh of regret. In fact, he quite liked the appearance of the sleek silver cat. If he could catch and tame it, it would make for a nice diversion during breaks from cultivation.
Yuan Ming moved forward, then something occurred to him, and he turned back a few steps to pick up an object from the ground — the black object the cat had been carrying. He examined it closely.
The object appeared to be a piece of leather with exquisite patterns on it, clearly man-made.
"There's no way such a thing could be found in these deep forests; could it have been left by someone?" With this thought, Yuan Ming hurried over to the grass where the silver cat had emerged but found nothing.
He examined the black leather in his hand again, bringing it to his nose to sniff.
A fishy smell assailed his nostrils, but it wasn't the odor of an animal's mouth; it was more akin to the rotting smell of aquatic plants.
Yuan Ming's gaze shifted to the verdant lake, and then he began searching along its shore, soon making a discovery.
On the damp soil by the lake's edge, there were a few shallow cat paw prints.
Following the prints, Yuan Ming pushed aside a patch of thick grass nearby, his pupils narrowing slightly.
There lay a large corpse, its upper body almost skeletal and its lower body embedded in the mud by the lake, obviously dead for a long time. Its clothes were rotted through, and it wore a black leather jacket on its upper body — the same kind of leather the silver cat had dropped.
Yuan Ming's eyes fell on the corpse's waist, where a piece of black Beast Skin was wrapped around. It appeared to be Furred Beast Skin.
He crouched down beside the corpse, touched the black Beast Skin for a moment, and untied it.
This item was entirely different from his White Ape Beast Skin; it was hairless and covered with dim white lines, with a gel-like substance resembling scale armor on its back, seemingly the outer skin of some aquatic Fierce Beast.
The rest of the Beast Skin was mostly intact except for a palm-sized tear at the back, likely penetrated by some sharp weapon.
Thi-s# con!t^e.n-t. is pre&s%e.n#ted by *!.+
Yuan Ming carefully pulled the corpse from the mud; several ribs around its heart at the back were broken, a fatal wound probably inflicted in a surprise attack from behind.
He searched around the body for a while but didn't find any clues. The corpse's Blood Storage Bag was also missing.
"It seems this person was more likely killed by another Fur Beast Slave rather than by a Fierce Beast," a chill crossed Yuan Ming's mind unbidden.
Fur Beast Slaves are both beast and slave.
Trapped within the Ten Thousand Mountains, it's the law of the jungle, survival of the fittest. Just as you eye your prey eagerly, aren't you the prey in someone else's eyes?
"That's right, Elder Hu Huo once hinted that these Beast Skins from Biluo Cave were laboriously refined by the Sect and are quite precious. Each skin has a magic mark embedded within. Whenever a Fur Beast Slave dies, the Sect sends someone to retrieve the Beast Skin following the mark. Why didn't they take this one?" Suddenly recalling this, Yuan Ming was puzzled.
He looked thoughtfully at the torn part of the black beast skin, pinched his fingers to release the White Ape Transformation, then channeled his mana into the black beast skin to activate the Fur Cloak Skill. The beast skin, however, remained motionless.
"It seems it's broken, and that's why no one came to retrieve it. What a waste of time," Yuan Ming murmured to himself, discarded the black beast skin, and turned to leave.
But after taking a few steps, he seemed to think of something, picked up the black beast skin again, and walked towards the woods by the lake. Soon, he arrived at a secluded spot.
Yuan Ming sat down, spread the beast skin out in front of him, and then summoned the Mysterious Incense Burner.
His white ape skin had undergone a subtle change upon touching the incense burner. Perhaps, it could also have some impact on this black beast skin, though that remained to be seen.
Of course, he didn't expect the incense burner to repair the black beast skin; he just wanted to take the opportunity to learn more about this green incense burner.
Yuan Ming placed the incense burner on the beast skin. As soon as they touched, the Mysterious Incense Burner suddenly lit up. A green light emanated from it, pouring a warm current of air into the black beast skin.
The dim white lines on the surface of the black beast skin, when merged with the green light, spread out like water entering a channel. Wherever the light passed, the faint lines brightened, and the entire black beast skin began to tremble slightly.
The green light swiftly flowed through every part of the beast skin, converging towards the tear at the back. There, the white lines were exceptionally dense, seemingly a crucial junction.
It was no wonder that the beast skin was rendered useless with such an area destroyed.
The green light surged around the tear, the white lines there flickering ceaselessly. Soon, a somewhat blurry phantom emerged from the tear in the beast skin—a toad with a large head and a round body, its limbs splayed out.
"What's this? Could it be the soul of a toad fierce beast? My white ape skin also revealed a phantom of White Ape under the influence of the incense burner before. It seems that all Fur Beast Skins contain a beast soul," Yuan Ming thought quietly.
The toad phantom within the green light gradually solidified and, after letting out a "croak," vanished in a flash into the tear, leaving no trace.
With a slight "sizzling" sound, the white lines around the tear stretched out like living things, bypassing the tear and rejoining together.
"It can actually repair itself like this!" Yuan Ming exclaimed, both shocked and delighted.
Once those white lines reconnected, a subtle ripple of energy appeared across the entire black beast skin, clearly fully repaired.
Not only that, but the black beast skin also appeared as good as new, its natural patterns much clearer, as if it had just been skinned, similar to what happened to the white ape skin after the influence of the incense burner.
Yuan Ming channeled his mana into the black beast skin, activating the Fur Cloak Skill.
The black beast skin wrapped around his body like a living thing, covering every part of him. He quickly completed the transformation.
His body was now covered in black beast skin, his back speckled with bulging black lumps that looked very sturdy. Webbed membranes grew out between his fingers and toes, and his eyes heavily drooped.
Yuan Ming put away the incense burner and went to the lakeside to look at his reflection. At this moment, he looked very much like a humanoid toad.
"No wonder I heard some strange noises earlier. It turns out to be a toad skin. When I first got the white ape skin with no offensive capability, I was frustrated enough. I didn't expect someone else to be worse off than me. What good is a toad?" Yuan Ming said somewhat speechlessly as he looked at his ugly reflection in the water.
Yuan Ming moved his body, feeling for the abilities that came with his toad transformation.
He felt a faint current within his chest cavity, and his belly appeared to have grown much larger. Each breath was much deeper than before, and the intervals between breaths grew longer and longer.
Yuan Ming took a deep breath, and air rolled into his body, causing his belly to expand continuously until he looked like a woman in the late stages of pregnancy.
However, he didn't feel uncomfortable at all and stood still, holding his breath.
A quarter of an hour passed, and Yuan Ming still felt no discomfort or shortness of breath; he could move with ease.
He leaped into the lake and dove toward the bottom.
The lake's surface rippled and then calmed quickly, returning to serenity.
After another quarter of an hour, water splashed on the opposite bank of the lake as Yuan Ming's figure emerged, leaping ashore.
A glint of excitement flashed in his eyes. The toad beast skin had allowed him to go without breathing for two whole quarters of an hour.
Wulu had mentioned that some parts of the Ten Thousand Mountains were filled with deadly Poison Miasma. With this toad beast skin, should he unfortunately encounter it, at least he'd have enough time to escape.
In addition, after transforming into a toad, his swimming speed in the water was quite fast, making it a decent means of escape.
Compared to the toad's effortless movement in water, its mobility on land was much less efficient, restricted to somewhat clumsy hopping without much offensive capability—at least he hadn't discovered any yet.
With this in mind, he couldn't help but feel some sympathy for the fellow who used the toad skin for his Fur Beast transformation.
Yuan Ming pinched his fingers to release the toad transformation and carefully stored away the black beast skin.
The combat capability of the black toad seemed far inferior to the White Ape Transformation at present, but in certain environments, it might prove to be highly useful.
However, the greatest gain today was the further understanding of the green incense burner.
This Mysterious Incense Burner seemed capable of restoring damaged Beast Skins in some way, and perhaps it could even draw out some of the skins' latent abilities. This was something he could utilize in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 42 - 22 Making Friends
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming dug a pit by the lake and buried the body. Then, standing in front of the slightly barren mound of earth, he remained motionless for a long time.
"You must have already been reincarnated, in your next life may you not be a Beast Slave again. The path of cultivation is so cruel, it might be better to live carefree as a commoner."
"Today you have me to bury your remains, but if I meet with misfortune one day, who will collect my body?"
"Heaven and earth are merciless, it's the survival of the fittest. If I can't rid myself of the status of a Beast Slave by my own power and get accepted into Biluo Cave, my end might be even worse than yours."
