Yuan Ming whispered a few words to the little mound, it seemed to remind himself of the harsh reality and at the same time, to strengthen his determination to return to the Central Plains.
He didn't transform into the White Ape and continued his journey, quickly leaving the lake behind and entering a dense forest.
Not far away, on the branches of a large tree, a silver shadow crouched. It was the same silver cat from before, its slender pupils tightly following Yuan Ming's retreating figure.
As the light dimmed around him, Yuan Ming slowed down and became very cautious.
Suddenly, he stopped in his tracks and squatted down.
On the ground, he found another set of footprints, matching the size of the person he had been tracking.
Yuan Ming followed the footprints, and before long, he heard the sounds of fighting ahead, mixed with the roars of Fierce Beasts.
Yuan Ming raised an eyebrow and quickened his pace until he reached the source of the noise.
This was an open space in the forest, where two large Exotic Beasts were fighting desperately for their lives. Several large trees had collapsed, and dust was swirling about in the open space.
One of the combatants was an upright, blue-colored wolf beast, standing one and a half zhang tall, with thick limbs exuding a domineering presence, its might surpassing even the transformed White Ape that Yuan Ming had become.
The wolf beast's eyes were narrow, the pale blue pupils filled with coldness, yet even more so with calmness, clearly a Fur Beast Slave.
The other Exotic Beast was a sprawling black crocodile on the ground, three zhang in length, covered in thick scales, its yellow eyes emitting a hungry, savage light.
This crocodile was not only immense in size but also extraordinarily strong. Its long tail, like a black steel whip, swept deep marks into the ground with each swing, and its thick crocodile mouth could easily snap thick tree trunks, making it far more formidable than the previous brown bear.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave was clearly not a match for the Black Crocodile in terms of strength, but it excelled in agility and leaping power. It continually dodged the attacks of the Black Crocodile, seeking opportunities to strike with its scythe-like sharp claws.
However, the scales of the Black Crocodile were extremely tough. The claws of the Green Wolf could only leave shallow scratches, not even drawing blood, resulting in a stalemate.
"This Green Wolf Beast Slave is extraordinary in strength, and their cultivation should be above mine," Yuan Ming had initially planned to hide and watch, but after a moment's thought, he decided to reveal himself in his White Ape form.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave immediately noticed Yuan Ming's presence, its eyes sweeping across with a gleam of cold light.Visit My Virtual Library Empire (*) for more.
The Fur Beast Slaves of these mountains, although all collecting Essence Blood for the Biluo Cave, had far from harmonious relationships with each other. Competition and subterfuge, even murder and pillaging, were not uncommon, all of which Biluo Cave ignored.
Now, suddenly a White Ape Beast Slave emerged, clearly intending to wait for the Green Wolf and the Black Crocodile to both suffer injuries before taking advantage of the situation.
However, the Green Wolf Beast Slave was also puzzled. Such underhanded tactics usually involved ambushing from hiding, so what was the White Ape's direct approach about?
The Black Crocodile took advantage of the Green Wolf Beast Slave's momentary distraction, opening its mouth and spitting something out.
A bright stream of water, like an arrow, shot from the mouth of the Black Crocodile, slashing towards the legs of the Green Wolf Beast Slave with such speed that it almost trailed an afterimage.
As if anticipating this, the Green Wolf Beast Slave leaped up. His large frame jumped three feet into the air, easily avoiding the assault of water.
He then descended, whether by accident or design, right on the Black Crocodile's back, and his right leg suddenly moved.
His claws turned into a flash of green shadow, aiming for the eyes of the Black Crocodile.
Startled, the Black Crocodile quickly twisted its head to avoid the blow.
But the Green Wolf Beast Slave's strike was so swift that the Black Crocodile couldn't completely avoid it, getting its snout scratched.
With scales covering its body, the Black Crocodile's nose was relatively fragile. Immediately, five long gashes appeared, and blood flowed.
The Black Crocodile let out a furious roar as its enormous body rolled on the spot, stirring up clouds of dust.
Wary of the Black Crocodile's brute strength, the Green Wolf Beast Slave quickly leaped away.
"Roar!"
The Black Crocodile's yellow eyes fixated on the Green Wolf Beast Slave, threads of blood appearing within them. The originally black skin began to show sinuous blood-red lines, and the body swelled even more.
"What kind of power is this?" Yuan Ming, watching from a distance, let out a light exclamation of surprise.
"It's a Bloodline Crocodile!" the Green Wolf Beast Slave exclaimed in human language, with a tinge of astonishment.
In the blink of an eye, the Black Crocodile's transformation was complete, growing by a third in size, with many blood-red lines on its scales, and the injury on its nose stopped bleeding.
All four of its limbs slapped the ground hard, its massive body surged towards the Green Wolf Beast Slave with a gust of wind, creating a loud wafting noise across several meters.
Seeing the crocodile's momentum, the Green Wolf Beast Slave did not dare to confront it head-on and dodged to the side.
However, after transforming, the Black Crocodile became much more agile. Its tail whipped on the ground, instantly changing direction, continuing to pounce towards the Green Wolf Beast Slave. Its speed did not wane in the slightest, and in the blink of an eye, it caught up with its prey.
The crocodile's mouth stretched out like lightning, almost leaving an afterimage, biting onto the Green Wolf Beast Slave's left arm, one thick forepaw pressing on him, looking as if it was about to pin him down.
At that moment, a green shadow shot out from afar, heading straight for the Black Crocodile's left eye.
The Black Crocodile, though engaged in combat, had not lost its senses. Its head turned slightly, and the green shadow hit the scales near its left eye—an item that turned out to be a green bamboo tube.
Bang!
The bamboo tube burst open, spilling out a pale purple liquid that showered the Black Crocodile's head and dripped into its eyes.
The Black Crocodile's eyes burned with intense pain and quickly turned black and rotten, emitting anguished screams as its mouth opened wide.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave quickly pulled out his left arm, breaking into a cold sweat.
But this man was extremely fierce; not only did he not retreat, he took advantage of the situation and lunged towards the Black Crocodile, his right claw extending swiftly.
Blood Light flashed!
The right hand of the Green Wolf Beast Slave pierced into the crocodile's right eye, gouging out its eyeball.
The Black Crocodile let out an earth-shattering roar, its massive body rolling violently as its tail thrashed around crazily; nearby trees were smashed to pieces, creating a terrifying commotion.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave had leaped away in time and was not affected by the Black Crocodile's frenzied attacks, and he looked towards Yuan Ming in the distance.
He saw clearly that the bamboo tube had been thrown by Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming nodded to the Green Wolf Beast Slave but continued to stand there, showing no intention of getting close.
After raging wildly for a while, the bloodlines on the Black Crocodile's body rapidly receded, and its size returned to its original state.
"So such aberrations are time-limited," Yuan Ming thought to himself.
As the Black Crocodile's body recovered, so did its rationality. It ran away with the speed of lightning, its claws pounding the ground thunderously, heading into the distance.
Blind in both eyes, it was no match for the Green Wolf Beast Slave, leaving only a path to certain death.
However, having lost its sight, the Black Crocodile couldn't discern directions and ran headlong into a massive tree, as large as a grinding wheel, after not getting far.
With a "bang," the huge tree was struck and split in half, collapsing to the side.
The Black Crocodile was also knocked to the ground, exposing its pale, soft underbelly.
Cleary an experienced beast hunter, the Green Wolf Beast Slave immediately leapt forward, plunging two claws into the crocodile's belly and yanked fiercely.
Several long gashes were torn in the crocodile's belly in an instant, and blood gushed out, leaving red and white innards all over the ground.
The Black Crocodile struggled in frenzy once again, but having suffered fatal injuries, it soon lay still.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave bent down to collect the Black Crocodile's blood with a Blood Storage Bag, all the while casting a cautious eye towards Yuan Ming close by.
Yuan Ming still stood quietly in the same spot without any suspicious movements. Seeing this, the eyes of the Green Wolf Beast Slave somewhat softened.
"Thank you for your assistance just now. I am Hagon. May I have the pleasure of knowing your name?" said the Green Wolf Beast Slave, finishing his collection and bowing to Yuan Ming.
"I am Yuan Ming," Yuan Ming returned the gesture.
"So you are Brother Yuan. This place isn't suitable for conversation. Let's find another place to talk," suggested Hagon.
The recent battle had caused a tremendous commotion, so naturally, Yuan Ming had no objection.
They quickly left the area, soon arriving by a lakeside.
Yuan Ming's brows furrowed slightly, recognizing the lake as the one where he had found the Black Beast Skin.
Hagon, covered in dust, washed himself in the lake, released the Fur Cloak Skill, and revealed his true form: a man in his twenties, tall, with blonde hair and blue eyes—a typical appearance of Southern Border people.
Yuan Ming had by now also put away the Ape Skin, showing his own appearance.
"Are you Central Plains people?" Hagon asked with a hint of surprise in his eyes.
"Indeed. Through some fortunate coincidences, I entered the Biluo Cave to become a Beast Slave," Yuan Ming did not hide the truth.
"I see. But Brother Yuan seems somewhat unfamiliar," Hagon acknowledged with an 'oh,' not prying further into Yuan Ming's identity."
"Indeed, I have not been here for long. I happened to see Brother Hagon fighting the Black Crocodile and stayed out of curiosity to watch; I hope Brother Hagon doesn't mind," Yuan Ming said amiably.
"Not at all. If it weren't for Brother Yuan's timely assistance, I would have been skinned if not dead by now. I should be the one thanking you," Hagon answered earnestly.
Yuan Ming, seeing Hagon's sincere attitude, felt even more resolute about making a new acquaintance.
After talking further, they gradually became more familiar with each other.
From the conversation, Yuan Ming learned that Hagon had been a Fur Beast Slave for two years, qualifying as a veteran.
"Brother Hagon, how much do you know about Biluo Cave, the sect we're in?" Yuan Ming inquired about his concerns.
"My experience is much like yours, Brother Yuan. I was also inexplicably captured and brought here. I do not know much about Biluo Cave, only that it is a major faction in the Southern Border, with numerous disciples and three Core Formation Stage Cave Masters at the helm, dominating the Ten Thousand Mountains, a massive mountain range with considerable power," Hagon explained.
"Ten Thousand Mountains—is that this area of forests we're in?" Yuan Ming asked, recalling the Southern Border characters on the large stone.
"Exactly," Hagon nodded.
Yuan Ming turned and looked around him. Mountains rose on all sides, stretching out beyond the horizon, with no end in sight.
"Ten Thousand Mountains is one of the largest mountain ranges in the Southern Border. You won't see the end just by looking," Hagon laughed heartily.
Yuan Ming smiled faintly; he wasn't really trying to see the end of Ten Thousand Mountains, just reacquaining himself with the mountain range under Biluo Cave's control.
"Brother Hagon, within Ten Thousand Mountains, do you know how many Fur Beast Slaves like us there are?" Yuan Ming asked after turning his attention back from the scenery.

chapters.title: Chapter 43 - 23: Forming Factions and Alliances
chapters.content:
"All over the Ten Thousand Mountains, Fur Beast Slaves collect Fierce Beast Essence Blood. I don't know exactly how much there is. I only recognize a few people from nearby regions and have never had contact with those further away." Hagon could see that Yuan Ming had helped him just now to glean some information, but he didn't mind.
Yuan Ming nodded slowly and then asked several more questions about the Fur Beast Slaves, to which he received fairly satisfactory answers.
"Brother Hagon, I have another question. I have been practicing the Fur Cloak Skill for several months, and a few days ago, when I used it, a sudden urge for bloodshed surged from within me, almost controlling my will. Do you know why this happened?" Yuan Ming asked about the matter that most concerned him.
"It's quite normal, it's the backlash from using the Fur Cloak Skill," Hagon replied calmly.
"Backlash?" Yuan Ming's expression tightened as he immediately followed up.
"The Fur Cloak Skill is a unique secret technique of Biluo Cave, designed to merge specially-made beast skins with those who have just started on the path of cultivation, granting them the formidable strength to withstand demon beasts. It is indeed a powerful spell, but this strength, after all, is not cultivated by ourselves, and it comes with severe side effects," Hagon sighed and explained.
"The side effect, is it the backlash you just mentioned?" Yuan Ming asked urgently.
"The beast skins in our hands were made from the hides of fierce beasts throughout the Ten Thousand Mountains, refined through a secret technique by Biluo Cave. These skins contain the original demonic power and sinister energy of the fierce beasts, which will gradually erode our bodies. Once it reaches a certain extent, backlash will occur, ultimately leading to a complete fusion with the beast skin and transforming into a monstrous creature that knows only slaughter," Hagon's voice carried a hint of bitterness.
"Is there any way to avoid the backlash of the Fur Cloak Skill?" Yuan Ming inquired.
"No, as long as you use the Fur Cloak Skill, the sinister force within the beast skin will continue to erode our bodies. The more often the skill is used, the greater the risk of backlash, and eventually, one would completely turn into a bloodthirsty monster. It's a point of no return, and no one can escape it," Hagon's eyes flashed with pain.
"How long can we Fur Beast Slaves normally hold on?" Yuan Ming's expression grew grave as he asked.
"If one only hunts five beasts a month and uses the Fur Cloak Skill as little as possible, it's not a problem to last four or five years or even longer. However, if they frequently use the Fur Cloak Skill, it's not uncommon to be completely insane within a year or two," Hagon said.
"Biluo Cave just allows this to happen?" Yuan Ming couldn't help but feel a sudden heaviness in his heart, and after a moment of silence, he spoke.
"Why would Biluo Cave care about the life and death of us Fur Beast Slaves? Right, if one can collect a thousand portions of Essence Blood before completely losing their mind, perhaps one could be accepted as a Registered Disciple and escape having to use the Fur Cloak Skill," after saying this, a self-mocking smile appeared on Hagon's lips.
"You've also accepted this mission?" Yuan Ming asked.
"Heh heh, anyone who performs conspicuously well in the first few months, those elders who manage us will quietly offer this mission, encouraging us to collect as much Essence Blood as possible in a short amount of time," Hagon chuckled, casting a sidelong glance at Yuan Ming.
"If it's as you said, I'm afraid one might go insane before even gathering enough Beast Blood," Yuan Ming said with a wry smile.
"Not necessarily. There are those with exceptional talent. If they haven't lost their sanity, it shows great mental fortitude, and such a person would surely not be rejected by Biluo Cave," Hagon replied noncommittally.
Yuan Ming nodded silently, about to ask more questions, when suddenly his eyebrows shot up, and he looked over his shoulder into the dense woods behind him. At the same time, he activated the Fur Cloak Skill, transforming into the form of a White Ape.
Hagon, on the other hand, swiftly turned around, his figure already morphing into the shape of a Green Wolf.
Five figures flitted out of the dense jungle, all of them Fur Beast Slaves, enclosing Yuan Ming and Hagon in a fan-shaped formation with swift movements.
Almost as soon as Yuan Ming and Hagon completed their transformations, the encirclement was already in place.
Yuan Ming frowned; it hadn't been easy to find even one Fur Beast Slave before, but now, just a short while into the forest, he had encountered six.
However, the intent of these five newcomers was clearly malicious.
"It's you lot!" Hagon spoke at ease, recognizing the incomers.
"Brother Hagon, we meet again. Just now over there we saw the corpse of a Bloodline Crocodile—must've been your hunt, right? It seems your strength has improved. I'm impressed, really impressed," a Red Tiger Beast Slave stepped forward, glanced at Yuan Ming and spoke to Hagon with a smile.
This man's body was huge, even larger than Hagon's Green Wolf transformation, with a physique full of muscles and strength, obviously the leader of the group.
"Zan Bai, you've become even more hypocritical after joining the Green Wolf Gang. Out with it, what do you want?" Hagon snorted lightly.
"Hagon, you've messed with our people on several occasions. If we don't punish you harshly, what would others think of me? Since we both joined Biluo Cave at the same time, hand over your Blood Storage Bag, and I'll let you leave," Zan Bai spoke indifferently.
"Really?" Hagon seemed somewhat interested.
"Of course, you should know that we people of the Hei Mu Clan keep our promises," Zan Bai declared proudly while patting his chest.
"Wuli, the Spotted Leopard was discovered by us at the same time, right? Just because you lacked the ability to kill it doesn't mean you should prevent others from acting," Hagon retorted to the Gray Wolf Beast Slave with a snicker.
"Nonsense, it was you who stole my prey," Wuli, the Gray Wolf Beast Slave, retorted angrily.
Zan Bai's gaze swept over Wuli sharply, as though rebuking him for speaking recklessly.
Wuli's heart jolted, and he stepped back, not daring to say more.
"Hagon, let's cut to the chase. You've provoked our people time and again; if there's no severe punishment, how will others view me? For the sake of both of us joining Biluo Cave at the same time, hand over your Blood Storage Bag and I will allow you to leave," Zan Bai said blandly.
"Is that so?" Hagon seemed to be swayed.
"Certainly, you know the people of the Hei Mu Clan honor our word," Zan Bai said with a touch of pride, patting his chest.
"Fine, you've got me surrounded today, I give up, catch." Hagon took a Blood Storage Bag from his bosom and threw it to Zan Bai.
Yuan Ming felt slightly surprised; the bottom of this Blood Storage Bag was stained with a bit of blood, and it wasn't the same one Hagon had used before. Could it be something he had taken after killing a Fur Beast Slave?
Hagon seemed to notice Yuan Ming's gaze and looked over in this direction, his left hand behind his back, gesturing towards the front-left.
Upon seeing this, Yuan Ming's expression turned thoughtful.
Zan Bai also looked somewhat surprised. He caught the Blood Storage Bag subconsciously and suddenly felt something off about the texture, the bottom of the bag had a hole, and inside was a black ball.
He looked carefully and his expression immediately turned to shock and anger.
The black ball "bang" exploded, and a large cloud of black smoke burst into existence, engulfing a dozen or so feet around the lakeside in an instant.
"Go!" Hagon's form turned into a green streak, flying away towards the front-left.
Although Yuan Ming couldn't see Hagon, he immediately ran in that direction and easily escaped the encirclement of the Red Tiger Beast Slave and the others.
"Haha, Zan Bai, till we meet again!" Hagon laughed heartily, leading Yuan Ming deep into the jungle.
The instant Yuan Ming entered the jungle, he swiftly took two stones from the bag on his back and threw them left and right.
The stones shot out and struck two spots in the jungle, causing the leaves there to rustle violently.
Figures moved within the black smoke; Zan Bai and the others flew out but saw no trace of Hagon and Yuan Ming by the lakeside, only three swaying areas of bushes, unsure of which direction the two men had gone.
Zan Bai's eyes were full of anger as he clenched his fists.
...
Yuan Ming followed Hagon and didn't stop until they were seven or eight miles away, seeing no one pursuing them.
"Hagon, who were those guys?" Yuan Ming caught his breath and asked.
"Those guys are from the Green Wolf Gang. Like us, they are all Fur Beast Slaves. Their leader is called Wu Bao, who, with a dozen or so men, formed a group specializing in plundering others," Hagon said, leaning against an old tree.
"Not daring to hunt demon beasts themselves but instead targeting others, what's the difference between them and bandits?" Yuan Ming said disdainfully.
"Actually, there are quite a few groups like them out there, but most choose to hunt beasts together. Only a few engage in plundering. Yuan Ming, with your skills and courage, you might as well join a group; it could be easier for you," Hagon sighed and said.
Sourced directly from *.
"What about you, are you a member of a group too?" Yuan Ming raised his eyebrow and asked.
Hagon shook his head and said, "I used to be, but I left."
"Why?" Yuan Ming asked curiously.
"We part ways when our paths do not align. Once a group forms, there must be a leader, and a hierarchy gets established. When hunting beasts, it certainly has advantages and can greatly prevent casualties. But when it comes to sharing the spoils, it's not so harmonious. The leader and his close associates naturally get more, as for everyone else... Heh," Hagon didn't finish his sentence, but Yuan Ming already understood.
"In that case, it's better to operate alone," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"No matter what, surviving here is not an easy thing. Just a reminder, don't trust others too easily, and don't help others too readily. When push comes to shove, people are capable of anything," Hagon said with a complex expression.
"I have my own principles when it comes to doing things," Yuan Ming nodded and replied with a smile.
Hearing this, Hagon didn't say much more.
After resting for a while, Yuan Ming suddenly spoke, "Hagon, what was that thing you threw earlier that released so much smoke?"
"That thing is called a Smoke Bomb, something the Registered Disciples of Biluo Cave came up with. It's very useful for escaping," Hagon replied.
"Smoke Bomb? Something made by the Registered Disciples of Biluo Cave, how did you get it?" Yuan Ming asked in confusion.
"What, you haven't been to Toad Valley yet?" Hagon asked, somewhat surprised.
"No," Yuan Ming shook his head.
"Alright then, I've got nothing else to do today, so I'll take you there for a look. It's a place for barter. You can use parts from demon beasts or directly use Blood Food to exchange for things you need," Hagon smiled, stood up from the ground, patted the dirt off his backside, and said.
"Isn't that just like a market? There's such a place here?" Yuan Ming's curiosity was piqued.
"It's something that the Biluo Cave Disciples came up with. They sometimes need us to risk our lives to obtain things from demon beasts. Come on, it's not far from here, you can get there in half an hour," Hagon grinned and said.

chapters.title: Chapter 44 - 24 Energy Storage Arm
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming followed Hagon, traversing forests and leaping across streams. After more than half of two hours, they finally arrived at a secluded valley.
Just as they reached the mouth of the valley, Yuan Ming wrinkled his nose and stopped.
"What's this strange smell?" he asked, covering his nose.
He smelled something akin to sulfur, but in actuality, it was much more complex.
"The scent of Beast Repelling Powder. It can drive away some poison insects and Fierce Beasts, preventing them from getting close to this place," Hagon explained, pointing to the red and white intermixed powder on the ground not far ahead.
"Can you also trade for this stuff inside?" Yuan Ming asked, his eyebrow raised.
"You can, but there's not much use for it. Sure, it can fend off some poison insects and Fierce Beasts, but it also easily gives away your hiding spot. Sometimes, people are more dangerous than Fierce Beasts," Hagon said.
The entrance of the valley was quite narrow, like a natural choke point, but once inside, it opened up generously, becoming quite spacious, much like moving from a toad's mouth to its belly.
The moment the two of them entered the valley, they hadn't taken many steps when several crudely styled stone houses constructed of stones appeared ahead.
The stone houses didn't have doors, just open doorways, through which one could vaguely see figures inside.
Around these few stone houses were also some people dressed in Beast Skins, not many in number, each with an expressionless face, showing no emotion.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to approach for a closer look, he was stopped by Hagon.
"Be careful what you say later. Don't provoke those Registered Disciples. Most of them have rather bad tempers," Hagon said as a precaution.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming silently nodded.
He walked up to the first stone house, took a glance inside, and saw that the interior was furnished quite simply, with just a wooden table and a reclining chair.
A young man in a green Cloth Robe was leisurely lounging in the chair, idly swaying, holding a blue paper scroll in his hand that covered half of his face, looking utterly content.
In front of him on the table stood a wooden sign, with a white paper attached, on which was written, "Buying aged Spirit Grass, various types of ore."
It was just a simple sentence, with the specifics of what was being bought and the exact age not specified.
In the stone house next to his, there was a similar table, with a wooden sign upon which was also a white paper, on which was written, "Buying Spirit Grass, ores, Beast Bones, Blood Food."
However, this house was empty, with no one inside.
The other two stone houses had a similar setup, each with a display, but all seemed rather rudimentary.
In the last stone house, Yuan Ming happened to see two Fur Beast Slaves trading with a Registered Disciple inside.
The Disciple appeared impatient, picking through the two dark red ores and a plant that resembled ginseng but was wax-yellow in color brought by the Fur Beast Slaves.
In the end, he sent the Fur Beast Slave away with a small white porcelain bottle.
After thanking profusely, the Fur Beast Slave left with the bottle, a look of joy coloring his face.
"Two pieces of Fire Pattern Iron Ore and one Red Yellow Spirit, all for a bottle of Blood Replenishing Pills, these guys are really getting greedier," Hagon, who was alongside Yuan Ming, muttered to himself, unable to hold back.
He spoke so softly that virtually no one aside from himself could hear.
But Yuan Ming heard it clearly.
However, he didn't inquire further on the spot; instead, he waited until he and Hagon had walked away before speaking up:
"So, did that Fur Beast Slave get a bad deal just now?"
"It's common to get a bad deal, but this time that guy pushed the price down too ruthlessly. Just those two blocks of Fire Pattern Iron Ore would be enough to trade for a bottle of Blood Replenishing Pills, not to mention that Red Yellow Spirit, that thickness would mean it's at least fifty years old, it's practically like giving it away," Hagon responded first in surprise and then indignantly.Brоught tо yоu by МV6LЕМРY6R.
Yuan Ming was not yet clear about the ins and outs of all this, so he asked Hagon for more details, learning about the names and features of some Spiritual Medicine and ores that those Registered Disciples often collected.
"I am quite surprised that Biluo Cave would allow this trading place to exist," Yuan Ming remarked with amazement.
"The longer you stay, the more you'll realize that Biluo Cave's management of these Registered Disciples is very lax. They usually just have to complete the Sect's missions, and the Sect doesn't care about anything else," said Hagon, tugging at the corner of his mouth.
Yuan Ming felt that these matters were still too far removed from what he was currently doing, so he didn't take too much interest.
After strolling around the valley, Yuan Ming bid farewell to Hagon and left on his own.
Hagon simply said goodbye, and the two parted ways, neither mentioning the possibility of meeting again in the future.
...
Time flew by, and more than three months passed.
It was Noon, yet the sky was overcast, with dense clouds hanging low, pressing down on the ancient trees of the forest, creating a somewhat oppressive atmosphere.
In the thick mountain forest, a robust White Ape was stretching its long arms between the towering ancient trees, swinging and propelling itself forward with each swing covering a distance of thirty feet, moving with remarkable swiftness.
This was, of course, not an ordinary forest ape but Yuan Ming transformed by the Fur Cloak Technique.
At the moment, his body was soaked with sweat, with several ghastly wounds on his skin, yet his eyes remained bright, vigilantly scanning his surroundings while occasionally glancing back.
Not more than ninety feet behind him, the ground shook violently, trees snapped and plumes of dust rose into the air.
A black-furred wild boar with a body length of ten feet and a height of six feet was roaring, exhaling hot breath as it furiously pursued Yuan Ming.
By its mouth, there was a pair of white tusks as sharp as halberds, gleaming with a chilling white light, so sharp that it could pierce through any tree in its path.
At the same time, an invisible light shield, triangular in shape, would flash between the two tusks, enveloping the boar's head and effortlessly splitting any tree pierced by the tusks into fragments.
The wild boar, one of its eyes wounded by Yuan Ming, was a bloody mess, while the other eye burned with a deep crimson hue of hatred and murderous intent, hellbent on killing Yuan Ming.
Although its speed was not slow, and its strength tremendous, the countless ancient trees blocking its path meant it continually faced obstructions, making it nearly impossible to catch up to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming seemed to be banking on this fact, not hastening to escape but deliberately suppressing his speed to maintain a distance that allowed the boar to keep him in sight.
Should he notice the boar slackening, he would even stop to provoke it, luring the Fierce Beast to keep chasing after him.
Yuan Ming was not idly toying with the creature for no reason, but instead aimed to use this method to wear down the boar's ferocity and stamina until it was weakened enough for him to deliver a fatal blow.
Thus, the ape and the boar continued their chase throughout the forest for more than an hour.
Yuan Ming listened closely with his ears, noticing that the boar's breath from its snout was growing heavier and the thunderous sound of its galloping steps was becoming more chaotic, a sign that its speed smashing into the ancient trees was waning—he knew the moment had come.
He hung onto an ancient tree with one arm, gasping for breath as if he could run no more.
Upon seeing this, the already exhausted wild boar became spirited again, bellowed with a loud roar, and charged at Yuan Ming with all its might.
This time, Yuan Ming deliberately slowed down and only when the boar closed in to a distance of about twelve feet did he swing his arms again, abruptly changing direction, leaping towards another pair of ancient trees.
As the boar followed, its body shifted dramatically to make a sharp turn, barreling toward Yuan Ming's direction.
It saw the two adjoining trees and leapt to pass between them.
The gap between the two trees seemed just right for the boar, neither too much nor too little, barely wide enough for its body to pass through.
However, in reality, these two trees were precisely the ones Yuan Ming had earlier selected for it.
As the boar leapt, Yuan Ming twisted his body and came to a halt.
He picked up a White Bone Short Spear that had been placed there in advance, his body's Nine Elements Technique surging wildly, Dan Tian Power turning into a warm current coursing up from within, traveling along his meridians to his right arm.
His right arm's veins bulged, hair bristled, and muscles swelled, visibly expanding to twice its size, becoming larger than before.
This was the second Divine Skill derived from practicing the Fur Cloak Technique with the White Ape Skin after entering the Qi Refining Second Level, which he named "Energy Storage Arm."
Once this skill was activated, his right arm would transform, and the power it could unleash would instantly increase threefold.
However, this burst of strength was transient and could not be sustained for long.
Taking advantage of this feature, Yuan Ming developed a technique for stored power throwing and long-range attacks.
His palm gripped the short spear tightly, his arm tensed instantly as he continued to gather and store strength, which, along with his arm's swing and a simultaneous bellow from his mouth,
"Go."
As the sound rang out, the White Bone Short Spear he held was also thrown, emitting a sound of tearing through the air.
The Fierce Beast boar had just reached the center between the two old trees when it was squeezed by them on both sides, unable to dodge and only able to rely on the protective Light Shield on its head to face Yuan Ming's charged strike head-on.
It was like a spear-and-shield duel, ending the battle in the very instant they made contact.
The White Bone Short Spear pierced through the invisible shield with a "thwack," burying itself deep into the boar's head, then continued through its entire body and shot out from its rear end.
The boar's airborne body slumped down lifelessly, landing perfectly wedged between the two old trees.
Yuan Ming's face showed delight, both from successfully killing the Fierce Beast and from satisfaction with the strength of his Energy Storage Arm.
He quickly approached, took out the Blood Storage Bag from his waist, and began skillfully collecting the Blood Food from the boar.
After collecting everything, Yuan Ming went to retrieve the White Bone Short Spear and then used the spear's tip to split open the boar's mouth on both sides, exposing the roots of both long tusks.
These tusks were also his target, for they contained a trace of Spiritual Power, one of the spiritual materials sought by the Biluo Cave Disciples.

chapters.title: Chapter 45 - 25 Coercion and Co-optation
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming pulled out two long tusks from a wild boar beast and secured them with prepared bark rope, planning to exchange them for goods in Toad Valley.
Before that, however, the plump wild boar naturally should not go to waste—perfect for a sacrificial offering to the viscera temple.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to skin the wild boar, footsteps suddenly echoed from the surroundings, and he immediately gripped the White Bone Short Spear, warily looking around.
The next moment, four figures sprang out from the surrounding forests, encircling Yuan Ming.
"Friends from the Green Wolf Gang, what is the intention of rushing out like this?" Yuan Ming said as he slightly frowned upon seeing these people.
"What's the matter, lad, not planning on running this time?" The leader among them, a burly man clothed in green wolf skin with dark, reddish skin indicative of his wild origins, sneered.
Yuan Ming had already dealt with these people a few times. More accurately, these people had repeatedly tried to ambush him several times before, though Yuan Ming, always on high alert, had managed to escape before they could close in on him.
This time, having finally cornered Yuan Ming, why would they easily let him go?
Yuan Ming already had an unfavorable opinion of these people and always avoided them when possible. But today, it seemed he could not avoid confrontation.
"Less nonsense, hand over those two wild boar teeth and the blood food in your Blood Storage Bag, or else next year's today will be your death anniversary," the burly leader declared.
They clearly had the upper hand in numbers and strength and did not believe Yuan Ming posed any resistance.
Yuan Ming sighed inwardly, realizing he likely would not get to enjoy the wild boar meat, and felt quite regretful.
However, he exhibited no fear; among these people, the burly leader at most reached the Qi Refining First Level, and the other three following him were not even at the first level. Even combined, they were no match for him.
He casually slung the bound wild boar teeth across his back and gently fondled the White Bone Short Spear with his fingers.
This gesture, to the members of the Green Wolf Gang, clearly signaled his unwillingness to hand over the beast teeth. They hurriedly donned their furred beast skins, ready to display the Fur Cloak Technique and transform.
Just then, Yuan Ming, who had just secured the tusks, erupted without warning. With a renewed force in his hand, the White Bone Short Spear hurled towards the leader in front of him.
Catching sight of this, the man was startled; he did not expect Yuan Ming to dare attack him. It was too late to use the Fur Cloak Technique, and the spear "whooshed" right in front of his chest.
With a "bang," a muffled sound echoed!
The man was struck hard, his body violently flung backward, smashing against a sturdy ancient tree—blood spewing from his mouth as he heavily fell to the ground.
Seeing this, the others hurriedly performed the Fur Cloak Technique.
But by the time they were ready, Yuan Ming had already leaped forward, right in front of the burly man.
He picked up the White Bone Short Spear and rested it against the man's neck, saying,
"If I wanted to kill you, just now it would have been the spear tip aimed at you, not the handle. I'm sparing your life this time so you can go back and tell your leader, I just want to hunt peacefully, don't provoke me!"
As he uttered the last line, Yuan Ming's voice sharply rose, brimming with warning.
The man, frightened, nodded repeatedly, trying to speak, but his throat was full of blood, unable to articulate anything clear.
"Looks like I went a bit too far," Yuan Ming thought to himself, picking up the White Bone Short Spear and walked away.
As Yuan Ming disappeared into the distance, the burly man spit out the blood in his mouth with force and then hoarsely said, "You dare sneak attack me while I'm unprepared… I'll surely kill you one day."
The three men accompanying him, seeing this, also dared not speak up.
"You three are useless! Double the blood food dues for the gang this month. You've got three days, no matter the method, bring it to me," he declared harshly, and then looking at the three men, his anger unabated.
"Please, Boss Zaha, show mercy!"
"Just the monthly dues we have to submit to the sect and the gang are already suffocating us!"
"Yes, the day to pay our dues to the sect is just days away. We won't manage to collect enough in three days! If we can't make the payment, it's a death sentence from the sect."
Hearing this, the three men's faces turned pale, and they immediately knelt down, pleading desperately like pounding garlic with their heads.
With their strength, hunting enough to pay the sect dues of five portions of blood food every month was already a stretch, and they occasionally suffered from raids by others, which forced them to join the Green Wolf Gang; it served both as protection and a means to overpower the fewer and rob them in turn.
Of course, the Green Wolf Gang didn't shelter the useless and also demanded its members to submit a certain amount of blood food on time every month, inadvertently increasing the pressure on its members.
"Just three days! You know the consequences if you don't deliver,"
He showed no mercy towards their pleas, needing to vent his anger somewhere.
Seeing they were knocking their heads bloody, the burly man remained unmoved. Realizing it was futile, the kneeling men stood up.
Their expressions gradually shifted from panic to calm and then turned cold. They exchanged glances and then collectively advanced towards the burly man.
The stocky man had been cursing nonstop, but when those three people grabbed his shoulders, he finally realized something was amiss. His voice trembled slightly as he asked, "What... what do you want to do? Do you have a death wish!"
"It's all your fault, don't blame us..."
Soon, a piercing scream rang out, quickly muffled into a low moan.
...
In the jungle, a communal campsite sprawled out.
The houses, made of bluish-brown wooden planks, were nailed together using the massive branches of huge trees as their foundation. They were perched on the trees, varying in height and numerous in quantity.
On the ground below, there were only a few simple stoves surrounded by stones with a thick layer of grass ash concealing the burning fire seeds, from which faint heat waves emanated.
In one of the fire pits, a bonfire was set up with a large stone pot simmering on top, bubbling with thick white broth and exuding a rich meaty aroma.
Around the bonfire, about a dozen strong, dark-skinned men gathered.
Nearly all of them were half-naked, with half-cut beast skins wrapped around their waists, primarily made from the likes of green wolves and black leopards. Their beast skin headgear dangled behind them, clearly identifying them as Fur Beast Slaves.
At that moment, three figures hurried back to camp, directly going to the bonfire and kneeling before a seated man in the center.
The three kept their heads pressed to the ground, not daring to look up.
"Wu Bao... Gang Leader, Zaha... Zaha is dead," one of them reported, his voice tight with tension.
The seated man had scattered black hair, eyes sharp as blades, a high bridged nose with a tip slightly curved downward like an eagle's beak, and his face bore three long scars almost entirely crossing his cheeks, giving him a sinister and ferocious look.
"Who dares kill a member of the Green Wolf Gang? Which power does it belong to?" Wu Bao paused his eating to ask.
"It's not any particular force; that guy seems to be from the Central Plains and has always been a loner. Zaha had his eye on him for a long time. Previous attempts to ambush him failed as he managed to escape. This time when we finally cornered him, he turned the tables and killed Zaha," said the man, steadier now as he relayed his rehearsed account.
Upon hearing this, Wu Bao frowned, stood up from the ground, and threw the bone in his hand back into the stone pot, asking,
"Four of you against one, and Zaha got killed in return? How strong is this man?"
"Not... not sure; the opponent used just one move, and Zaha was dead..."
"A loner daring to kill our people freely shows the Green Wolf Gang has been too soft recently, making others think we are easy to bully," Wu Bao swept his gaze over those around him and slowly added.
The ones who had just hurried back bowed their heads lower, too frightened to respond.
"Gang Leader, tolerating those who dare kill our people is inexcusable. I am willing to lead men in pursuit and will ensure he doesn't escape again. If I can't bring back his head, I shall present mine instead," at that moment, a bald man walked out from beside Wu Bao, thumped his chest, and declared solemnly.
"Gang Leader, I have a different view, if it's appropriate to speak it?" At that moment, someone stepped forward from the crowd and spoke up.Notefromtheeditor:Alwayscheck*forcorrections.
The bald man turned to look at him, his eyes instantly showing a hint of disdain.
"Wulu, you've only joined the Green Wolf Gang a few days. Since when do you have the right to speak here?" the bald man chided.
Upon hearing this, Wulu just continued to stare fixedly at Wu Bao, not retorting.
"Bayin, don't rush. Let's hear what he has to say," Wu Bao intervened.
The bald man named Bayin, though dissatisfied, suppressed his feelings and looked at Wulu.
"Gang Leader, if I'm not mistaken, that Central Plains man should be Yuan Ming," Wulu stated.
"You know him?" Wu Bao asked, frowning.
"This man became a Fur Beast Slave with me, and he is quite skilled. Being able to kill Zaha from the Qi Refining First Level, I think his strength must be nearly at the Second Level by now. Rather than wasting time and effort hunting him down, it would be better to recruit him to become one of us," Wulu nodded as he spoke.
Hearing Wulu's words, the expressions of the people around subtly changed.
A guy who had only recently become a Fur Beast Slave and was already nearing the Qi Refining Second Level? The majority among them had been cultivating for years and still hadn't even reached the Qi Refining First Level.
Within the entire Green Wolf Gang, only Gang Leader Wu Bao and Vice Gang Leader Bayin, both at the Qi Refining Third Level, could surely surpass him.
In comparison, Yuan Ming was an outstanding individual.
"No, he killed our man; we can't let him go. Otherwise, if word gets out, how will the Green Wolf Gang continue to stand in the Ten Thousand Mountain Range!" Bayin immediately objected.
"Vice Gang Leader Bayin, surely you can understand, ten Zahas cannot compare to one Yuan Ming. If we can bring him over, the benefits will be much greater than killing him," Wulu looked at the bald man and spoke.
After a moment of contemplation, Wu Bao stated, "I will give him one chance. The rest is up to you, Wulu."
"I will handle it immediately," Wulu immediately bowed and responded.

chapters.title: Chapter 46 - 26 The Way of Spells
chapters.content:
Meanwhile, after escaping, Yuan Ming first returned to his hiding place, then hurried off to Toad Valley.
He stopped at the entrance of the first stone house in the valley, where the same Registered Disciple was lying on a chair reading a book.
"Zhao Tong, it's time to do business," Yuan Ming called out.
The man on the chair, hearing the voice, slowly moved the scroll away, revealing a pale, clean, round face with a hint of baby fat, somewhat thick eyebrows, and round, bright eyes. He was not exactly handsome, but he had a decent appearance.
Seeing that it was Yuan Ming who had come, a slight smile appeared on his face.
Yuan Ming had dealt with him a few times before. Although they weren't very close, they were at least acquainted.
There were many Registered Disciples in Toad Valley who did business, but all of them carried an arrogant air, looking down their noses at others. Among them, Zhao Tong was somewhat more reasonable, but when it came to bargaining with the Fur Beast Slaves, he was never soft on driving down the price.
Perhaps because they were both originally from the Central Plains, he treated Yuan Ming rather fairly, thus Yuan Ming usually preferred to trade with him when he had something to sell.
"Heh, these Wild Boar Teeth are quite nice. The spiritual power within is restrained, and they've already reached the threshold for refining a Low-level Magical Artifact. What do you want to exchange for this time?" asked Zhao Tong.
"Wood Stabbing Technique," Yuan Ming replied without hesitation.
"You are really persistent... But rules are rules. The price I quoted before can't change. Have you saved up enough?" Zhao Tong inquired.
"I have everything right here," Yuan Ming said with a nod.
As he spoke, he began to remove the pair of Wild Boar Teeth from his body, took down two pouches from his waist, and then pulled out two dark red stones and a withered purple herb from his bosom.
Hearing this, Zhao Tong stood up and started to examine each of the items Yuan Ming had placed on the table.
After a careful inspection, he nodded in satisfaction and said, "Good, everything's accounted for. To tell you the truth, I thought it would take you at least six months to gather all these items. I didn't expect it to take you less than three."
"I was in a hurry for the Wood Stabbing Technique, couldn't wait six months," Yuan Ming said.
His experiences over the past period had made him acutely aware of his own lack of strength.
He might fare somewhat better against Fierce Beasts, but when conflicts with other Fur Beast Slaves arose, Yuan Ming always felt he had too few tricks up his sleeve, which was too dangerous.
Especially now that he had directly offended people from the Green Wolf Gang, his situation was only going to become more perilous.
He had inadvertently learned from Zhao Tong that Qi Refining Stage Cultivators could also learn some spells, and the Wood Stabbing Technique was a primary Lower Stage offensive spell that Qi Refining Stage Cultivators could relatively easily learn; its power depending on mana.
Of course, these spells were only accessible by truly joining the Biluo Cave and becoming a Registered Disciple, but for the sake of profit, naturally, some disciples would secretly copy them and exchange them with Fur Beast Slaves, although the asking price was usually not low.
T$h^i^s* c$hap$t-er@ is p*a!rt of the c&o#ll-ec+tion on *.&
"Alright, here is the copied manual for the Wood Stabbing Technique. You have two hours to memorize it," Zhao Tong said as he took out a thin white booklet from his bosom and casually tossed it to Yuan Ming.
"I can't take it with me?" Yuan Ming asked, frowning.
"What are you thinking? If the manual for the cultivation technique gets taken by you and after you learn it, you then sell it to someone else, how will I continue doing business?" Zhao Tong replied with a sneer.
"Fair point," Yuan Ming nodded.
After that, he opened the booklet and started to scrutinize it carefully.
While he read, Zhao Tong's voice reached his ears, "If you have any questions during this time, you can ask me at any time."
As the rustling of pages echoed, Yuan Ming showed no reaction to his words, as if he hadn't heard them at all, which slightly irked Zhao Tong.
But before Zhao Tong managed to settle back into his chair, Yuan Ming had already closed the book, stood there with his eyes closed, and began to chant the words silently to himself.
A moment later, he opened his eyes again and looked at Zhao Tong, asking, "The cultivation technique states that when executing this spell, mana must be channeled into the ground to connect with the Earth's Primordial Qi. Is it necessary to touch the ground with one's hands?"
At this, Zhao Tong was momentarily taken aback, then replied:
"Oh... that's correct. There are three stages in executing the Wood Stabbing Technique. Initially, when the mastery of the magic is not sufficient, to shorten the release time, it's best to touch the ground with your hands for the highest efficiency. Once the magic reaches a moderate level of proficiency, there's no need for hands, and you can communicate with the ground just by standing on it."
"Then when it reaches a high level of proficiency, even if someone is in mid-air, they can still execute the Wood Stabbing Technique by sealing and releasing mana?" Yuan Ming pondered briefly before asking further.
"Exactly. But that requires not only sufficient mana but also a mastery of the magic," Zhao Tong nodded.
"I understand, thank you," Yuan Ming said with a fist-and-palm salute.
"If you have more questions, feel free to ask," Zhao Tong said with a self-satisfied smile.
"No more questions," Yuan Ming said indifferently, then returned the "Wood Stabbing Technique" back to him.
Zhao Tong was a bit bewildered by Yuan Ming's action and asked in confusion, "Not going to read more?"
"I've memorized it all. There's nothing I don't understand for now. If there are any doubts, I'll have to find them through practice," Yuan Ming nodded and said.
"Although the 'Wood Stabbing Technique' is only three thousand words, you've memorized it all in less than the time for one cup of tea?" Zhao Tong asked incredulously.
"I've memorized it," Yuan Ming affirmed.
The "Wood Stabbing Technique" is, after all, just a Lower Stage Wood Attribute secret technique, much simpler than the "Nine Elements Technique".
"Could it be that you have a photographic memory?" Zhao Tong inquired doubtfully.
"I suppose my memory has always been quite good," Yuan Ming said with a bow, then took his leave.
Zhao Tong watched his retreating back with increased interest. Photographic memory wasn't something extraordinary for cultivators, but those who didn't have it, just didn't have it. It might as well be considered a divine skill given by the heavens.
"Brother Yuan."
Yuan Ming had just walked out of the valley entrance when someone called out to him.
Not far from him, a man jumped down from a large rock and approached.
"Wulu, what do you need me for?" Yuan Ming recognized the person and couldn't help but be a little surprised.
Their interactions were usually infrequent, and Yuan Ming couldn't think of any reason why he would come looking for him at this time.
"Did you kill someone from the Green Wolf Gang?" Wulu got straight to the point.
"There was a conflict, and I injured one. What... Did that guy die?" Yuan Ming frowned upon hearing this, puzzled.
"He's dead. They mentioned someone from the Central Plains, so I guessed it was you," Wulu said, grinning without any concern for the man's death.
"They?" Yuan Ming asked in confusion.
"I've joined the Green Wolf Gang," Wulu admitted openly.
"So, you're here to capture me?" Yuan Ming's gaze sharpened as he asked.
"I'm here to persuade you." Wulu shook his head.
"To persuade me?"
"I told them I'd come to persuade you to surrender and join the Green Wolf Gang. But I know your character; you definitely won't agree. So I'm here to give you an early warning, to be more vigilant," Wulu said with a smile.
Yuan Ming felt slightly taken aback upon hearing this.
"Surprised, are you? This is also a way to repay you for your past kindness," Wulu asked, then answered his own question.
"Then I owe you one." Yuan Ming also showed a hint of a smile and said.
"After I go back this time, they will probably issue an order to hunt you down and offer a reward for your capture. Based on their usual methods, as long as someone reports your whereabouts, that person will not be harassed by the Green Wolf Gang and might even receive their protection. So, your situation won't be good," Wulu continued.
"I figured as much," Yuan Ming nodded, unsurprised.
"If I'm not mistaken, the person sent after you will be Ba Yin, a bald man with a fierce face who has recently broken through to the Qi Refining third level. He can be considered as one of the top experts among the Fur Beast Slaves in the Ten Thousand Mountains. Don't take him lightly if you come across him," Wulu added.
"Understood, thanks," Yuan Ming nodded and expressed his gratitude.
Seeing this, Wulu's smile gradually faded to a serious expression, "Brother Yuan, that's all the help I can provide for now. If we meet again, we might be enemies, though I hope we won't be."
Yuan Ming paused for a moment before nodding again.
After that, Wulu left first, and Yuan Ming also exited Toad Valley, returning to his hiding place.
Once back in the cave, Yuan Ming immediately started practicing the Wood Stabbing Technique.
...
Half a month later, in a sparse woodland area.
Yuan Ming crouched down, one hand supporting himself on the ground, the other hand forming seals. A strand of mana flowed into the ground from his palm.
A flicker of light passed through his eyes as he shouted in a low voice, "Rise!"
At the sound of his voice, a green light flashed five zhang away from him, and a sharp green wooden thorn, similar to a spear, stabbed up from the ground.
The wooden thorn, as thick as a child's arm and no more than a foot long, had a tip that shone with a metallic sheen, evidently very sturdy and sharp.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming wiped the sweat from his forehead with the back of his hand, a smile flickering in his eyes.
After this period of practice, the distance at which he could execute his Wood Stabbing Technique had extended several times from the initial mere zhang, and both the sharpness and the sturdiness had improved significantly, to his great satisfaction.
"This Wood Stabbing Technique isn't too difficult to cultivate, but it consumes quite a bit of mana. Continuous use could drain my mana too quickly. I need to improve my cultivation," Yuan Ming mumbled to himself.
Just then, his ears twitched, and he suddenly turned his head towards one direction, shouting, "Who's there?"
No sooner had the words left his mouth than rustling sounds erupted around him, and five figures emerged, surrounding him in the center.
"Good job, you're quite hard to find," one of them stepped forward and said.
With a bald head and a broad face radiating a fierce aura, Yuan Ming immediately realized this person was Ba Yin, the one Wulu had mentioned.
His brow furrowed as he immediately wore the Ape Skin and performed the Fur Cloak Technique, transforming into the likeness of a White Ape.
"I'd advise you not to resort to violence. I don't want to kill," Yuan Ming spoke out.
Unintimidated, Ba Yin laughed in response, "Just because you killed that trash Zaha, do you really think you're something special? If I don't twist your head off today and bring it back, I don't deserve to be the Vice Gang Leader of the Green Wolf Gang."
With that, he too put on a Beast Skin and executed the Fur Cloak Technique.
His body slightly swelled as thick, long fur grew all over him, his forehead became broader, his eyes smaller and rounder, his nose flatted and blunt, and his hands and feet sprouted sharp and hard claws.
But the most conspicuous feature was the two-foot-wide strip of white fur that ran from the top of his head to his back, making it seem as if he had donned a silver-white cloak.

chapters.title: Chapter 47 - 27 Pursuit
chapters.content:
"Is that... a honey badger?" Yuan Ming looked at the animal Ba Yin had transformed into, somewhat dumbfounded.
Unlike others who underwent the Fur Cloak Technique and experienced significant changes in size, Ba Yin's size hadn't changed much, which made the sight somewhat comical.
However, seeing its eyes flashing with a crimson hue, the heavy breathing from its nose, and the fierce aura emanating from its body, it was clear that this creature was not as easy to provoke as it seemed.
Following closely behind, several other members of the Green Wolf Gang also employed the Fur Cloak Skill, transforming into three Green Wolves and a Black Leopard.
Yuan Ming's gaze quickly swept around before pulling out two White Bone Short Spears from the ground behind him, holding one in each hand.
His gaze moved from one Green Wolf Gang member to another as if he were looking for a target to strike. Three of them were the ones who had followed Zaha before and, having witnessed Yuan Ming's methods, understood what he was about to do and withdrew.
"Afraid of what, I'm here!" Ba Yin roared with a voice as loud as a bell.
However, just as the echo of his words faded, the sound of something whistling through the air suddenly attacked.
Yuan Ming hurled his Bone Spear with all his might, using the Energy Storage Arm technique, shooting it like an arrow straight toward Ba Yin's heart.
Just as it was about to pierce his chest, a palm suddenly struck down from above, heavily smashing down on the White Bone Short Spear.
With a bang, Yuan Ming only saw a shadowy light explode beneath the badger's paw, and his White Bone Short Spear shattered into pieces, as if struck by a heavy hammer, and fell to the ground.
But right behind, another whooshing sound broke out.
The second White Bone Short Spear had already burst through the air, heading straight for Ba Yin's face.
With a loud roar from Ba Yin's mouth, he didn't even flinch; he directly met the White Bone Short Spear with his head.
There was a snap.
The White Bone Short Spear ricocheted off Ba Yin's forehead and was caught firmly in his hand.
At the same time, a figure suddenly darted past him and leaped towards the distance.
"Still want to run?"
Ba Yin sneered, his body swiftly turning as he reversed the White Bone Short Spear tip and fiercely hurled it towards the fleeing Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming, already in mid-air, reached out for a vine hanging low, when the whooshing sound of wind from behind alerted him; he quickly recoiled his neck and dropped downward.
The White Bone Short Spear grazed past his scalp, breaking the vine he was about to grasp and with a bang, bored a large hole into an old tree farther away, and then pierced through another behind it.
"Such formidable strength," Yuan Ming muttered to himself.
As he fell to the ground, the silhouettes of two Green Wolves, having transformed from the Fur Beast Slaves, attacked from both sides with their massive jaws aiming for each of his arms.
Helpless, Yuan Ming could only roll on the spot and dodge forward.
As he got back to his feet, he saw a Black Leopard in front of him, its teeth and claws bared, blocking his escape.
This time, there was no way to avoid it.
As the Black Leopard rushed towards him, Yuan Ming propped himself up with one hand on the ground, erecting the other in front of him with finger mnemonic ready, and uttered in a low voice, "Rise."
In an instant, the ground just three feet in front of him burst with a yellow light, as a sharp yellow stone spike suddenly rose and pierced through the Black Leopard's chest.
Blood splattered, and the Fur Beast Slave transformed into a Black Leopard howled in agony.
Yuan Ming brushed past it, accelerating his pace to escape into the depths of the forest.
"Everyone, be cautious, that boy knows spells!" Ba Yin thundered as he pursued.
Seizing this opportunity, Yuan Ming leaped into the trees and made his way into the distance.
The three Green Wolves immediately followed closely. Although they were swifter and kept closing in on Yuan Ming, they consciously maintained a certain distance.
Only the honey badger Ba Yin had transformed into, lacking in speed, slowly fell behind.
As Yuan Ming ran, he observed the surroundings and continuously assessed the direction.
His face was taut, but his eyes were not in panic.
Clearly, he had already planned for his current predicament.
The three Green Wolves kept up their relentless pursuit of Yuan Ming. The chase went on for half an hour.
However, the distance between them and Yuan Ming had increased considerably. It wasn't that they couldn't keep up, but knowing that Ba Yin had been left far behind, they didn't dare follow too closely, fearing an unexpected counterattack from Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming too had thought of turning back to attack, but he wasn't sure of Ba Yin's strength and when he might catch up; if he got entangled by the three Green Wolf Beast Slaves and then Ba Yin arrived, the situation would not be good.
He did not stop along the way, heading straight to the deep valley cradled between two towering ridges, and glanced into the valley.
It was now Noon, yet the mist inside the valley had not completely dissipated, the smoke within was hazy, as if an illusion.
Yuan Ming did not hesitate, and plunged headfirst into the mist of the valley.
Just as he entered the valley's mouth, a breeze carrying a burning scent hit his face, causing him to furrow his brows involuntarily.Content presented by *.
By the time he entered the valley, past that windy spot, the pungent odor was not as strong.
The woods within the valley were sparser than outside, and one could spot some Fierce Beasts, but they seemed very cautious and timid by nature. When they heard the noise made by Yuan Ming, they took off running.
Yuan Ming continued inward for about half an hour when the air in the valley suddenly became murky, filled with a piercing sulfur smell.
When he rounded a bend in the gorge, the scene before him opened up brilliantly, and not far ahead, a sulfur lake spanning about ten acres in size and irregular in shape came into view.
The waters of the lake were clear yet a golden hue, and along the stone banks at its edge, a layer of White Frost formed. From a distance, it looked like a gigantic yellow gemstone set in the middle of the valley.
On the seemingly tranquil surface of the lake, one could see one skeleton after another, some still maintaining a relatively complete shape, while others were fragmented, standing on the surface of the lake like plants that had grown out of the water.
Spread across the cliff face close to the lake were a dozen caves of varying sizes, some as high as over thirty feet, while others were as small as dog holes.
Yuan Ming glanced at the entrances to those caves and then quickly bypassed the lake, running towards them.
Outside the valley, Ba Yin ran up frantically, only to see his subordinates pacing outside the valley, not daring to go in.
"Where's the kid? What are you dallying around here for?" Ba Yin immediately berated them.
"Gang Leader Ba Yin, he ran into the valley. The mist is dense inside, and we dare not rush in recklessly for fear of his ambush," one of the Green Wolves spoke up.
"Useless wretches, get in there and chase him now! If he escapes again, I will cast you out of the Green Wolf Gang to fend for yourselves," Ba Yin scolded furiously.
Upon hearing this, the men panicked.
They usually relied on the name of the Green Wolf Gang to do a lot of misdeeds but seldom faced retribution. However, without this identity as protection, they would only die faster than others.
The three Green Wolf Beast Slaves said nothing and rushed into the valley, with Ba Yin closely following them.
On the other side, Yuan Ming, who was running along the shore of the lake, suddenly saw a shadow swiftly passing over the water, speeding towards him. As it drew closer, the shadow grew larger and larger.
He immediately stopped in his tracks, his eyes focusing on the surface of the water. But only when the shadow rushed towards the bank did he suddenly realize the danger and looked up at the sky.
There, a giant black raptor with massive wings spread suddenly retracted its wings and dove at him with great force.
Yuan Ming immediately stepped back, his fists clenched, waiting for the raptor to approach.
As the raptor neared, suddenly a "swoosh" sound was heard.
The raptor let out a piercing scream as Blood Light suddenly appeared on its enormous body, and its form, as if sliced by several blades at once, split into seven or eight chunks, plummeting to the ground.
Bright red blood sprayed in midair, narrowly missing splashing all over Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming was shocked. He hastily retreated several feet, not knowing what had happened.
But when he looked up at the sky again, he discovered that several crisscrossing blood-red lines had appeared in the Void about ten meters high, floating in midair.
Upon closer inspection, Yuan Ming realized that these blood-red lines extended out to form a massive spider web that almost covered the entire sulfur lake.
If it weren't for the blood of the raptor on it, it would have been difficult for anyone to notice it.
"How careless, I didn't notice it just now," he thought with a chill, feeling extremely frightened.
At this moment, noises from behind approached again; the men from the Green Wolf Gang had caught up.
Yuan Ming looked back, a look of relief crossing his face, as if he was worried they wouldn't dare to follow him.
He hurriedly picked up his pace, running towards the direction of the cliff.
Ba Yin, seeing Yuan Ming running towards the cliffs, thought he was trying to climb the cliff to escape, and immediately shouted, "Don't let him near the cliff, stop him for me!"
As he spoke, he chanted under his breath, and wisps of pink mist began to rise from all over his body, his muscles bulging, and his running speed increased instantly as he charged toward Yuan Ming.
The two Green Wolves took the lead, catching up swiftly, flanking him from left and right, as they both pounced towards Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming sidestepped left and right, swinging both arms in turn, striking the spines of the two Green Wolf Beast Slaves and flipping them over.
But then the third Green Wolf Beast Slave also circled around and blocked his path.
Seeing this situation, Yuan Ming seemed very annoyed and let out an angry roar.
Without his White Bone Short Spear in hand, he could only rely on his bare fists to fight the three Green Wolf Beast Slaves. His heavy punches sent them yowling in pain, but the close combat didn't give him much advantage. His arms and shoulders were bitten in many places, blood streaming down.

chapters.title: Chapter 48 - 28: Drive Spiders and Swallow Wolves
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming and the three Green Wolf Beast Slaves were in a deadlock when Ba Yin finally caught up and joined the battle without a word.
He charged out suddenly with a barbaric collision, heading straight for Yuan Ming.
In haste, Yuan Ming could only cross his arms in front of him, but he was still knocked backward by the formidable ghostly strength, slamming heavily against the mountainside.
Yuan Ming felt a sweetness in his throat, and a mouthful of fresh blood already spilled from the corner of his mouth.
"Indeed very strong."
In his heart, he made a judgment about Ba Yin. With his current strength, a direct confrontation was absolutely out of question, especially with three others assisting from the side.
Just then, Yuan Ming suddenly heard a rustling sound above his head, followed by a cascade of small stones rolling down from the mountainside behind him.
"Finally here."
After murmuring, Yuan Ming unexpectedly undid the Fur Cloak Technique, reverting to his human form.
This action was akin to disarming on the battlefield, leaving Ba Yin and the others somewhat surprised, unclear about what he intended to do.
Yuan Ming had no intention of explaining. He immediately took a paper package from his bosom, viciously tore it open, and scattered its contents over himself.
The red and white powder instantly coated his entire body, spreading a pungent odor.
Ba Yin wrinkled his nose, then heard one of the Green Wolf Beast Slaves say, "Boss Ba Yin, this seems to be… Beast Repelling Powder."
Though he didn't know what was going on, he vaguely sensed something was amiss.
"Don't mind it, hurry up and go, kill him for me," Ba Yin bellowed.
The three Green Wolf Beast Slaves lunged at once. Yuan Ming, who had reverted to his human form, did not use the Fur Cloak Technique again but instead turned and scrambled up the mountainside.
One of the Green Wolf Beast Slaves sprinted swiftly, its forepaws grabbed a protruding rock on the mountainside to leap forward, and it opened its huge mouth aiming to bite at Yuan Ming's calf.
Just as its fangs were about to sink into Yuan Ming's calf, a "whoosh" sound of something cutting through the air suddenly rang out.
Immediately afterward, a black sharply-pointed bone spur flew past Yuan Ming's back, instantly piercing through the head of that Green Wolf Beast Slave, splattering blood everywhere.
The body of the Green Wolf Beast Slave, propelled by the powerful inertia of the bone spur, crashed to the ground, dead on the spot.
The other two Green Wolf Beast Slaves, seeing this, were terrified, halting their forward momentum abruptly.
Lifting their heads to look up towards Yuan Ming, they saw a huge hole in the rock face above, from which a giant black head was poking out.
The head was as large as an ox's, covered in black short fur, with eight neatly arranged compound eyes on the top and a pair of curved mandibles below, shimmering with a dark luster, and notably, a sharp black horn on the top of its head.
"What the hell is that?" one of the Green Wolf Beast Slaves exclaimed.
His voice immediately caught the attention of that strange head—eight eyes staring straight at him. The sharp horn on its head flashed darkly, and a black bone spur was suddenly shot out swiftly.
The Green Wolf Beast Slave reacted extremely fast, immediately dodging to the side.
The black bone spur grazed his back, cutting just a scratch, but missing the vital parts.
Seeing that its strike missed, the bizarre head moved quickly, extending forward, coming fully out of the hole. Subsequently, its whole body and eight spear-like black spider legs also crawled out.
It clung to the steep rock face, its eight spider legs firmly nailed into the crevices of the rocks, as stable as Mount Tai, without any sign of falling.
"A Single-horned Wolf Spider, why is there such a thing here?" Ba Yin couldn't help but shout.
As soon as his words fell, looking back at the Green Wolf Beast Slave who was just scratched by the bone spur, he had already collapsed on the ground, black blood leaking from his mouth and nose, already dead.
The remaining Green Wolf Beast Slave, seeing this, was even more petrified on the spot.
"Such potent venom."
No sooner had Ba Yin spoken than another black bone spur was already whistling through the air, heading straight for his face.
He immediately swung a hand to flick the bone spur, using the original force to twist its direction, sending it flying back towards Yuan Ming.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming quickly dodged to the side, then once more climbed upwards.
He was the closest to the Single-horned Wolf Spider, which had already sensed his presence.
However, because his body was covered in Beast Repelling Powder, the Single-horned Wolf Spider did not attack him immediately. Instead, it prioritized attacking Ba Yin, who posed the greatest threat.
The Single-horned Wolf Spider rapidly scurried down, speeding towards Ba Yin, its eight spear-like spider legs supporting its body, reaching Ba Yin in just a few strides.
Its spider leg tips were extremely sharp, constantly thrusting at Ba Yin.
Ba Yin could only wave his badger paws, continuously deflecting with the tips of his claws, setting off a series of metallic clashing sounds.
The delicate-looking legs of the Single-horned Wolf Spider kept colliding with the sharp claws, but instead of being damaged, they forced Ba Yin into a position where he was constantly exposed, leaving streaks of blood on his body.
Shortly, blackness spread over his wounds, a clear sign of poison.
Yuan Ming took the opportunity to start climbing rapidly, and soon reached the cave where the Single-horned Wolf Spider resided.
He flipped himself into the entrance, immediately greeted by an indescribable complex odor.
Yuan Ming glanced around and saw on both sides of the entrance clean-gnawed Bai Gu and scattered pieces of tattered and incomplete flesh.
In the center of these filthy objects, there lay a dark red object, resembling a Lingzhi herb, its texture similar to wood but with a slight animalistic writhing motion.
"That's right, it's the meat Ganoderma mentioned in the 'Herborist'," Yuan Ming's eyes lit up, immediately overjoyed.
Some days ago, when he was out hunting, the prey he had already injured disappeared after running into this secluded valley. Later, when searching, he realized it was taken by the Single-horned Wolf Spider.
When he came to check, he found this meat Ganoderma and knew it was a precious Spiritual Medicine recorded in the 'Herborist' and was tempted to take it away.
However, after trying, Yuan Ming realized he was no match for the Single-horned Wolf Spider, so he devised the plan to drive the spider and swallow the wolf, luring the Green Wolf Gang that was chasing him to snatch the treasure in the chaos.
Seeing the treasure before him, Yuan Ming immediately walked forward, dug up the palm-sized meat Ganoderma completely, wrapped it in Beast Skin prepared in advance, and tucked it into his chest.
With the item in hand, Yuan Ming moved to the entrance, planning to observe the outside situation before making further plans.
However, no sooner had he reached the entrance than a terrifyingly pale human face suddenly dangled down, its round eyes staring straight at him.
Those eyes were pitch black like ink, devoid of any whites, giving off an exceedingly sinister look.
Yuan Ming jumped back, startled, and only then did he clearly see that the pale human face was actually a special pattern located on the head of an entirely black spider.
This spider was much smaller than the Single-horned Wolf Spider, its eight legs as thin as twigs and its body both slim and long, but its head was remarkably round and bore a pale, dismal human face.
As Yuan Ming watched it, it also watched him, but in those black eyes, nothing could be seen.
Then, the strange human face suddenly split into a grin, revealing no teeth and not even a mouth; it was as if there was only a tangible yet intangible skin stuck on the forehead of the spider.
This eerie sight made Yuan Ming's scalp tingle, and he instinctively wanted to flee.
But the cavern on the cliff was shallow, and there was only one exit, trapping Yuan Ming inside.
He had no choice but to use the Fur Cloak Technique, transforming into a White Ape. In a pile of Bai Gu, he blindly grabbed a bone, not knowing from which beast, and readied himself to throw it with the Energy Storage Arm.
Before he could use it, the ancient bone snapped with a "crack".
Yuan Ming hastily picked up another bone, but it also crumbled with a squeeze.
He cursed under his breath and reached for another one, preparing to throw it when he suddenly realized that something felt off. On closer inspection, he discovered that what he held was not a bone but an Ancient Bronze Sword covered in rust.
Note: Check * for any corrections.
Just then, the human-faced spider launched its attack first, sending a delicate spider leg speeding towards Yuan Ming like a steel spear, faster even than the Single-horned Wolf Spider.
Yuan Ming, having no time for anything else, hastily placed the sword horizontally to block.
A sharp clang resonated!
The long sword collided with the spider leg, sparking a burst of sparks.
Yuan Ming felt a great force strike him, causing him to involuntarily step back. He then looked at the long sword in his hand and found that it was only slightly chipped, but otherwise unscathed.
Then, the attack of the human-faced spider came again, two spider legs thrusting in, continuously and aggressively targeting Yuan Ming from both sides.
As Yuan Ming swung his sword to block, he desperately pushed towards the direction of the cave entrance.
The limited space inside the cave restricted his movements, putting him on the defensive.
While under attack from the spider legs, Yuan Ming pressed closer to the entrance. Then, the small abdomen of the human-faced spider suddenly contracted, and from a small opening in its belly, a burst of white fluid shot out, expanding in mid-air into a white spiderweb heading straight for Yuan Ming's face.
Upon seeing this, Yuan Ming blocked the thrusting spider legs with his sword and, with his hand open, grabbed the spiderweb, swirling his arm to entangle it, immediately rolling it into a knot.
A sharp, intense pain shot through his palm instantly, a powerful corrosive force seeping into it. Even with the protection of the Ape Skin, the flesh in his palm was instantly corroded, leaving deep wounds.
The burning pain caused Yuan Ming's eyes to bulge in anger as an uncanny ferocity, seemingly not his own, was ignited.
