As she jumped off the back of the falcon hawk, her chest, which seemed to hold two pure white jade rabbits, bounced incessantly, causing all the Fur Beast Slaves, who hadn't seen a woman in who knows how long, to stare with wide-eyed fixation.
Seemingly unconcerned about their bold gazes, the woman pushed out her chest and struck a coquettish pose, standing beside the short-bearded man.
Behind her was another young man in a green robe, his figure slender, with a shy smile on his face, yet his eyes were fixed intently on the ground just in front of his toes.
The robe he wore, although a different color from the previous two, was of the same design, with an emblem of a Pill Furnace on his chest, and beneath it, the words "Refining Furnace Hall" were written in Southern Border script.
The last one wore a fiery red short skirt; her style was different from the previous three, with the characters "Fire Refining Hall" written beneath the emblem on her chest.
This woman had delicate features and an extremely beautiful face, especially her almond eyes, which were brimming with spiritual energy. Complemented by her short garments, her exquisite figure was showcased perfectly, making her look both lively and beautiful, as well as efficient and capable.
As soon as she appeared, she immediately drew away most of the attention that was focused on the coquettish woman.
However, unlike the coquettish woman, she was quite displeased with those presumptuous gazes on her. Resting one hand on the Green Vine Whip coiled at her waist, she glared angrily at the crowd.
The Fur Beast Slaves, swept by her sharp gaze, all lowered their heads.
Yuan Ming stared at the words "Fire Refining Hall" on her chest, slightly spellbound, reminded of what he had learned from Zhao Tong that the Fire Refining Hall was the branch of the sect responsible for refining magic artifacts.
That guy had previously mentioned asking around to see if there were any brothers from the Fire Refining Hall who could help etch Array Patterns onto the Green Fish Sword, but it had led to nothing but silence.
"Snap"
Just then, a whistling sound suddenly came through the air.
Yuan Ming instinctively dodged, only to see a whip shadow flash by his side, then snap back into place.
Confused, he seemed unaware of why the woman had suddenly struck at him.
Seeing that his gaze had moved away from her chest, the woman in the red skirt didn't bother with him anymore, coiled up her whip, and hung it at her waist.
"What a temper," Yuan Ming whispered under his breath, cursing inwardly.
Elder Hu Huo, as if he heard nothing, only spoke up when the woman no longer dwelled on the issue:
"Everyone, all my Fur Beast Slaves are here. You can select any you like, and it's fine even if you take them all away."
The Fur Beast Slaves listened in confusion, not having received an explanation from him.
"Elder Hu Huo, we are merely looking for guides. One or two will suffice; there is no need for so many," the woman in the red skirt spoke first.
"Sister Chen Wan, perhaps we should bring a few more? In case we encounter danger, having more people would provide a buffer," the slender young man in the green robe suggested, looking toward the woman in the red skirt.
What is 'a buffer'? Just a scapegoat.
Hearing this, discontent arose in Yuan Ming's heart, and the same reaction appeared on the faces of the other Fur Beast Slaves, though they dared not act out.
"Ba Da, with us here, what is there to worry about? For our mission this time, whether we bring one or two Fur Beast Slaves or ten or more, what difference does it make?" the bearded man laughed, dismissing the concern with contempt.
"Exactly, having too many people is just a burden," the coquettish woman chimed in, her voice sultry. Even as her words were of disdain, they made the Fur Beast Slaves tremble with longing, each one desiring to follow her.
"Kun Tu, Yang Chan, this trial is no child's play; think it over carefully," Elder Hu Huo reminded them.
"Elder need not worry; as this is our trial, how can we rely solely on Fur Beast Slaves to pave the way?" the bearded man, named Kun Tu, waved his hand dismissively.
Afterward, he seemed to point randomly toward the crowd: "You, you, the two of you come with us."
His seemingly casual pointer caused all eyes to converge on the two "lucky ones" chosen.
Wu Bao gave a toothy grin, looking over at Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming, however, couldn't help but frown.
"Brother Yuan, this doesn't seem like a favorable assignment," Hagon voiced his concern.
The two chosen by Kun Tu were none other than Wu Bao and Yuan Ming.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 - 43 Human Demon
chapters.content:
"Yuan Ming, Wu Bao, step forward," Elder Hu Huo commanded without hesitation.
Wu Bao was the first to leave the row, with a proud expression on his face.
Yuan Ming, however, frowned and followed a step behind, displaying a noticeably different attitude.
The rest of the Fur Beast Slaves, seeing this, were full of envy and lamented amongst themselves.
"You have been chosen; set off immediately," Elder Hu Huo instructed.
"Thank you," Chen Wan, the lady in red, said with a fist salute in gratitude.
The other three also bid farewell and then led Yuan Ming and Wu Bao off in the direction of the Ten Thousand Mountains.
"During this time, you must continue to hunt, and if you encounter a Registered Disciple, you are not to resist their call. Those who disobey the order... I trust you will not disobey," Elder Hu Huo added before dismissing everyone.
...
The several Registered Disciples walked ahead briskly, with Yuan Ming and Wu Bao following hurriedly behind, more like attendants than guides.
However, once the group passed through the gorge and officially entered the territory where Fierce Beasts roamed, they stopped.
Chen Wan took out a Beast Skin map from her bosom, spread it on a rock, and summoned Yuan Ming and Wu Bao. She asked, "Which one of you has been to this place?"
Her slender, fair fingers were pointing to a basin deep within the Ten Thousand Mountains.
After looking carefully for a moment, a confused expression appeared in Wu Bao's eyes.
These Fur Beast Slaves simply wandered wherever they were taken, only remembering enough to make their way back, so maps were of little use to them.
It was Yuan Ming who was frowning deeply, scrutinizing the map with a thoughtful look.
"Do you understand it?" Chen Wan inquired.
Wu Bao looked embarrassed and could only shake his head, but seeing Yuan Ming's demeanor, he cursed inwardly, "What are you trying to play at?"
"Chen Wan, I brought them just to fulfill a task. You really expect them to be of any help?" Kun Tu said with a self-satisfied smile, shaking his head.
"We are currently at the entrance of the gorge, which is here. The farthest I've been is the Purple Bamboo Forest, which is at least a two-day walk from the place you're asking about." No sooner had he finished speaking than Yuan Ming's voice rang out.
The genuine article resides on M|V|L&EMPYR.
Upon hearing this, Chen Wan, who had lost hope, lit up and continued, "How long would it take to get to the Purple Bamboo Forest from here?"
"If we avoid most of the Fierce Beasts and try not to delay the journey by fighting, we can get there in five days," Yuan Ming said.
As he spoke, he looked up and averted his gaze, only to see the Refining Furnace Hall Disciple named Ba Da, stealing glances at Chen Wan's shapely legs.
While appearing shy, this fellow was far from honest.
Despite Yuan Ming's contempt, he chose not to meddle by exposing him.
"If we ride Spirit Beasts, it won't take five days," Kun Tu interjected.
After that, he patted the Spiritual Beast Bag at his waist, and a beam of green light flew out, landing nearby, materializing into a giant Green Wolf two zhang in length.
This wolf, with its muscular body and eyes glinting with a faint dark red hue, had a tuft of white fur in the center of its forehead. Its protruding snout bore two long and sharp fangs, exuding both ferocity and might.
"Chen Wan, my Green Wolf is a First-level Upper Stage Fierce Beast, not only fast but also comfortable and steady to ride. Why don't you ride with me?" Kun Tu, with a smiling face, offered the invitation.
Hearing this, Yang Chan from the Beast Taming Hall furrowed her brow immediately, clearly displeased with Kun Tu's overt advances.
"Thank you for your kindness, Elder Brother, but it's not necessary. I have my own Spirit Beast," Chen Wan declined calmly and indifferently.
She then patted her own Spiritual Beast Bag, and a beam of green light shot out, transforming into a Green-skinned Rhinoceros about one zhang and two chi long.
Compared to Kun Tu's Green Wolf, this rhinoceros was smaller in size, but its head and neck were fitted with metallic armor. Its back carried a saddle made of leather that looked quite comfortable.
"It seems I have been presumptuous, assuming your Spirit Beast wasn't well equipped. I apologize for the inconvenience, Elder Sister," Kun Tu said, unaffected by her refusal and promptly excusing himself.
Immediately afterwards, Yang Chan also patted her Spiritual Beast Bag and summoned a seven zhang-long fiery red python. She leapt onto it and relaxed against the python's coiled body.
The python raised its head, accommodating her graceful figure.
Ba Da likewise called forth his Spirit Beast—an enormous boar covered in black fur. Although its stature was unimpressive compared to the previous beasts, the two snow-white tusks protruding sharply like lances made it clear that it was no ordinary creature.
"Elder Brother Kun Tu, we two women cannot take them with us. How about you and Brother Ba Da each take one?" Chen Wan looked at Yuan Ming and Wu Bao as she spoke.
Upon hearing this, Kun Tu frowned, and Ba Da too lifted his head, showing blatant reluctance.
"Elder Sister, they are merely lowly Fur Beast Slaves; they are not worthy of riding our Elder Brother's Spirit Beasts," Yang Chan said in indignation.
"We need them to guide us. Without the Spirit Beasts to carry them, we would be much slower, which would be counterproductive," Chen Wan replied calmly.
"You are right, Elder. Such mounts as Spirit Beasts are beyond us," Wu Bao quickly agreed, his face filled with feigned terror.
Then, Ba Da spoke up, "Elder Sister Chen Wan, they are Fur Beast Slaves, having employed the Fur Cloak Technique, they should be nearly as fast as Spirit Beasts. Don't worry too much."
Hearing this, Chen Wan gave up the idea and turned to Yuan Ming, asking, "Can you keep up?"
Not wanting to delay any further, Yuan Ming simply nodded.
Although he was somewhat envious of the Spirit Beasts owned by the registered disciples, what concerned him more was how to complete the mission to obtain as many Blood Food rewards as possible.
"Alright then, let's not delay any further and set off immediately," Chen Wan said.
Yuan Ming, taking the lead as the guide, executed the Fur Cloak Technique and transformed into a White Ape, bounding forward and heading deep into the mountain forest.
"I'll cover our rear to prevent any accidents," Kun Tu said after glancing at the others.
Without hesitation, Chen Wan immediately spurred her Green-skinned Rhinoceros to catch up, with Ba Da following closely behind and Yang Chan swiftly keeping pace as well.
Only after the group had run out of sight did Kun Tu, riding his Green Wolf, turn his gaze towards Wu Bao.
"This Yuan Ming doesn't seem like a simpleton. Can we recruit him into our ranks?" Kun Tu asked.
Upon hearing this, Wu Bao felt a tremor in his heart and hastened to say, "Master, this fellow is quite obstinate and doesn't take well to being under others. I've tried to recruit him before, but not only did he refuse, he also killed quite a few of our men."
"Enough of that, he's just a mere Beast Slave. If we want one, there are plenty. I will help you eliminate him this time, but afterwards, the tribute you provide each month needs to be increased by ten percent," Kun Tu said, his brows furrowing, then continued.
"Thank you, Master," Wu Bao immediately said.
"I cultivated the Green Wolf Gang and Hyena Hall for you to do my bidding, not to cause me trouble. This should not become a precedent. If it happens again, you and Jin Kun can step down and let others take your place," Kun Tu declared, then rode his Green Wolf and sped away.
Wu Bao nodded repeatedly, his back already soaked with cold sweat. He too quickly employed the Fur Cloak Technique, transforming into a Green-Furred Wolf Man and chased after them at full speed.
...
It was deep into the autumn season, at night.
A raging bonfire burned in the mountain forest while Kun Tu and his three companions sat around it, feasting on freshly roasted meat.
Four Spirit Beasts each lay coiled behind their respective masters, forming a protective circle around them at the center.
Yuan Ming and Wu Bao, the two Fur Beast Slaves, naturally did not qualify to mingle with them and were stationed far out on the perimeter to keep watch.
The night breeze was gentle, and Yuan Ming sat alone atop an old tree, his eyes shut in meditation, cultivating in a cross-legged position.
He was very familiar with this area, previously home to a Green-Scaled Lizard, which he had slain last month. Therefore, it was unlikely for other Fierce Beasts to settle here for the time being.
Given the presence of those four Spirit Beasts guarding, they really didn't need him to keep watch.
Just then, Yuan Ming's ears twitched suddenly, and he immediately opened his eyes, scanning the dark forest before him. He quickly spotted a dark figure dashing through a bush.
He flipped off the tree and pursued in the direction of the shadow.
However, before he had gone many steps, he saw the dark figure ahead suddenly stop and turn its head toward him.
Yuan Ming was taken aback and immediately came to a halt, facing off against it.
In front of him stood a creature nearly eight feet tall, humanoid in shape, covered in hair all over its body—even its face not exempt—resembling an upright, white-haired old ape.
But its eyes were a blood-red hue, reflecting a murderous glint in the darkness that sent a chill down Yuan Ming's spine.
At that moment, Yuan Ming also heard a commotion coming from behind him.
"Damn it, I've been ambushed," Yuan Ming's heart went cold, sensing an unfavorable situation.
"Over there," came a woman's shout at that moment.
Soon after, several figures rushed out from the back, arriving next to Yuan Ming; it was Chen Wan and the others.
Yuan Ming breathed a sigh of relief. When he turned back to look at the creature, however, he found the space in front of him empty, with the monster nowhere in sight.
"Why are you out here?" Chen Wan immediately asked upon seeing Yuan Ming.
"I was keeping watch outside and encountered a long-haired humanoid monster, so I followed it here," Yuan Ming honestly replied.
"Where's the monster?" At this, Kun Tu's fear turned to excitement, and he eagerly asked.
Chen Wan and Yang Chan's eyes also lit up, their gazes focusing on Yuan Ming with a hint of surprise.
"It ran off. It was right there a moment ago, but when you all came chasing, it disappeared," Yuan Ming blinked and said.
"Which way did it go?" Kun Tu immediately asked.
Yuan Ming hadn't noticed which direction the monster ultimately fled, but he casually pointed and said, "I think it went that way."
Kun Tu didn't hesitate and chased after it.
His Spirit Beast, the Green Wolf, leaped over the heads of the crowd, pursuing in that direction as well.
Yang Chan also quickly followed suit.
"Chasing after a Human Demon without using the Fur Cloak Technique, are you seeking death?" Chen Wan scolded Yuan Ming, and she too chased after them immediately.
Ba Da, riding a black-haired wild boar, sneered at Yuan Ming before bringing up the rear.
"Human Demon? What's that?"
Yuan Ming ignored Chen Wan's scolding, his interest sparked by the term 'Human Demon' she had mentioned.

chapters.title: Chapter 64 - 44: Keeping Watch
chapters.content:
"It seems that the Sect's training of these people is somehow related to this Human Demon..." Yuan Ming muttered to himself and followed along.
A group of people searched all night and ultimately found nothing.
"Hey, Beast Slave, did you really see a Human Demon?" As dawn broke, everyone stopped searching, and Kun Tu, somewhat displeased, asked Yuan Ming.
"What Human Demon?" Yuan Ming feigned confusion.
"The monster you described last night!" Kun Tu said angrily.
"If I hadn't seen that monster, how could I have described it?" Yuan Ming retorted.
That comment stopped Kun Tu, leaving him without an excuse to be angry.
"According to the information from the Sect, the Human Demon shouldn't be active in this area," Ba Da said.
"Perhaps the situation has changed, and the feedback from the Execution Hall's investigation might not be accurate," Chen Wan suggested.
Yuan Ming hesitated for a moment before speaking, "If by Human Demon you mean the creature I saw last night, then, as early as last year, someone had already encountered it."
"What did you say? Last year... where?" Chen Wan asked anxiously, the others also looked over with varying expressions.
Yuan Ming then recounted the attack on Hagon to them.
"How is that possible?" Yang Chan said incredulously.
Kun Tu turned to look at Wu Bao, who subtly nodded, serving as a confirmation of what Yuan Ming had said.
"If that's the case, then the Human Demon has been active longer and in a wider area than the Sect told us, which is certainly not good news," Chen Wan said, her expression growing more serious.
"So... should we report this to the Sect?" Ba Da asked tentatively.
"Report? Why should we report? Isn't it better if only we know this information?" Kun Tu countered.
"If we don't report it, other members might be caught off guard and attacked," Chen Wan said.
"Sister Chen Wan, don't forget, this trial is crucial for us to become Inner Sect Disciples smoothly. If we go back to report and delay our progress, allowing others to get ahead..." Kun Tu mused.
He did not directly contradict Chen Wan, but his words made her expression change.
Seeing that Chen Wan stopped speaking, Kun Tu's lips twitched, revealing a scornful smile.
Afterward, the group's pace slowed down as they continued to search for the Human Demon while also moving forward.
However, taking two days longer than expected, they ultimately didn't encounter the Human Demon again.
...
"Boom"
A thunderclap exploded, and a streak of snow-white lightning lit up the high skies, briefly tearing a gap in the gloomy, pitch-black sky.
The drizzle began to fall, immediately shrouding the once tranquil forest with the sound of dense rain, and the air began to fill with the smell of dust and green grass.
Kun Tu looked up at the leaden clouds almost touching the treetops and rode the Green Wolf over to Chen Wan.
"Junior Sister, given the look of these clouds, the rain wouldn't be light, and it's already getting late. Why don't we find a place to rest for now and continue on once the rain stops?" he suggested.
"Yuan Ming, is there a suitable place nearby to take shelter and rest?" Chen Wan turned to Yuan Ming and asked.
Throughout the journey, she had come to recognize Yuan Ming's skill in leading the way.
Under Yuan Ming's guidance, though they hadn't found the Human Demon these past few days, they had also not encountered much attack from fierce beasts, making good use of their time.
Although Kun Tu and Yang Chan still looked down on this Fur Beast Slave, they also instinctively cast inquiring looks at him.
"I haven't been to this area before, we'll just have to walk and see," Yuan Ming said.
Chen Wan, hearing this, wasn't too disappointed and nodded her head, continuing on.
After about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, the thunder grew more frequent, and the rain grew heavier.
The light in the forest dimmed, the surroundings foggy and pitch darkness settled in, and the temperature dropped further.
Just then, Yuan Ming saw a large dark shadow in the mountains ahead. He wiped the rain from his face and was trying to look closely when a flash of lightning illuminated the area.
"There seems to be a house over there." Yuan Ming pointed to the shadow and shouted.
Saying this, he led everyone hurriedly towards it.
Upon approaching, he could see clearly that it was a dilapidated building.
A lower half of the building's walls was made of rock, while the upper half was built with adobe. The plaster was peeling severely, covered with pits and various-sized holes.
"This style of house, could it be a temple worshipped by the Wild Men?" Wu Bao, who had been mostly silent in the group, suddenly spoke up.
The temple had no grand entrance, only an empty portal that led into pitch darkness, obscuring everything from view.
Yuan Ming reached into his robe to fetch a fire stick to light his way when suddenly, a "whoosh" sounded beside his ear, and a fist-sized fireball flew into the temple.
"Fireball Technique?" Yuan Ming instinctively turned around and saw that Chen Wan was the caster.
This content is presented by *.
Immediately after, another "whoosh" echoed, and three or four more fireballs flew into the temple, illuminating the interior brightly.
Yuan Ming entered the temple and saw it was empty, almost devoid of any furnishings, with thick dust covering the floors and walls, making the place look desolate and rundown.
Turning around, he saw a three-foot-high altar with a mud sculpture of a divine statue on it.
This divine statue was unlike any ordinary one, with a tiger's back and a wolf's waist, two heads, and four arms. It exuded not an ounce of solemnity but instead looked sinister and sneaky.
Upon closer inspection, Yuan Ming noticed that one of the heads on its shoulders was that of a fox, and the other, a wild wolf.
The damage to the statue was severe, with its wooden framework and straw stuffing exposed in many places, suggesting it had been abandoned for a long time.
"Good, good... the roof is intact. Let's rest here for the night," Ba Da, surveying the surroundings, was evidently pleased with the place.
"Wu Bao, you go out and bring back some meat. Yuan Ming, you'll gather firewood," Kun Tu commanded.
Wu Bao hurriedly ran out, and Yuan Ming obediently went to collect firewood.
Before long, two bonfires were set up in the temple. One was surrounded by Kun Tu and a few registered disciples, and the other was sat opposite by Yuan Ming and Wu Bao.
Wu Bao was diligently tending to the wild boar roasting over the fire, while Yuan Ming closed his eyes to rest, not uttering a word.
Just then, Kun Tu suddenly looked towards Yuan Ming and instructed, "Yuan Ming, you're on guard duty for the first half of the night. Go stand watch outside."
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming opened his eyes and stepped outside.
The rain outside continued to drizzle down, and intermittent bursts of thunder lit up the night sky.
Yuan Ming stood by the temple portal, leaning against the wall. The short and shallow eaves overhead hardly shielded all the rain, and soon his clothes were soaked through.
The cold mountain wind cut right through him; even Yuan Ming felt a bone-chilling cold, dispelling any semblance of sleepiness, leaving him only to stare into the pitch-dark woodland night.
The chatter from Chen Wan and others drifted out from the temple, and Yuan Ming, listening intently, quickly caught the gist of it.
It turned out that not only Chen Wan and a few others were here in Ten Thousand Mountains as registered disciples, at least over a hundred from the Sect had participated in this trial.
Their goal for the trial was to hunt the Human Demon.
According to Kun Tu, their performance in this trial might even determine whether the elders would notice them, and whether they might become direct disciples, that is, Inner Sect Disciples.
Though not entirely aware of the specifics, Yuan Ming guessed that this must be a great honor; otherwise, these people wouldn't risk so much venturing into Ten Thousand Mountains.
In the pitch-black rainy night, without the moon visible, it was hard to discern the time.
Suddenly, Yuan Ming smelled a rich scent of meat emanating from inside the temple and immediately wrinkled his nose, looking inside.
He saw Kun Tu and others still seated together chatting, while above the bonfire in front of Wu Bao, the roasted wild boar had turned golden-red, glistening with a shiny gleam, sizzling with fat, and was irresistibly appetizing.
"Didn't expect this guy to be quite the cook," Yuan Ming couldn't help but express his admiration.
Just then, he noticed Wu Bao's forehead was sweating, his face seemed tense, and his eyes occasionally darted towards Kun Tu and the others.
While he was surprised at why Wu Bao was acting so sneaky, Wu Bao suddenly turned his head to look his way.
Yuan Ming immediately turned around, back facing the temple door, looking every part the diligent guard.
After pausing for two breaths, Yuan Ming suddenly turned back just in time to see Wu Bao, trembling, pulling out a small porcelain bottle from his robe, removing its stopper, and sprinkling the liquid inside over the roasting wild boar.
"What is he trying to do?" Yuan Ming wondered to himself.
He furrowed his brow and sniffed the air again, not detecting anything unusual. Combined with Wu Bao's guilty demeanor, he knew it couldn't be a spice, increasing his suspicion.
"Could it be poison?" Yuan Ming's brow furrowed deeply.
Just then, Wu Bao's gaze shifted back towards him.
Yuan Ming, already alert, had turned his back again, his mind churning with various thoughts.
"Wu Bao, this chap, wouldn't dare to poison these registered disciples unless he doesn't want to live, right?" Yuan Ming's mind raced.
But obviously, a leader who could rally and ascend to such a position wouldn't seek death for no reason.
Yuan Ming's brow remained furrowed as he was about to turn and report the matter when a sudden alarm blared in his mind:
"Right, there's no way Wu Bao doesn't want to live. He must have been emboldened to do this by someone else's orders, so the person behind this..."
Yuan Ming's eyes darted around, finally resting on Kun Tu.

chapters.title: Chapter 65 - 45: Save Others Save Yourself
chapters.content:
"Is this the beginning of an internal conflict?" Yuan Ming wondered.
If they were going to such lengths to use poison, it certainly wasn't to target himself. With Ba Da and Yang Chan behaving like followers, it wasn't hard to guess whom Kun Tu was after.
Before Yuan Ming could fully understand, Wu Bao's voice rang out, "Reporting to the honored ones, the wild boar meat is ready. Please taste it."
"Are we about to make our move?" Yuan Ming hesitated for a moment before deciding not to intervene just yet.
"Bring it here," Kun Tu ordered.
Wu Bao immediately moved the whole roasted wild boar meat in front of Kun Tu and the others.
Kun Tu took out a short dagger and gently made several cuts on the pig's flesh, splitting the large piece of wild boar meat into seven or eight sections.
"Junior Sister Chen Wan, the meat looks quite good. You should have some too." He reached for a piece from the back and handed it to Chen Wan first.
Chen Wan felt it would be rude to refuse and accepted it.
The others also each picked up a piece of meat and began to relish it eagerly.
At that moment, Kun Tu suddenly thought of something and said to Wu Bao, "Go and get a piece for Yuan Ming as well."
"Master… The lord has rewarded you with this." Without hesitation, Wu Bao immediately brought a large piece of the pig's leg over to Yuan Ming with both hands.
Yuan Ming accepted it with an expressionless face and thanked him perfunctorily. Had he not known there was something wrong with the meat, he might actually have been touched by Wu Bao and Kun Tu's sudden show of goodwill.
"Try it," Wu Bao said with a smile that did not reach his eyes as he watched Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming took a bite and chewed, mumbling, "Tastes good."
Seeing this, Wu Bao turned and went back to the temple. Yuan Ming immediately spat out the wild boar meat in his mouth and rinsed with a mouthful of rainwater before stopping.
From within the temple came occasional praises of the food, even Chen Wan felt Wu Bao's cooking was not bad.
However, it wasn't long before Yuan Ming heard a disturbance from inside, seemingly the sound of someone falling.
Followed by Kun Tu feigning concern, "Junior Sister Chen Wan, what's wrong, sister?"
As Yuan Ming listened to the noises inside, he inwardly sneered. With the cover of a thunderclap, he sheared off and discarded the meat he was holding, leaving only the bone in his hand as he lay down against the wall, pretending to be poisoned.
Inside the temple, Kun Tu continued to call out for Chen Wan, though she was now unconscious with closed eyes and trembling lashes.
"Enough, stop calling her, she has already passed out," Yang Chan said with her arms folded under her chest, casting an impatient glance at Chen Wan.
Heh heh, "This little beauty," Kun Tu spoke with evident pride in his tone, "always looks down on me with the Fire Refining Hall's old hen guarding her. Today, she's in my hands, and I'll make sure she knows what true bliss is."
"Brother Kun Tu, that… the drug is too strong. I didn't dare use too much of it. You need to hurry, lest she wakes up halfway and causes trouble," Ba Da approached and whispered, sneaking glances at Chen Wan on the ground.
"Alright, you think I don't know what you're thinking? Don't worry, after I've had my fun, I won't forget to share the spoils with you, haha…" Kun Tu laughed heartily.
Yang Chan glanced at the two men with disdain, muttering, "Not a single good man among you."
At these words, Kun Tu glanced at her with slight displeasure.
Seeing this, Yang Chan quickly changed to a smile and said,
"Men have to be a bit bad for women to love them. It's just this little wench, Chen Wan, who's clueless. She's only like this because she's inexperienced - once she's had a taste, even the Fur Beast Slave here would probably be unable to resist throwing himself at her."
Wu Bao, upon hearing Yang Chan mention him, quickly lowered his head, not daring to sneak another look at Chen Wan.
"Wu Bao, we're almost at our destination. Yuan Ming is of no use to us now. Go and slaughter him now, to avoid future trouble," Kun Tu bent down, reaching out to touch Chen Wan's cheek and then remembering something, tasked Wu Bao with an order.
"Yes, master." Without delay, Wu Bao hurried toward the temple entrance.
"Take him farther away for the job; don't let the smell of blood drift in here and spoil my good time," Kun Tu reminded him once more.
"Yes."
Wu Bao, stepping outside, glanced at Yuan Ming, who lay collapsed on the ground, and revealed a twisted smile.
He bent down, seized Yuan Ming's arms, and began dragging him into the downpour, heading deeper into the dark and silent forest.
Kun Tu affectionately stroked Chen Wan's cheek, pinched it with a smile, and said, "Such a lovely face, tsk tsk, it's a shame really, but it's your fault for not recognizing what's good for you."
As he spoke, he reached for her collar and gave it a tug downward. Her red dress was torn, opening her neckline to reveal an undershirt and a generous expanse of her fair, voluptuous skin.
Kun Tu was enthralled by the sight but was suddenly interrupted by a soft 'gulp' from behind – it was Ba Da ogling, unable to help swallowing his saliva.
Yang Chan glanced at him with even more contempt.
Kun Tu also felt somewhat uncomfortable being watched like that by the pair.T%hi!s^ co!ntent was fi@rst rel&e&ased% on *#.
He immediately reached for a green cloth bag at his waist with an elaborate rune stitched on it. The bag flashed with light.
At the next instant, a beautifully carved bed with a canopy appeared out of nowhere in the temple.
"Brother Kun Tu, you have a Storage Bag now?" Yang Chan was first taken aback and then realized, staring fixedly at the green bag hanging from his waist and exclaimed in surprise.
"Before I came out this time, Elder Meng Shan rewarded me with it," Kun Tu said with pride.
"To have earned such appreciation from Elder Meng Shan, this return, you're almost guaranteed to become an Inner Sect Disciple," said Yang Chan, her eyes filled with envy.
Kun Tu cracked a smile but said nothing, though internally he was full of disdain: "That old geezer has reaped so many benefits from me over the years, it's about time he promoted me to Inner Sect Disciple."
"Brother Kun Tu, don't talk too much now, you better hurry up," Ba Da urged impatiently on the side.
With a cold laugh, Kun Tu bent over and picked up Chen Wan, tossing her into the bed's canopy.
A flicker of resentment passed through Yang Chan's eyes as she twisted her waist and headed towards the temple's entrance, while Ba Da sat down reluctantly by the fire pit.
Outside the temple, a storm raged with black wind and pelting rain, lightning flashing and thunder roaring.
In the forest a hundred yards from the temple, Wu Bao, drenched to the bone, dragged Yuan Ming to a pit and carelessly threw him in, then drew a short dagger from within his clothes.
Looking at the man he had long resented, now limp like a clod of mud, a smile played on his lips. He bent down, aimed the tip of the dagger at Yuan Ming's heart, and was about to plunge it in.
He completely failed to notice that the sword Yuan Ming had always carried behind his back was now quietly grasped in his hand.
"Click"
A bright white flash of lightning illuminated the scene, reflecting off Wu Bao's short dagger and onto Yuan Ming's face.
To his horror, he saw that under the chilling glow of the blade, Yuan Ming had opened his eyes and was smiling back at him.
Before he could react, a surge of acute pain exploded from under his feet as a wooden thorn rose abruptly from the ground, piercing through his entire foot and driving into his crouched abdomen.
Wu Bao fought through the intense pain and pressed down with the dagger in his hand, attempting to kill Yuan Ming with one strike.
But Yuan Ming, ever vigilant, would not give him that chance. His hand shot out, clamping down on Wu Bao's wrist, while his other hand wielding the sword, swept it forward.
The blade reflected a faint cyan light, flashing swiftly across Wu Bao's neck.
In an instant, a jet of blood spurted out as a round head was sent flying into the air, rolling aside.
"Ah, now it's impossible to stay out of this," Yuan Ming retreated backward, sitting on the cold, slippery ground, raising his hand to wipe his face of both blood and rainwater.
Through the curtain of rain and dense tree shadows, he saw the faint glow of fire from the temple. Slowly standing up, he flicked the blood from his sword and walked towards it.
Returning to the temple, Yuan Ming did not rashly rush in, but instead carefully climbed onto the rooftop.
Peering through a hole in the roof's tiles, Yuan Ming saw the finely made bed that was out of place in the surroundings, the petulant Yang Chan sitting at the entrance, and Ba Da with a lewd expression sitting next to the fire pit.
Inside the canopy bed, Chen Wan's outer clothing had been completely stripped off, revealing her jade-white, glowing skin beneath the thin undergarment. The scene was enticingly alluring.
A gust of wind lifted a piece of the canopy, and Yuan Ming saw Kun Tu straddling Chen Wan's long legs, his head buried in her red skirt, greedily sniffing at its scent.
"How vile…" Yuan Ming muttered to himself as goosebumps formed on his back upon seeing this.
At that moment, he hesitated.
From his observations over the past few days, he realized that Kun Tu and the others' cultivation was not weak, all being at least at the Qi Refining Fourth Level. Even facing one of them, he had no assurance of victory, let alone three at once.
Yet if he did nothing, not to mention his own conscience, Kun Tu and the others would not let him go just for killing Wu Bao.
Not because of Wu Bao's life, but because he had witnessed what was happening now.
So, Yuan Ming only had a chance at saving his own life if he rescued Chen Wan.
"It can only be this way." His eyes flashed with a decisive light.
Just as Kun Tu reached out towards Chen Wan's delicate body, from beneath the two fire pits in the temple, suddenly two cyan thorns broke through the soil and overturned the campfires in one fell swoop.
Burning logs scattered in all directions, showering sparks and startling Ba Da, who was sitting by the fire.
The flying sparks landed on the bed, instantly igniting the canopy and causing flames to surge up, swiftly engulfing the entire bed structure.
Amidst the flames, Kun Tu's furious roar could be heard.
The next moment, a ring of white Wind Blades suddenly expanded from the bed's center, sweeping in all directions.
A chaotic clatter ensued as the encircling flames were blown apart by the gusts, along with the bed's canopy and posts, all severed by the Wind Blades and shooting outward.
With the Wind Blades scattering every remaining spark on the ground, the light inside the temple dimmed significantly, plunging into darkness.
"Hey, Ba Da, what the hell are you doing?" shouted a bare-chested Kun Tu, his rage boiling over.
Despite the commotion, Chen Wan remained unconscious.
"Brother Kun Tu, I didn't do anything," Ba Da quickly cried out in protest.
Without waiting to be accused, Yang Chan immediately denied any involvement, shouting, "It wasn't me either, I didn't do anything!"
At that moment, a crack of thunder suddenly sounded!
The already crumbling roof of the temple collapsed, "clang," as countless tiles fell, creating a gaping hole exposed to the sky.
A towering white shadow crashed through the open hole and descended with the force of a mountain, aiming straight for Kun Tu on the bed below.

chapters.title: Chapter 66 - 46 Drilling Holes
chapters.content:
Kun Tu, perplexed and not daring to rashly resist, could only leap aside, coming to Yang Chan's side.
The white figure crashed onto the bed frame, directly collapsing it before twisting its head to face Ba Da, who was closest, and opened its massive, bloody mouth to let out a savage roar.
"Roar…"
Ba Da's pupils dilated instantly; upon seeing the vague outline of the figure, covered in snow-white long hair, looking neither human nor beast with indistinct facial features.
"A Human Demon, it's a Human Demon…" His cry of terror came immediately.
Before his voice had even fallen, he hurriedly ran out from beside Kun Tu and Yang Chan.
Yang Chan hadn't felt very scared initially, but seeing him flee like that suddenly spurred her own desire to retreat. However, before she could make her move, Kun Tu grabbed her arm.
"What are you afraid of? Don't forget what we came here to do," Kun Tu roared at her.
Only then did Yang Chan remember that they came expressly to find and slay the Human Demon.
"Hmph, it's all that coward Ba Da's fault, making me jump too," Yang Chan spat a curse, steadying her mind.
Yuan Ming, who had transformed into a White Ape using the Fur Cloak Technique, sighed inwardly upon seeing they were not scared off but showed no sign of backing down as he leaped forward, fists clenched into hammers slamming towards the ground.
A loud "bang" sounded.
The temple floor shook violently, and the ground beneath the feet of Yang Chan and Kun Tu instantly cracked, sending up countless fragments.
A damaged stone pillar near the two developed larger cracks and burst apart with a "bang," bringing down half of the roof with it, as a multitude of tiles and dust poured down.
Yang Chan and Kun Tu quickly dodged backward, eventually exiting the temple.
From within the smoke and dust, Yuan Ming picked up the prostrate Chen Wan and hastily readjusted her clothing before leaping toward the space above the rooftop.
That punch was not due to his sheer strength capable of bursting half the temple but was the result of using the Wood Stabbing Technique in combination with hitting the already rotting Stone Pillar to create this daunting spectacle.
Seeing an opportunity to escape, Yuan Ming did not dare to delay.
No sooner had he burst through the rooftop, feeling the touch of rain upon him, than he suddenly sensed a shadow overhead blocking the falling rain.
Looking up, Yuan Ming saw a pair of eerie green "lanterns" light up against the night sky. Around that dim green glow appeared several diamond-shaped dark red scales.
Before he could get a clear look, a hissing noise approached rapidly, and the shadow descended quickly, revealing a huge python head, its maw gaping wide as it bit down towards Yuan Ming.
"Yang Chan's spirit beast," Yuan Ming paused, sending a punch toward the space above.
A dull "bang" echoed as the large Fire Python's head retracted from the impact, and Yuan Ming's figure fell from the sky.
The moment the two hit the ground, from amidst the curtain of rain outside, Ba Da's shouting voice could be heard from afar, "Captain Kun Tu, Wu Bao is dead, and the Beast Slave Yuan Ming has disappeared!"
Hearing this, Kun Tu immediately came to his senses.
"We've been tricked, that's not a Human Demon inside, it's that Fur Beast Slave." He roared angrily and immediately slapped the Spiritual Beast Bag at his waist.
A streak of blue light shot out, and a massive Green Wolf Spirit Beast two zhang in length appeared.
Without Kun Tu's command, the wolf's bristles at its neck stood on end, its muscles tensed, and a pair of dark red eyes gleamed as it opened its mouth toward the already dilapidated temple and let out an earth-shattering roar.
"Roar…"
Accompanied by the roar, a tempest gushed from the Green Wolf's mouth, countless Wind Blades tinged with a blue glow shredding the rain, forming visible cyclones that slammed into the temple.
With a thunderous rumble, debris and tiles flew in all directions, striking inside the temple.
Feeling that fierce force, Yuan Ming had no choice but to dodge quickly, heading toward the side of the bizarre Divine Statue.
The fierce Wind Blades swept through, striking the still-standing rear wall and opening a large gash in the crumbling stone wall.
Yuan Ming looked back at the gash in the wall, ready to escape, when he noticed two green glows already rushing toward him from the darkness outside.
Since there was no Human Demon inside but only a Fur Beast Slave, Ba Da summoned his own spirit beast without any fear.
The black wild boar, its hair bristling and coated in a dark light, charged furiously toward Yuan Ming with a thunderous gallop, its two sharp tusks gleaming faintly as if coated with poison.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming's palm suddenly hit the ground, mana from his Dantian surged, pouring down toward the earth.
The Wood Stabbing Technique was immediately activated.
Just in front of him, two zhang away, the earth and rocks burst as three Wooden Thorns as thick as bull legs emerged at an angle, skewering up from the ground like stakes against the charging black boar.
With a "bang," the black boar slammed into the stout Wooden Thorns, a spray of blood erupting from it as it also shattered the thorns completely, dispersing them.
Yet its speed was only slightly reduced, and it still charged forward.
Yuan Ming felt a sinking feeling in his heart and quickly rolled to the side to dodge.
The spirit beasts of these Registered Disciples seemed to be similar to the Fierce Beasts he usually hunted, but their actual combat power was worlds apart, and they were not something he could easily handle.
Not to mention their masters, each of whom was a bona fide disciple of Biluo Cave, capable of learning various secret skills and techniques of the sect.
Yuan Ming suddenly felt a pang of regret in his heart, realizing that he should not have acted impulsively, leading himself to the brink of a desperate situation; he should at least have waited for a more suitable opportunity.
With a "bang" sound,Lovethisstory?Showsupportat*.
the rampaging black-furred boar slammed into the strangely shaped fierce god statue, causing it to crumble into pieces, even the base of the statue was thrown into the air.
The fierce impact made the black-furred boar somewhat dizzy, and after shaking its head to get its bearings, it charged toward Yuan Ming again.
The red Fire Python above him also opened its bloody maw, swooping down towards him.
Surrounded, Yuan Ming's eyes darted around, looking for a way out when he suddenly noticed that beneath the collapsed statue, a dark hole had appeared.
His mind raced, and he made a swift decision.
He dispelled the Fur Cloak Technique and, cradling Chen Wan in his arms, charged forward, avoiding the Fire Python's assault and heading straight towards the black-furred boar.
Just as they were about to collide, his body suddenly ducked low, sliding beneath the boar taking advantage of its size, and found himself beside the hole.
Yuan Ming peered into the hole, only to see pitch darkness inside, from which cold wind blew out, making it impossible to see how deep it was.
"Beast Slave, why not surrender?" came Kun Tu's voice at that moment.
He had rushed in with his Green Wolf Spirit Beast.
Without any time to think further, Yuan Ming scooped up Chen Wan and leaped into the hole.
After falling for three or four Zhang, he landed on a slope and began to slide rapidly downwards.
Seeing this, Kun Tu immediately gave chase and, arriving at the entrance, assessed its size before shouting to Yang Chan, "Quick! Send your Fire Python in. We must kill them today; otherwise, once we return to the sect, we're done for."
Yang Chan's expression was tense, and without wasting words, she immediately commanded the Fire Python to slither into the cave.
Unless several of them took the risk to chase personally, the only spirit beast that could enter the cave was the Fire Python.
The Fire Python dived into the cave, flicking its tongue and undulating, quickly chasing downwards.
The cave was far from smooth, with rocks jutting out everywhere; Yuan Ming bounced around, his body already covered in wounds, but he dared not slow down.
Suddenly, he heard a noise behind him and felt a sense of doom.
Then, a roar erupted behind him as the Fire Python caught up, its massive mouth opening wide and from within, a line of fire shot out, turning into a wave of flames that filled the entire cave.
Yuan Ming felt a sudden surge in temperature and, shivering with dread, immediately activated the Wood Stabbing Technique, causing three thick Wooden Thorns to rise from the ground behind him in an attempt to block the flames.
The raging fire passed through the gaps in the Wooden Thorns, furiously erupting and still scorching his back with intense Burning pain, nearly causing him to stop breathing.
"Bang"
The sound behind him was that of the Wooden Thorns being shattered, and the Fire Python relentlessly continued its pursuit, its gaping maw now just inches away.
Feeling the scorching heat from within, Yuan Ming gripped his sword tightly, readying himself for a final stand.
At that moment, he felt movement from the tender body in his arms; Chen Wan seemed to be waking up.
"Hey! If you don't want to die, think of something fast," Yuan Ming called out loudly.
Chen Wan's mind was cloudy and her eyes unfocused with bewilderment, but upon seeing what was happening behind them, her pupils constricted and she instinctively reached into her sleeve and threw something into the gaping maw of the creature behind her.
"Swoosh"
A walnut-sized metal pellet flew out, its engraved hollow Flames slightly lighting up, with tiny sparks visible inside, quickly disappearing into the mouth of the Fire Python.
The next instant, Chen Wan tucked herself into Yuan Ming's embrace.
Before Yuan Ming could react, there was a thunderous "boom" from behind.
A fierce explosion of flames erupted behind him, blowing the Fire Python's head to pieces, with the searing wave of fire impacting his back, pushing him to slide even faster downwards.
The explosion's waves surged furiously up and down the cave, the powerful shockwave causing incessant collapses; the cave crumbled in moments.
Rocks and soil fell, sealing the cave as debris turned into a roaring torrent chasing down Yuan Ming and Chen Wan.
The mighty shockwave mixed with the roaring explosion, resonating powerfully in the confined space. The force that struck Yuan Ming made his Sea of Consciousness tremble, and everything went dark as he passed out.
Chen Wan, in his arms, fared no better, also losing consciousness amid the tumultuous turmoil...

chapters.title: Chapter 67 - 47 Healing Wounds
chapters.content:
I don't know how long it had passed.
In the dim cave, Yuan Ming struggled to open his eyes, feeling sour and painful, and subconsciously he wanted to rub them, but suddenly he felt an icy sensation around his neck.
"Don't move if you don't want to die." At this moment, a cold yet clear female voice rang out.
"Chen Wan... Senior Sister?" Yuan Ming called out hesitantly.
"I'll give you one chance to explain, what exactly is going on?" Chen Wan asked.
She still remembered chatting and eating barbecued meat with Kun Tu and others in the temple, and remembered she seemed very sleepy and had fallen asleep.
In her slumber, she seemed to have dreamt of fighting fierce beasts.
When she woke up, she found herself lying in the arms of the Fur Beast Slave, sleeping in this deep and dark cavern.
Yuan Ming blinked hard, his vision still blurry, and his head felt heavy.
"You were conspired against by Kun Tu and the others; they drugged the meat they gave you, and after you passed out, they tried to take advantage of you. I saved you," Yuan Ming organized his words and said.
"Why would you save me? We're neither relatives nor friends," Chen Wan obviously didn't believe him and moved the cold object in her hand slightly forward.
"They wanted to silence me as well; I had no other choice," Yuan Ming said.
Chen Wan frowned slightly upon hearing this.
She had always known that Kun Tu coveted her, and she had always been reluctant to be on the same team with him, but she had never thought that he would dare use such despicable methods against her.
"You're lying. Kun Tu can silence you, but can he also silence Ba Da and Yang Chan?" Chen Wan's expression was still icy, but her tone had relaxed slightly.
"Even an outsider like me can see that Yang Chan is jealous of you, and Ba Da covets you. They teamed up against you. Otherwise, where do you think the drug that knocked you out came from?" Yuan Ming scoffed and said.
Chen Wan's heart sank when she heard this.
"And the Fire Python that chased us in the caves later, do you think it was there to rescue you? It was aimed at silencing you," Yuan Ming continued to add.
Hearing this, Chen Wan quickly felt inside her sleeve, and finding that a Red Fire Bomb was indeed missing, she realized that it was not a dream but a real experience.
Despite being half-convinced of what Yuan Ming said, she still withdrew the dagger from behind Yuan Ming's neck.
Chen Wan rubbed her slightly sore brow, raised her hand, and a ball of firelight lit up in front of her.
The concentrated ball of fire hovered in mid-air, illuminating the surrounding darkness, and Yuan Ming could now see clearly that they were inside a huge Underground River cave.
The place was cold and damp all around, and from the ceiling above hung stalactites, dripping water with a "drip-drip" sound.
In front of him, Chen Wan in a red dress looked disheveled with dirt on her face and her clothes in disarray presenting a somewhat pitiful and vulnerable appearance that involuntarily provoked pity.
He only glanced at her once before hurriedly averting his gaze.
Chen Wan subconsciously tightened her clothes, but the outer garment torn by Kun Tu couldn't be restored.
Her gaze fell on Yuan Ming opposite her, and her brows furrowed slightly.
He was covered in scratches and bruises everywhere, although they were no longer bleeding but had dried into crusts. Still, they looked rather shocking.
"You're injured," Chen Wan said.
Yuan Ming then looked down at himself, noticing his clothes were worn through on his arms and legs, then turned to look over his shoulder.
As he moved, intense pain caused him to grimace.
A burning pain spread from his back, seemingly more severe than other injuries.
"Turn around, let me have a look," Chen Wan said upon seeing this.
Yuan Ming hesitated for a moment, but still turned his body, enduring the pain.
The moment Chen Wan saw Yuan Ming's back, her eyes widened in shock, and she couldn't help but cover her mouth.
The skin on his entire back was scorched black, and his shoulder blades were grotesquely exposed, indicating a very serious injury.Fоr а smооthеr rеаding еxpеriеnсе, visit МV&LЕМРYR.
"How is he enduring such a severe injury?" Chen Wan couldn't help but wonder.
Looking at her own body, apart from disheveled clothes and some minor scrapes on her hands and feet, there were no other injuries, and she couldn't help thinking, "Did he sustain such severe injuries to protect me?"
Yuan Ming, unaware of her thoughts, asked doubtfully, "Are you done?"
"Your back is seriously burned and it's unlikely to heal quickly with just your body's energy. Don't move, let me... let me apply some medicine for you," Chen Wan suddenly came back to her senses, pausing slightly as she spoke.
"No need, I..." Yuan Ming instinctively wanted to refuse.
As he was about to turn back, he heard the stern voice from behind him say, "Don't move."
Yuan Ming was taken aback and really stopped moving.
Straight after, he heard the sound of a bottle stopper being pulled out from behind him, followed by a sharp burning pain on his spine that made him let out a low growl of pain.
"Er..."
Yuan Ming forcefully suppressed a low growl, the searing pain on his back lasted only three or four breaths before quickly turning into an oddly cold and refreshing sensation, which then began to feel slightly itchy.
He could feel the woman behind him moving carefully, sprinkling powder over each and every wound on his back.
At that moment, the fireball suspended midair suddenly extinguished, and Chen Wan's movements also stopped.
"The effect of the Jade Screen Powder is very fast, in at most half a day, your wounds will all have scabbed over, but it will still take three days for them to heal completely," Chen Wan's voice came through the darkness.
"Thank you," Yuan Ming expressed his gratitude.
He moved slightly and found the pain in his back had lessened a lot. He then pulled up the White Ape Beast Skin that was tied around his waist and draped it over his body.
In the darkness, neither of them spoke again, falling into silence for a time.
A moment later, Yuan Ming broke the silence and said, "We can't stay here for long. We need to find a way out."
As soon as he finished speaking, a fireball relit, whooshing upward and shooting into the high air, crashing against the dome of the underground cavern and sparking embers.
"Before you woke up, I had checked. We fell from a vertical shaft above, but the bend in the shaft has collapsed, making it impossible to return the way we came," Chen Wan said.
Yuan Ming looked up and struggled to his feet, stumbling a bit, and said, "Then we must find another way."
Afterward, he glanced around left and right.
"This place is a cave eroded by an underground river; during the flood season, it should be completely submerged by the river water. I've checked, and there are no exits on either side," Chen Wan sighed and said.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming walked forward about a dozen steps and indeed saw an Underground River stretched out in front, with gentle currents that gave no indication of its depth.
He reached out to touch it and felt a bone-chilling cold.
At this moment, Chen Wan also came over, glanced at it, and suddenly furrowed her brow, "The water level's risen, when I came to check earlier, the waterline hadn't reached here. How did it rise so much in just a short while?"
"Although it's not the flood season, the rain that fell yesterday was heavy, it's not surprising the water level in the Dark River would rise, just don't know by how much," Yuan Ming pondered.
With that, he walked back to the opposite stone wall and sized it up from top to bottom, his brows furrowing.
"What's wrong?" sensing something, Chen Wan asked.
"Look, there's a clear waterline mark on the stone wall, the upper part looks somewhat dry with moss growing on it, while the lower part is more moist and smooth, it seems this place has been frequently flooded recently," Yuan Ming said.
Chen Wan looked at the waterline about a yard high and her face involuntarily took on a slight change of color.
"If the water level continues to rise, it will flood this place sooner or later. We can't just sit and wait for death, we must find a way to escape," Yuan Ming continued.
"How can we escape, there's absolutely no way out here," Chen Wan said.
"If there's no way on land, we can take the underwater route, the Underground River will definitely have an exit," Yuan Ming looked at Chen Wan and said.
Chen Wan showed a troubled expression, hesitatingly said, "I... I can't swim."
"Then... I'll go down and explore the water first, you wait here for a moment," Yuan Ming was slightly taken aback before promptly saying.
After speaking, he removed the bronze longsword hanging from his waist and took off the White Ape Beast Skin he had donned, retrieving a black, rough-skinned Beast Skin from the torn clothes at his chest, and wrapped it around his body.
He walked to the river's edge, activated his Mana, and cast the Fur Cloak Technique.
Subsequently, the black Beast Skin wrapped around his body like a living creature, quickly covering all parts of his body and completing the transformation.
Now he was covered in black Beast Skin with large black bumps on his back that looked extremely tough, webbing grew between the fingers of his hands and toes as well, but his eyes drooped a lot.
The figure resembled that of a humanoid toad.
Chen Wan was startled by his sudden transformation and couldn't help but step back, distancing herself from him somewhat.
Yuan Ming moved his body, opened his mouth for a deep inhale, feeling a faint current of air in his chest, as if his abdominal cavity had expanded a lot. With a sudden push off the ground with his legs, he leapt up and plunged straight into the water.
A chilling cold engulfed him, causing Yuan Ming under the water to shiver involuntarily, and he quickly kicked his legs, diving underwater in a frog-like swim, moving with the flow of the river.
Splashes formed on the surface of the water, and soon calmed down, with Yuan Ming's figure disappearing.
Chen Wan stood on the shore, waiting silently.
However, time passed and there was no sign of activity from under the water, and Yuan Ming did not return.
Just then, a series of thunderous noises emanated from the cavern, rumbling, causing Chen Wan's heart to palpitate.
After the Fireball Technique extinguished, she immediately conjured another, illuminating her surroundings.
At that moment, she felt a sudden coolness at her feet, and looked down to find that the surface of the Dark River had risen again, seemingly faster than before.
Chen Wan hurriedly retreated, getting anxious and concerned in her heart.
But the more anxious she became, the more rapid the rumbling noises in the cavern grew, and the Dark River became turbulent in response.
Seeing the surging waves and the visibly faster flow of the Dark River, Chen Wan sensed something bad was about to happen, realizing that this was a sign of flash floods, and the water level would soon rise rapidly, submerging the entire cave.
But Yuan Ming had yet to reappear.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 48: Tyrant Salamander
chapters.content:
After roughly the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Chen Wan was forced to keep retreating by the rapidly rising water level. She clutched Yuan Ming's White Ape Beast Skin and bronze longsword in her arms, with her back already pressed against the stone wall.
By now, the river water had filled the entire cave, and the water level had already reached Chen Wan's waist.
From anxiousness, her heart had turned to despair, and she couldn't help but think, "How could I be so foolish; he's not coming back..."
After all, that guy was just a Fur Beast Slave. Even if nothing had gone wrong and he really had found a way out, he wouldn't risk coming back to save her, since they were strangers met by chance, not related by blood or obligation.
It was laughable that when he left, leaving behind his Beast Skin and longsword, she had felt an inexplicable sense of relief.
Just as Chen Wan was wallowing in self-pity, the water in front of her suddenly churned, and a dark figure burst forth, gasping with a "huff, huff" sound.
She almost couldn't resist launching a Fireball Technique at that person.
When she recognized the ugly salamander-like figure, a wave of emotion suddenly washed over her, and her eyes started to moisten.
Yuan Ming, who had rushed back, was also surprised by the changes here and said in a deep voice, "Looks like a flash flood has erupted. I almost couldn't find your position."
"Did you find an exit?" Chen Wan asked eagerly.
"The Underground River is far longer than I expected. I swam for a long time but couldn't reach the end," Yuan Ming shook his head and said, gasping for breath.
Chen Wan's expression immediately stiffened, her heart sinking to desolation.
"However, I found a cavity up ahead that's much larger than this place. It won't be submerged for now. We can rest there for a while, catch our breath, and then continue to look for a way downstream," Yuan Ming took a deep breath and continued.
"We have no choice but to try," Chen Wan said, somewhat speechless at Yuan Ming's gasping speech.
Seeing the water level rising to her chest, she didn't want to stay a moment longer.
"How long can you hold your breath?" Yuan Ming asked.
"I haven't cultivated Water Technique. At most, I can last half a quarter of an hour," Chen Wan answered after pondering.
At this moment, she regretted looking down on Water Technique just because she was a disciple of Fire Refining Hall. Fortunately, Fire Refining Hall Disciples were required to exert themselves in long sessions of Artifact Refining, which demanded good breath control, so her breathing capacity was not weak.
"Half a quarter of an hour should be enough," Yuan Ming mused, then said, "You'll need to lie on my back, and I'll carry you as we swim."
At his words, Chen Wan glanced at Yuan Ming's back, covered in black lumps, and hesitated.
"With your speed, without my assistance, you would definitely not reach there in half a quarter of an hour," Yuan Ming looked at her and said indifferently.
Chen Wan took a deep breath and nodded.
With one hand, she held onto Yuan Ming's White Ape Beast Skin and bronze longsword, and with the other, she tried to overcome the discomfort as she placed her hand on Yuan Ming's shoulder.
"Take a deep breath," Yuan Ming instructed.
Chen Wan immediately complied.
In the next instant, Yuan Ming's body suddenly submerged, plunging with Chen Wan into the water forcefully.
Yuan Ming kicked hard with both legs spread out, then brought them together and kicked again, shooting swiftly downstream with the current, covering seven or eight zhang in no time.
They reached the edge of the cavern where the river converged and entered a tunnel.
Without any pause, Yuan Ming, carrying Chen Wan, dived into it and swam vigorously downstream.
Inside the cavern, there was nothing but darkness.
With her eyes tightly shut, Chen Wan could only hear the muffled sound of the water, her heartbeat accelerating, her grip on Yuan Ming's shoulder involuntarily tightening, her body instinctively pressing closer to his back.
Yuan Ming felt Chen Wan's nervousness from behind and had no choice but to move his limbs faster, swimming swiftly downstream.
About the time it takes to drink a cup of tea later, Chen Wan gradually grew accustomed to the chilling sensation underwater and couldn't help but open her eyes.
However, she couldn't see anything in the pitch-black water, feeling only the presence of stone walls all around, which brought on a claustrophobic fear.
After looking around for a while, she closed her eyes again, finding it more bearable that way.
But just then, she suddenly felt something touch her heel.
She hadn't moved at all, nor had she made any kicking motions, so it was impossible for her to have touched anything other than water.
If that was the case, then something must be following her and touching her.
"Are there fish in this underground river?" Chen Wan thought, puzzled.
Before she could figure it out, the sensation of being touched came again, stronger than before.
Realizing something was wrong, Chen Wan immediately opened her eyes and turned to look back.
What she saw shocked her so much she almost couldn't help but cry out, and her hand gripping Yuan Ming's shoulder tightened.
Behind them in the dark waters, a giant black shadow suddenly emerged, and it did not resemble a fish in any way.
Chen Wan suppressed her fear and, with her hands clutching the Beast Skin and the bronze longsword, she forcefully slapped Yuan Ming's back.
Yuan Ming immediately realized something was wrong and twisted his neck to look back, wanting to see what the problem was, when he heard a "woo-woo" crying sound behind him.
The sound was somewhat childish, and as it traveled through the water, it clearly pierced into his ears.
If he were not wearing Toad Beast Skin, at this moment his hair would certainly stand on end, and his back would be covered in goosebumps.
It was then that Chen Wan pushed the White Ape Beast Skin and the bronze longsword beneath her, channeled Mana within her body, and waved her palm toward what was behind them.
A hazy red light immediately lit up in her palm, brightening the water behind them by a fraction.
In the dim light, she saw a huge yet flattened white face with a gaping mouth that took up one-third of the face, and two small, black eyes, like beans, sparingly placed on the sides of the cheeks.
She screamed in shock, and water choked her throat, her breathing instantly disrupted.
The pale and dreadful face seemed to be shocked as well, and the "woo-woo" crying grew more urgent. Red and black patterns suddenly appeared on the white cheeks, and it opened its enormous mouth, biting towards Yuan Ming and her.
In the instant he turned his head, Yuan Ming also saw the creature's face, and he thought to himself, "Tyrant salamander?"
He immediately kicked his legs and swam forward powerfully, quickly increasing his speed and putting some distance between them and that spectral thing.
However, the "woo-woo" behind them grew louder, and the creature that seemed to be a tyrant salamander was not willing to let them go, furiously chasing after them.
In her terror, Chen Wan had completely lost her composure. Her five fingers dug into Yuan Ming's back, her nails embedded deeply in his skin, and she had already choked on several mouthfuls of the cold river water.
Just then, she felt a searing pain at her ankle. Looking back, she realized that the humanoid monster could actually spit out a red and sticky liquid like magma from its mouth.
The sticky substance adhered to her ankle, corroding a large hole in her clothing and also burning her skin.
The sharp pain, however, ignited Chen Wan's fighting spirit, snapping her out of her panic. Reaching into her sleeve, she pulled out another Red Fire Bomb.
But just as she was about to throw it, she recalled the scene when they had been chased by the Fire Python in the cave. Throwing the Red Fire Bomb here might not kill the fierce beast, and the shock of the water waves could likely knock them both unconscious.
If the cave were to collapse again, they wouldn't even leave full corpses behind, directly buried here together.
Chen Wan felt extremely frustrated. Here in the water, her expertly trained Fire Technique was greatly restricted; she could not even cast the Fireball Technique.
As she hesitated, she suddenly noticed Yuan Ming slowing down and placing a hand on the rock wall.
"What is he trying to do?"
The next instant, two green halos suddenly lit up on the rock wall behind them, and two sharp Wooden Thorns, each about two feet long, jutted out.
"Wood Stabbing Technique." Chen Wan was surprised; she did not expect the Fur Beast Slave to know Magic.
The tyrant salamander, in its pursuit, was stabbed by the Wooden Thorns, ripping a long gash in its body from which crimson blood flowed.
Writhing in pain, its ferocity exploded; it opened its mouth and sprayed out a large mass of sticky red liquid, covering Chen Wan.
If she were to be hit, half of her back would probably be corroded.
In the nick of time, the hand Chen Wan had on Yuan Ming's shoulder was suddenly grasped, and with a pull forward, she was flung from his shoulder.
The red sticky liquid immediately fell on Yuan Ming's back, hissing upon contact.
Yuan Ming gritted his teeth against the sharp pain and surged forward, reaching Chen Wan's side. He drew the bronze longsword from her hand and pushed on her shapely, curved hips, sending her ahead.Sample from My Virtual Library Empire—read more on M&VLEMPY&R.
He then turned around abruptly, channeled Mana into the Green Fish Sword in his hand, and slashed at the chasing tyrant salamander.
"Swoosh"
The Green Fish Sword lit up, and its powerful force parted the water, striking directly at the face of the tyrant salamander.
The creature let out a wretched howl, and as its face split open from the strike, its mouth sprayed out a surge of poison, shooting towards Yuan Ming.
As Yuan Ming turned to flee, a Dark Lump on his back suddenly sprayed out black poison, scattering in the water and forming dots that surged towards the tyrant salamander.
The two types of poison mixed together, slightly offsetting the pursuit of the salamander's corrosive poison.
Yuan Ming took the opportunity to swim vigorously forward, catching up to Chen Wan. He embraced her and kicked rapidly with his legs, swimming frantically ahead with her in his arms.
Behind them, the tyrant salamander plunged into the area of mixed poison, and the water there immediately began to boil.
The toxin formed by the mixture of the two poisons turned out to be unbearable even for it.
The tyrant salamander wailed miserably, no longer able to chase after them.
After this ordeal, not to mention the physical drain on Yuan Ming and Chen Wan, their breathing was also disrupted; it was uncertain whether they would be able to make it to the cavity.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 - 49 Wang
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming had no time to think at this moment, he could only swim with all his might, hoping to reach the next place where they could take a breath before Chen Wan's air supply was exhausted.
Chen Wan was also paddling with her arms to help move forward quickly.
This time she had taken the risk to participate in the trial in order to take a step further to become an Inner Sect Disciple, naturally, she didn't want to just die here.
As time trickled away, the little air she had reserved in her lungs was about to run out. The feeling of suffocation in her chest at the beginning turned into a pain that felt like it would explode.
She was reaching her limit, and she couldn't hold on any longer.
Just when Chen Wan's body had started to uncontrollably convulse, she found that Yuan Ming was rapidly surfacing with her, and all at once, they broke through the water's surface.
"Huh..."
The moment Chen Wan broke through the water, she expelled all the stale air from her chest, and then felt a stinging pain in her lungs, making her involuntarily let out a soft gasp.
But immediately after, she began to breathe in the fresh air around her in short, greedy gulps.
Only when she had finally regained some composure did she look around, only to find that they were still inside the cave, with a pitch-black dome not far above their heads.
"How much further is it to the cavity you mentioned?" Chen Wan inhaled deeply and asked.
Yuan Ming's gaze was solemn, he replied, "We've already arrived."
"Already arrived?" Chen Wan was shocked as if struck by lightning.
"The water in the Underground River has risen too violently, this area will also be completely submerged soon." Yuan Ming let out a sigh and said.
In the darkness, his gaze fell on Chen Wan, whose clothes clung tightly to her exquisite body and whose wet hair stuck to her fair cheeks, making her appear somewhat disheveled but not detracting from her beauty, instead evoking sympathy.
But at this moment, Yuan Ming couldn't afford to feel sympathy, his mind was occupied with the matter of life and death, wondering whether to abandon her there and then.
After all, if it was just him, he would certainly be able to swim faster and preserve air longer, perhaps managing to survive until finding the exit of the Dark River.
Rght at that time, Chen Wan suddenly raised her palm high, and a burst of light ignited within it, which then shot forth and pierced towards the cave's dome.
Yuan Ming was about to question her when he saw that the Fireball kept ascending higher and higher, burrowing its way into the dome.
The next instant, a flash of excitement appeared on his face.
"There's a vertical shaft in the dome," Chen Wan shouted, her tone full of surprise.
By this time, the Fireball that had risen seven or eight zhang away seemed to have hit something, bursting into fierce flames for a moment, before suddenly going out.
"Could it be a dead end?" The hearts of Yuan Ming and Chen Wan both sank upon seeing this.
"I'll go up and take a look," Yuan Ming said.
He then clamped his Toad Beast legs together with force, causing water to be squeezed out from between his legs, and the upward force suddenly propelled his body out of the water and up towards the dome above.
As he crashed into the vertical shaft, Yuan Ming spread his arms to both sides, steadying himself against the shaft walls.
After that, he used his hands and feet to support and climb his way up quickly, soon reaching the end of the vertical shaft, where the residue heat of the Fireball Technique still lingered.
"How is it?" Chen Wan asked anxiously from below.
After a long silence in the dark, Yuan Ming's voice sounded a little muffled as he replied, "There's a slanted shaft connected, not sure where it leads to?"
"Pull me up first, the water level is rising quickly, and the current is getting stronger," Chen Wan urged urgently.
The water level had already risen too much, and she was just about three feet away from the dome.
After waiting for a moment, a hand reached out from the vertical shaft above and pulled her into the tunnel.
Yuan Ming carefully crawled ahead, turning into the slanted tunnel at the end, continuing onwards, with Chen Wan silently following behind, her heart filled with many emotions.
She never imagined she would go through this with a Fur Beast Slave she had just met not long ago.
Not knowing how long they had been crawling in the cramped and dark cave, Yuan Ming suddenly stopped.
"What is it?" Chen Wan's heart tightened as she quickly asked.
She feared receiving an answer that it was a dead end.
"There seems to be some noise up ahead," Yuan Ming said in a hushed tone.
"A noise... doesn't that mean we're about to get out?" Joy sprung in Chen Wan's heart, but she soon noticed Yuan Ming's tensed body in front and immediately sensed something was amiss.
Had they encountered some new danger?
"What... what's wrong?" Chen Wan also lowered her voice involuntarily.
"That noise doesn't seem to be made by a person; something's not quite right. I'll go ahead to check it out, don't rush to follow," Yuan Ming said as he took off his Toad Beast skin and pulled on his White Ape Beast Skin.
Without employing the Fur Cloak Technique, he kept low to the ground and continued crawling forward.
After quite a while, a glimmer of light finally appeared in the darkness ahead, and the cave entrance was in sight.
Yuan Ming crawled to the entrance and didn't rush out.
After carefully checking, he discovered that this exit was actually on the wall of another underground cave, and right in front was a hanging stalactite, concealing the entrance and making his position very hidden.
Yuan Ming quietly poked his head out, bypassed the hanging stalactite, and looked toward the distance.
At this glance, his eyes widened instantly.
He saw in a corner of the cave, sunlight from a hole above shone down, illuminating a relatively bright area below.
In that area, there was currently a large group of creatures covered in white long hair, with skinny arms and black sharp claws, looking like some kind of strange human-like monster.
"Human Demons!" The thought flew into Yuan Ming's mind almost instantaneously.
He silently counted them and found that there were as many as seventeen in number.
However, what baffled him was that these Human Demons were all gathered together, each standing with hands drooping, bodies slightly swaying like a bunch of drunken brutes, appearing very odd and grotesque.
Considering his limited knowledge of these creatures, he dared not act rashly and could only retreat to call over Chen Wan.
The two of them squeezed at the cavity entrance, peering out.
Upon seeing this scene, shock clearly flickered across Chen Wan's face, followed by a profound confusion and disbelief.
"Impossible, this can't be…" she murmured softly.
"What's impossible?" Yuan Ming immediately asked.
"Judging by their appearance, these fellows are definitely Human Demons, but… but Human Demons are thought to be devoid of spiritual intelligence, insensible to pain, only knowing to fight and devour, even against their own kind. They simply couldn't gather together peacefully like this," Chen Wan couldn't make sense of it.
"They're all gathered here, how are we supposed to get out?" Yuan Ming was actually worried about this.
Just then, Chen Wan's expression changed again, as if she thought of something terrifying, and her mouth opened slightly in shock.
"What is it?" Yuan Ming frowned.
"There's only one reason that can make Human Demons gather without fighting…" Chen Wan said with a trembling voice.
Yuan Ming's gaze sharpened as he guessed the answer, "Are they being controlled by something?"
"It's the King. A king has emerged among the gathered Human Demons. Only the Human Demon King can control these creatures," Chen Wan said.
"Human Demon King…" Yuan Ming murmured thoughtfully.
"This is bad, very bad, I have to report back to the Sect immediately," Chen Wan said anxiously.
With that, she was about to rush out of the cavity.
Yuan Ming quickly grabbed her and whispered harshly, "If you want to die I won't stop you, but don't drag me down with you. Do you want to serve yourself as food to those creatures by rushing out like this?"
"You don't understand, if a Human Demon King has emerged, then this trial task is compromised, many people may die," Chen Wan said, her face pale, struggling to get her words out.
"Explain clearly, what exactly is going on?" Yuan Ming grabbed her shoulders, demanding.This chapter was made possible by the community at *.
The Registered Disciple of Biluo Cave in front of him was obviously inexperienced in facing danger directly. Her panicked behavior reflected her lack of experience, and Yuan Ming could not help but feel disdain.
"This trial is an entrance evaluation for us Registered Disciples. The objective is to investigate and kill Human Demons. Disciples who perform well may be chosen by the elders of the various halls to become Inner Sect Disciples," Chen Wan explained, her mind stabilizing after Yuan Ming's grip.
"You said that if there's a Human Demon King, there will be a problem. What does that mean?" Yuan Ming pressed on.
