Although Yuan Ming had many methods at his disposal, being at the Qi Refining Fifth Layer placed him slightly lower among the Registered Disciples, and it would be best to advance to the sixth-tier Qi Refining before attempting it.
With the extraordinarily fast cultivation speed of the Nine Elements Technique, another month would suffice to reach the sixth-tier Qi Refining. However, all preparations for taming beasts were already made, and waiting another month would be an excessive waste of time.
Yuan Ming gritted his teeth in his mind, took out a watery Immortal Peach, which was the same red peach he had picked from Mist Island.
He had already inquired clearly that this peach was known as a Red Core Spirit Peach, a rather rare type of Strengthening and Nourishing Spirit Fruit. Judging by its appearance, it was almost a hundred years old, suitable for refining into elixir or could be consumed directly like meat Ganoderma.
Given his current status and means, he naturally had neither the channels nor the capital to refine it into an elixir.
Yuan Ming took a bite of the peach, swallowing it in just a few bites.
The flesh soon turned into a liquid that flowed into his stomach, and a copious amount of Spiritual Power began circulating throughout his body.
Yuan Ming closed his eyes and circulated the Nine Elements Technique to absorb this Spiritual Power, causing fluctuations in his Mana to gradually rise.
A day and a night passed quickly.
Yuan Ming's aura surged dramatically, and his clothes fluttered without wind, the surrounding air also moved and shook before finally returning to calm.
He opened his eyes and a smile graced his lips.
The nearly hundred-year-old Red Core Spirit Peach indeed had a potent medicinal strength. Even without being refined into an elixir, its abundant Spiritual Energy greatly pleased him and allowed him to break through to the sixth-tier Qi Refining as he wished.
With this, his confidence and ability to protect himself in taming a spirit beast had both increased.
The next day, Yuan Ming greeted Fang Ge and then applied for the Sect-leaving token, leaving Biluo Cave.
Disciples of Biluo Cave who wish to tame their own spirit beasts usually head deep into the Ten Thousand Mountains, where Fierce Beasts are numerous, to find suitable targets.
However, since the depths of the Ten Thousand Mountains are vast, finding a suitable spirit beast depends on luck. Many search for months without finding their desired beast, which is not only time-consuming and labor-intensive but also fraught with immense danger.
For this reason, most disciples buy their spirit beasts from the Beast Taming Hall rather than seeking them out on their own.
Yet, Yuan Ming was not concerned about this. When he had previously sought advice from the Three Cave Masters on the art of taming beasts, he had already decided where to look for his quarry - Mist Island.
The island was teeming with strange Fierce Beasts, and capturing any one of them would yield a fine spirit beast.
The only trouble was the black aquatic monster surrounding the island. However, he was now different from before and had prepared some countermeasures.
Yuan Ming left the Sect and quickly arrived at the shores of Qianlu Lake.
Instead of binding a raft again, he waved his hand towards the lake, and a small boat appeared and settled on the water's surface.
The boat, crafted by a disciple skilled in handiwork within the Sect, was much faster than his previous raft on the water.
He leapt aboard, paddled the oars, and headed in the direction of Mist Island.
After two hours, Yuan Ming reached an area with particularly dense mist.
Using his memory and lifting the incense burner several times to search from the sky, he eventually found Mist Island again.
This time Yuan Ming was lucky, not encountering the black aquatic monster. However, to be safe, he still packed away the boat from a distance and flew directly onto the island with the incense burner, landing within a purple forest.
"This is not the Black Pine Forest..." he was rather disappointed.
Impressed by the effectiveness of the Red Core Spirit Peach, he initially hoped to land from the side of the Black Pine Forest and pluck all the Spiritual Peaches there. It seemed now that would not be possible.
He would look for that fruit tree once he finished handling his affairs.
Yuan Ming surveyed his surroundings, looking at the nearby Purple Trees. Their leaves were palm-shaped, resembling maple leaves, and emitted a faint, pleasant fragrance.
In the time since, he had brushed up on a lot of knowledge about the Ten Thousand Mountains, including the trees and vegetation. However, these purple maple trees had not appeared in the Classics, nor had the earlier Black Pine Trees.
Yuan Ming looked at the other plants, which were also unfamiliar.
"This island is quite peculiar. Its vegetation seems to be completely separate from that of Ten Thousand Mountains. Could it be due to being surrounded by water on all sides?" He pondered quietly to himself.
Yuan Ming didn't immediately venture deeper into the island but first found a safe place in the maple forest to completely restore his Mana before setting off into the island.
It seemed that the Purple Maple Forest was devoid of Fierce Beasts. He walked out of the forest without any danger approaching.
He continued forward, and the fog ahead thinned out, revealing a vast, open swamp. With his vision, he could see more than ten zhang away.
The swamp was filled with dark green mud, and looking around, there were lush water plants everywhere, with occasional trees standing tall, saturating the air with a rotting smell.

chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 97 Initial Beast Taming
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming halted his pace, his gaze shifting between the swamp and the Purple Maple Forest, eyebrows twitching.
"It's just an island, yet the environment is so complex and changeable, and each area's terrain and vegetation is distinctly different. If this were naturally formed, it would be too coincidental."
"It seems someone did this intentionally, could it be the Master Hei Mu?"
The remains of Master Hei Mu were on this island, and with his capabilities, he indeed could have achieved this. Moreover, according to the records in that journal, this person was truly one with unconstrained and imaginative thinking.
Thinking deeper, those fierce beasts on the island were probably also brought here by Master Hei Mu, no wonder they were all so rare.
Yuan Ming quickly shook his head and stepped forward.
No matter whether this place was the work of Master Hei Mu or someone else, it didn't concern him. He just wanted to capture a suitable spirit beast.
As he walked through the swamp, Yuan Ming found it difficult because of the muddiness. He took out the toad skin, cast the Fur Cloak Skill, and transformed into the shape of a toad.
In these recent days, he had thoroughly investigated the origin of this toad skin. It came from a water-dwelling fierce beast called the Black Pattern Poison Toad, which was more suited for movement in such a damp and muddy environment than the White Ape Transformation.
Since perfecting the first level of the Moonlight Technique, his resistance to the backlash of the Fur Cloak Skill had greatly increased. He no longer needed to be as cautious as before, and the evil aura triggered by the Black Toad Transformation was far less than that of the White Ape Skin.
After transforming into the Black Toad Form, Yuan Ming moved much more freely. The muddiness no longer stuck to his feet, and he could easily cross any puddle he encountered.
Quite satisfied, he quickened his pace.
At that moment, a number of green plants with large leaves appeared ahead, some with pink, basin-shaped flowers blooming amidst them, resembling lotuses, and a faint fragrance wafted over on the gentle breeze.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to take a closer look, his head suddenly felt dizzy, and his legs turned weak.
"The scent of the flowers is poisonous!"
His mind sharpened, and he immediately retreated.
A streak of green shot out from beneath the vibrant lotus leaves, snapping at his calf—it was a flat-headed green snake.
Yuan Ming struggled to leap backward, narrowly dodging the green snake's attack, his right hand forming a seal and pointing forward.
A faint green light emerged from the nearby flora, and several grass stems suddenly came to life, lunging at the green snake.
The green snake, taken by surprise, desperately dodged left and right. Grass stems surrounded it from all angles, leaving it with no escape, and it quickly became entangled.
The grass stems intertwined and knitted together. In the blink of an eye, they formed a grass cage, trapping the green snake within.
The green snake exhibited fluctuations of spiritual power, signifying its strength. These grass stems, at most as thick as a finger, should have snapped with a single struggle, but no matter how the green snake twisted its body, it couldn't break free. Instead, it was wound tighter and tighter, until it could no longer move at all.
Yuan Ming retreated a considerable distance, completely away from the pink lotus before stopping, and sat down cross-legged to run the Nine Elements Technique, trying to neutralize the poison.
After advancing to the sixth-tier Qi Refining, his mana had thickened again, now capable of permeating his organs. With the circulation of mana, the dizzy and weak sensations quickly faded, and he soon recovered.
Yuan Ming then stood up and looked at the immobilized green snake, his gaze flickering slightly.
This grass cage was actually the Wood Prison Technique, which he was using in actual combat for the first time.
Unlike the Wood Stabbing Technique, the Wood Prison Technique relied on nearby plants to capture the enemy. Therefore, the power of this spell depended to some extent on which plants were used to cast it.
The grass stems were fragile, yet the cage they formed could trap the green snake. If he were to use other more robust trees to cast the Wood Prison Technique, the binding power would surely be greater.
Yuan Ming gestured with his hand, and several wooden thorns emerged from around the pink lotus, shredding the flowers so that the fragrant air quickly dissipated completely.
He waited in place for a while, then approached, grasped the green snake's head, and chanted an incantation.
Waves of black air began to well up from his palm, becoming more and more abundant until they engulfed the green snake's head.
At the same time, faint silver patterns began to appear on Yuan Ming's forehead, rapidly spreading down his arm, reaching his hand quickly.
There was a soft "pop" sound, and the black air swirling above his palm morphed into several black tendrils that burrowed into the green snake's head.
The green snake suddenly showed a look of agony, struggling incessantly.
However, Yuan Ming's grip was like an iron hoop, firmly holding onto the green snake. The blackness in his hand grew denser, drilling even faster into the green snake's head.
The expression of pain on the green snake intensified, with a raspy cry emanating from its mouth.
As time ticked by, there was a soft bang from inside the green snake's head, as if something had burst. Its body became limp, lifeless.
Yuan Ming's expression stiffened as he released his grip.
"Beast Taming Technique is indeed difficult. I was as careful as I could be, yet I still destroyed this snake's Divine Soul," he sighed.
He had been practicing in secret these days, thinking he had mastered the Beast Taming Technique well, only to realize that in actuality, it was not the case.
The key to the Beast Taming Technique lay in overpowering the fierce beast's consciousness. However, the Divine Soul was inherently fragile, and the slightest mishap could result in its destruction.
"It seems I need more practice," Yuan Ming thought to himself as he continued on his way.
Half a day later, in a part of the swamp where the aquatic plants thrived.
Yuan Ming used the Wood Prison Technique to capture a gray fox fierce beast, roughly as tall as half a person, pressing his palm against the fox's head as streams of black air surged into it.
The Gray Fox cried out in pain, its body trembling incessantly.
Yuan Ming paid no mind, murmuring incantations, and continued casting.
This was already his fifth attempt at taming a Fierce Beast; the previous four attempts all resulted in failure, with the beasts' Divine Souls bursting and perishing.
Yet with each failure, Yuan Ming summarized his experience, becoming increasingly adept at using the Beast Taming Technique. He felt that success was getting closer and closer.
A quarter of an hour passed quickly, and although the Gray Fox was still struggling painfully, its Divine Soul had not burst.
The ferocity in its eyes weakened gradually, and after a while, it let out a low whimper, signaling its submission.
"Finally succeeded!" Yuan Ming's eyes lit up with joy, but suddenly he stopped casting, retracted his palm, and the Wood Prison that held the Gray Fox also dispersed.
The Gray Fox regained its freedom, paused in confusion before it realized what had happened, then turned and fled into the depths of the swamp, vanishing in the blink of an eye.
For character sheets and glossaries, visit *.
Yuan Ming watched the Gray Fox escape without taking any action.
According to the Bone Scroll given to him by the Three Cave Masters, controlling a spirit beast with the Beast Taming Technique involves the power of the Divine Soul. For a Qi Refining Stage Cultivator, whose Divine Soul is too weak, only one spirit beast can be subdued and controlled.
This Gray Fox was just a Level 1 Intermediate-stage Fierce Beast without any special abilities, so naturally, Yuan Ming would not choose it as his spirit beast.
He continued onward, searching for a Fierce Beast that met his criteria.
The area of this swamp was vast, far exceeding that of the Purple Maple Forest and Black Pine Forest he had encountered before. Although there were many Fierce Beasts living in the swamp, unfortunately, their strength was quite average, all at the Lower or Middle level, far from comparable to the Four-eyed Golden Ape, the Black Giant Crow, or the Earth Demon he had encountered before. None were worth taking as a spirit beast.
Even as the day turned into night, Yuan Ming had not found an appropriate candidate to tame.
He was not in a hurry nor did he leave the place. He took out a tent and set up camp in a relatively dry area to rest.
Because he was in a strange environment, Yuan Ming did not sleep that night, meditating instead; no accidents occurred.
The next day, Yuan Ming set off again.
The puddles in the swamp became fewer as he advanced, with dry areas increasing.
"I'm finally about to leave this region," Yuan Ming said with a relieved expression, quickening his pace slightly.
The swamp was full of mud and a pervasive stench; the conditions were quite harsh. Happy to be leaving this place, he continued on his way.
After walking for a while, Yuan Ming suddenly halted.
Before him, there spread a field of rich green lotus leaves with large pink flowers dotted in the middle— the same poisonous lotuses he had encountered before.
Unlike the few Bilian he had seen previously, the expanse of lotus flowers here was abnormally large, dominating the area ahead with no visible end. Thousands of pink flowers were standing tall, swaying in the wind.
Yuan Ming spotted those pink lotus flowers from a distance and stopped in his tracks.
So many lotus flowers together meant that the toxin concentration would undoubtedly be much higher than before; getting poisoned would be troublesome.
Yuan Ming decided to bypass the lotus grove, walking around its periphery.
Just at that moment, a hissing sound came from within the flowers, followed by a multitude of green snakes slithering out densely packed. It was the same kind of green snakes he had encountered before, and there were at least forty or fifty of them, all lunging towards Yuan Ming.
His expression changed slightly, but he did not take it too seriously, turning and swiftly retreating into the distance.
With such an open gap, the green snakes couldn't possibly catch up to him.
As expected, the green snakes gave up the chase after following him for a distance. They hissed at Yuan Ming for a while, then all slithered back into the thick of the flowers.
Yuan Ming's eyebrows twitched. The hissing of the green snakes carried a threatening tone, as if warning him not to approach.
"I was quite far from the lotus grove just now, theoretically not within the green snakes' attack range, yet they were so vigilant. Could there be something inside the flowers?" A hint of curiosity rose in his heart.
After considering for a moment, Yuan Ming shook his head and gave up the idea of investigating.
The flower grove was filled with toxic pollen, and there were those venomous green snakes. Lacking a means to deal with these dangers, it was better not to invite trouble.
Yuan Ming walked around the edge of the lotus grove, making his way forward.
Ga ga ga...
An ear-piercing cry came from behind, in the swamp. It sounded like the call of some bird, shrill and lingering, suggesting the coming creature was not small.
"A bird-type Fierce Beast!" Yuan Ming frowned, hastily hiding in a dense patch of grass nearby.
Within Ten Thousand Mountains, every noise must be treated cautiously, as a fearsome creature might suddenly appear. Moreover, since he had the incense burner, he could fly away at any time and wasn't concerned about the ordinary Land Beasts, but he was quite wary of bird-type Fierce Beasts.
No sooner had Yuan Ming concealed himself when a giant white figure flew out of the depths of the swamp, passing directly over his head.
Yuan Ming observed the true identity of the white figure: a giant eagle several zhang long, with eyes like copper bells, black claws, and snow-white feathers. Its massive size was no less than that of the previously encountered Black Giant Crow, clearly a formidable avian Fierce Beast.
The White Eagle glanced at the bush where Yuan Ming was hiding with its pale yellow eyes but ignored him, heading straight for the center of the lotus grove and vanished in an instant.
Yuan Ming stood up from the bushes, gazing into the sky.
"That White Eagle looks quite powerful, and it also has keen vision. It could spot me even through the mist. It seems to be a decent spirit beast, but its speed was too fast. Even using the incense burner, I couldn't possibly catch up to it, let alone subdue it."

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 98: Leveraging Momentum
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming shook his head and was about to continue moving forward when a sudden hissing of numerous snakes and a clutter of bird calls erupted from deep within the flowerbeds. It seemed that the White Eagle and the green snakes among the flowers had started fighting, causing the fog within the flowers to churn incessantly.
However, the place where the eagle and snake were fighting seemed deep within the flowerbeds, quite far from the outside, making it hard to see the specifics.
"That White Eagle seems to have headed straight for the flowerbeds; could it be aiming to snatch a few green snakes for a meal?" Yuan Ming squinted his eyes, circulated the Moonlight Technique, and his Divine Soul left his body, drifting towards the depths of the flowerbeds.
The Divine Soul, being a yin body, felt quite uncomfortable venturing out in daylight, but it was bearable since the distance was not too great.
Encountering a decent Fierce Beast was rare, and missing the opportunity always felt frustrating.
The poison of the pollen was harmful to the human body but had no effect on the soul body, so Yuan Ming's Divine Soul reached deeper into the flowerbeds without any trouble and stopped there.
This was the limit of how far his Divine Soul could leave his body, he could not proceed further, but fortunately, he could now see both the White Eagle and the green snakes.
He peered intently, and couldn't help but let out a soft gasp of surprise.
The White Eagle was circling low, swooping down now and then.
On the ground below, the green snakes gathered, forming a huddle of hundreds that opposed the eagle.
Amidst the group of snakes was an enormous green python, many times thicker than the other green snakes. Its body was covered with armor-like bright green Scale Armor, and it had a jade-green growth resembling a sole horn on its head; it appeared to be the Snake King.
This Snake King was coiled in a snake cake shape, lying across a not-so-small pit under it, which densely filled with dozens of Green Snake Eggs.
The target of the White Eagle seemed to be these eggs; each dive was aimed directly at the pit, while the Snake King and other green snakes desperately resisted.
The Scale Armor of the Snake King was tough and durable, its strength immense and its speed extraordinarily swift, blocking most of the attacks from the White Eagle. The remaining attacks were taken by other green snakes, and the outcome of who would prevail was not yet clear.
Seeing this scene, Yuan Ming suddenly came up with an idea, his Divine Soul swiftly left and quickly returned to his body.
He muttered to himself, green hues flickered on his skin, his aura began to recede, and soon he blended perfectly with the nearby bushes—to the extent that even someone standing beside wouldn't notice him.
As for his Mana aura, it was completely concealed, clearly the effect of the Wood Concealment Skill.
A yellow rabbit ran over from nearby, gnawing on a weed resembling lettuce in the bushes.
Yuan Ming raised an eyebrow and waved at the yellow rabbit, which, notorious for its vigilance, didn't notice at all.
"The effects of this Wood Concealment Skill are not bad," he nodded silently, held his breath, and walked toward the flowerbeds.
The yellow rabbit heard the noise and then became aware of Yuan Ming's presence, rapidly scampering away.
Yuan Ming paid it no mind and quickly reached the edge of the flowerbeds, stopping in his tracks.
As far as he knew, typical poisonous pollen entered the body through respiration, causing poisoning, but these pink lotuses didn't look like typical poisonous substances. Whether holding breath would isolate him needed to be tested.
After a few breaths passed, his body showed no abnormalities, his nerves relaxed, he quickly held his breath and entered the flowerbed.
The venomous snakes inside the flowerbed seemed to have all been lured away by the White Eagle; Yuan Ming didn't encounter a single one and quickly reached the spot where his Divine Soul had stood, looking towards the ongoing battle.
The White Eagle dove down again, still blocked by the Snake King and the other green snakes.
The White Eagle let out a sharp screech, apparently infuriated, its broad wings suddenly vibrating intensely, causing a storm around it, bending down many pink lotuses, cracking and tearing leaves in the process.
Fierce winds whisked away many green snakes, and the Snake King was also blown swaying from side to side, moving slightly away from the pit.
The White Eagle's talons turned into two dark shadows, aiming straight for the snake eggs within the pit.
The Snake King, furious, snapped its vast jaws directly at the White Eagle's talons while also fiercely whipping its tail at the White Eagle's body.
With a loud "bang", the White Eagle's substantial body was struck by the snake's tail, feathers breaking and floating down—clearly a deep dent was visible at the hit spot, seriously injured.
But the White Eagle's talons had broken past the Snake King's defense and successfully grabbed two snake eggs, flapping its wings to fly high.
Yuan Ming had been waiting for that moment, his right hand formed a spell and pointed out.
Suddenly, several lotus stems in the nearby flowerbeds rose from the ground, elongating like ropes in the wind, and wrapped around the White Eagle's body, halting its ascendancy.
The green Snake King, initially fuming with shock and anger, watching this scene, immediately let out a hissing sound, its body shot upwards, taking advantage of the unsteady state of the White Eagle to quickly coil around its body, even securely binding one of its wings.
Taken by surprise, the White Eagle plummeted to the ground.
The Snake King opened its vast jaws and clamped down on the White Eagle's neck, the other green snakes also pounced.
The White Eagle struggled furiously in anger, but since its wing was restrained by the Snake King, relying solely on its talons and sharp beak, it couldn't stop the multitude of green snakes, soon swallowed by the mass of snakes.
Yuan Ming's expression subtly changed upon witnessing this scene.
He had interfered with the White Eagle to let the group of snakes injure it, intending to take the opportunity to tame it, but he hadn't expected the Snake King to react so swiftly and trap the White Eagle almost instantly.
If the eagle were to die here, all his calculations would be thwarted.
Yuan Ming activated a spell, this time casting the Wood Stabbing Technique.
The ground near the pit "crashed," and five sharp wooden thorns emerged, piercing into the cluster of snakes, brutally skewering over a dozen green snakes, and two thorns even stabbed into the body of the Snake King.
The Snake King had not anticipated an attack at this time and screamed in agony, its body wrapped around the White Eagle loosening.
The nearby lotus stems extended again, this time aiming for the Snake King, wrapping around its body.
The White Eagle narrowly escaped death and immediately displayed the previously used Wind-Blowing Divine Power, flapping its wings rapidly, casting shadows in its wake.
A gust of wind suddenly erupted, blasting all the surrounding green snakes away, and the Snake King was also flung several feet away.
Seizing the opportunity, the White Eagle flapped its wings and took off, somewhat unsteadily ascending into the sky, heading deep into the swamp.
The Snake King roared at the White Eagle a few times but did not pursue futilely, with the White Eagle disappearing into the mist shortly after.
To report errors, please visit the original post on *.
Not far away, Yuan Ming also disappeared from the flowers.
The White Eagle barely flapped its wings, heading toward its old nest deep in the swamp.
It regularly preyed on various poisonous snakes in the swamp, especially the green-banded snakes among the pink lotuses, and had developed some resistance to snake venom, but this time it fell into a swarm of snakes, bitten by who knows how many green-banded snakes, especially the venom from the Snake King, which was fierce. At this moment, the White Eagle's body was limp, and its flying speed was not even half of what it once was.
The White Eagle was quite powerful, and its spiritual intelligence was nearly comparable to a human's. A hint of anthropomorphic hatred flashed in its eyes; it had almost died in that group of green-banded snakes. Once it recovered from its injuries, it would surely seek revenge.
However, the recent strangeness of the lotus stems was quite peculiar, as far as it knew, the green-banded snakes did not possess the ability to manipulate flora.
The White Eagle suddenly remembered that right before entering the flowers, that cultivator hiding in the bushes, could it have been his doing?
At that moment, a green shadow flashed through the mist nearby, and a green long sword shot out, aiming straight for the White Eagle's chest.
Taken by surprise, the White Eagle quickly dodged to the side, narrowly avoiding the long sword's blade.
The sword, which should have missed, suddenly turned its direction as if driven by an invisible hand, and with a "puff," it stabbed into one of the White Eagle's wings, penetrating through.
The White Eagle, already struggling to fly, now with a wing severely damaged, immediately plunged downward.
Yuan Ming, holding an incense burner in one hand, emerged following the green long sword, pursuing relentlessly.
Upon seeing Yuan Ming, the White Eagle was momentarily stunned and then furiously understood that the earlier anomalies were all his doing.
Its uninjured wing suddenly unfolded, a burst of blue light emitting from its surface.
Shoo, shoo, shoo!
Dozens of feathers shot out, emitting a piercing screech, heading towards Yuan Ming.
These feathers were not shot randomly; each had a specific target, and although there were only a few, they sealed off all of Yuan Ming's possible escape routes.
Yuan Ming's expression darkened, his Divine Soul Power sensing the direction of the feathers, he immediately interrupted the Exorcism Technique.
The green light on the incense burner suddenly vanished, and he fell downwards along with the incense burner.
The White Eagle had predicted all possible directions Yuan Ming could dodge, but it had not expected him to suddenly plummet, causing all feathers to miss.
Yuan Ming once again displayed the Exorcism Technique, the green light rekindling on the incense burner, stabilizing his body.
The White Eagle, both shocked and angry, was about to strike again when a green shadow shot out from the other side—it was the Green Fish Sword. With a "puff," it pierced through the wing that was still intact.
The White Eagle, now with both wings damaged, could no longer stabilize its form and fell downwards, crash-landing into a puddle, splashing water everywhere.
A bush near the puddle flashed green, as numerous branches swiftly extended, wrapping around the body of the White Eagle, instantly forming a cage of branches.
The White Eagle, both shocked and furious, struggled desperately to break free.
Its strength far exceeded that of the previous green snakes and the Gray Fox. The cage of branches shook violently; however, these branches were much sturdier than the previous grass cages. Although the cage swayed left and right, there were no signs of damage.
Yuan Ming floated down from midair, landing in front of the White Eagle, he placed one hand on the eagle's head, starting to cast the Beast Taming Technique.
Streams of black energy flowed from the palm of his hand, like a starving wolf seeing delicious prey, flowing completely into the head of the White Eagle.
The White Eagle's body shuddered violently, emitting a painful cry as its body twitched and struggled again.
However, given its current state, such struggles were pointless; it had no chance of breaking free from the cage of branches.
Yuan Ming concentrated on casting the Beast Taming Technique, and soon a quarter of an hour had passed.
The White Eagle showed no signs of submission, its will to resist seeming even stronger than before.
Yuan Ming was not surprised; considering the eagle's combat performance against the snakes, its strength definitely reached the Level 1 Upper Stage, not so easily subdued.
However, he was not overly worried. His Mana had achieved the Sixth Level of Qi Refinement, and after mastering the first level of the Moonlight Technique, his Divine Soul Power had far surpassed those of the same realm. As long as there were no external disturbances, he could continue to cast the Beast Taming Technique for up to two hours if necessary.
Such prolonged casting had exceeded the capabilities of a typical Qi Refining Stage Cultivator, and Yuan Ming did not believe there was any Level 1 Fierce Beast that could withstand it.
The only concern was the intensity of the casting, which must be carefully controlled to avoid accidentally destroying the White Eagle's Divine Soul, which would render all his efforts wasted.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 99 Demon Vine
chapters.content:
Billows of black air surged out of Yuan Ming's palm, seemingly endless, continuously pouring into the brain of the White Eagle.
As time passed, the consciousness of the White Eagle indeed began to gradually disintegrate, its resistance growing weaker and weaker.
A slight smile curved Yuan Ming's lips as he continued to operate his Beast Taming Technique, determined to subdue the White Eagle in one go.
Given the current circumstances, this time, there was a very good chance of success.
Just at that moment, a sudden change occurred!
The ground beneath Yuan Ming's feet unexpectedly split open, and a purple-black vine shot out, swiftly entwining his legs.
This vine was only as thick as a finger, with a smooth surface and delicate leaves adorned with purple spots, making it quite beautiful to look at.
However, this slender and beautiful vine contained an astonishing amount of strength; his legs were instantly tightened, rendered completely immobile as if bound by iron chains.
Though taken by surprise, Yuan Ming did not panic, and he even did not give up on subduing the White Eagle, gesturing towards the nearby Green Fish Sword.
The Green Fish Sword leaped up, transforming into a fan-shaped cyan shadow that chopped down on the purple-black vine.
A soft "bang" sounded as the vine was slashed, creating only a shallow cut that was less than a third of the depth of the vine itself.
A flicker of shock finally crossed Yuan Ming's face.
Although the Green Fish Sword was only a half-magical artifact, its power had increased significantly as his cultivation advanced, easily able to slice through tree trunks as thick as water buckets — to think it couldn't subdue a slender vine?
The purple-black demon vine twisted like a snake, quickly burrowing out from the ground and wrapping towards Yuan Ming's upper body.
Yuan Ming hurriedly drove the Green Fish Sword again, aiming for the slit in the demon vine.
However, as if the demon vine were sentient, it rapidly twisted and dodged.
With a "bang", the Green Fish Sword struck the vine, but it hit a different part and the previously split section emitted faint purple-black light, healing at a speed visible to the naked eye.
Yuan Ming's pupils constricted, and he quickly gave up on subduing the White Eagle, retracting all his Mana.
Without his Mana to sustain it, the tree prison confining the White Eagle also disintegrated; the eagle barely escaped with its life and immediately struggled to flit away without looking back.
Yuan Ming couldn't afford to pay attention to the White Eagle. He gathered all his Mana into the Green Fish Sword, which glowed with a misty cyan light, and fiercely chopped at the base of the demon vine that clung to the ground.
With a soft "puff," the vine was largely severed, spewing out purple fluid from the cut.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming was delighted and immediately drove the Green Fish Sword again, intending to completely sever the vine.
Just at that instant, the ground split open once more; a slightly thinner purple vine shot out, swiftly coiling around the Green Fish Sword and wrapping several loops around it.
Yuan Ming hadn't expected this twist, quickly trying to control the Green Fish Sword to break free.
However, the Green Fish Sword, being only a semi-magical artifact and essentially no different from ordinary swords, needed to accelerate over some distance to exert its edge's power and was thus unable to significantly damage anything wrapped tightly around it. No matter how the Green Fish Sword thrashed, it couldn't shake off the entangling vine.
More and more vines emerged from the ground and bound Yuan Ming's body.
His upper body was quickly covered by the demon vines, making it impossible to move his arms, and his face under the frog skin turned red from the pressure.
The strength of these demon vines was truly astonishing, squeezing him so tightly that his bones made a "cracking" sound and he could barely breathe.
A chilling sense of fear surged in Yuan Ming's heart. He knew that the Black Toad Transformation was utterly ineffective against these demon vines.
Now, with his body completely entwined in purple-black demon vines, it was already impossible for him to switch to the White Ape Transformation.
"Right! Since this vine is a plant, it should also be vulnerable to the Toad Poison Arrow," Yuan Ming suddenly remembered, channeling his Mana into the poison sack on his back.
Streams of Black Toad Poison Liquid shot out, striking the purple-black demon vine.
A sizzling sound of corrosion rose as the touched vines rapidly withered and shriveled.
The purple-black demon vines twisted violently, even emitting a rustling sound, as if a living creature were crying out in pain.
The vines binding Yuan Ming loosened significantly, and he could breathe smoothly once more.
Relieved, he continued to spray the poison on the demon vines, attempting to break free.
At that moment, Yuan Ming felt a sharp pain in his calf, as though someone had stabbed him with a knife.
He quickly looked down, his face changing color.
He saw that, unbeknownst to him, the tip of a purple vine had easily reached his calf and sharpened, piercing through the Black Toad Skin and burrowing into his flesh.
With the situation critical, Yuan Ming didn't have time to think; he leaned over and grabbed the tip of the demon vine, pulling it out.
However, the Black Toad Transformation hadn't enhanced his arm strength, and he simply couldn't pull out the vine. Moreover, the portion of the vine inside his calf continued burrowing deeper into his body, causing the nearby muscles and skin to quickly swell up.
"What in the world is this thing!" Yuan Ming cursed aloud, continuing to pull fiercely on the vine.
At the same time, a stream of black air emerged from his right hand, surging into the interior of the demon vine; it was the Beast Taming Technique.
Though the vine appeared plant-like, Yuan Ming had to treat it as a Fierce Beast like the White Eagle due to its series of baffling actions, adopting a desperate measure.
Indeed, once the black air of the Beast Taming Technique entered the demon vine, its movements immediately stiffened.
Encouraged, Yuan Ming powered up the Beast Taming Technique to its fullest, continuing to disrupt the demon vine.
The poisonous sack on his back never stopped discharging poison liquid, drenching the bizarre vines on his body with black poison liquid, causing large patches of the purple vines to begin wilting.
Under such a dual attack, the amplitude of the purple-black demon vine's attacks became increasingly smaller.
Where the demon vine connected to the ground, there was a "whoosh" sound as a thick root covered with black tendrils emerged from the ground, still caked with much soil.
Through the roots and soil, one could see that the base of the demon vine had several wrinkle-like slits forming a wriggling, ugly face.
"Demon Vine!" Yuan Ming couldn't help but widen his eyes.
He had read in the classics of the Gui Cang Pavilion in Biluo Cave that the fierce beasts of the Ten Thousand Mountains were not always animals like tigers, leopards, wolves, and bears; some trees and plants, if circumstances allowed, could awaken their spiritual intelligence and absorb nature's spiritual energy to transform into fierce beasts.
The vine root swung upward with a whoosh, emitting a dull whooshing sound and, with a bang, struck the back of Yuan Ming, who couldn't avoid it.
Yuan Ming felt as if he had been struck by a heavy hammer, toppling to the ground as he spat out a mouthful of fresh blood, and his Beast Taming Technique was disrupted.
Without the suppression of the Beast Taming Technique, the stiff and immobile purple-black demon vine immediately regained its ability to move, wrapping Yuan Ming up tightly once again.
Dozens of black roots on the vine root suddenly grew longer in the wind, swift as arrows leaving a bowstring, all piercing into Yuan Ming's back.
All the poisonous sacks on the frog's back were pierced by the roots, and the swollen poisonous sacks, like deflated rubber balls, shriveled up, and the spraying of poison liquid also immediately ceased.
Not only that, but the black roots also exuded a strange suction force, causing the blood inside Yuan Ming's body to boil and surge toward the black roots.
Yuan Ming felt his strength draining along with his Qi-Blood, hastily flipped over, gathered his dissipating Mana, and resumed casting the Beast Taming Technique.
This time, he called upon all of his Mana and Soul Power without reservation, frantically driving the Beast Taming Technique.
With a boom, a surge of black mist, several times more intense than before, burst from Yuan Ming's hands, rolling into the body of the purple-black demon vine.
All movement of the purple-black demon vine froze once again; however, the bloodthirsty black roots didn't stop. The originally black roots turned blood red, and other areas of the demon vine also began showing hints of blood color.
The previously poison-damaged vine body began to heal rapidly.
Yuan Ming's expression was grim, but he didn't distract himself by casting spells to stop the vine roots from drawing blood, as all his Mana was still used to cast the Beast Taming Technique, like a tidal wave crashing into the consciousness of the purple-black demon vine.
His Mana and Soul Power were nearly exhausted, and if he spread his energies further, it would be even harder to make an impact.
The only strategy left was a desperate one, using the Beast Taming Technique to destroy the consciousness of the demon vine, which might give him a slim chance of survival.
The man and the vine were thus locked in a standstill.
Time slowly passed.TheM|V|LE&MPYRteamworkedhardonthischapter.
Yuan Ming's face was pale, his body swaying as though he would collapse at any moment, appearing in dire straits.
His mana and soul power had both hit rock bottom, most importantly, his blood had been drained by the demon vine by almost half, causing waves of dizziness in his mind. If his body hadn't always been robust, he would have already fainted.
The state of the purple-black demon vine wasn't much better either, having endured the impact of the Beast Taming Technique for so long. The will of the demon vine was on the verge of collapse, and most of the vines wrapping around Yuan Ming had fallen off.
"This is bad! Although the consciousness of this demon vine has greatly weakened, it can still hold on for a while, and my condition is terrible, with both mana and soul power nearly exhausted—I could collapse at any moment!" Yuan Ming thought anxiously, glancing at his right arm.
Biting his teeth slightly, he divided a strand of mana and soul power, injecting them into the incense burner mark on his right arm.
Based on past experience, whenever his Divine Soul Power was greatly depleted or attacked, the incense burner would emit a warm flow similar to soul power, aiding him significantly.
At this moment, Yuan Ming's soul power was immensely depleted, and the incense burner still remained silent. Out of desperation, he risked triggering it.
The mark emitted faint green light, and the green incense burner flashed out, flying autonomously to hover above Yuan Ming's head, stopping at the Bai Hui acupoint on his head.
Yuan Ming, upon seeing this, was stunned.
Other than that time when it carried his Divine Soul Possession into the body of the young Emperor, the green incense burner had always obediently followed his commands upon being summoned, and such a scenario had never occurred before.
Before he could think further, a thick stream of warm flow burst out from the incense burner, passed through the Bai Hui acupoint, and entered the Sea of Consciousness.
Yuan Ming's exhausted spirit immediately revitalized, and he hurriedly circulated the Moonlight Technique to absorb the warm flow. The nearly dried-up Divine Soul Power in his Sea of Consciousness began to recover.
However, the warm flow from the incense burner was too vast this time, and the Moonlight Technique couldn't absorb it fast enough, with nearly half of the warm flow being directly injected into the Beast Taming Technique.
The black mist produced by the Beast Taming Technique suddenly exploded in intensity, resembling a black furious dragon charging into the body of the purple-black demon vine.
The purple-black demon vine trembled violently, its resistance will retreating progressively.
Perhaps sensing that Yuan Ming couldn't absorb it, the warm flow from the incense burner suddenly split in two. The majority continued to enter Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness, while a minor part was introduced into the Black Toad's skin.
An eerie black light surfaced on the Black Toad's skin, with the toad phantom reappearing, looking much clearer than before, with many green spots on the surface, exactly matching the color of the incense burner.
The toad phantom opened its mouth and spewed a black light, merging into the heavily scarred toad's back.
The poison sacs, perforated by the roots of the demon vine, slowly began to move, secreting streams of black poison liquid once again, enveloping the roots of the purple-black demon vine.
This Black Toad poison liquid had also undergone some changes, the color was much lighter, and it distinctly also mixed with specks of green, exactly like the toad phantom.
Although the color of the poison liquid had lightened, its potency had significantly increased. As soon as it touched the roots of the demon vine, they immediately began to rapidly dissolve. The entire root base of the demon vine was slowly sinking, appearing to be corroded and engulfed by the Black Toad poison liquid.
Facing attacks from both sides, the will of the purple-black demon vine collapsed even faster.
Just as Yuan Ming gritted his teeth, preparing to continue driving the Beast Taming Technique for one final fierce attack, the green incense burner suddenly trembled, its surface green light also flashing.
Yuan Ming's mind boomed as if a thunderclap had exploded, his vision instantly turned pitch black, and he fainted.

chapters.title: Chapter 120 - 100 Vine and Toad
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming gradually regained consciousness after an indeterminate amount of time, slowly sitting up from the ground.
Surrounding fog swirled and drifted, obscuring his view of the sun and making it impossible for him to judge how long he had been unconscious.
His mind was still a bit muddled, and only after shaking his head did he recall the events that led to his fainting, hastily scanning his surroundings.
Although the will of the Purple-Black Demon Vine had been crushed by his Beast Taming Technique, considering the tenacity of such a creature, it might not be dead.
All was quiet around him, not a single insect was to be found, let alone the demon vine.
The Green Fish Sword was slanted into the ground beside him, the blade emitting a faint glow.
"Not seeing the corpse of the demon vine means it probably isn't dead. Could it have escaped by tunneling underground?" Yuan Ming muttered to himself.
If he had fallen into a coma and the demon vine was still alive, why hadn't it seized the opportunity to kill him? Perhaps it had been frightened by the Beast Taming Technique?
He slapped his cheeks forcefully and stood up.
"Eh!" Yuan Ming suddenly noticed something strange; he had somehow deactivated the Fur Cloak Skill and the Black Toad Beast Skin was nowhere to be seen.
"It's one thing for the Purple-Black Demon Vine to be missing, as it could have escaped on its own, but why would the Black Toad Beast Skin also disappear? Could someone have come by?" Yuan Ming considered the possibility and quickly checked his belongings.
Everything inside the Storage Bag was intact, nothing was missing, and the Mysterious Incense Burner had turned into a mark, quietly residing inside his arm with no abnormalities. Even the conspicuous Green Fish Sword wasn't lost; it didn't look like anyone had been there.
Yuan Ming silently picked up the Green Fish Sword, about to comb the area, when his expression shifted, looking off in a direction.
Something over there seemed to be connected to his heart and mind, albeit very faintly and indiscernible.
"What is that?" Yuan Ming was quite surprised.
The presence of a heart-mind connection signified a deep secret technique, similar to the Beast Taming Technique, or a blood-sworn Magic Artifact.
His Beast Taming Technique had yet to subdue a spirit beast, and the only item he had acknowledged with his blood was the Mysterious Incense Burner, which was perfectly situated within the Incense Burner Mark of his right arm. What else could be forming a connection with his heart and mind?
Unable to grasp the issue, Yuan Ming quickly stopped overthinking and started searching nearby for the Black Toad Skin but found nothing.
"Forget it, the Black Toad Skin was merely an auxiliary tool. If it's gone, it's gone," he sighed, sat down cross-legged, and began running the Nine Elements Technique to recover his mana.
A short while later, Yuan Ming's mana was fully restored, his strength returning to him.
However, the Purple-Black Demon Vine had drained nearly half of his Qi-blood, making his muscles feel weak. Fortunately, it did not hinder his movements.
Yuan Ming took out the White Ape Skin, but instead of casting the Fur Cloak Skill, he wrapped it around his waist and dashed off toward the distance.
The disturbance there continued to pull at his heart and mind; it was better to clarify it.
After a quarter of an hour, Yuan Ming arrived next to a swamp that was several acres in size, where the object connecting with his heart and mind lay submerged in the water.
As he got closer, his heart-mind resonance with the object in the puddle strengthened significantly, and he could finally sense what it was.
"No way!" Yuan Ming found it hard to believe; the situation was too bizarre.
Just at that moment, the puddle suddenly exploded, water churning violently, and a grey fierce creature emerged from the depths—a grey crocodile several zhang in length.
This crocodile had a dark red head, especially its blood-red eyes, which looked extraordinarily vicious.
"Not good, it's an adult Blood Head Crocodile!" Yuan Ming recognized the creature.
An adult Blood Head Crocodile's strength was at least at the peak of Level 1 Middle Stage, with exceptionally tough scale armor, immense strength, and a proficiency in water combat, making it one of the most formidable mid-level fierce beasts.
However, this particular Blood Head Crocodile was visibly panicked, rapidly twisting its body and fleeing in a desperate hurry.
Before it got far, a slender purple-black object broke through the water, wrapping around the crocodile's body in rapid coils—it was a purple-black vine.
The vine, devoid of leaves and translucent throughout, showed thin bloodlines within its eerie form.
Yuan Ming's pupils contracted sharply.
Despite its changed appearance, he could tell that this purple-black vine was none other than the very same Purple-Black Demon Vine that had almost claimed his life earlier!
The Blood Head Crocodile struggled fiercely, but the demon vine was extremely resilient, unaffected by the crocodile's attempts to break free.
One end of the demon vine started to hiss, sharpening before suddenly shooting out and striking the back of the Blood Head Crocodile.
With a soft "puff," the vine easily penetrated the crocodile's tough skin and buried itself inside its body.
The Blood Head Crocodile let out a mournful scream, its thick body shaking violently, the intensity of its tremors diminishing until it ceased entirely.
A few breaths later, the creature stopped breathing, and its bloated corpse floated to the surface.
With a "splash" from the water, a black shadow slowly emerged—an ebony toad the size of a fist, its back adorned with a round, swollen purple-black sac resembling the folded leaves of some plant, surrounded by a dozen or so poisonous sacs. Its cold, dark eyes fixed on the Blood Head Crocodile.
Yuan Ming's face strained to maintain calm, but the shock and doubt in his eyes were indiscernible no matter how hard he tried.
This black toad, in both skin color and shape, was identical to his Toad Beast Skin, only much smaller in size.
A piece of Beast Skin had come to life out of thin air—what a miraculous event this world had borne witness to!
The purple-black Demon Vine shot out from a bulge on the toad's back; a stream of blood-red light flowed swiftly back along the vine into the toad's back. A faint glow of blood light appeared on the toad's body, which quickly dissipated, but its form seemed to grow imperceptibly larger.
The purple-black Demon Vine flew back and disappeared into the bulge on the toad's back.
The toad seemed to sense something and turned its head towards Yuan Ming nearby, a hint of alarm in its eyes, and then it turned to flee.
"Come here!" Yuan Ming's expression darkened slightly as he coldly commanded, his right hand forming a spell, with black light flashing at his fingertips.
The Black Toad trembled but did not move.
Yuan Ming's face showed a look of surprise. Only when he exerted the Beast Taming Technique to its maximum did the Black Toad reluctantly swim over and hop in front of him.
He raised his hand to the Black Toad's head, and dense black Qi gushed from his palm, rolling into the creature.
A moment later, he withdrew his hand, his face showing a complex expression of surprise, joy, and mostly confusion.
Yuan Ming had just now used the Beast Taming Technique, combined with Divine Soul Power, to check. For some reason, the original Black Toad Beast Skin had indeed grown internal organs and shown signs of a Divine Soul, turning into a living being.
The Purple-Black Demon Vine had fused with the toad's internal organs through the bulge on its back, becoming an organ within it. With each beat of the heart, the toad's blood not only circulated through its veins but also through the Demon Vine to the rest of the body.
This Black Toad appeared to be a Black Pattern Poison Toad, but it was actually two entirely different creatures that had merged into a strange hybrid.
And within the Demon Vine was a rune imprinted, the Beast Taming Rune, which contained Yuan Ming's Divine Soul Power, and it seemed to be a condensation of his Divine Soul.
Yuan Ming had just now felt a faint connection with this Beast Taming Rune and found it unbelievable, but the reality was right before his eyes, leaving no room for doubt.
Regardless, it seemed he had unwittingly tamed a spirit beast.
Given his current level in the Qi Refinement Realm, he could not tame a second spirit beast unless he killed the Demon Vine and destroyed the Beast Taming Rune within it.
"Fine, a Demon Vine it is then. This vine's capabilities are quite decent, and now it has fused with this Black Toad, who knows what special Divine Skills it might develop?" After much consideration, he decided to keep the vine.
Yuan Ming sat down cross-legged in front of the Black Toad, continuing to communicate with it using the Beast Taming Technique, probing its internal condition.
More importantly, he needed to understand the Black Toad's current Divine Skills.Love this story? Show support at *.
After half a day, he stopped casting, a glimmer of joy in his eyes.
As he had speculated earlier, the fusion of the Black Toad with the Demon Vine greatly altered their Divine Skills. The most notable change was the blending of their powers, with the Demon Vine now containing the Black Toad's poison, significantly enhancing its ability to attack enemies in battle.
The reason the Purple-Black Demon Vine could easily pierce through the Blood Head Crocodile's skin was precisely because of this.
Furthermore, the Black Toad had also acquired a powerful self-healing ability akin to that of the Demon Vine. Combined with the Demon Vine's blood-draining trait, its self-healing capability had reached a monstrous level, allowing it to recover quickly from any non-fatal injuries.
"Stick with me from now on!" Yuan Ming exhaled gently. This Black Toad had become a monster-like existence, and having it as a spirit beast might not be such a bad thing after all.
The Black Toad glanced at Yuan Ming but made no move.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming slightly increased his Mana to drive the Beast Taming Technique, making the Black Toad reluctantly croak and leap onto his shoulder, where it crouched.
"This Black Toad is a product of mutation. The Beast Taming Rune that I've imprinted into the Demon Vine, I'm unsure how effective it is in restraining this creature... But this little thing is so dark it can hide well without easily being discovered," he thought.
Yuan Ming quickly moved on, having settled the matter of taming a spirit beast. With the Black Toad by his side, his strength had increased significantly, and he planned to continue exploring the island.
Most importantly, he wanted to find the Four-eyed Golden Ape.
The effects of those Red Core Spiritual Peaches were unforgettable to Yuan Ming. If he could find them, and with the miraculous effects of the Nine Elements Technique, it was entirely possible for him to advance his cultivation to the eighth or even the ninth level of Qi Refinement in a short period.
...
Two days later.
Yuan Ming arrived at a region of low hills on the island, where the hills were gray-black, oozing dense Yin Qi from within the rocks, filling the air with a chilly sensation that was quite uncomfortable.
The vegetation inside the low hills was sparse, clearly unable to withstand the oppressively Yin Qi of the land.
Yuan Ming, accompanied by the Black Toad, entered and began searching the area.
Over the last two days, he had searched various parts of the island. Although he hadn't found the location of the Four-eyed Golden Ape, he had made no small gains, discovering seven or eight precious spiritual materials, which could be exchanged for a considerable number of Contribution Values at the sect.
However, the island was alarmingly large. After three days of searching, he still hadn't found the same spot he had landed on last time.
This made him somewhat anxious. He had only five days authorized for his leave from the sect, and now there wasn't much time left. If he didn't find it soon, he'd have to wait for the next opportunity.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 - 101: Assisting in Battle
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming rounded a bend past a rock formation and stopped in his tracks.
Before him stood a withered old tree next to a cliff wall. Its bark had long since fallen off, exposing a shriveled trunk riddled with large holes and signs of decay. It looked as if it had been dead for many years.
Yuan Ming paid no attention to the rest of the tree, his gaze fixed on a black Lingzhi mushroom growing at the base of the tree, right against the ground. It was as large as a palm and edged with a band of silver patterns, clearly not an ordinary item.
"It really is Yin Yuanzhi!" he crouched down and murmured joyously after taking a closer look.
According to the "Herborist," it was a rare type of yin attribute spiritual material. While it couldn't be consumed directly like meat Ganoderma or Red Core Spirit Peach, it could be used to refine yin attribute elixirs.
Yuan Ming had seen someone in the Execution Hall offer five contribution points for this Yin Yuanzhi. He wondered if that task had been completed yet.
He carefully harvested the item and placed it into a jade box, then tucked it away.
This Yin Yuanzhi was the most valuable spiritual material he had found so far. Finding a few more of these would make his trip worthwhile even if he didn't find the Red Core Spirit Peach.
Yuan Ming got up and continued on his way. He hadn't gone far when his eyes suddenly sharpened looking toward the cliff ahead.
In the shadow of the cliff, a black spirit grass stood about two feet tall. Its leaves were oval-shaped and emitted a faint black spirit light.
Yuan Ming looked towards the top of the spirit grass, where a black spirit fruit was growing.
The fruit was the size of a pigeon's egg, its surface marked with fine and densely packed patterns that at a glance appeared to be many scales. A faint fragrance wafted through the air.
"Hey, isn't this the Black Scale Fruit that Silver Cat asked me to find?" Yuan Ming rejoiced internally.
The Second Cave Master's herbarium included drawings of the Black Scale Fruit, identical to the one before his eyes, both in appearance and description. The age was also sufficient; his luck was indeed good.
He briskly walked over, intending to pick the fruit.
"Quack quack!" The nearby Black Toad suddenly emitted a series of frantic croaks.
Yuan Ming immediately halted, then his expression shifted slightly as he rapidly retreated backward using the Shadowless Step.
A dark shadow descended from above, slamming into where Yuan Ming had just been standing, smashing the ground into a large pit, and sending fragments of rock flying in all directions.
Yuan Ming continued to retreat, dodging the flying rocks now coming straight at him, only then catching a clear view of the dark shadow.
It was a fierce beast resembling a lion, its head and neck covered with gray-white fur, while heavy scale armor covered its spine and underbelly. It stood in front of the Black Scale Fruit and growled at Yuan Ming as if it were guarding the fruit.
"This beast looks like the Lion Scale Beast from the Ten Thousand Mountains, but those have red fur and scales, and this one is gray-white…" Yuan Ming thought to himself while withdrawing the White Ape Skin and casting the Fur Cloak Skill to transform into the form of a White Ape.
Upon seeing Yuan Ming not backing away but instead transforming into a White Ape, the Lion Scale Beast, interpreting it as a challenge, roared and lunged at him.
Yuan Ming didn't counterattack but continued to retreat to the side using the Shadowless Step, casting the Wood Stabbing Technique behind him.
The ground in front of the Lion Scale Beast cracked, and five thick wooden thorns burst out, aiming for its neck.
The Lion Scale Beast halted briefly, sweeping a front paw and snapping the wooden thorns as easily as pulling up weeds.
Yuan Ming wasn't surprised by this. The Lion Scale Beasts of Ten Thousand Mountains were first-level upper-stage fierce beasts. Although this one differed in color, it matched perfectly in aura, size, and strength—it was likely another upper-stage fierce beast, naturally not something that could be easily harmed by the Wood Stabbing Technique.
He flipped his hand and drew out the Green Fish Sword; his right arm suddenly grew significantly bulkier, its veins bulging—a display of his "Energy Storage Arm" Divine Skill.
"Go!" Yuan Ming shouted, swinging his arm with all his might. The Green Fish Sword turned into a green streak hurtling towards the chest of the Lion Scale Beast.
The Lion Scale Beast opened its mouth, and a grey Fireball the size of a human head shot out, matching the speed of the Green Fish Sword and colliding head-on with it.
With a loud "bang," the gray Fireball exploded, causing a visible wave of air that blew the Green Fish Sword back.
Foreseeing this, Yuan Ming flicked his hand, stopping the outwardly flying Green Fish Sword midair. It circled around and resumed its slash towards the Lion Scale Beast.
The Lion Scale Beast's hooves shone with gray-white light, its speed surged, easily dodging the attack of the Green Fish Sword and continuing its charge at Yuan Ming.
At that moment, the ground beneath it cracked again, and a Purple-Black Demon Vine shot out, wrapping around the beast's two front limbs and chest.Alwa$ys r@ead@ at the sou-rce#—*.*
From behind a large rock some yards away, the Black Toad lay quietly in the shadows, from which the Purple-Black Demon Vine had shot, disappearing into the ground.
The Lion Scale Beast, startled, thrashed its robust limbs against the ground, attempting to break free from the vine by brute force. However, the length of the vine took it by surprise, rapidly shooting out of the ground.
As the Lion Scale Beast leapt about twenty to thirty feet away, the Purple-Black Demon Vine still hadn't tensed.
The increasingly elongating vine twisted and also firmly wrapped around the hind limbs of the Lion Scale Beast.
Sssss...
The vine secreted a black Poison Liquid, infiltrating the body of the Lion Scale Beast. Its flesh dissolved on contact, and in many places, bleach-white bones were exposed. The blood that flowed out was a dark red, and the scales were corroded unevenly.
Mixed with shock and anger, the Lion Scale Beast spewed a gray Fireball from its mouth, hitting the vine wrapped around its body regardless of the injury it caused itself.
With a loud blast, a large section of the vine was torn apart, and the Lion Scale Beast freed most of its body, nearly escaping completely.
The vines around the Lion Scale Beast suddenly glowed green, swiftly weaving and threading through each other. In the blink of an eye, they formed a Purple Vine Cage, securely trapping the Lion Scale Beast, preventing any movement at all.
It was the "Wood Prison Technique."
After Yuan Ming completed casting, he dashed forward, his hand flickering with a red light, revealing a dark red hammer that he had obtained from this island.
He activated his mana and infused it into the hammer, making it shine with a dazzling red light, like a cluster of crimson flames.
The Lion Scale Beast sensed the astonishing aura emitted from the dark red hammer and, both terrified and alarmed, opened its gaping mouth.
A gray-white fireball the size of a millstone flew out and struck the purple vine cage surrounding it.
With a thunderous "bang," a gray-white mushroom cloud soared!
The Purple Vine Cage trembled violently; several demon vines were blown apart, but the cage itself was almost undamaged, still securely imprisoning the Lion Scale Beast.
The power of the Wood Prison Technique depended largely on the type of tree used to form the prison. The Purple-Black Demon Vine was already strong; a Wood Prison made from it had great power, making it very difficult for a Qi Refinement Realm fierce beast to escape.
A red hammer shadow whistled down and struck the head of the Lion Scale Beast.
The head of the Lion Scale Beast burst open upon impact, with a mixture of red and white substances splattering everywhere; it fell dead before it had the chance to scream.
The purple-black demon vine shot out, piercing into the wound of the Lion Scale Beast, rapidly absorbing the blood within.
Yuan Ming paid no attention to the actions of the demon vine, staring blankly at the lifeless body of the Lion Scale Beast, somewhat lost in thought.
After the recent exchange, he deeply felt the terror of this gray-white Lion Scale Beast, no less formidable than the Four-eyed Golden Ape and Black Giant Crow he had faced before.
He had once embarrassingly fled from under the Golden Ape Giant Crow, but now he could easily kill a fierce beast of the same level. It must be said that the Black Toad and demon vine's contribution was indispensible.
Unexpectedly, the help of a capable spirit beast could be so great.
Yuan Ming walked forward a few steps and picked up a piece of vine that had been blasted off the ground, frowning.
Although the demon vine was resilient, being a wood attribute creature, it was still heavily suppressed by an attack of the fire attribute.
Fortunately, the Purple-Black Demon Vine had a strong self-healing ability and was now integrated with the Black Toad. As long as there was sufficient Qi-Blood, such damage could quickly recover.
Yuan Ming discarded the vine in his hand, ignored the corpse of the Lion Scale Beast, and turned to walk towards the Black Scale Fruit, carefully harvesting the fruit and storing it away.
At this time, the Purple-Black Demon Vine had also finished absorbing the blood of the Lion Scale Beast. This time it didn't feed back to the Black Toad's body but started to repair its own damage. The blasted vine trunks rapidly grew back, and in a few breaths, most of it had recovered.
Yuan Ming continued forward, and the sound of water "splashing" came from ahead.
He went around a low hill, and a gray-white stream lay in front of him, filled with dense yin qi, detectable even from a great distance.
Yuan Ming paused and then his eyes lit up with joy.
This was exactly the stream he had encountered the first time he landed on the island.
Finding this place made things easier; he followed the scenery from his memory, traveling upstream along the stream. A small mountain appeared ahead, precisely where Master Hei Mu's hidden Cave Mansion was located.
The gate to the Cave Mansion was still open, with previous footprints faintly visible on the ground at the entrance, everything maintained as it was back then.
Yuan Ming entered the cave, keeping the Black Toad close at his side, alert for the Earth Demon he had encountered before.
The interior of the cave was also preserved in its original state. He searched the Cave Mansion again thoroughly and even released his Divine Soul to check the surrounding walls for any hidden rooms or compartments, but unfortunately, there were no more secrets to be found here.
Yuan Ming was quite disappointed and approached the casting furnace.
The only thing left of value here was this casting furnace. Last time, he fled hastily due to the Earth Demon and didn't have the chance to take it with him; this time, he would not miss the opportunity.
He activated his black Storage Bag, attempting to collect the furnace.
However, after a series of castings, the furnace remained immobile in its original place.
Yuan Ming looked surprised, as the space inside the black Storage Bag was definitely large enough to accommodate the furnace.
With a hint of confusion, he began to examine the furnace and soon discovered the reason.
The ground around the furnace was engraved with a circle of dense, complicated red runes that seemed to have a special connection with something underground. Unless these runes were destroyed, it was impossible to move the furnace.
After a moment of contemplation, Yuan Ming drew out the Green Fish Sword and slashed at the runes on the ground.
Before the blade could touch the runes, a layer of red light burst forth, repelling the Green Fish Sword.
"Could it be an array?" Yuan Ming looked puzzled. After pondering for a while, he gave up on trying to take it.
He had heard from Brother Fang Ge that some skilled Artifact Refiners used furnaces that were similar to Magic Artifacts, containing special runes inside that provided special benefits during the refining process.
Even more skilled Artifact Refiners would engrave arrays to further enhance various aspects of the furnaces, greatly aiding the refining process.
Since Master Hei Mu had left such an array and furnace here, there must be a reason. If he rashly destroyed the array, it would be like ruining half of the furnace, so he might as well wait until his cultivation was sufficient in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 122 - 102 Lost
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming resealed the mechanisms of the stone chamber used for casting and blocked the entrance of the cave mansion with a large rock. He then looked around, a hint of disappointment flashing in his eyes—the Earth Demon had not shown up.
Unlike the Lion Scale Beast previously encountered, the Earth Demon contained within it a Transforming Soil Stone that could be refined into various earth-tunneling treasures, which were quite valuable.
He continued upstream along the creek, quickly reaching the Black Pine Forest.
Yuan Ming knew nothing about the Black Giant Crow and whether it had spiritual materials on its body that could be collected. Not wishing to recklessly provoke it, he executed the Wood Concealment Skill to hide his tracks carefully as he crossed the forest.
Today his luck was good. He didn't encounter the Black Giant Crow and smoothly arrived at the area where the Four-eyed Golden Ape was located.
His previous encounter with the Red Core Peach Tree was purely by chance, and now he couldn't recall where the tree was located. Thus, he maintained his Wood Concealment Skill and began searching around.
"Quack quack..." Suddenly, the Black Toad perched on Yuan Ming's shoulder let out a few low croaks.
Yuan Ming shivered and stopped moving.
The Black Toad had sent a somewhat vague message through their mental connection, indicating that there was a scent of blood ahead.
Purple-Black Demon Vines could suck blood and were extremely sensitive to the smell of it.
Yuan Ming followed the direction indicated by the Black Toad, cautiously moving closer. He soon reached a lush thicket in the distance, pushed aside the wild plants, and his expression shifted slightly.
Two large bodies were lying there, one of them being the Four-eyed Golden Ape, and the other, the Black Giant Crow.
The Four-eyed Golden Ape had a huge hole in its chest, clearly a fatal wound, likely caused by a sword or similar weapon.
Apart from the wound in its chest, all four eyes of the Golden Ape had been gouged out, leaving behind four bloody, fleshly holes.
The Black Giant Crow had also died from a blade piercing its chest. Its claws and head were severed and nowhere to be found, evidently taken away by someone.
"No wonder I didn't encounter the Black Giant Crow just now. It turns out it was already killed. From the looks of the wounds, both the Four-eyed Golden Ape and the Black Giant Crow were killed by cultivators! Someone else has been here!" Yuan Ming muttered to himself.
He wasn't particularly surprised that others had found their way here.
If he could find this island, so could others.T#h!i%s c%o-n.ten%t% or&i#g%in%ates fr!o.m *,& My Vir#t#ual$ Li#b$r#ar^y& Em*p.i#re!.!
Judging from the wounds on the Four-eyed Golden Ape, it had not been dead for long—probably only a matter of two or three days.
Besides the chest and eye injuries, the Four-eyed Golden Ape bore no other wounds. The four eyes had likely been dug out afterward, just like the Black Giant Crow, which only had one fatal wound.
There were no signs of a struggle in the vicinity, suggesting that both the Four-eyed Golden Ape and the Black Giant Crow had been killed by someone with a single strike, an act beyond the capabilities of a Qi Refining Stage Cultivator.
Yuan Ming couldn't help feeling a little frightened. Cultivators were often steeped in bloodshed. The island was rich in resources and, with Master Hei Mu's Cave Mansion, it was something of a treasure trove. If that person discovered his tracks, it was very likely that he would be casually killed to silence him.
Suppressing his uneasy feelings, Yuan Ming quickly called the Black Toad and headed towards the lakeshore.
Although he didn't know if that person had left, he knew he had to hurry and leave himself.
He hadn't gone far when the trees ahead became sparse, and a peach tree stood silently in the clearing—it was the Red Core Spiritual Peach.
Yuan Ming's heart skipped a beat; he had been planning to leave, but by a fluke, he had stumbled upon the tree.
However, when he took a closer look, all the joy on his face vanished.
On the peach tree, there were only leaves left—all the Spiritual Peaches had disappeared, most likely picked by the person who had slain the Four-eyed Golden Ape.
Yuan Ming sighed inwardly, not lingering, and quickly reached the lakeshore.
He used the same method as before, moving across the sky with the incense burner to get as far away from the island as possible to avoid the water creature, then left on a small boat.
Fortunately, the trip was fairly calm, and he did not encounter the black water creature.
After distancing himself from the island, though still surrounded by a pervasive white mist, Yuan Ming finally breathed a sigh of relief.
He was basically safe once he reached this point.
"Who could that person be who got to it before me? An elder of the Biluo Cave Sect or someone from another sect?" he murmured.
Qianlu Lake was closest to the Biluo Cave Sect, so it was unlikely that someone from another sect would come here.
If it was an elder of the Biluo Cave Sect, he would have to be careful, and if possible, not come back again.
He had concealed the entrance of Master Hei Mu's Cave Mansion, but such a level of disguise could easily be seen through, and although he had taken almost everything from inside the mansion, the casting furnace was still there.
Those familiar with Master Hei Mu might find clues on that furnace and come to this island again, which would be too dangerous.
"Anyhow, I've already subdued the spirit beast, so there's no need to come back," Yuan Ming decided resolutely.
He took out a compass, verified the direction, and after less than half a day's journey, he reached the shore of the lake.
Yuan Ming rested in a hidden spot by the lake, quickly fully recovering his mana, and then set off to return to the sect.
For the following two days, he did not go out, dutifully working in the Fire Workshop and proceeding with his cultivation as usual.
Everything within the sect was as calm as ever, and there was nothing unusual in the Fire Workshop.
He deliberately paid attention to Fang Ge, Chen Wan, and the others, but they did not show any unusual behavior.
Yuan Ming was quite surprised. If Master Hei Mu's Cave Mansion had really come to light, other places might not notice, but the Fire Workshop here should not be so quiet.
"It seems I was wrong. Maybe that person didn't discover it, or perhaps they are not an elder of the Biluo Cave Sect?" Yuan Ming mused, his mind easing.
With the matter of the spirit beast wrapped up, he now had to start looking for the other three spiritual materials besides the Black Scale Fruit.
...
Three days later, Toad Valley.
Yuan Ming, who hadn't visited this place in a long time, looked at the desolate scenery inside the valley and felt somewhat dazed for a moment.
Strictly speaking, it hadn't been all that long since he had shed his identity as a Fur Beast Slave, but now looking back on those days, there seemed to be an illusion of having been lifetimes apart.
He made his way to the entrance of a stone house as if on familiar ground and immediately spotted Zhao Tong, who was perched on a lounger with his legs crossed.
In his hands, he held a fairly wide, thread-bound book. Its grayish-green cover was adorned with an exquisite white drawing, delineated with dark gold lines, and beside it, in Central Plains script, was written "Warm Pavilion and Warm Jade."
"That's a deluxe illustrated edition you've got there, must've cost you quite a few contribution points," Yuan Ming remarked.
The book slowly lowered to reveal a smiling face: "Hehe, what's this? Have you finally gotten the knack and recognize a good thing when you see it?"
"It's just as well that the Law and Regulations Hall hasn't banned the perusal and circulation of erotic literature, otherwise you, a disciple of that hall, would be the first to get a spanking," Yuan Ming teased.
"You wouldn't come to me without a reason, so spill it, what do you want?" Zhao Tong sat up and asked.
"I want to buy some things from you," Yuan Ming replied.
"Like what?" Zhao Tong frowned.
"Ghost Faced Grass, Purple Core Pollen, and Yin Marrow Liquid," Yuan Ming listed.
"Are you going to do alchemy?" Zhao Tong questioned in confusion.
"Just tell me if you have them or not," Yuan Ming didn't elaborate.
"There's plenty of Ghost Faced Grass, and as for Purple Core Pollen... I believe there's still some stock left from the last collection. But I don't have any Yin Marrow Liquid; however, you might be able to buy some from the Refining Furnace Hall," Zhao Tong pondered and replied.
"Give me a price," Yuan Ming said straightforwardly.
"Neither Ghost Faced Grass nor Purple Core Pollen are too rare, so you can exchange one portion of each for two contribution points," Zhao Tong said.
"I knew it..." Yuan Ming's mouth twitched as he spoke.
"Knew what?" Zhao Tong asked, puzzled.
"I went to the Refining Furnace Hall before coming here. Guess how they sell these two items?" Yuan Ming said.
"Knowing those guys, they'd charge at least double," Zhao Tong laughed.
