The Silver Cat Xi Ying was incredibly fast, and Yuan Ming couldn't catch up. Xi Ying darted into the forest and vanished in an instant. With the limited range of his Divine Sense, Yuan Ming couldn't track him down.
Only then did Yuan Ming realize that the incense burner was in the hands of the Silver Cat Xi Ying.
He couldn't understand why Xi Ying would suddenly snatch his incense burner. Was it really just to borrow it for a few days?
In the past, Yuan Ming had taken out the incense burner more than once, even handing it directly to Xi Ying to examine. He'd never seen Xi Ying make any suspicious moves then.
The incense burner was of great significance to him. Yuan Ming tried to calm his agitated thoughts. He pressed two fingers to his forehead and cast the Moonlight Technique, drawing three soul crows from his Sea of Consciousness.
The soul crows spread their wings and flew into the forest in search of Xi Ying.
However, they couldn't find any trace of the Silver Cat Xi Ying anywhere.
Yuan Ming's brow furrowed into knots as he had long realized that if Silver Cat Xi Ying intended to hide, he would not be able to find him at all.
"Stay calm, I have to stay calm, there must be another way…" Yuan Ming stopped and forced himself to think calmly.
After regaining composure and thinking calmly, Yuan Ming indeed thought of a solution.
The incense burner was more than an ordinary Magic Artifact for him; there was a special connection between him and the burner.
Yuan Ming looked at his arm and then recalled the soul crows before sitting cross-legged on the ground.
He then touched the tattoo where the incense burner had once been on his arm and, with a focused Divine Thought, began to try and communicate with the incense burner, sending out the intention to summon it back.
Yuan Ming didn't know if this would work but it was the only thing he could try at the moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 157 - 137: Angry
chapters.content:
On the other side,
the Silver Cat Xi Ying took the incense burner and arrived at a large tree not far away.
This was a gigantic century-old tree, and at a branch ten zhang from the ground there was a hidden little tree hollow that had been dug out. The hollow was padded with fur and silk, and there was also a pillow made of silk.
The Silver Cat Xi Ying placed the tripod in front of her and raised a paw onto it.
A silvery light lit up from the center of her paw, and the silver glow formed an array that enveloped the body of the burner, with strands of light converging towards the incense burner.
However, after waiting for a moment, there was no reaction from the tripod.
Doubt flashed in the eyes of the Silver Cat Xi Ying, and her furry little head moved closer to take a careful look, when suddenly she discovered that the tripod began to light up on its own and its body started becoming transparent and virtual.
The eyes of Silver Cat Xi Ying flashed as she quickly withdrew her mana.
But the virtualization of the incense burner did not stop, and under her gaze, it completely virtualized and finally disappeared.
The Silver Cat Xi Ying puffed out her cheeks, feeling annoyed, "Ah, this damned son of a bitch, how did he do it?"
...
At the same time, Yuan Ming felt a warm sensation on his arm.
A blue-black incense burner tattoo gradually became clear and emerged.
"It's back!" declared Yuan Ming, overjoyed at the sight.
He touched the tattoo on his arm, then got up, looked around, and not seeing the silver cat, he turned and returned to his dwelling.
After going back, he lost the impulse to light the incense and try possession, instead he sat up straight at his desk, quietly waiting for the appearance of the Silver Cat.
As expected, moments later, the Silver Cat once again appeared at the window.
It still walked with an elegant stride, not showing the slightest guilt for its earlier behavior, instead it huffed looking at Yuan Ming.
"You take my things without asking, and you're the one angry?" Yuan Ming said, annoyed.
"Hmph, was just borrowing it to play for a few days, you're being too stingy." Seeing Yuan Ming's questioning, the Silver Cat Xi Ying was furious, her claws grinding against the window frame as her voice rang in Yuan Ming's ears.
"This thing is not for casual playing, it would be trouble if it got stolen," Yuan Ming said seriously.
"Stolen? Who would dare! Do you not see who I am?" the Silver Cat boasted proudly. The M|V|LE&MPYR team worked hard on this chapter.
"It's not a matter of 'if', but 'just in case'. This incense burner is very important to me," Yuan Ming said patiently.
"I just want to play with your incense burner, I just want to play! You penny-pincher, don't you see who is helping you with your cultivation? What's wrong with playing for a bit? Huh? What's wrong? Stingy!" Silver Cat Xi Ying wouldn't listen to Yuan Ming at all, interrupting him and starting to rant.
Yuan Ming felt a twinge of guilt hearing this and with a wave of his hand, the incense burner reappeared in his hand. He placed it on the desk, saying, "Alright, alright, go ahead and play, just play here."
"I'm not interested anymore, don't care for it now." The Silver Cat glanced at the incense burner, then slowly laid down on the windowsill, resting her little head on her front paws, looking away.
The atmosphere became a bit tense; Yuan Ming thought for a moment and then said:
"What do you want this incense burner for? Can you tell me?"
In truth, Yuan Ming had always been skeptical about the appearance of the Silver Cat, and had remained on guard at first, but as they spent more time together, and since the Silver Cat had indeed provided a lot of help and even saved him, he had come to think of the Silver Cat as a friend deep down.
"Not telling you, I don't feel like bothering with you now," the voice of Silver Cat Xi Ying echoed in Yuan Ming's mind.
"Then let me guess," Yuan Ming said.
Silver Cat Xi Ying shifted her gaze and looked at Yuan Ming with her eyes blinking twice; she seemed curious about what Yuan Ming would come up with.
"When I cultivate the Moonlight Technique and summon this incense burner, I feel it helps to stabilize the divine soul and enhance soul power. You must have the same feeling, right?" Yuan Ming continued.
He had long noticed that the playful Huo Chan'er from the Three Cave Masters had taken a liking to him, mostly likely for the same reason.
"It seems you're not dumb, have you finally gotten a clue? Let me touch your head, maybe you've grown horns," said the Silver Cat, extending her crystal clear paw towards Yuan Ming's head.
Yuan Ming instinctively dodged; he still vividly remembered the scene where Xi Ying's single strike brought down the Kun Tu and certainly did not want that paw to touch him.
"Stop, stop, your paws are too heavy, it's too frightening," Yuan Ming said, startled.
"Coward, if I really wanted to harm you, would I have waited until now? I would have struck you with one claw and taken the burner already," Silver Cat Xi Ying said disdainfully.
"Then why didn't you make your move?" Yuan Ming asked curiously.
"Not telling you, goodbye." Suddenly, the Silver Cat leaped away like a flash of lightning, sweeping her claw and snatching the piece of torn paper from the desk before jumping to a nearby tree.
Yuan Ming thought to himself, "Xi Ying, she doesn't seem to be angry anymore..."
"Xi Ying, I'm going to start my retreat in the Ten Thousand Mountains for cultivation tomorrow," Yuan Ming called out to the outside.
"Whatever you want." The latter didn't look back and disappeared from his view.
Yuan Ming looked in the direction where the Silver Cat Xi Ying had gone, his face filled with a mix of emotions.
Since he met the silver cat, he noticed that its originally aloof personality gradually underwent a significant change, sometimes it even seemed rather cute.
In fact, after his cultivation had progressively improved, he realized that connecting with the Divine Soul was not simple.
The origins of Xi Ying must be extraordinary, and the name "Xi Ying" sounded like it had been given by a woman?
A moment later, Yuan Ming came back to his senses, closed the window, and placed the incense burner back on the table, lighting the homemade Black Incense.
This time, before possession, he likewise silently invoked the Emperor in his heart—yet he did not manage to possess the Emperor, but found himself possessing a servant in the General Mansion instead.
This confused Yuan Ming; he didn't know whether his earlier speculation was incorrect, or whether his focus had not been sharp enough before this possession attempt.
After all, having been tormented by the Silver Cat Xi Ying, his mind indeed had not settled down, cluttered with various thoughts.
However, no matter the reason, he had to put a temporary pause on it for some time now, he couldn't forget the necessity of diligent cultivation just because of the potential benefits of possession.
His true foundation lay in his own strength; in the following period, he must focus on secluded cultivation.
The next day, Yuan Ming set off for the Ten Thousand Mountains.
He found a lush forest and started felling trees to build a simple wooden hut on a towering ancient tree.
With the abundant Wood Attribute Spiritual Energy here, this would be his place of secluded cultivation for a while.
By evening, the wooden hut was ready.
Yuan Ming went to the base of the tree and, following the habits he had when he was a Fur Beast Slave, used stones to create a fire pit and filled it with firewood and dry leaves.
But this time, he did not use a Fire Stick to ignite the fire.
Instead, he stood a zhang away from the fire pit and firmly planted his feet apart, raising both hands, one hand holding the other's wrist.
Then, with his eyes closed and spirit focused, he recalled the memory of possessing the Emperor and using the Burning Explosion Skill together.
As he softly chanted, the Mana within his body also began circulating along a predetermined path, flowing toward the tip of his raised index finger.
The next instant, a fist-sized flame "whooshed" to life and hovered at his fingertip.
The flame gathered, emitting waves of heat, the scorching temperature spreading and stirring up gusts of air that caused Yuan Ming's hair to lift slightly, his face glowing red in the firelight.
Yuan Ming steadied his mind and began to pour Mana into the already formed fireball as he had guessed earlier.
At first, he dared not act rashly, being careful to control the Mana to trickle in like a fine stream into the fingertip.
The initially walnut-sized fireball spewed out a tongue of flame at the instant Mana flowed into it, then stabilized, but the volume of the fireball began to swell slowly.
Feeling nothing amiss, Yuan Ming confidently fed more Mana into it.
Surges of Mana rushed out of his Dantian, constantly pooling into the fireball, which had now begun to grow rapidly, soon reaching the size of a baby's head.
The flame changed from a reddish color to bright yellow, the searing heat making Yuan Ming's skin tighten and a smell of scorching filling the air.
But with that heat came the rapid depletion of Mana within him, almost reaching the point of losing control.
Just as Yuan Ming felt his Mana reaching its limit and was about to throw the fireball, the Mana within his Dantian had already run out first.
The huge fireball's flames stopped spewing, its growth halted, and after sustaining for a moment or two, it "bang" shattered, breaking into numerous sparks that dispersed into the air.
Yuan Ming slumped to the ground, feeling an emptiness in his Dantian and as if he had been drained of energy.
He quickly took out a Spirit Stone, clutched it in his hand, and sat cross-legged, absorbing the Spiritual Power within to help him recover quickly.
After this experiment, Yuan Ming found that the Mana reserve in his Dantian was actually inferior to the Emperor's.
The latter could support the growth of the fireball until it reached the size of an adult's head, whereas he could not.
It could be said that Yuan Ming's accidental possession had opened the path of cultivation for the little Emperor, so their cultivation time was comparable, yet Yuan Ming was significantly behind.
Of course, there would be differences in external conditions—as the Emperor of Da Jin Country, he would not lack cultivation resources, but his aptitude for cultivation was probably one in ten thousand.
"This Burning Explosion Skill seems to be able to sustain growth as long as Mana is continuously infused. At least with my Mana, I am temporarily unable to test its limits," Yuan Ming pondered.
It was not until the latter half of the night that Yuan Ming finally restored his Dan Tian Power.
He could hardly wait to start experimenting again.
This time, he closely monitored the changes in his Dan Tian Power and did not allow the fireball to exhaust all his Mana and extinguish itself as before.
Rather, the instant before his Mana was about to run out, he mustered all his strength and hurled it into the fire pit in front of him.
The bright yellow fireball flew into the fire pit, and the moment it landed, a loud "boom" resounded.
A huge burst of Flames erupted from the fire pit, countless fireballs mixed with earth and stone splattering out, forming a circle with a radius of about ten feet of spilling flames.
"That was too much!" the thought flashed through Yuan Ming's mind.
The intense heat combined with the shockwave of dirt and stones swept outward with an incredibly forceful impact.

chapters.title: Chapter 158 - 138 The 4th Ability
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming saw that the situation was dire, and he hurriedly retreated to dodge, but he still couldn't completely avoid it and was blown away by a scorching blast of air.
When he got up from the ground, rubbing his chest and covered in dust, he finally saw that the fire pit he had built with stones had turned into a three-foot-wide charred pit, from which wisps of white smoke were still rising.
The trees within a thirty-foot radius had been torn apart, shabby and unsightly, with their trunks scorched black, and flames could still be seen burning.
The scene before him left Yuan Ming somewhat dumbfounded.
It wasn't his first time seeing the Fireball Technique, this most basic of fire-attribute attack magic that Chen Wan had previously unleashed, yet the power of the Burning Explosion Skill was incomparable, not even by ten Fireball Techniques.
He feared that even an Inner Sect Disciple a few levels higher in cultivation than himself, or even a Cultivator in the early stage of Foundation Establishment, wouldn't be able to face this strike directly!
After the surprise, what followed was a strong shock and delight.
"I must focus on cultivation," Yuan Ming thought to himself. "Only by gathering more mana can I increase the power of this technique." With this skill at his disposal and the proper application, especially if supplemented with spirit stones, he wouldn't have to worry even if he encountered the situation where he was surrounded and attacked by people like Kun Tu again.
"Boom"
Just then, a huge shadow crashed down in front of Yuan Ming with a loud noise, startling him.
The treehouse he had spent a day building collapsed in front of his eyes along with the broken trunk, shattering into pieces.
"Sigh, it seems I need to find a new place."
...
Time flew by, and several months passed.
Within the dense woods of the Ten Thousand Mountains,
A treetop of an ancient tree supported a man-made wooden platform where a figure sat cross-legged, bathing in the bright moonlight.
He held a green incense burner in his arms, his whole body emitting a faint glow.
At that moment, the glow enveloping his body suddenly constricted and re-entered his body.
At the center of his eyebrows, however, a light shone, and a pure black raven with a tuft of white feathers on its brow emerged from the hazy light and flew high towards the east.
Immediately after, a black soul crow flew out, heading west.
Then the third one followed, and finally, the fourth one took flight.
The four soul crows headed in the four directions of southeast, northwest, and Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness immediately received different perspectives from each of the soul crows' perspectives.
Just now, he had finally reached the second layer skill of the Moonlight Technique, his Divine Soul Power surged, and he had condensed the fourth soul crow.
The four soul crows continued to soar into the distance, not particularly fast, equivalent to ordinary ravens, but the distance they covered this time was significantly increased.
At twenty miles out, the connection with Yuan Ming began to wane, and the scenes in his vision became blurred.
With a thought, Yuan Ming recalled the four soul crows back to him.
After a session of feeling and experiencing, he noticed that the soul power fluctuations of the four soul crows were considerably stronger than before, meaning that if he used his soul collision ability again, it would be much more potent than previously.
Any Cultivator of the same cultivation level as him would absolutely not withstand a single soul collision attack from him.
During this time, Yuan Ming intensified his practice of the Nine Elements Technique by day and diligently cultivated the Moonlight Technique by night, not only making significant progress in his Soul Cultivation Method but also advancing his Nine Elements Technique to the Ninth Level.
At this point, Yuan Ming's cultivation had reached the Qi Refining Ninth Level.
The growth in his Magic Power Cultivation allowed for more proficiency in magic such as the Wood Stabbing Technique and the Wood Prison Technique, increasing the speed and power of his spellcasting.
The four soul crows gradually flew back, re-entering Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness.
Yuan Ming slowly opened his eyes, a joyful expression on his face.
Just then, a silver figure descended slowly down from an ancient tree in the moonlight and came to Yuan Ming's side.
"For such a fool to condense a fourth soul crow is truly beyond my expectation," a familiar voice of Silver Cat Xi Ying sounded within Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness.
Indeed, Silver Cat Xi Ying showed up, and he could feel that during the time of his seclusion, this silver cat had always been around.
He immediately looked over and said, "Xi Ying, I've gained a new ability."
"What ability?"
Xi Ying's tone carried a slight surprise.
"Corpse Control," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"How is that possible? Normally, a Soul Cultivator needs to be at least at the Foundation Establishment Stage before they can master Corpse Control, as their Divine Soul's strength would otherwise be insufficient to sustain it," the Silver Cat found it quite unbelievable.
Yuan Ming's Divine Soul was much stronger and grew much faster than ordinary people, which Silver Cat was aware of, but she hadn't expected it to be so incredibly strong.
"It's impossible to know if it can be done without trying," Yuan Ming said.
"I'm actually curious to see if you can really do it," the silver cat's voice rang out in his Sea of Consciousness immediately.
Yuan Ming nodded, immediately began to pinch his fingers and closed his eyes to cast the Divine Soul Secret Technique.
Before long, a soul crow struggled to fly out from his glabella, entering the high sky, circled slightly, and then flew towards a certain direction.
The soul crow had flown seventy to eighty feet away when it suddenly plunged headfirst toward the ground.
In the mountain forest below lay a body in a pit full of dead branches and fallen leaves, sprawled out with extensive rot, its clothing reduced to mud.
Its chest and abdomen were impaled by wooden thorns from the bottom of the pit, but the fatal wound was its collapsed skull, which seemed to have been smashed to death by a Fierce Beast like a bear.
The black raven flew to the front of the corpse, hesitated a moment, then dove into its collapsed head.
The next instant, as if ghost fire had risen, a green light glowed in the eyes of the corpse.
On the other side of the mountain forest, Yuan Ming's face contorted with expression as he maintained the soul crow's perspective in his Sea of Consciousness, although the viewpoint seemed somewhat odd.
At this moment, he felt as if, besides his own eyes, he had grown an extra pair, and through these eyes, he viewed a world shrouded in a pale green gloom.
"How is it? Quickly tell me," the voice of Silver Cat Xi Ying resonated in his Sea of Consciousness.
"It should be... successful," Yuan Ming said, somewhat uncertain.
"You've got some talent after all," Silver Cat Xi Ying's voice timely sounded in Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness. "If the soul crow enters a body and can see the outside world through the corpse's eyes, then you have succeeded halfway. Now you can try to control the body's movements."
He immediately began to try.
With a move of his hands and a thought in his mind, the corpse's arm dozens of feet away slowly and stiffly lifted, but almost at the same time, his own arm in meditation was involuntarily raised as well.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming quickly lowered his own arm, but the corpse lowered its hand as well.
His brow furrowed, Yuan Ming tried again to control the corpse by moving its leg; consequently, his own leg involuntarily moved as well.
Yuan Ming pressed his leg with one hand and tried again using his will to control the movements of the corpse.
This time, with the external force pressing down, his own leg did not interfere any further, but this was clearly not a long-term solution.
In a way, the man and the corpse had become a pair of conjoined twins.
"After several attempts, I find when I try to control the corpse's movements, my intentions inadvertently influence my own body; when the corpse moves, I move along with it," Yuan Ming said with a troubled look after several trials.
After a moment, Xi Ying's voice resonated in his mind:Note: Check * for any corrections.
"This is quite normal for a Soul Cultivator trying corpse control for the first time. Controlling a corpse requires sending out a Divine Thought to manage another body, which is naturally ten times more difficult than simply extending a Divine Thought to observe the outside world."
"What should I do to control it as freely as you do?" Yuan Ming asked.
"There's no special technique; you just need to keep practicing. Did you think you were a genius like me?" Xi Ying didn't offer a shortcut and took the opportunity to belittle Yuan Ming a bit.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming stopped getting distracted and began to immerse himself fully in trying to control the corpse.
At this moment, Xi Ying seemed deliberately to keep sending telepathic messages to him, disrupting his rhythm: "The longer a body has been dead, the less water retention and muscle vitality it holds, making its movements more rigid and difficult to control. Conversely, if the body has just died and retains some Spiritual Power, with proper control, it can even exhibit its innate combat instincts from when it was alive."
Yuan Ming took these messages to heart but didn't stop his practice of controlling the corpse.
Until the next day at dawn, with mist enveloping the mountain forest, a highly decomposed black corpse staggered out from the mist and stumbled to Yuan Ming's front with rigid steps.
The next instant, the corpse flopped to the ground, and a black soul crow flew out from its glabella, entering Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness.
At this moment, Yuan Ming's face was covered in exhaustion, but his eyes could not hide the delight within.
After a night of repeated practice, nearly depleting all the strength of the four soul crows, he finally grasped the knack of controlling the corpse and cut off the interfering connection between himself and the body, akin to conjoined twins.
"You do have a slight talent for Soul Cultivation—managing to become proficient with corpse control in just this short time is quite remarkable. It's already close to one-tenth of my capabilities back in the day," Silver Cat Xi Ying stated, having stayed with Yuan Ming throughout the night.
"Can you tell me the story of your past?" Yuan Ming asked with great curiosity.
Without replying, Silver Cat Xi Ying had already left.
After thanking the direction in which Silver Cat Xi Ying had departed, Yuan Ming bathed in the morning light, continuing his meditation and restorative practice for his Divine Soul.
However, as he was deep in contemplation, his mind suddenly "boomed" as if a heavenly bell had been struck.
Consequently, fragments of images began to emerge, flooding over like a tide in his mind.
Yuan Ming felt an intense pain in his head, involuntarily clutching his head in agony and collapsing to the side.
After a long while, he stopped struggling, drenched in cold sweat, and slowly lifted his head.
His eyes were focused and clear, seemingly unchanged, yet there was something different about them from before.

chapters.title: Chapter 159 - 139: Foundation Establishment Opportunity
chapters.content:
Two days later.
Yuan Ming returned to the Sect and did not go back to the Fire Refining Hall but directly headed to the Execution Hall, planning to find some suitable tasks to accumulate some contribution points.
However, when he arrived at the square outside the Execution Hall, he found it unexpectedly bustling with people.
At least a hundred disciples from various halls were gathered around a notice board on the square, intensely focused on some captivating news that had them all discussing it with great enthusiasm.
Driven by curiosity, Yuan Ming finally squeezed through the crowd, tiptoed, and looked at the notice board, only to see a conspicuous red paper posted on it, which turned out to be a notice issued by the Sect.
"White Deer Hill Conclave?" Yuan Ming skimmed through, but a huge question arose in his heart.
He turned to a round-faced disciple beside him, brimming with excitement, and asked, "Senior Brother, could you kindly tell me what this White Deer Hill Conclave is about?"
"You don't even know about the White Deer Hill Conclave? Have you been cultivating so hard that you've become foolish?" The man looked him over with a slightly disdainful tone.
"I've just recently joined the Sect, indeed I'm not familiar with it; I would appreciate it if Senior Brother could enlighten me," Yuan Ming replied with a smile.
Seeing that Yuan Ming was fairly polite, the man, eager to show off, cleared his throat and prepared to impart his knowledge.
But before he could begin, someone else from the side beat him to it.
"The White Deer Hill Conclave is an exchange event held jointly by the Five Great Sects of the Southern Border and the Northern Territory, occurring once every ten years. It gathers the young elites of the Five Great Sects; having just joined the Sect, you probably won't have the chance to participate," said a lanky disciple from the Refining Furnace Hall.
The round-faced disciple, upon being cut off, immediately glared at the man and scoffed, "You aren't new here, yet you speak as if you have a chance to participate? Attendance at the conclave is based on strength."
"And how high is your strength? Not only do you lack the strength, but I doubt you even have the courage to participate…" the tall disciple retorted, unwilling to back down.
"What abilities do you have, relying on your master's connections for every good opportunity?"
...
Seeing the two red-faced and about to fight, Yuan Ming quietly slipped away from the crowd.
The notice only mentioned that the White Deer Hill Conclave would be held in half a year, and those interested should sign up with the steward of their respective halls; beyond that, there wasn't much else provided.
Although Yuan Ming was somewhat curious about the White Deer Hill Conclave and wanted to learn more, his primary focus was on quickly improving his cultivation strength; otherwise, knowing more would be futile.
After making a round inside the Execution Hall and not finding any suitable tasks, he headed back to the Fire Refining Hall and went straight to the Fire Workshop to concentrate on refining embryos.
Artifact Refining is ultimately a skill of the hands, and not practicing for a long time would inevitably lead to rustiness.
Since the time had already passed for early class, almost all the disciples had left the Fire Workshop. Yuan Ming then started the fire pit himself, beginning to noisily refine the embryo.
At this point, whether in terms of strength or skill, he had matured, and completing a thousand hammer strikes posed no difficulty; he found his rhythm quickly and soon finished refining the embryo.
When he put down the final hammer, a standard longsword was already forged.
"Clap clap"
At that moment, applause sounded from behind. Senior Brother Fang Ge had walked over at some point.
"There's improvement; the patterns on the sword are very nice, and its form is quite symmetrical," Senior Brother Fang Ge complimented generously.
"Senior Brother, you flatter me. I haven't practiced for quite a while, and have gotten a bit rusty, please give me more guidance," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"Don't be modest; I noticed quite early on that while the process of learning might not be shorter or faster than others, once you've mastered it, your performance is very stable," Fang Ge waved his hand and said.
Yuan Ming thought about it and suddenly realized that was indeed the case.
Whether it was refining embryos or drawing talismans, as long as he truly grasped the method, the success rate was always high.
"Have you visited our master yet?" Fang Ge inquired.
"I just returned to the Sect today and haven't had the chance to pay a visit. Is there any instruction from the Three Cave Masters?" Yuan Ming asked somewhat surprised.
"Yesterday, Sister Chen Wan came looking for you, saying our master wanted you to go to the back mountain. Unable to find you and in a hurry to enter seclusion, she entrusted me to pass the message once I saw you," Fang Ge explained.
Yuan Ming paused briefly, guessing it was mostly regarding taking care of Huo Chan'er.
"I'll go to the back mountain shortly. Before that, I have something else I'd like to discuss with Senior Brother," Yuan Ming said.
"Feel free to speak," Fang Ge nodded.
"Senior Brother, do you know what the White Deer Hill Conclave is all about?" Yuan Ming questioned.
"You've been to the Execution Hall, haven't you? Counting the time, it's also about half a year away," Fang Ge queried.
"Indeed, I saw quite a few disciples gathered around the notice, talking about some sort of decennial grand event," Yuan Ming said.
"White Deer Hill is a forbidden place within the Ten Thousand Mountains, perpetually obscured by lethal poison miasma. Every ten years, the miasma in certain areas of the Hill dissipates for seven days, during which time the five great sects of the Southern Border and Northern Territory jointly enter White Deer Hill for exploration. This alliance serves as an exchange event for Qi Refining disciples of the five great sects, and also as a test of the strength of each sect's newer generation. After all, the five great sects share the same root," Fang Ge explained in detail.
"Exploration?" Yuan Ming felt a stir in his heart.
"It involves searching for various spiritual materials within White Deer Hill," Fang Ge said.
"Are there many spiritual materials in White Deer Hill?" Yuan Ming pressed on.
"Naturally. White Deer Hill is a unique existence within the entirety of the Ten Thousand Mountains. Due to the shield of deadly poison miasma, ordinary cultivators cannot enter, and numerous fierce beasts are also kept out. Consequently, it contains a large number of exotic beasts and many unique spiritual materials not found elsewhere, providing substantial benefits to the five great sects," Fang Ge explained.
"Exotic beasts? It seems it's not exactly peaceful inside," Yuan Ming said.
"There are indeed dangers. The perennial poison miasma in White Deer Hill breeds a variety of toxic beings and various strange fierce beasts, so casualties are inevitable. Moreover, with such a meetup, there's always some danger as the sects subtly compete with each other to measure their respective harvests and rank them. Therefore, competition between them is inevitable, and conflicts may arise," Fang Ge explained.
Yuan Ming nodded, deciding not to ask any further.
"What about it? Junior Brother Yuan, are you also interested in participating?" Fang Ge asked.
"Forget it, I've just joined the sect recently and my strength is still shallow. I better just focus on my cultivation," Yuan Ming said.
He had been somewhat tempted, but after talking with Fang Ge, he temporarily shelved the idea of participating. After all, he still had half a year's time, and he could make a decision based on the circumstances then.
"Mmm, steadily cultivating is indeed the correct path. Moreover, since you have just joined, and since you are not in a rush to achieve Foundation Establishment, it's not necessary for you to participate," Fang Ge nodded approvingly of Yuan Ming's pragmatic approach.
"Are you saying that it also involves Foundation Establishment?" Yuan Ming asked, puzzled.
"The sect highly values the output from White Deer Hill and to motivate Qi Refining disciples to select those with potential, various additional rewards are given to participating disciples. All treasures obtained in White Deer Hill can be exchanged for sect contribution points, which can be used to acquire various magic artifacts, spiritual materials, elixirs, and even cultivation techniques. For particularly outstanding disciples, the sect might award the opportunity for Foundation Establishment. But, you should not entertain that thought," Fang Ge continued.
When the matter of Foundation Establishment came up, Yuan Ming's eyes noticeably brightened.
Although he was just beginning his path of cultivation, he understood that for cultivators, Foundation Establishment was the first major hurdle on the long road of cultivation, and whether one succeeded in Foundation Establishment dictated two dramatically different life paths.
The reason was nothing else but life span.
Ordinary mortals live their lives with a lifespan of merely a few decades; those who live to be seventy are already rare in ancient times, yet, stepping onto the path of cultivation and with proper cultivation techniques, one could significantly extend one's life span.
Thus, most Qi Refining cultivators, if they do not die prematurely due to accidents, are not unusual to live to over a hundred years old.
But that is the limit; though much stronger than ordinary mortals, if they are fortunate enough to achieve Foundation Establishment, living more than two hundred years is no problem.
And a prolonged life span means more time to cultivate to higher levels and obtain a longer life span.
Yuan Ming had already advanced to the Ninth Level of Qi Refinement, with only a step away from the Tenth Level. Once he reached the Tenth Level of Qi Refinement, he would initially be eligible for Foundation Establishment, making this opportunity for Foundation Establishment substantial for him.
With this realization, Yuan Ming immediately changed his mind—he would participate in the White Deer Hill meetup.
He decided not just to participate but to prepare thoroughly in advance to strive for that precious opportunity for Foundation Establishment.
Because without the support of sect resources for a successful Foundation Establishment, no matter how he cultivated by himself, it was impossible to succeed.
After saying goodbye and leaving the Fire Workshop, Yuan Ming headed straight to the back mountain.Reader support at * made this translation possible.
As he arrived at the courtyard of the Three Cave Masters, Yuan Ming straightened his clothes and called out respectfully, "Disciple Yuan Ming, greeting the Three Cave Masters."
No sooner had he finished speaking than a sharp little head peeked over the courtyard wall, two black eyes, round like beans, swiftly turned and fixed on Yuan Ming with a shrill cry.
Following this, a red shadow leaped out from inside the courtyard, climbed onto Yuan Ming's shoulder in an instant, and affectionately rubbed against Yuan Ming's neck with its head.
Yuan Ming plucked it from his neck and gently stroked its head.
At that moment, the door of the courtyard creaked open by itself.
"Come in," the voice of the Three Cave Masters came from inside the courtyard.
Holding Huo Chan'er, Yuan Ming quickly stepped inside and immediately saw the Three Cave Masters sitting by the stone table.
"Yuan Ming greets the Three Cave Masters," Yuan Ming said as he placed Huo Chan'er on his shoulder and bowed.
The Three Cave Masters looked at the intimately behaving Fire Mink, nodded, and spoke, "Fang Ge mentioned that you had been out for secluded cultivation?"
"Yes, disciple just returned to the sect today," Yuan Ming responded.
"I will be entering seclusion again soon. Huo Chan'er will need you to take care of it for a while longer," the Three Cave Masters said.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 - 140: Encounter with Wulu Again
chapters.content:
"Three Cave Masters, may I ask, how long will your seclusion be this time?" Yuan Ming inquired hesitantly upon hearing those words.
"A few weeks, at the least, but it could be several months. Do you have other matters to attend to?" The Three Cave Masters frowned slightly, seemingly displeased.
"Yes, I plan to participate in the White Deer Hill gathering in half a year's time, so during that period, I will need to make some preparations and might not be able to take care of Huo Chan'er for an extended duration," Yuan Ming explained, after a slight hesitation.
"You're going to participate in the White Deer Hill gathering? If I remember correctly, it hasn't been long since I took you in as my disciple," the Three Cave Masters expressed in surprise, clearly taken aback.
"Yes, I will never forget the kindness of the Three Cave Masters," Yuan Ming said, clasping his fists.
"There are casualties in every gathering. You've finally rid yourself of being a beast slave; you should focus on cultivating peacefully and not risk danger," the Three Cave Masters advised.
"It's a rare opportunity, and I'm willing to take the risk. There's a saying I read in books, 'Seedlings in a greenhouse never grow tall,'" Yuan Ming persisted.
"Fine, if you're set on it, I'll submit your name," said the Three Cave Masters.
"Thank you. I will devote myself to caring for Huo Chan'er during this time; please rest assured," Yuan Ming said.
"There is another matter for which I must apologize in advance; please do not blame me," Yuan Ming continued.
"Speak your mind," the Three Cave Masters said.
"This time, I'm willing to forego any other reward. I only wish to seek guidance from you, Three Cave Masters, on how to advance the Green Fish Sword into a true magical tool," Yuan Ming asked, feeling somewhat relieved.
"You want to prepare for the White Deer Hill gathering?" the Three Cave Masters quickly guessed Yuan Ming's thoughts.
"Yes, I cannot hide anything from you. This sword has been by my side and fought with me on several occasions. I've always wanted to refine it into a personal magical tool, but when I sought the advice of Brother Mu He, I learned from him that the Green Fish Sword is not like ordinary half-magical artifacts. Its internal spiritual power is exceptionally dense, thus it can't be reforged or advanced into a magical tool in the usual way," Yuan Ming said.
Hearing this, the Three Cave Masters nodded in agreement.
"Mu He is not wrong. When I made this Green Fish Sword, I was over-ambitious, and put a lot of effort into gathering several high-grade spiritual materials. I wanted to create a top-grade magical tool, but unfortunately, I missed the last piece, the thousand-year-old ice crystal, and never found it. In my impatience, I ended up creating this half-magical artifact, the Green Fish Sword," the Three Cave Masters said with some regret.
Yuan Ming felt somewhat disheartened upon hearing this.
He was aware of the reputation of the thousand-year-old ice crystal, having come across many references to this precious material in the books about spiritual materials in Biluo Cave, where it was often described as the ideal choice for refining top-grade magical tools with a cold attribute.
Considering the status and cultivation of the Three Cave Masters, if even they could not find such a treasure, Yuan Ming, a mere Qi Refining Stage Cultivator, certainly had no chance.
Seeing the change in Yuan Ming's expression, the Three Cave Masters knew what he was thinking and spoke up, "If you simply wish to enhance the Green Fish Sword to the level of a magical tool, you could try to find some cold attribute low-level ores. If you manage to find suitable materials, I can help you with the refinement."
"Three Cave Masters, you would help me refine it?" Yuan Ming could hardly believe his luck upon receiving this unexpected news.
"Don't be too quick to rejoice. I'm willing to refine the Green Fish Sword for you, but there are conditions," the Three Cave Masters said.
"Please speak," Yuan Ming nodded, feeling that this seemed reasonable.
"There are many special spiritual materials in White Deer Hill that are difficult to come by in the outside world. I've heard that Sang Yan, a disciple of the Black Fire Sect, brought back White Flame Gold. This time, I need you to keep an eye on this disciple of the Black Fire Sect. She will certainly look for such materials again. Find an opportunity to take her storage bag," the Three Cave Masters said.
"Three Cave Masters, what is this person's strength? Will there be other members from the Black Fire Sect helping her?" Yuan Ming asked, contemplatively.
"She's only around the Qi Refining Eighth Level, and your Green Fish Sword will be more than enough to deal with her," the Three Cave Masters said.
"If that is the case, I will give it my all," Yuan Ming said.
"Also, Chen Wan has overestimated her abilities and decided to participate in the gathering. She has already gone into seclusion in order to prepare. When the time comes, you both should support each other and make sure this task is accomplished," the Three Cave Masters continued.
"Of course," Yuan Ming nodded.
"Well then, now go and try to find the spiritual materials. If you can complete the refining before the White Deer Hill gathering, that would be ideal," the Three Cave Masters said.
After thanking the Three Cave Masters, Yuan Ming left with Huo Chan'er.
That night, coinciding with the appearance of Silver Cat Xi Ying, he took the opportunity to ask some questions about the cultivation of the Moonlight Technique and also informed her of the White Deer Hill gathering.
She seemed to have already been aware of it and, dismissing the event as "child's play, in which I have no interest," she turned and vanished into the night.
Knowing Silver Cat's personality all too well, Yuan Ming didn't mind and proceeded with his own cultivation.
For the first time in a long while, Huo Chan'er felt a sense of comfort and instinctively aimed to burrow into Yuan Ming's arms.
But as it drew close, it suddenly came to its senses and guiltily glanced towards the window.
Even though it didn't see Silver Cat Xi Ying, in the end, it just settled down beside Yuan Ming's legs and lay down.
...
The next day.
Early in the morning, Yuan Ming made a trip to Gui Cang Pavilion, where he used his remaining contribution points to exchange for two sets of magic.
One of them was named "Green Sword Skill," a mid-level Qi Refinement spell, which was an advanced version of the Wood Stabbing Technique. Similar to its predecessor, it also involved releasing wooden thorns, except that it no longer required condensation from trees or the ground.
Instead, one simply had to channel their mana, and sharp wooden thorns could be conjured from thin air, and projected through the void, much like controlling a flying sword, with both power and speed being quite impressive.
The other spell was a low-level defensive magic named "Wood Shield Skill."
When casting this spell, one would also need to condense mana, and through a special circulation method, release it from the palm and fingertips to form a green round shield with a diameter of three feet.
When the round shield was deployed, its surface would glow with a green light, showing a layer of wood grain texture; it looked just like a verdant wooden shield and could defend against attacks from mid and low-level Qi Refinement spells.
After obtaining the spells, Yuan Ming began to practice them diligently.
Since he already had a foundation with the Wood Stabbing Technique, the learning of the Green Sword Skill went quite smoothly. In just three short days, Yuan Ming had essentially mastered it.
On the other hand, the Wood Shield Skill took much more of Yuan Ming's energy to cultivate.
Although it was only a low-level defensive spell, executing it was not easy; it required strict control of the flow and output of mana. The mana output from the fingers had to be even, or else it would be difficult to form a complete shield.
If the shield was unbalanced, its defensive effect would be greatly diminished.
This version is sourced from MV3L3MPYR.
Eventually, after nearly half a month, Yuan Ming finally mastered this technique. However, it was then that he received a message from Chen Wan saying that the Three Cave Masters had exited seclusion.
In the evening, Yuan Ming went to the back mountain and returned Huo Chan'er to the Three Cave Masters.
Seeing that he had not yet found the spiritual materials needed to refine the Green Fish Sword Magic Artifact, and that he hadn't requested any contribution points as a reward, the latter simply gifted Yuan Ming the storage bag and the spiritual beast bag that had been lent to him earlier.
After thanking him, Yuan Ming left the Fire Refining Hall.
In a valley near the peak of the Refining Furnace Hall, Yuan Ming met with Wulu.
Previously, in order to avoid suspicion, Yuan Ming had not visited Wulu even when he returned from his travels outside.
After coming out of seclusion this time, he had intentionally paid attention to the news of the Beast Slave Hall and the Beast Taming Hall, seeing that both sides had been quiet, before he actively arranged to meet Wulu.
The first time Yuan Ming saw Wulu, he was somewhat surprised.
Before him, Wulu was wearing the ensemble of a registered disciple from the Beast Taming Hall, his face adorned with a faint smile, his whole aura having undergone a tremendous change.
"Brother Yuan, why do you look at me in such a manner?" Wulu was the first to laugh proudly.
"Brother Wulu has changed so much that I almost didn't recognize you," Yuan Ming said.
"After Kun Tu's death, Elder Meng Shan took notice of me. Seeing that my aptitude was passable, he smoothly filled the vacancy and I managed to become a registered disciple through adept work. I'll have to ask for Brother Yuan's care in the future," Wulu said.
"Congratulations, congratulations. You really have genuine ability. In the future, I may have to ask Brother Wulu to take care of me," Yuan Ming said politely.
"Brother Yuan is too modest. I have something to tell you; that sudden incident last time, where Brother Kun Tu died unexpectedly, even after the sect's investigation, nothing came out of it, and it was left unresolved. Now that more than half a year has passed, it's probably hard to find the perpetrator," Wulu added.
"What should we do about this? Aren't we still going to be uneasy when we go out on sect duties?" Yuan Ming pretended to be alarmed, but the stone in his heart had completely settled.
"What's there to worry about? I think the sect won't send us out for a while, and everyone can comfortably cultivate for some time," Wulu said with a smile instead.
Yuan Ming nodded in understanding.
"Brother Yuan, the White Deer Hill Alliance is about to begin. Will you participate?" Wulu changed the subject and asked.
"I am indeed planning to attend, how about you?" Yuan Ming replied.
"You're really going? I thought after your last brush with danger, you wouldn't take the risk again," Wulu said, surprised.
"To improve oneself, some risks are necessary," Yuan Ming said with a wry smile.
"That's true. I'm also planning to try my luck this time. Relying on the sect's offerings, how can one advance? We'll have to look after each other when the time comes," Wulu nodded and spoke with a smile.
"With Brother Wulu's careful planning, where would you need my care?" Yuan Ming glanced at him and remarked.
After the last incident, Yuan Ming had realized that Wulu's identity might not be simple. That level of insight, skill, and temperament were not something someone from a wild man's background could possess.
"Brother Yuan doesn't know. I've inquired with those who have been there before and found out that in past alliances, not only do the Five Great Sects fight and incur casualties among themselves, even our own people will fight over external possessions. Therefore, before this alliance, the sect will gather all participating disciples and establish rules; even the Great Elder may come forward," Wulu explained.
"I see, how can there be infighting among sect disciples, the elders indeed need to take care of this," Yuan Ming said indignantly, yet this was news that the Three Cave Masters had not mentioned.

chapters.title: Chapter 161 - 141: Patterns
chapters.content:
"Fellow disciples killing each other, bloodshed between father and son, sibling rivalry—it is all too normal," Wulu said, dismissing it with nonchalance.
"Brother Wulu, why the sudden sentimentality?" Yuan Ming asked, puzzled.
"Haha, it's nothing, just some old memories that came to mind. Speaking of which, where are you headed, Brother Yuan? If there's anything I can help with, do not hesitate to let me know," Wulu chuckled, swiftly changing the subject with a smile.
"Brother Wulu has many connections, and those you've befriended are indeed of a higher status than myself. In fact, there is something I would like to trouble you with," Yuan Ming replied, taking the opportunity.
"But speak, Brother Yuan, as long as it is within my power, I will certainly lend my support," Wulu's expression tightened slightly, unsure if the other had missed the perfunctory tone or was doing so on purpose, but he quickly continued with a smile.
"Hehe, no need to be nervous, Brother Wulu. I just wanted to inquire if you know where to procure some high-quality Frost Attribute spiritual materials," Yuan Ming asked with a chuckle.
"It seems Brother Yuan is looking to refine a Magic Artifact! However, as a mere newly registered disciple, I'm afraid I'm of no help. If even the Sect's Qingfu Hall doesn't have them, you might try your luck in the outside market," Wulu said, his demeanor relaxing as if he had let out a sigh of relief.
"Market?" Yuan Ming said, surprised.
"It's essentially a trading spot where loose cultivators and some sect cultivators gather, similar to the previously mentioned Toad Valley, but with a mix of good and bad, real and fake items. With some luck, you might find the spiritual materials you seek," Wulu explained.
"How can I find such a place?" Yuan Ming inquired further.
"According to what I know, the nearest one from here is the Black Rock City Market. Isn't the White Deer Hill alliance meeting about to start soon? It's considered a major decennial event of the Five Sects of the Southern Border and Northern Territory, and I expect it will be quite lively there soon," Wulu pondered before answering.
"Brother Wulu truly is experienced and knowledgeable; thank you for sharing this," Yuan Ming said, not expecting that his casual question would be so fruitfully answered.
"Hehe, it's just a small matter, not worth mentioning! Honestly, I've only heard about it, and with my status, I'm likely to be looked down upon there. If you decide to go, Brother Yuan, be careful on the road," Wulu added, his tone growing serious as he advised.
"Thank you for the pointer; I will keep that in mind," Yuan Ming responded earnestly.
After asking Wulu for directions to Black Rock City, the two parted ways.
...
Upon returning to his quarters.
Yuan Ming closed the doors and windows, summoned the incense burner, and lit a stick of Black Incense, placing it inside.
Having resolved to make attending the White Deer Hill alliance meeting a top priority, he knew he needed to use the time wisely to maximize his powers.
Besides attempting to truly refine the Green Fish Sword into a Magic Artifact, he was still filled with anticipation for the incense possession, attempting it once every seven days.
As the green smoke curled upwards, Yuan Ming's vision began to blur, yet his Divine Thought remained exceptionally clear.
In his mind, he meticulously recalled the face of the Emperor of Da Jin, sketching out his features bit by bit, paying close attention to every detail, continuously whispering a name to himself, "Liu Tianming."
Liu Tianming was indeed the name of the Emperor.
Since advancing to the second level of the Moonlight Technique, Yuan Ming's Divine Soul Power had also increased, and fragments of memories started to emerge in his mind, though they remained somewhat scattered and incomplete.
Yuan Ming needed time to sort through these fragments to piece them together.
It was in these memories that Yuan Ming saw his past as a study companion to the young Emperor and learned his name.
The next moment, his consciousness plunged into darkness and then brightened again.
The surroundings were dim, the air filled with the scent of vegetation, and Yuan Ming's vision, through his host's body, only saw an open area ahead, densely vegetated everywhere.
In his direct line of sight, about twenty-five yards away on an open patch of ground, stood a wooden dummy clad in full armor, human-height, with a target hung on its chest, and nothing else within several yards around it.
"Your Majesty, everything is ready; we can begin," a shrill voice spoke from the side.Chаptеr sоurсе: Мy Virtuаl Librаry Еmpirе (М|V|L4ЕМРYR).
"Everyone, stand back; I am about to perform the technique," a familiar young voice declared.
"Great, it worked!"
Yuan Ming was overjoyed inside, just as he had speculated, he had once again possessed the body of the young Emperor.
The next instant, the young Emperor assumed a horse stance and began to chant the mnemonic.
Seizing this rare opportunity, Yuan Ming immediately concentrated, beginning to feel the flow and changes of Mana within the body of the young Emperor.
Each of these immersive, firsthand experiences was a precious treasure for him, greatly facilitating his own understanding and mastery of the Burning Explosion Skill, allowing him to bypass many detours.
The fingers of the young Emperor stretched out, a firelight ignited at the fingertips, a hot power gathering, and a fist-sized Fireball with flickering flames began to expand, soon reaching the size of a human head.
At the same time, the Emperor's mana in his Dantian also began to deplete rapidly.
However, unlike last time, just before his mana was about to run out, the Emperor decisively shouted, "Go."
The fireball then "whooshed" out of his fingertips, shooting towards a wooden dummy seven or eight zhang away, hitting the target squarely.
There was a loud "boom."
Intense flames soared into the sky, and the armor on the wooden dummy detonated violently, scattering pieces of various sizes along with countless sparks in all directions. The dummy itself burst open from the immense impact.
A powerful current of air also exploded, impacting everything in all directions.
The surrounding flowers and plants, several zhang away, were also affected, toppling over from the central point of the exploded dummy.
"What immense power!" Yuan Ming felt a surge of excitement inside. The Burning Explosion Skill that the Emperor had cast, exhausting all his mana, was quite a bit stronger than his own.
Once the aftermath had dissipated, a large group of eunuchs and palace maids rushed over from all directions, carrying copper basins and wooden buckets to extinguish the scattered sparks.
"Good, good, good..." Just then, a series of clapping sounds approached, followed by three praises.
Upon hearing this, the Emperor turned around, and Yuan Ming's gaze also shifted to look behind him.
He saw a gaunt old Taoist priest dressed in an Eight Diagrams Cloud Pattern Purple Gold Taoist Robe, wearing a golden silk lotus treasure crown, coming their way, his hand touching the three long whiskers on his chest.
He did not seem to walk fast, but the two small eunuchs following him were panting and could hardly keep up.
Yuan Ming recognized him at a glance—it was none other than Master Yu Hu, the State Preceptor who had taught the Emperor the Nine Elements Technique.
"State Preceptor," the Emperor greeted with a smile.
"Hehe, Your Majesty is talented and diligent in cultivation. You've made quick progress..." Master Yu Hu stopped in front of the Emperor and spoke.
"I have much to improve still. I hope the State Preceptor will not hesitate to give guidance," the Emperor said. Although he spoke modestly, Yuan Ming could feel the thrill and slight pride inside him.
Hearing this, Master Yu Hu's face showed hesitation, as if he indeed had something to say.
Yuan Ming was about to focus and listen when, before Master Yu Hu's response could arrive, his consciousness sank and he plunged into darkness.
When his Divine Soul returned to his body, he looked at the incense burner before him, his eyes still brimming with excitement—not for any other reason, but because he had sensed an important rule regarding incense possession.
Incense possession indeed was not entirely random; it was closely related to his mental state, or perhaps his intentions.
Reflecting on it, Yuan Ming initially possessed the Emperor because he was facing difficulties in the Ten Thousand Mountains, desperately wanting to cultivate mana, and a strong will naturally emerged from his heart, as if making a vow, and the incense burner fulfilled that desire by granting him the Nine Elements Technique.
Afterward, when he possessed the body of Wang Shun, the coachman at the General Mansion, it was due to his past and his longing for home. This seemed more like a subconscious pull rather than an active guidance of his mind.
In the times that followed, he almost always ended up in bodies within the General Mansion, driven by the unchanged desires of his subconscious, though the specific person he possessed was not precise.
The experiences of possessing Wang Shun twice and the Emperor twice allowed Yuan Ming to further conjecture about some rules of possession.
However, his initial experiments had not been successful.
This time, Yuan Ming's thoughts were firm, focused entirely on the Emperor, making his intentions even purer.
Furthermore, after cultivating the Second Level of the Moon Technique, his memory had mostly recovered; he not only remembered the Emperor's name but also recalled many related memories.
This was probably the key to his successful possession of the Emperor this time.
Besides, the Black Incense inserted in the incense burner likely not only affected the success of the possession, but the duration and effects of the possession as well.
At least when he used the three original Black Incenses that came with the incense burner, not only did they last quite long, but he could also completely control the body of the person he possessed, though he did not know what changes occurred to the possessed person at the time and whether there would be some effects afterward?
Of course, these were just the differences he could perceive at the moment. His intuition told him that the Mysterious Incense Burner and Black Incense probably had many more secrets that he was yet to learn.
Especially its effects on repairing and nurturing the Divine Soul, not only did spirit beasts like Huo Chan'er relish it, even Silver Cat Xi Ying spent a lot of effort getting close to it.
The unique effects of the incense burner could greatly mitigate the backlash that powerful Soul Cultivators like himself often faced, making it a heavenly object for someone like him.
At this moment, Yuan Ming's mind was cluttered, and he couldn't calm down.
He closed his eyes and activated the Moonlight Technique to calm his inner turmoil. After a period equivalent to thirty minutes, he finally managed to suppress those thoughts.
He opened his eyes and, with great care, began to slowly input mana into the incense burner, aiding the restoration of the Tai Chi Diagram.

chapters.title: Chapter 162 - 142 Five Sects of the North Territory
chapters.content:
Three days later, one clear morning.
Yuan Ming casually accepted a task to find spiritual materials at the Execution Hall, then bid farewell to Fang Ge and left Biluo Cave's gate, heading toward the northeast.
After he was far from the gate, he murmured incantations, and a layer of air-like azure light surrounded his body, making him exceptionally light. With a gentle touch on the ground, he could leap forward several meters.
This was the Wind Swift Skill he had acquired from the Fire Summoning Place. He had practiced it during his spare time in the past two days and had already grasped the basics.
Such spells were generally not something one would spend time mastering thoroughly; instead, they could gradually improve proficiency through daily use while traveling.
With this skill, Yuan Ming's traveling speed had significantly increased. He could now travel nearly 300 li a day, and at night, he would simply find a nearby mortal town to stay, meditate, and cultivate.
A few days later, at noon, he arrived at the entrance to a remote valley located about a hundred li from the nearest mortal town.
The valley looked lush and verdant; a thick white mist permeated the entrance. Perhaps because the mountains on either side were too tall and blocked out the sunlight, looking from afar, the valley was always shrouded in a large shadow. Besides this, there was truly nothing remarkable about it.
Yuan Ming arrived at the entrance of the valley, paused briefly, then stepped forward and plunged into the white fog.
After progressing for only 15 minutes, the scene before him suddenly cleared, and a fairly large town appeared before his eyes. The fog that had been pervasive earlier had already dispersed.
The buildings in this town were all constructed of a type of black rock. At first glance, they seemed somewhat disordered, but they faintly centered around the valley, clustering into a circular formation resembling a giant black boulder.
Seeing this, a slight smile appeared on Yuan Ming's face.
This was the Black Rock City that Wulu had mentioned, not an ordinary mortal town but a town of cultivators. The mist outside the valley was to prevent ordinary mortals from mistakenly wandering in.
Before setting out, he had even taken some time to consult the Gui Cang Pavilion for records about this town, knowing that its location was quite special, situated at the intersection of the territories of Biluo Cave, Green Rock Association, and Black Fire Sect, and at a respectable distance from the other two sects; thus, it was initially established to facilitate the commute of cultivators from various sects.
Over time, as cultivators from the Southern Domain and Central Plains, as well as some loose cultivators, came here, the town gradually flourished, becoming a rather famous market in the Northern Territory.
It was said that this market currently did not belong to any of the Five Sects of the Northern Territory; instead, it was owned by an ancient cultivation family which dispatched a city lord to govern it.
This family was very mysterious and low-profile, so much so that few in the Northern Territory knew where it hailed from, but people from the Five Sects dared not show the slightest disrespect and conducted their business in the city earnestly.
At this time, Yuan Ming was not dressed in the robes of a Biluo Cave disciple but wore a set of common attire from the Southern Border and a hat with a veil to cover his face.
The mix of characters inside Black Rock City meant that many, especially loose cultivators, dressed this way. He was simply following the crowd while also avoiding some troubles.
At the entrance of the town stood two guards, one tall and the other short, both clad in black armor and exuding a mana presence. Both were at least at the Qi Refining Fourth Level.
"Would you like to enter the city, sir? Please provide a spirit stone as the entry fee," the short, round-faced guard in black armor stopped Yuan Ming and politely said.
"Why is there an entry fee now?" Yuan Ming frowned slightly upon hearing this.
He did not have many spirit stones on him, and yet he was required to give one up before he had seen anything inside.
"Recently, the number of cultivators coming and going has increased. To reduce the chaos caused by idle folks in the city, we have temporarily required an entry fee. If you're unwilling, please turn back," said the tall, thin guard who resembled a bamboo pole, speaking indifferently.
"It's just one spirit stone, take it," Yuan Ming snorted and handed a fire attribute spirit stone to the round-faced guard.
The guard accepted the spirit stone and stepped aside, allowing Yuan Ming to enter the city.
This соntеnt wаs first rеlеаsеd оn МV_LЕМРYR.
He hadn't felt it from outside, but upon entering, Yuan Ming could sense the unique bustling atmosphere of Black Rock City.
Ahead was a slightly empty but wide black stone street that could accommodate three chariots from the mundane world abreast. The shops by the street had an ancient design, with very small doors and windows, resembling small fortresses.
It seemed these were shops selling goods, mostly mundane items like rice and flour, as well as insect food from the Southern Border. Many people were busy inside, all of them ordinary mortals without mana.
Every now and then, a beast cart would leave a shop, carrying various kinds of food supplies into the city.
Yuan Ming was not surprised by this; cultivators are essentially beings of flesh and blood too. Before reaching the stage where they can fast, they also need to eat and drink; especially low-level cultivators who had just reached the Qi Refining Tenth Layer and could only maintain fasting for a month or so.
The ordinary people on the street seemed accustomed to the presence of cultivators and ignored Yuan Ming's arrival, continuing with their activities.
Yuan Ming walked to the end of Black Stone Street, where a broader street appeared before him.
The shops on both sides were also lined up here, larger than those at the entrance, with windows and doors proportioned almost normally. At first glance, it was evident that the shops here sold cultivators' items.
There were quite a few cultivators coming and going, but the street was spacious and did not feel crowded. The sounds of talking and hawking rose and fell, mingling into waves of noise that stimulated one's ears.
"Come and see, Blackback Lizard brains, one spirit stone per bottle!"
"Selling green jade, two spirit stones per catty!"
"Bloodwing Bat livers, eating them enhances eyesight, only two spirit stones per catty!"
Almost every shop had an attendant standing at the doorway calling out to passersby, no different from the vendors in the mundane world.
Yuan Ming looked around curiously, especially at the items inside the shops on either side.
He had been in Biluo Cave for some time, and along the way, he had some opportunities, obtaining classics on spiritual materials such as "Herborist" and "Record of Strange Stones," and he was quite confident in identifying spiritual materials. However, the variety of goods in the Black Stone Street Market was vast, and many of them were still unheard of, which opened his eyes considerably along the way.
"It seems I should visit such markets more often, if only to broaden my knowledge," Yuan Ming thought excitedly.
"Selling spiritual beasts! We have flying spiritual beasts, water element spiritual beasts, don't miss out!" a voice as loud as a cracked gong came from ahead, brimming with enthusiasm and drawing sideways glances from nearby people.
"That voice..." Yuan Ming looked startled and looked ahead.
Not far ahead, a large shop appeared, occupying a substantial space, featuring white walls and green tiles, standing out from the surrounding shops like a crane among chickens.
Through the wide-open doors, a portion of the interior could be seen. Many cages housed various fierce beasts, and the one calling out at the doorway was a round-faced youth with bushy eyebrows and big eyes—his old acquaintance, Zhao Tong.
"Is that him? What's he doing running a shop in Black Rock City?" Yuan Ming was quite surprised.
His gaze then moved upward to the shop sign above the door, which bore three large characters in gold on a white background: "Biluo Shop."
"Biluo Shop? They're selling spiritual beasts, and with Zhao Tong attracting business, this shop must be an official enterprise of Biluo Cave," Yuan Ming thought to himself, his heart still not quite settled.
He had known that Biluo Cave had businesses in Black Rock City, but he hadn't expected them to be selling spiritual beasts.
The Biluo Cave was renowned in the North Territory for beast taming. Spiritual beasts were fundamental to the Biluo Cave, yet they were also willing to sell them in Black Rock City?
Yuan Ming, of course, didn't know that the daily expenses of the sect were substantial, and the various resources and spiritual materials needed were not minor. Biluo Cave could not be completely self-sufficient; it needed frequent interactions with the outside world, and the shops set up in various markets were among its significant channels and sources of income.
In the face of absolute benefits and needs, selling the sect's foundational spiritual beasts was quite normal, albeit not cheap.
Spiritual beasts from the Biluo Cave were very popular, and people were frequently drawn inside. Most of those who came out were smiling, with an extra Spiritual Beast Bag at their waist.
Yuan Ming already had a Black Toad and had no intention of buying another spiritual beast. Under these circumstances, he had even less intention to catch up with Zhao Tong and passed by as if nothing was unusual.
After a few medium-small shops, another large shop appeared ahead. The doorway was deserted, hanging a signboard that read "Black Fire Pavilion" in three large characters.
"Black Fire Pavilion? Could it be like the Biluo Shop, a property of Black Fire Sect in this city?" Yuan Ming looked inside the Black Fire Pavilion.
The layout inside the Black Fire Pavilion greatly differed from ordinary shops. Looking in through the door, only a few cabinets could be seen, and it wasn't clear what the shop was selling.
Yuan Ming summoned his Divine Sense and quickly scanned the inside.
Inside the Black Fire Pavilion, like the Biluo Shop, there were many sealed cages and cabinets, not enclosing spiritual beasts, but refining corpses and housing ghosts.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming had no more doubts.
The Black Fire Sect excelled in controlling refined corpses and nurturing ghosts; this Black Fire Pavilion must undoubtedly be a property of the Black Fire Sect.
"Biluo Cave and Black Fire Sect both have shops here; the other three sects of the Southern Border and Northern Territory—Hundred Poison Cave, Beast King Sect, and Green Rock Association—probably also have shops here," Yuan Ming thought to himself.
From the information he had hastily reviewed before leaving about the Five Sects of the North Territory, the Black Fire Sect, adept at controlling refined corpses and banishing ghosts, was the strongest. The strength of the other four sects was comparable.
The Hundred Poison Cave specialized in using poison, particularly skilled in taming various poisonous creatures, which had some similarities to the beast-taming skills of the Biluo Cave.
The Beast King Sect excelled in tattooing secret techniques that enhanced physical strength, favoring close combat.
As for the Green Rock Association located in the Kasi Clan's territory, it was quite special. This sect occupied the largest spirit stone mine in the Southern Border and Northern Territory and was the wealthiest among the Five Sects.
The Green Rock Association was the newest among them, initially a large trading company that maintained a long-term trade relationship with sects like Biluo Cave. After forming a sect, it expanded its spirit stone business to other regions of the Southern Border and even to Central Plains Da Jin.
In terms of cultivation techniques and secret skills, the Green Rock Association had nothing unique. The cultivation methods practiced by the disciples of the association were all focused on utilizing spirit stones, either bought or secretly learned from the other four sects. Since they started trading with Da Jin, they also learned the spells of Central Plains, making it a sect with a mixture of various traditions.
Although the other four sects were not pleased with this, they all needed the spirit stones from the Green Rock Association, so they turned a blind eye, maintaining a peaceful coexistence over the years.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 - 143: Came to the Right Place
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming left the Black Fire Pavilion and took a stroll around the area, soon discovering the shops set up by the Hundred Poison Cave, Beast King Sect, and Green Rock Association, all concentrated in this district. He had a preliminary understanding of the situation here.
As a Sect founded on a merchant guild, Green Rock Association operated the largest store among the Five Sects, selling a wide variety of items, mainly various grades of spiritual materials, to attract the passing cultivators.
The shop of Hundred Poison Cave sold various deadly poisons and precious poisonous insects.
As for the Beast King Sect, a body-refining sect, it sold body-tempering spiritual liquids, elixirs, and so on, being the smallest in scale.
Yuan Ming was quite interested in the deadly poisons from Hundred Poison Cave and the body-tempering elixirs from Beast King Sect, but his finances were tight. Since he came here to look for frost spiritual materials, he focused on finding this item first and decided that other things could wait until later.
"I've recently been preoccupied with studying the incense burner. Once I wrap up these matters, I need to find a way to earn more Spirit Stones," Yuan Ming thought to himself.
Before he came to this market, he hadn't realized how important Spirit Stones were. Only upon arriving here did he discover that everything was priced in Spirit Stones, which could not only buy all sorts of rare spiritual materials but could even be used to commission other cultivators to do things.
It seemed that in the cultivation world, with Spirit Stones, one could indeed do whatever they wished.
With this thought, Yuan Ming stepped into the three-story building housing the Qingyan Shop.
The first floor of the shop was spacious with numerous counters lined up neatly with various types of spiritual materials, dazzling to the eyes.
Customers either wandered alone or in small groups, continuously weaving through the counters.
Yuan Ming looked around briefly and made his way directly to a counter.
In Qingyan Shop, spiritual materials were arranged by attribute, and the counter he approached displayed water attribute materials.
A man with black whiskers stood behind the counter, engaged in a fierce price negotiation with a short and plump young man of a genial appearance over two blue Spirit Grasses.
In such a large shop, the rule of first come, first served was observed. Yuan Ming stood by patiently, not interrupting.
The short and plump young man was an expert in bidding, eloquent and astute. After a barrage of aggressive haggling that left the whiskered man unable to retort, the latter reluctantly agreed to the young man's price.
Yuan Ming watched with amazement. He had always considered his own speaking skills to be decent, but compared to this short and plump young man, he was far inferior.
The young man, at the mere Qi Refining Third and Fourth Level, had such impressive eloquence. Yuan Ming wondered how he had developed it, as the cultivation world truly contained all kinds of people.
The young man left with satisfaction, materials in hand.
"Esteemed customer, are you looking to buy some spiritual materials?" the whiskered man noticed Yuan Ming waiting and awkwardly asked.
"Do you have any frost attribute spiritual materials in your shop?" Yuan Ming didn't beat around the bush and went straight to the point.
"Oh, you are knowledgeable, customer! You've come to the right place! Speaking of frost materials, they are indeed rare items. Other stores might not have them, but our Qingyan Shop naturally does," said the man with black whiskers, his voice tinged with unabashed pride.
"Regarding the grade, do you have mid-grade ones?" Yuan Ming asked, also excited, hope shining in his eyes.
According to the Three Cave Masters, the higher the grade of the frost attribute spiritual material, the better it would meet the Green Fish Sword's advancement requirements.
"Just getting a few frost spiritual materials cost our shop a considerable amount; we don't have mid-grade frost spiritual materials for the time being," the whiskered man's smile stiffened and then turned to a slight embarrassment as he shook his head.
Yuan Ming felt quite disappointed, but he didn't mind too much as he hadn't expected to find them at the first shop he visited, and he had other purposes for coming here.
"Do you purchase spiritual materials here?" he didn't leave, instead asking another question.
"Of course, we buy! We offer fair prices and treat young and old equally. Esteemed customer, if you have any exceptional items, we can sit in a private room inside and discuss in detail," said the man with black whiskers.
A quarter of an hour later, Yuan Ming walked out of the Qingyan Shop, a smile appearing beneath his wide-brimmed hat.
He sold off the spiritual materials he had obtained from Hu Huo and Kun Tu, as well as materials he had saved up before, excluding a few he needed, all in exchange for over thirty Spirit Stones.
With his original savings, Yuan Ming now had a total of seventy Spirit Stones in his possession.
This was a considerable fortune for a Qi Refining Stage Cultivator who had just entered the cultivation world less than two years ago.
Based on his research beforehand, the typical value of a mid-grade spiritual material was around forty to fifty Spirit Stones. Even if frost spiritual materials were more precious, seventy Spirit Stones should be more than enough.
Yuan Ming proceeded, soon spotting another seemingly respectable spiritual material shop and stepping in.
Less than half an hour later, he walked out and continued on.
A two hours passed quickly.
In a tavern in the market, Yuan Ming sat at a window-side seat on the second floor, silently eating his meal and not seeming to be in the best of moods.
During that two hours, he had asked seven or eight small shops selling spiritual materials, but he still had nothing to show for it.
Black Rock City was one of the biggest markets in the Southern Border and Northern Territory, and if he couldn't find the frost spiritual materials he needed here, it would likely be in vain to look elsewhere.
Yuan Ming was secretly anxious, considering his next move for the afternoon.
The footsteps clattered from the stairwell, and two figures walked in.
