He looked regretfully at the other two gems on the belt; if those stones were also inscribed with Light Body Runes, he could only imagine how formidable the belt's acceleration effect would be.
Although only one gem was intact, it was enough for his use.
The only problem now was that the belt belonged to Sang Yan and wearing it outside posed a risk of being noticed by the people of the Black Fire Sect.
However, this wouldn't stump him. With a proper disguise, there should be no issues.
Yuan Ming wore the belt inside his clothes and covered it with his robe. He then gathered the Storage Bags from the five Loose Cultivators who had died at the hands of the Snake King before turning to leave for Bai Ye.
Huan Shi had also regained consciousness by now. His look towards Yuan Ming was complex, as he evidently had learned everything from Bai Ye.
Seeing that Yuan Ming did not touch the corpses of the ten members of his alliance, Bai Ye inwardly sighed with relief, and his opinion of Yuan Ming greatly improved.
"Fellow Daoist Hagon, you have hidden depths. I'm impressed," Bai Ye said, cupping his hands in salute.
"You flatter me, I took a risk just now," Yuan Ming said, blinking.
"What I admire even more is your righteousness," Bai Ye said, saluting with his hands again.
"Now that there is no longer a threat outside, you should be able to handle your injuries on your own. I shall take my leave," Yuan Ming said, and then turned to leave.
"Fellow Daoist Hagon, please wait a moment," Bai Ye suddenly spoke.
"Alliance Leader Bai Ye, do you have anything else?" Yuan Ming turned back to look.
"Fellow Daoist Hagon, you killed both Golden Flower Snake Kings. I was wondering if their Snake Pearls are still with you?" Bai Ye hesitated before asking.
"There is one left. What do you want with it, Alliance Leader Bai Ye?" Yuan Ming asked, nodding slightly.
"To be honest, our White Night Scatter Alliance was commissioned by Eastern Domain White Dragon Island to hunt the Golden Flower Snake Kings and obtain a Snake Pearl. I am willing to offer two thousand Spirit Stones to purchase the Snake Pearl from you. Would you be willing to part with it?" Bai Ye hurriedly said.
"A Snake Pearl doesn't seem to be worth that many Spirit Stones. Besides, as far as I know, the Young Master of White Dragon Island is already dead," Yuan Ming slowly said. Although he had never sold a Golden Flower Snake Pearl, he had seen similar Second-level Fierce Beast Spiritual Materials in the Black Rock City Market, worth at most a thousand Spirit Stones. Bai Ye was willing to pay double the price.
"Although the Young Master of White Dragon Island is dead, this matter involves the reputation of our alliance, and I hope you can part with it," Bai Ye said with a wry smile. What he left unsaid was that without the Snake Pearl, it would be impossible to make up for the alliance's losses.
Yuan Ming nodded, produced the Snake Pearl from the Single-Horned Snake King, and tossed it over.
Bai Ye quickly caught it and presented two thousand Spirit Stones.
"One thousand three hundred is enough," Yuan Ming only took one thousand three hundred Spirit Stones.
He felt somewhat fond of the alliance leader, viewing a potential connection favorably. The other party had suffered heavy losses, and based on his own personality, he was not one to kick someone when they were down. Since staying in Biluo Cave wasn't a long-term plan, perhaps Alliance Leader Bai Ye could be useful in the future.
"I said two thousand, and it cannot be less," Bai Ye insisted.
"No need, both of you take care," Yuan Ming said with a slight bow, and then his figure flickered and vanished like the wind.
Bai Ye was shocked. During the earlier battle, Hagon hadn't shown such speed. Could it be that he still had reserves during the fierce battle?
If that were truly the case, the potential of this Qi Refining Stage Cultivator was too great!
"Big brother, can you tell where this person comes from..." Huan Shi couldn't help but ask.
Bai Ye gave Huan Shi a look, indicating him to be quiet.
Realizing his blunder, Huan Shi quickly shut his mouth.
Only after a good while, when they felt Yuan Ming was far enough away, did they begin to speak again.
"Hagon saved us not once but twice. Once we get back to Black Rock City, let's not look into his background, and don't mention him to anyone. We'll tell the master of the White Dragon Island that we obtained the Snake Pearl through a fierce battle by the whole alliance!" Bai Ye said.
"Understood. But it may be troublesome if the Black Fire Sect investigates," Huan Shi nodded.
"What's so troublesome about that? With so much miasma in the valley, everyone was scattered. Who knows where they went, and the dead weren't our doing," Bai Ye said.
"That's true," Huan Shi agreed.
"Second brother, I'm sorry. The Foundation Establishment Pill you painstakingly prepared for Tuozhe—under the urgent circumstances, I gave it to Hagon to reciprocate for his earlier assistance," Bai Ye said.
"Zhe'er has already perished, even if the Foundation Establishment Pill is still intact, he can't use it anymore," Huan Shi sadly said.
"This mission cost us so many hands, and the Purple Flame Flag was also damaged; it's all my fault. I really shouldn't have been greedy and accepted this mission," Bai Ye slowly stood up, looking towards where the members of the White Night Scatter Alliance had fallen, his face filled with regret.
"Elder brother, you don't need to blame yourself so much. I agreed to the mission too, and we took the deposit. Who could have foreseen that there would be two Snake Kings in this place, one of which was on the verge of progressing to the Flood Dragon stage. Luckily, the mission is already complete, and the generous reward from White Dragon Island can somewhat compensate for the losses. We'll do our best to make amends to the families of the fallen when we return," Huan Shi consoled.
Bai Ye shook his head with a bitter smile. Most of the participants in this mission were core members of the White Night Scatter Alliance. The death of each one was a tremendous loss, something that could not be made up for with mere wealth.
"Sigh, how is your recovery coming along? Let's leave as soon as possible!" He looked at Huan Shi.
Huan Shi leaned against the stone wall and slowly stood up.
The two picked up the storage bags scattered by their comrades and gathered the bodies, then made their way towards the exit.
A soul crow stood in the miasma ahead of Bai Ye and Huan Shi. It turned and flew away as they approached.
...
At this very moment, an illusion burst out from the Snake King Cave, revealing Yuan Ming's figure.
He had overheard the conversation between the two through the soul crow and nodded slightly.
Yuan Ming returned to the cave from before, sealed it with the Four Directions Sealing Spirit Talisman, and continued cultivating and controlling his breathing.
After half a day, Yuan Ming's mana was fully restored, and the injuries caused by the previous magical battle had healed completely.
With a gentle pat of his hand, "whirr," a small pile of items appeared before him. It was the gold-plated gauze, along with the Bone Map, Sang Yan, and other people's magical artifacts, storage rings, storage bags, and more.
This content is hosted at *.
Yuan Ming first picked up the gold-plated gauze. Three fist-sized holes had been torn in its delicate fabric. Although the runes hadn't been destroyed, its power was greatly reduced.
This was something Xi Ying had lent him to use, and now that he had damaged it like this, he wondered if Xi Ying would be angry. He would have to find a way to restore it to its original condition.
The one-armed old man at the Black Rock City Ghost Market had mentioned that the gold-plated gauze was refined using gold-plated silk, soft gold stone, and refined iron as the main materials. He planned to try and collect these three materials after returning to his sect, and then find someone to see if it could be repaired.
He put away the gold-plated gauze and picked up the Black Needle Magical Artifact from the Bone Map.
In the world of cultivation, flying needle artifacts are small, making the inscription of runes difficult, and their refinement extremely challenging. But once successfully refined, they are quite powerful.
Yuan Ming activated his Divine Sense to examine it and his face lit up with joy.
This Black Needle was a formidable Mid-Grade Magical Artifact. The runes inscribed within included one for sharpness, and another he had not seen before which, by the feel of it, probably related to Concealment.
With its small size and the Concealment rune, it could be used to ambush others. Bone Map had tried to do just that, but unfortunately ran into Yuan Ming, a Qi Refining Realm junior whose Divine Soul was far superior to his peers, and whose ruse had been easily seen through.
Yuan Ming carefully stored the needle away and took the second magical artifact he had obtained from Bone Map—the Nine-Ring Gold Saber.
This saber was also a Mid-Grade Artifact, with two inscribed runes related to sharpness; its destructive power was significant. In terms of raw power, it was not inferior to the Cold Star Sword, but unfortunately, it lacked any special abilities.
Lastly, Yuan Ming picked up Bone Map's storage ring, and his expression became stiff as he probed it with his Divine Sense.
Almost nothing was left inside Bone Map's storage ring, save for two to thirty Low Grade Spirit Stones, a few ordinary spiritual materials, two worthless magical artifacts, and a jade scroll—it hadn't even used up one percent of its capacity.
Yuan Ming was thoroughly disappointed. He had hoped to earn a significant amount of wealth from the storied storage ring of a Foundation Establishment Elder from the Black Fire Sect, only to find that the man's fortune was so meager, he was practically a pauper.
What Yuan Ming did not know was that Bone Map had spent all his resources on refining the Black Needle Magical Artifact, which is why his storage ring was so empty.
The Black Needle, similar to the Cold Star Sword in appearance, was made from an exceptional primary material—a small chunk of Nine Heavens Meteorite Iron.
Nine Heavens Meteorite Iron, from the regions beyond the Outer Nine Heavens, had been tempered by the Nine Heavens Gang Wind, Power of the Sun, essence of the Yin, and even the power of starlight, resulting in an almost indestructible quality, making it a precious mineral fit for refining magical treasures.
Having come into possession of this material by chance, Bone Map lamented the meager quantity. After much consideration, he barely managed to refine a single flying needle from it.
Despite its small size, the Black Needle held great potential. Bone Map had intended to use the Black Needle as his Lifebound Magical Artifact, planning to advance it to a High Grade Magical Artifact and, upon reaching the Core Formation stage, even a magical treasure. He had spent all his savings to ask an Artifact Refining Master from the Black Fire Sect to refine this Flying Needle for him, but now all his effort would be to Yuan Ming's benefit.
Naturally, Yuan Ming was unaware of these details and turned his attention to the other items in Bone Map's storage ring.
The spiritual materials were common and worthless. He glanced at them and then moved on, turning his Divine Sense to inspect the two magical artifacts.
One was a gray short knife, identified as a Low Grade Magical Artifact with ordinary materials—it was clearly forgotten and neglected.
As for the other artifact, it was a black iron nail with a weak aura that also looked like a Low Grade Magical Artifact.
The black iron nail was smeared with some fresh blue-black gelatinous substance, as if it had just been pulled from somewhere, sticky and somewhat disturbing to look at.

chapters.title: Chapter 196 - 176: Unexpected Discovery
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming glanced at the iron nail a few times, and soon stopped paying attention to it, his gaze shifted to the last jade scroll.
He activated his Divine Sense to delve into it, and a pleased expression appeared on his face as he finally found something useful.
This jade scroll contained a cultivation technique known as "Ghost Spirit Skill," which, according to the description at the end, was a splendid inheritance of the Black Fire Sect. The scroll recorded mnemonics from the Qi Refinement Realm to the peak of the Foundation Establishment, having significant value.
The "Ghost Spirit Skill" also included some secret techniques for refining corpses and insights into corpse control, presumably written by the Bone Map. Yuan Ming truly broadened his horizons with the subtle refinements detailed within, and gained a preliminary understanding of the Black Fire Sect's corpse control secret techniques.
The corpse control secret technique of the Black Fire Sect, strictly speaking, was quite similar to the Corpse Control Divine Ability of the Moonlight Technique, both involving the sealing of a part of one's Divine Soul within the refined corpse to manipulate it.
However, the starting point for the Corpse Control Divine Ability of the Moonlight Technique was very high, requiring one to cultivate the Moonlight Technique to the second layer and possess an exceptionally strong Divine Soul to use it; whereas the threshold for the Black Fire Sect's corpse control secret technique was much lower, accessible even if the Divine Soul was not too weak.
The entry-level threshold for the Black Fire Sect's method of corpse control was low, but to control a refined corpse, it required a long period of sacrificial refining and adaptation. In the initial stages, it was very prone to backlash, far less convenient than the Moonlight Technique, which allowed immediate control.
Yuan Ming, without time to study in detail at this moment, put away the jade scroll and began to examine the storage bags of Sang Yan and the three others.
All four individuals were Qi Refining Stage Cultivators and seemed to lack powerful backgrounds within the Black Fire Sect, using only Low Grade Magical Artifacts with rather modest power, except for Sang Yan's pair of black gloves, which had some distinctive features.
These gloves were significantly different from ordinary magical artifacts; they contained an internal space about a meter in size, filled with a lot of Black Mist, which was actually dense corpse qi with strong toxicity.
Yuan Ming had seen Sang Yan use these gloves before to release the corpse qi within and attack enemies.
The structure of the black gloves was somewhat similar to that of storage magical tools, but unlike storage magical tools, the space in the gloves was very fragile and could only store gases such as mist and smoke.
These gloves could indeed be put to good use, but the toxicity of the corpse qi inside was too weak; it all needed to be discharged later to fill it with Black Toad poison mist instead.
Yuan Ming then took over the storage magical tools of Sang Yan and the three others, activating his Divine Sense to inspect them.
The four of them were not wealthy, their Spirit Stones totaling less than three hundred, and the other contents of the storage magical tools were quite ordinary too.
Yuan Ming's expression suddenly changed as he found a palm-sized grey pouch in Sang Yan's storage magical tool. The pouch, woven from special materials, emitted no trace of spiritual power, and was bulging with contents.
He untied the hemp rope of the small pouch, and a chicken egg-sized white mineral tumbled out, radiating a faint white light. Inside the mineral, a flame-like radiance floated, visible from the outside and rather magical.
His face lit up with joy; could these minerals be the White Flame Gold mentioned by the Three Cave Masters?
From its appearance and characteristics, it was very possible; the Three Cave Masters mentioned that Sang Yan had acquired some during the last alliance meeting at White Deer Hill, so it was not surprising to find them on him now.
After carefully putting away the White Flame Gold, Yuan Ming collected the items from the others and began to examine their Corpse Nourishing Bags.
The black-clothed woman, the youth with sword-like eyebrows, and the rugged man's Corpse Nourishing Bags all contained ordinary refined corpses, with combat power comparable only to Qi Refining Middle Stage Cultivators—not comparable to the two Green Steel Corpses of the Bone Map, and thus of no great value.
Yuan Ming took over Sang Yan's Corpse Nourishing Bag, his Divine Sense indifferently probing inside, but his expression suddenly changed dramatically.
The Corpse Nourishing Bag contained a towering corpse about a meter high, covered in green fur, much like a Human Demon.
There were nine talismans attached to the green-furred corpse's body, which judging from their aura, should have effects similar to the Sealing Spirit Talisman.Your support on * keeps this series going.
However, the aura of the green-furred corpse was extraordinarily powerful, obviously far surpassing the existence at the Core Formation Stage; these talismans could not completely seal it.
Yuan Ming was shocked. Could this green-furred corpse be that of a Core Formation Stage cultivator? Sang Yan and the others sneaked into Snake King Valley, laboring to break the array inside that ancient castle—could it have been related to this green-furred corpse?
Now, combining the various behaviors seen earlier, it somewhat made sense; the Black Fire Sect was a Corpse Refining Sect, and they would only value corpses that contained potent powers.
Yuan Ming examined the green-furred corpse, his Divine Sense suddenly focusing on its forehead, where there was a thumb-sized blood hole, with the adjacent scalp stained with black-green slime.
This wound...
He took out an object, which was the iron nail magical artifact with black-green slime on it.
The size of the nail and the slime on it matched the green-furred corpse; could it be that this nail was previously embedded in this Core Formation Stage corpse?
Just then, the aura of the green-furred corpse suddenly began to strengthen, a powerful surge of Corpse Qi raging outward, the nine talismans fluttering and their runes brightening and dimming rapidly, quickly fading, unlikely to hold much longer.
The control measures applied to the green-furred corpse were all Sang Yan's doing. Now that she was dead, those measures naturally failed, and relying solely on nine Corpse Suppressing Talismans could not restrain this green-furred corpse.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming was secretly anxious, and he quickly took out the Bone Map's jade scroll, rapidly perusing the contents about controlling corpses, hoping to find a solution.
However, the corpse control secret technique of the Black Fire Sect was profound and inscrutable; Yuan Ming could hardly master it briefly, and moreover, many corpse controlling techniques required auxiliary items, none of which he possessed.
As the aura of the green-furred corpse grew increasingly powerful, the nine Corpse Suppressing Talismans were already on the verge of collapse.
With a grit of his teeth, Yuan Ming took a desperate measure, releasing a soul crow into the Corpse Nourishing Bag, plunging it into the eyebrow center of the green-furred corpse as he employed the Corpse Control Divine Ability.
The aura of the green-furred body abruptly paused, swiftly retracting, and its tightly shut eyes slowly opened, revealing eerie green pupils.
Yuan Ming was both shocked and delighted; the Corpse Control Divine Ability of the Moonlight Technique was indeed mysterious—he had only tried it as a last resort, and to his surprise, he had actually managed to control this Core Formation Stage corpse!
He performed a gesture, and the green-furred corpse flew out of the Corpse Nourishing Bag, landing on the ground, motionless.
Yuan Ming circled around the corpse twice, his mind urging it on.
The green-haired corpse let out a beast-like low growl, and its green-black fist covered in green hair smashed forward.
The air in front exploded, a visible blast of fist wind erupted, easily tearing through the Barrier laid down by the Four Directions Sealing Spirit Talisman and striking the cave wall.
With a thunderous roar, a huge pit about ten feet deep appeared in the mountain wall, spiderweb-like cracks spreading from the pit across the entire cave, small and large stones cascading down.
Yuan Ming's mouth slightly agape, he knew this Core Formation Stage corpse contained astonishing power, but he hadn't imagined it would be this terrifying, a light punch almost collapsing the cave.
After his surprise, delight surged in his heart.
After the soul crow's possession, he had already thoroughly investigated; this Core Formation Stage corpse had transformed into a being similar to a Human Demon, unable to wield any more Magic Power Divine Abilities, leaving only its physical strength.
Even so, this corpse still represented a tremendous and formidable combat force.
Yuan Ming closed his eyes and circulated the Corpse Control Divine Ability to become familiar with various aspects of the green-haired corpse for future use.
Time ticked by, quickly encompassing a quarter of an hour.
Yuan Ming was still sensing the situation of the green-haired corpse and did not notice a surge of ink-black qi suddenly emerging from its gloomy green eyes.
An aura of evil suddenly seeped from deep within the corpse and wrapped around the soul crow, then ventured into Yuan Ming's Sea of Consciousness through it.
Yuan Ming's body shook violently, and a thought of murderous bloodlust suddenly surged, several times stronger than the backlash from the Fur Cloak Skill.
Startled, he circulated the Moonlight Technique on one side to suppress the bloodthirsty thought while retracting the soul crow on the other.
However, the evil aura within the green-haired corpse seemed like tentacles, clutching the soul crow and refusing to release. It took Yuan Ming the strength of nine bulls and two tigers to barely pull the soul crow out, dispersing the thoughts of bloodlust and slaughter immediately.
However, without the soul crow's control, the aura of the green-haired corpse exploded again, all nine Corpse Suppressing Talismans shattered.
The green-haired corpse broke all constraints, its aura wildly surging, and its originally hollow gaze seemed to regain a hint of vitality.
Yuan Ming was both shocked and anxious, about to grit his teeth and use another soul crow to control the corpse again.
Just then, a buzzing sound suddenly emerged, originating from the black iron nail he was holding.
The black iron nail hummed and trembled, and its tip pointed toward the green-haired corpse's head.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming resolutely inserted the iron nail into the blood hole on the green-haired corpse's forehead.
The burgeoning aura from the green-haired corpse immediately subsided and rapidly disappeared.
A few breaths later, the powerful aura from the corpse completely dissipated, leaving only a trace, barely stronger than an ordinary yin corpse.
Yuan Ming heaved a sigh of relief; this iron nail was indeed for the sealing of the green-haired corpse, and looking at the old aura on the nail, it should have originally been on the corpse, not the doing of the Black Fire Sect.
His interest in this green-haired corpse grew; such a powerful entity could not have appeared out of thin air.
Yuan Ming retrieved Sang Yan's and the Bone Map's storage magic tools and examined them carefully, soon finding a fragmentary map from Sang Yan showing the terrain right here in Snake King Valley, with some text written on the back of the fragment.
After going through the map and text, he finally understood the origin of the corpse, which was originally named "Heavenly Snake Master," no wonder it chose to be buried in Snake King Valley.
There were many secrets in Snake King Valley, including that ancient castle and the black stone pillar deep in Snake King Cave, all were quite peculiar.
However, he had no immediate intention to explore these.
Yuan Ming placed Heavenly Snake Master's corpse into the Bone Map's Corpse Nourishing Bag and turned to walk out, quickly reaching near the entrance to Snake King Valley.
"Goo goo…"
Inside the Spiritual Beast Bag, the Black Toad made a series of anxious sounds, sending a thought of unwillingness to leave this place.
"Do you want to stay here to cultivate?" Yuan Ming communicated with the Black Toad through his Divine Thought.
After the Black Toad's breakthrough to the Second Level, its spiritual intelligence had improved significantly, and it nodded repeatedly.
Yuan Ming looked towards Snake King Valley, which was warm and moist, indeed a suitable environment for the Black Toad. Although the two Snake Kings had perished, there were still plenty of Golden Flower Poison Pythons in Snake King Valley, which were great nourishment for the Black Toad.
Moreover, with the Black Toad's current Divine Skills, there was no need to worry about safety issues.
"All right, you may stay here for this period, and I will come to fetch you when needed," Yuan Ming said, releasing the Black Toad.
The Black Toad called out twice to Yuan Ming, hopping into Snake King Valley, its figure quickly disappearing into the dense miasma.
Yuan Ming did not linger and swept towards Biluo Cave.

chapters.title: Chapter 197 - 177: Pigeons Occupy the Magpie's Nest
chapters.content:
Having returned to the Sect, two days had already passed.
Yuan Ming didn't go straight back to his residence, but instead made a detour to the Fire Workshop.
"Junior Brother Yuan, you've been out for quite a long time recently, and many of the Fire Refining Hall's duties have been left unattended. I'm afraid you don't have enough contribution points left to deduct, do you?" Fang Ge saw Yuan Ming and couldn't help but put on a serious face.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming knew that Brother Fang Ge was always fair and wasn't deliberately making things difficult for him. He spoke out of duty, and there was even a hint of concern for him.
After all, not participating in the Sect's daily duties for a long time meant not only would there be no contribution points to collect, but there would even be a deduction of the existing points.
The Sect certainly wouldn't support idlers.
"Brother Fang Ge, the recent alliance meeting at White Deer Hill had me itching to focus on cultivation, so I neglected my duties here. I apologize for making you worry on my behalf. However, rest assured, I did complete quite a few other tasks earlier, so I still have some contribution points left," Yuan Ming said with a smile, approaching him.
"You manage your own affairs. I'm only reminding you. But Artifact Refining is a skill that requires practice. If you don't do it for too long, you'll inevitably become rusty," Fang Ge nodded. He had no intention of scolding and simply spoke his thoughts.
"I understand. Just the other day, I found a very interesting metal while I was out in the workshop. I wonder if you could take a look for me?" Yuan Ming suggested with a smile.
"Show it to me," Fang Ge replied, clearly interested.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming immediately twisted his wrist and took out a fist-sized dark red metal block and handed it to Fang Ge.
"Is this... Fire Red Copper? This thing is not easy to find," Fang Ge said after carefully observing the metal for a moment, a rare expression of surprise appearing on his face.
"So it's Fire Red Copper. Brother Fang Ge is indeed experienced and knowledgeable," Yuan Ming pretended to suddenly realize and commented.
"Junior Brother Yuan, how much of this spiritual material do you have, and would you consider selling some to me?" Fang Ge, who was hard-pressed to let go of the metal, eagerly inquired.
He had been trying to refine a Magic Artifact of a particular quality, and a shortage of this material had kept him from completing it.
"This item is of no use to me. If you like it, Brother, feel free to take it," Yuan Ming replied.
Hearing this, Fang Ge's joyful expression stiffened, and he quickly realized that Yuan Ming wasn't unfamiliar with the item; it was clear that he had been looking for an opportunity to give it to him.
"Junior Brother Yuan, I appreciate your kindness. But things must have a price. Tell me what you want for it now; I cannot take advantage of you," Fang Ge said earnestly.
"Alright, to be honest, I got it at the workshop market as a bargain, just two spirit stones," Yuan Ming sighed.
He was lying; he had actually found it while rummaging through the storage bag of some unlucky fellow.
"I'll give you three spirit stones," Fang Ge proposed after some thought.
"Just two. This is a token of my appreciation. If it were a business transaction, I wouldn't sell it," Yuan Ming said, looking at him with a half-smile.
"Alright," Fang Ge swiftly agreed without any hesitation.
After happily accepting the metal, Yuan Ming bid farewell and then proceeded to the Artifact House to see Mu He.
Yuan Ming had also prepared a gift for him.
Unlike Brother Fang Ge's strictly by-the-book manner, Mu He readily accepted the gift without even thanking him.
More than receiving gifts, he was interested in Yuan Ming's previous endeavor to refine the Green Fish Sword.
Upon learning that Yuan Ming had successfully had the sword refined by an outsider, Mu He earnestly requested to see the sword for himself.
Unable to refuse, Yuan Ming took out the Cold Star Sword and presented it for Mu He's appreciation.
After inspecting it, Mu He was even more enthusiastic than the Three Cave Masters, exclaiming "exquisite" repeatedly as he cradled the Cold Star Sword in his arms, refusing to put it down and insisting on seeing Yuan Ming demonstrate its power for him.This сhаptеr wаs mаdе pоssiblе by thе МV_LЕМРYR соmmunity.
Yuan Ming finally managed to extricate himself and left the Artifact House to head straight for the residence of the Three Cave Masters.
However, the Three Cave Masters were not there.
Unable to find the person he was looking for, Yuan Ming turned and went to the valley between the mountains of the Fire Refining Hall and the Alchemy Hall.
The Fisherman was rolling up his sleeves and trousers, bending over and wielding a hoe to loosen the soil of the medicinal fields. Seeing Yuan Ming arrive, he placed the hoe on his shoulder and straightened his back.
"Elder Fisherman, I have brought you some wine. Is there any meat to eat today?" Yuan Ming promptly took out the two jars of fine wine he had prepared, holding them high with both hands and calling out from afar.
"You, young man, it's been quite a while since you've come to see this old man," the Fisherman complained slightly.
"These past days have been busy indeed. Haven't I come to visit you as soon as I had the chance?" Yuan Ming responded with a smile.
Hoisting his hoe, the Fisherman walked onto the field ridges, casually pulling up a spiritual medicine from the ground.
"Did you manage to buy those Central Plains spices I asked you for last time?" the Fisherman inquired, waiting for Yuan Ming to approach.
"I only managed to find some Sichuan pepper and cinnamon. The rest are really hard to come by," Yuan Ming replied truthfully.
"Hmm... Not bad, not bad at all. With these two, we can already make something with a different flavor," the Fisherman said delightedly, leading the way ahead, guiding Yuan Ming back to his thatched cottage.
After seating Yuan Ming, the Fisherman went out to practice his traditional skill of fishing.
In a short while, when he returned, his fish basket was filled with three plump Silver Scale Colorful Fish.
The fisherman never needed Yuan Ming's help and quickly prepared the Silver Scale Colorful Fish before stewing it in a pot.
While waiting for the fish to stew, Yuan Ming got some wine bowls and poured wine for both the fisherman and himself. They started eating and drinking with some sauce-coated meat and side dishes that Yuan Ming had brought back.
After two bowls of wine, the fisherman first praised them heartily, then, noticing how Yuan Ming was drinking his wine, he became displeased.
"Look here, Yuan, what are you doing, sipping like it's tea? You're barely having any," the fisherman said discontentedly.
"I was just trying to leave more for you," Yuan Ming said with an awkward smile.
"I've been here for so many years, and it's not often I meet someone I take to like you. Drink up when you're here. I won't say much else, but there's always enough fish," the fisherman said and took a big swig of the wine himself.
Yuan Ming followed suit and drank heartily as well.
"Don't restrain yourself when drinking, and don't use your mana to dissipate the alcohol. It's better to feel a bit drunk," the fisherman emphasized.
"Elder, is there something troubling you?" Yuan Ming asked, sensing that the fisherman was a bit off today.
"I'm just a wanderer with no worries. Come on, let's eat some fish," the fisherman said, shaking his head. He then picked up a big piece of fish with his chopsticks and started eating.
Seeing that the other party did not wish to talk, Yuan Ming did not press further, and the two chatted sporadically.
This was one of the rare places in Biluo Cave where he could truly relax.
"How did you come to Biluo Cave?" the fisherman suddenly asked.
Yuan Ming thought for a moment and did not hide anything; he recounted how he had struggled for survival as a Fur Beast Slave and how he joined the sect.
The fisherman listened attentively to the whole story, said nothing, and simply clinked bowls with Yuan Ming, both taking a big gulp.
Before they knew it, the sun had set, and in the gaps between the mountains, they could see the twilight gradually being engulfed by darkness. Yuan Ming's cheeks were flushed red from drinking, and he felt a buzz of tipsiness.
"Yuan, while I'm three sheets to the wind, I'll tell you, this place wasn't originally called Biluo Cave," the fisherman said as he looked into the distant shadows.
"What was it called then?" Yuan Ming said, surprised.
"This place had no name before. I named it Three Stars Mountain because these three peaks stand side by side, corresponding to three stars in the sky," the fisherman explained.
"You named it?" Yuan Ming asked, increasingly curious.
"Yes, I did," the fisherman nodded.
Yuan Ming's hand, holding the wine bowl, suddenly froze.
"You... you're not..."
In his heart, he had always suspected that this kind old man might be the stabilizing force of Biluo Cave, the elusive Great Elder whose name was known but who remained unseen.
But after more interactions, Yuan Ming thought it unlikely.
However, hearing him now, Yuan Ming couldn't help but wonder again. He reasoned that aside from the Great Elder, he couldn't imagine who else would have the authority to name or rename Biluo Cave.
"I'm not," the fisherman said with a glance, guessing Yuan Ming's thoughts.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming, without realizing it, breathed a sigh of relief.
Deep down, he didn't want the fisherman to be the Great Elder.
"There must be some unknown story behind the renaming of Three Stars Mountain to Biluo Cave," Yuan Ming said, puzzled.
The fisherman didn't answer directly but began to tell a story:
"Do you know, in the Central Plains there's a bird called the cuckoo? They don't build nests but lay their eggs in the nests of magpies. To ensure their offspring hatch, they push the magpie eggs out to break them, thereby taking over the magpies' nests," he said.
Yuan Ming was familiar with the tale of the cuckoo usurping the magpie's nest and listened with bated breath, the drunkenness fading away.
"May I ask, Elder, what became of the magpies whose nest was taken?" he asked cautiously.
"The magpies? They built themselves a little nest under the tree. They planted flowers and fished every day, and lived quite comfortably," the fisherman replied with a slight smile and an air of tranquility.
"So, you were the former master of Biluo Cave!" Yuan Ming exclaimed in astonishment.
"When one is idle, they tend to become nostalgic. I just miss the pristine beauty of Three Stars Mountain," the fisherman sighed.
"Well, it's good. No conflicts, no worries. Elder, you truly are clear-headed," Yuan Ming consoled.
The fisherman neither agreed nor disagreed, simply taking a light sip from his cup.
"I've always known that the fisherman wasn't ordinary, but I didn't expect you had such a past," Yuan Ming reflected.
"These Three Stars Mountain, I lost them after a fight. Although my heart was full of reluctance and bitterness, there was a bet beforehand. I honored the gamble and admitted defeat; after all, a loss is a loss. At that time, Chen Cangqiong had a certain degree of tolerance. He didn't kill me or drive me away but wanted to recruit me to serve under him," the fisherman confessed in response to Yuan Ming's question.

chapters.title: Chapter 198 - 178: Bring It On
chapters.content:
"Could it be that the Chen Cangqiong mentioned by the Fisherman is..." Yuan Ming wondered aloud.
"He is now the Great Elder of the Biluo Cave." The Fisherman replied.
"Since he didn't make things difficult for you, why do you choose to live in seclusion here? Wouldn't it be better to leave?" Yuan Ming asked.
"I have thought about leaving, especially after learning about those shady and sordid affairs that happened in Biluo Cave later on..." The Fisherman began, but suddenly fell silent.
A moment later, after taking a sip of wine, he continued, "But my former subordinates had to stay in Biluo Cave. Most of them come from Artifact Refining backgrounds, and their combat power isn't very high. While Chen Cangqiong's cultivation kept rising, he also slowly cultivated more strength, and I did not wish to make him target my former subordinates if I left, so I gave up the idea. Gradually, I lost the will to leave."
Yuan Ming didn't respond; he understood the Fisherman's decision.
"That Chen Cangqiong truly is capable. Originally, the Southern Border and Northern Territory had Four Major Sects. After taking over, he turned the once obscure Three Stars Mountain into one of the Five Great Sects of the Southern Border and Northern Territory. His methods are indeed impressive." The Fisherman added.
"Chen Cangqiong is actually so formidable, but don't the other four families suppress him? How strong is he?" Yuan Ming inquired.
"In terms of strength, none of the elders from the other sects can defeat him in a one-on-one fight. What can they do to him?" The Fisherman answered.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming felt respect rising within him for this Great Elder whom he had never met.
"Do you know why I indulge Huo Chan'er so much?" The Fisherman said after a long silence, speaking up once more.
"Could it be that one of the Three Cave Masters is an old friend of yours?" Yuan Ming quickly guessed the answer.
"Almost all the elders from the Fire Refining Hall were once my subordinates. Over the years, some have reached the end of their life spans, others met with accidents and perished. Ling Songhua has become one of Biluo Cave's Three Cave Masters. I once had a Loose Cultivator friend named Hei Mu who was exceptional in Artifact Refining, and he often visited Three Stars Mountain to exchange insights on refining with Song Hua," The Fisherman nodded.
"The Three Cave Master is Ling Songhua! He often exchanged Artifact Refining insights with Hei Mu at Three Stars Mountain! Could Master Hei Mu and the Three Cave Master have had something more between them!" Yuan Ming almost couldn't help exclaiming in shock.
Seeing his astonished expression, the Fisherman asked, "Surprised, are you?"
"The junior has just never seen the Three Cave Master visit you here, so it seems a bit unbelievable," Yuan Ming said, masking his true reaction.
"Song Hua blames me for Hei Mu's disappearance. She thinks I should take responsibility," the Fisherman sighed, his words coming slowly.
"Could it be that you have feelings for the Three Cave Master!" A wild thought came to Yuan Ming, and he blurted it out. For a split second, Yuan Ming considered telling the Fisherman that Master Hei Mu hadn't disappeared but was already dead; however, he dared not voice this thought.
"Don't be disrespectful. You could be a novelist with your storytelling. I confide old stories to you, and you make jokes about this old man," The Fisherman said to Yuan Ming with a laugh.
"I'm sorry, I was wrong," Yuan Ming hurriedly apologized.
"Three cups of wine as punishment!" The Fisherman pretended to be angry.
When the sky turned dark, they had finished off two jars of wine and all the fish, both host and guest thoroughly enjoyed themselves, and Yuan Ming then took his leave.
After stepping out of the valley, Yuan Ming gathered his mana, uttered a soft chant, and dispelled all the alcohol fumes from his body. Then, he quickly used the Wind Swift Skill to hurry back to his residence at the Fire Refining Hall.
Back at his dwelling, Yuan Ming still couldn't contain his excitement.
He never would have imagined the Fisherman, the Three Cave Master, and Hei Mu to have such a history. It was no wonder the Fisherman had been so lenient with him when they first met. He just couldn't understand why neither the Three Cave Master nor the Fisherman knew about Hei Mu's Cave Mansion, to the point where he had been gone for so long without their knowledge.
After a short rest, Yuan Ming went to the window to sit quietly and began to meditate on the "Nine Elements Technique."
In the middle of the night, a faint noise came from the window, and Yuan Ming slowly opened his eyes to see the silver cat approaching him with light steps.
"Xi Ying, you came quickly?" Yuan Ming stopped his cultivation practice and called out.
The silver cat simply walked into his room and sat down on the desk, asking:
"Tell me, what interesting things happened on your trip? I could use a distraction."This content was first released on *.
Yuan Ming then exaggerated his experiences in Snake King Valley, recounting them with embellishments.
The story was heavily embellished, especially detailing how he fell into danger, was ambushed, entangled with the Snake King, and finally achieved a hard-fought victory.
Even though Xi Ying was no stranger to grand spectacles, she was still swayed by Yuan Ming's vivid narrative; at the suspenseful parts, her bi-colored pupils would unwittingly contract, her claws almost tearing the desk apart.
After the recitation, Yuan Ming marvelled at his own talent for storytelling.
"That really does sound fun. It's a shame I didn't go. Next time, you have to take me along," Xi Ying said earnestly after listening, her emotions finally settling down, but not without expressing her regret.
Seeing her look of disappointment, Yuan Ming couldn't help but feel amused. He then shared the old stories he had heard from the Fisherman about Biluo Cave with Xi Ying, who seemed to have already known them.
As Xi Ying lingered, Yuan Ming said, "Aren't you in a rush to cultivate? You've been here for quite some time."
"Are you chasing me away? Give me back my stuff," Xi Ying demanded, stretching out a paw and making a grasping motion with her fluffy fingers.
When Yuan Ming heard this, he knew that the inevitable had arrived. He had thought that his elaborate narration might sidestep the matter and that he could secretly repair and return the Gold-plated Gauze to Xi Ying later. But she had not been distracted at all and still remembered the gauze.
"Um, Xi Ying, about that... Could I borrow the Gold-plated Gauze for a bit longer? It's really quite handy, and I plan to go to the workshop in a few days to see if there's any work I can do," Yuan Ming said somewhat awkwardly.
"We'll talk future matters later. Where is the Gold-plated Gauze? Give it back," Xi Ying insisted, extending a paw and making a scooping motion.
"I accidentally damaged the Gold-plated Gauze," Yuan Ming said helplessly, telling the truth.
"Let me have a look," Xi Ying instructed.
Yuan Ming sighed and, feeling anxious, took out the gold-plated gauze and handed it over.
Xi Ying caught it, examined the damaged area closely, and said, "It seems you really did go through a tough battle..." With a wave of her paw, she stored it away and then added, "What's a magic artifact compared to one's life? I won't blame you, seeing how nervous you are."
On the contrary, Yuan Ming was stunned in place, feeling somewhat guilty and at a loss. He was about to explain to Xi Ying about the materials used for the gold-plated gauze, but by then, Xi Ying had already hopped away, moving off into the distance.
...
The next day.
Yuan Ming returned to the small courtyard in the back mountain, and this time, he finally met with the Three Cave Masters.
After learning about the situation of the Three Cave Masters from the Fisherman, Yuan Ming felt differently when he saw her again.
But for now, he could not reveal Master Hei Mu's affairs to her.
When the Three Cave Masters saw Yuan Ming's arrival, she was somewhat surprised, as his recent visits had been unusually frequent.
"What brings you here?" In the courtyard, the Three Cave Masters looked at Yuan Ming and asked.
Yuan Ming took off Huo Chan'er, who was clinging to his neck, and began to speak, "Disciple went out the day before yesterday and encountered someone in a hurry to sell an item at the workshop. It resembled the White Flame Gold you were seeking, so I spent some money to buy it."
Upon hearing this, the Three Cave Masters showed a flicker of emotion but quickly regained her composure.
"White Flame Gold of this sort is rarely found in workshops, and even if it appears, it will be snatched up immediately. How could you, a Qi Refining disciple, manage to buy it?" She said, smiling and shaking her head.
The implication was that Yuan Ming had probably been duped into buying a fake.
"Disciple doesn't know if it's real or fake, but I bought it anyway. I would like the Three Cave Masters to take a look," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
The Three Cave Masters thought for a moment and then replied, "Well, let's take a look at it."
She resolved to compensate Yuan Ming for the spirit stones he had spent, regardless of whether the White Flame Gold was real or fake. A registered disciple at the Qi Refinement Realm did not often come by such intentions, and she couldn't let him suffer a loss in vain.
Yuan Ming immediately slapped his storage bag and took out the chicken egg-sized piece of White Flame Gold.
Before returning, he went out of his way to find a volcanic crater, where he cast the White Flame Gold into the outer edge of the lava, allowing the sulfur-rich volcanic substance to mar its surface and giving it a pungent smell.
As expected, at first glance, the Three Cave Masters mistook the item for a volcanic rock.
But as soon as she casually picked it up, her wrist sank slightly, and she knew something was off-kilter.
Volcanic rocks usually contain plentiful bubbles, giving them a light and airy feel; it shouldn't have been so heavy.
The Three Cave Masters' expression grew concentrated as she held the piece of White Flame Gold closely, and her demeanor soon underwent a dramatic change, the joy in her eyes difficult to conceal.
"This... it really is a piece of White Flame Gold," the Three Cave Masters couldn't help but exclaim.
"I just felt it looked like White Flame Gold; the people nearby all weren't sure and told me not to buy it, but I insisted on buying it anyway. Turns out my luck is good," Yuan Ming declared, slapping his thigh, appearing even more excited than the Three Cave Masters.
"How much did you pay for it?" the Three Cave Masters asked.
"Not much; as long as it's the right thing," Yuan Ming waved his hand and said.
The Three Cave Masters didn't speak but looked straight at Yuan Ming, clearly expecting him to give a precise amount.
"Three spirit stones," Yuan Ming said with a resigned look.
"Really?" The Three Cave Masters frowned. That price didn't just suggest a bargain—it was practically a steal.
"It's true. People around said it was a fake, and the seller was flustered. When he saw I was willing to buy, he gave me such a price, and even if he asked for more, I didn't have it," Yuan Ming nodded emphatically.
"If that's the case, then it truly is your good fortune. I indeed need this White Flame Gold. Tell me, what would you like in exchange?" the Three Cave Masters said, now convinced.
"No need, no need, this is a token of this disciple's respect for you. I have always remembered the Three Cave Masters' kindness in accepting me," Yuan Ming waved his hands repeatedly.
He genuinely didn't intend to exchange it for anything. First, the White Flame Gold was truly of no use to him at the moment. Second, the Three Cave Masters had been truly good to him, a registered disciple, and third, it was also a form of gratitude to Master Hei Mu.
"If there's any magic artifact you lack, I can give you one," the Three Cave Masters thought for a moment and said.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming gave it careful thought and realized that he indeed didn't need anything for the time being.
Suddenly, he thought of something and asked, "Three Cave Masters, do you know about the existence of flying artifacts?"
"You want a flying artifact?" The Three Cave Masters paused, frowning.
It wasn't that she found Yuan Ming's request excessive, but rather, she genuinely didn't have such a thing.
"Disciple was just curious after reading about them in books," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"Flying artifacts are just one type among many. They can fly through the air, sustained by the special properties of spiritual materials and the enhancement of arrays, as long as spiritual power is continuously supplied," the Three Cave Masters explained.
"Why have I never seen the elders using one?" Yuan Ming asked, puzzled.

chapters.title: Chapter 199 - 179 White Horse Youth Journey
chapters.content:
"A Flying Artifact is, after all, merely a type of auxiliary Magic Artifact. Here in the Southern Border, they prefer directly controlling spirit beasts that can fly, while in the Central Plains, they are more partial to Flying Artifacts. The so-called Flying Sword Immortal is nothing more than someone controlling a sword to fly," explained the Three Cave Masters.
"I see," Yuan Ming suddenly realized.
After speaking, he removed Huo Chan'er from his shoulder and placed her on the ground.
"Three Cave Masters, I'm planning to go into seclusion in the mountains soon. I should take this opportunity to bid you farewell; I will take my leave now." Having said this, he bid farewell and turned to leave.
The Three Cave Masters was led off track by the topic of Flying Artifacts, recalling the refinement techniques of Flying Artifacts, and did not respond immediately. By the time she remembered that she had yet to pay for the White Flame Gold, Yuan Ming had already left.
"Flying Artifacts, huh…" the Three Cave Masters murmured to herself.
Yuan Ming went to the Fire Workshop and reported to his Senior Brother Fang Ge, then went back to pack up briefly before heading again towards Ten Thousand Mountains for secluded cultivation.
This time in seclusion, besides enhancing his cultivation, Yuan Ming also planned to incorporate various materials he had recently found into his incense making.
He believed that by finding the correct spiritual materials to replace the ordinary materials, the duration of the incense possession would definitely increase and the effect would surely come closer to that of the original Black Incense.
Having carved out a Cave Mansion in the mountains, he also constructed a tree house in an ancient tree outside.
After settling in, Yuan Ming began another round of incense testing.
This time he had reaped a bountiful harvest, and the types of spiritual materials he brought back were varied, leaving him somewhat unsure where to begin at first.
After much contemplation, he first took out the Yellow Springs Tree he had brought back from Snake King Valley, scraped off a small half cup of powder, and added it into his incense making ingredients.
Once the incense was made, Yuan Ming couldn't wait to light one.
Yellow Springs Tree inherently pertains to the Divine Soul, so Yuan Ming had high hopes for this batch of incense.
"Liu Tianming…
Yuan Ming watched the wisps of smoke rising, silently calling out the Emperor's name in his mind while picturing his face, as his vision gradually blurred until he was engulfed in endless darkness.
After a moment, Yuan Ming's vision brightened again, and he immediately saw a wide desk covered in bright yellow silk and a pair of fair hands resting on it.
The owner of the hands was dressed in a bright yellow Dragon Robe, looking down at a letter placed on the desk.
Yuan Ming confirmed that he had once again possessed the body of Emperor Jin, but still in the state of an observer, only capable of feeling the Emperor's emotions without controlling his actions.
However, Yuan Ming felt an incredibly strong excitement and exhilaration.
He could even sense that the Emperor's arms, propped on the desk, were trembling uncontrollably.
Looking down with the Emperor's line of sight, Yuan Ming saw the handwriting on the letter seemed familiar. Upon closer inspection, he realized it was indeed the letter he had written to General's Mansion to report his safety.
The Emperor grabbed the letter, held it aloft while shaking it forcefully, and excitedly said, "General Yuan, this is wonderful! I knew Brother Ming wasn't so easily vanquished. I will send someone to fetch him back, right now, immediately."
Following the Emperor's raised line of sight, Yuan Ming saw a middle-aged man in court attire standing in front of the grand hall.
With sharp eyebrows, piercing eyes, a proud nose, lips framed by a circle of dark short beard, and a tall and imposing figure, his demeanor was calm and collected, standing there like an immovable stele.
Not seeing this face, Yuan Ming had a vague impression of him, but the moment he saw the face, it crisply and vividly formed in Yuan Ming's heart.
But compared to the father he remembered, the hair at his temples had inexplicably grown somewhat whiter.
"Father…"
Yuan Ming could not speak out loud, but the voice shouting in his heart was trembling as well.
The tall and imposing General Yuan, looked much more composed than the Emperor, but the faint reddish tinge at the corners of his eyes showed he was not as serene as he appeared.
"It troubles Your Majesty to be concerned. My son's letter did not mention specific locations, only that the letter was sent from a military town of the Kasi Clan in the Southern Border. I have already dispatched personal soldiers to follow the spies from the Southern Border to investigate. Once reliable information is obtained, trusted envoys will be dispatched to meet him," General Yuan said with a salute.
"This guy, although he has sent a letter back, why didn't he specify where he is staying? What's worse, there's not a single word for me in the letter," the Emperor said somewhat dissatisfied as he put down the letter.
"He most likely has his unavoidable difficulties," General Yuan sighed.
Upon hearing this and thinking of the hardships Yuan Ming might be facing in the Southern Border, the Emperor could not bear to blame him further.
Yuan Ming didn't divulge his whereabouts to his family partly because he hadn't yet recovered his complete memory of being wronged, and partly because he intended to wait until his strength had improved and he was capable of self-protection before returning.
"General Yuan, about Brother Ming still being alive…"
"Your Majesty, rest assured, besides informing you, I have not told a third party," General Yuan understood immediately and said without delay.
"That's good. When he returns, I want him..." the Emperor began, but did not finish his sentence.
But Yuan Ming heard his heart's voice: "I want him to be my right-hand man, just like before…"
After General Yuan took his leave, the eunuchs and maids who had been dismissed came cautiously back into the hall.
The trusted eunuch serving beside the Emperor, seeing that His Majesty seemed to be in a good mood, asked, "Your Majesty, the Chief of Staff from the Ministry of Rites and the Ministry of Revenue seek an audience to discuss resuming trade with Southern Border. Shall we invite them in?"
"Today I will see no one. All matters will be discussed tomorrow," the Emperor replied without a moment's thought, waving his hand dismissively.
"Yes,"
the young eunuch responded and was about to exit to dismiss the two Chief of Staffs.
At that moment, the young Emperor suddenly spoke, "Bring over my treasure box."
"Yes," the young eunuch immediately responded.
Soon, a purple-red wooden box about two feet square was brought to the young Emperor's desk.
He then waved his hand, driving everyone out.
Afterward, the young Emperor unlocked the golden lock on the purple-red wooden box and slowly lifted the lid.
Inside the box, there were many miscellaneous small items: a black and white tiger stuffed toy, a finely carved small wooden sword, a crescent-shaped jade pendant, and many hand-bound books...
The young Emperor looked at these small items, his face showing a wistful expression.
"Brother Ming, you haven't finished the illustrations for 'White Horse Youth Journey.' You truly made me wait this time..." After a moment, he picked up a blue-covered bound book and spoke sadly.
The sorrow in his words was something Yuan Ming could deeply relate to.
In an instant, he felt as if he had been struck on the head, his mind swirling with thoughts, and vague memories began to surface.
But at the same moment, Yuan Ming's vision blurred again as the possession time ended.My Virtual Library Empire (*)
As his vision cleared, Yuan Ming stared at the burnt-out long incense, unable to focus his eyes for a long time.
In his mind, a scene was playing, like a rolling scroll flickering continually.
He saw his younger self and the equally youthful Emperor, both in the imperial garden's pavilion of the Imperial Palace, one painting with a brush, the other grinding ink, together crafting a painting.
"White Horse Youth Journey... I remember, it was a comic book series I created with the Sixth Prince, no, with His Majesty," Yuan Ming murmured to himself.
Back then, they were both about the same age, both with boundless imaginations, known to each other as confidantes and close friends. Their thoughts clashed and together they created a tale of a young prince eloping to the martial arts world, becoming sworn brothers with martial arts disciples, and adventuring through the martial arts world.
That story was 'White Horse Youth Journey.'
As these memories kept coming back, Yuan Ming became increasingly excited.
The feeling was complicated; it was like putting together a broken porcelain vase, as Yuan Ming was piecing together a complete version of himself using the recovered memories.
He didn't even realize that, in the process, his personality was also gradually changing.
When he had calmed down and reached for the incense burner, his movement suddenly paused.
"This possession time... seems to have greatly extended!" Yuan Ming suddenly realized with shock.
This possession allowed him to fully experience the interaction of the young Emperor with his father and even the young eunuch bringing in the treasure box, significantly longer than before.
"Yellow Springs Tree's wood powder can significantly extend the possession time. I must add rare spiritual materials to the incense!" Yuan Ming realized joyfully.
Although far from reaching the level of the original Black Incense and unable to control the actions of the possessed person, such a substantial increase in time was already a great achievement.
This experiment further spurred Yuan Ming's resolve to continue experimenting, prompting him to add all the spiritual materials he had purchased to the incense-making process, beginning a lengthy experiment.
While waiting for the incense burner to recover, Yuan Ming secluded himself in a cave, starting his closed-door cultivation.
In front of him on the incense burner, he lit a stick of Qingxuan incense.
As a wisp of Qingxuan smoke rose and gently curled upward in the room, that sensation of connection with the smoke again emerged in Yuan Ming's mind.
Within a few breaths, Yuan Ming felt a clarity refreshing his lungs and heart, sweeping away all fatigue.
He immediately took out a white porcelain bottle and poured a yellow-hued Nourishing Origin Pill into his mouth.
The pill melted as soon as it touched his mouth, causing Yuan Ming to involuntarily swallow, and he immediately felt a warm current flowing down his throat into his abdomen.
The next instant, the warm current gathered around his Dantian, seeming to nourish it.
Feeling this wonderful sensation, Yuan Ming immediately closed his eyes, sat cross-legged, and began to recite the Nine Elements Technique Cultivation Technique, starting his Circulation cultivation.
As the Mana inside his Dantian stirred, attempting to travel through his meridians, the warm currents around the Dantian began to move as well, dispersing into the meridians.
Yuan Ming felt the Mana coursing through his meridians surging suddenly, and the speed of his Circulation accelerated involuntarily.
Using Qingxuan Incense and Nourishing Origin Pill simultaneously, this dual enhancement doubled the efficiency of his cultivation.
So much so that he was shocked himself.
Yuan Ming quickly adjusted his mindset, seizing this opportunity to focus intensely on cultivation.
...

chapters.title: Chapter 200 - 180: Luring the Beast
chapters.content:
Time flew by, and more than half a month had passed.
Yuan Ming's cultivation had made swift and sudden progress as he broke through once again, finally reaching the Qi Refining Tenth Layer.
This meant that he was now qualified to undergo Foundation Establishment.
However, Yuan Ming did not immediately consume the laboriously obtained Foundation Establishment Pill.
Ordinary cultivators from Biluo Cave would rely on the Biluo Skill to cultivate up to the Qi Refining Tenth Layer before attempting Foundation Establishment, but his "Nine Elements Technique - Upper Chapter," if continued, could reach the rumored Qi Refining 13th Layer.
Even though Yuan Ming was still unaware of the profound impact these additional three layers would have on his future path of cultivation, he understood that a more solid foundation would be more beneficial to him.
Compared to the rapid progress in cultivating the "Nine Elements Technique," the speed at which he was cultivating the "Moonlight Technique" was considerably slower.
After advancing to the second layer, his cultivation speed in the realm of soul cultivators markedly slowed down.
Even with the lighting of the Soul Nourishing Incense, which nurtured the Divine Soul, the cultivation speed did not significantly increase; hence, Yuan Ming temporarily stopped cultivating the "Moonlight Technique" and focused all his efforts on cultivating the "Nine Elements Technique."
Meanwhile, every few days, Yuan Ming would pause his cultivation to test out the new incense he had formulated.
As it happened, this was inspired by a chance encounter with the "Immortal Xuanhua" in Black Rock Market. The Qingxuan Incense and the Soul Nourishing Incense were indeed quite mysterious and could aid in cultivation; if he could figure out how to create them himself, it would be greatly beneficial for his future cultivation.
This time, he added three types of spiritual materials to the incense at once, the main one being a spiritual material known as "Mist Xuan Grass," commonly used as the key ingredient in refining Illusion Spirit Pills.
The reason for choosing this material was its capacity to induce illusions. Similarly, Illusion Spirit Pills could temporarily transport a person into an illusion, affecting the Divine Soul to a certain extent.
Before lighting the incense, Yuan Ming inserted the long incense into the incense burner and took out a Detoxification Pill, putting it in his mouth first.
The reason for such caution was because of a previous incense experiment in which he accidentally added a toxic Spirit Grass. Upon lighting it, the colorless and odorless toxicity was magnified by the incense burner.
Within just a few breaths, Yuan Ming felt his limbs go weak, and his head grew dizzy.
At the same time, his vision began to blur, and for a moment, he did not know whether he was going to be possessed or poisoned into unconsciousness.
Fortunately, at the last moment, Yuan Ming accessed his Storage Ring and timely took out the Cold Star Sword. By channeling mana through the sword to release its icy aura, he managed to extinguish the incense fire and halt the experiment.
Yuan Ming did not manage to undergo possession in that chaotic state, nor did he recover immediately. Lying weakly, it took him a full hour to fully come around.
Because of this, Yuan Ming realized that experimenting with incense using various materials, and lighting it, also had risks.
This time, although the accident was minor and he stopped it promptly, he might not be so lucky next time.
After this incident, he made preparations against poison and, under the extinguished Tai Chi Pattern, attempted to light the previously made Poisonous Incense again with the incense burner. He found that the incense's potency was significantly enhanced.
The Level 1 Intermediate-stage Fierce Beast he had captured for the experiment collapsed within three breaths.
However, the effects of the Poisonous Incense were more about inducing stupor than causing death.
Moreover, the range of diffusion was limited, essentially covering only a hundred zhang in radius. Without the boost from the incense burner, the area would be halved.
After inhaling an entire stick of the incense, the Fierce Beast remained unconscious for at least an hour.
Following this, Yuan Ming decided to not only attempt to mimic the Possession Black Incense but also create various types of Spirit Incense with different functions, which could also have unexpected effects under the enhancement of the incense burner.
In his current attempt at Incense Making, Yuan Ming directly removed the incense ashes, which was the key factor in prompting possession, focusing solely on exploring the possibilities of making incense.
After lighting the long incense, a stream of white smoke slowly rose, the color was thick white, slightly different from usual.
Yuan Ming glanced subconsciously at the Green Wolf tied to the tree next to him, its four hooves bound.
Fear filled the beast's eyes as it struggled endlessly.
He waited a moment, but the Green Wolf continued to thrash about, showing no signs of succumbing or change in its gaze, with no obvious reaction to poisoning or hallucination.
"It doesn't seem to have any special effect..." Before Yuan Ming could finish speaking, he was suddenly taken aback.
Without noticing, a thick white fog had enveloped his surroundings, making him feel as if he were back in Snake King Valley.
But there was a difference -- the fog was much denser, milky white, and far more effective at obstructing vision.
Almost anything beyond five steps became hidden by the thick fog, rendering it invisible.
Yuan Ming picked up the incense burner and climbed a thousand-foot ancient tree next to him, reaching the top. Only by looking down from there could he see the ten-mile radius below completely obscured by the thick fog.
As he brought the incense burner to the top, white fog even began to gather in the surrounding high skies.
With a thought, he tried to extend his Divine Sense outward in all directions.
Only then did he discover that the thick fog not only obstructed vision but also significantly inhibited Divine Power.
He was not sure of the effect on high-level cultivators, but for him, his range of Divine Sense was compressed to just about ten feet, nearly the same as visual distance. In that moment, Divine Sense was essentially useless.
Amazed, Yuan Ming returned to the tree and watched the incense burner he was holding until the incense had extinguished and the fog around began to disperse.
It took the time it took to drink a cup of tea before it completely vanished.
Yuan Ming bundled the batch of incense he had made, wrapped them with a white strip of paper, and tied another loop around them. Then he took a pen and wrote "Fog Incense" on it, storing it alongside the "Poisonous Incense" he had made earlier.
This was the second special Spirit Incense he had tried to create.
…
Time passed, another month went by as he diligently practiced cultivation and attempted incense making.
Yuan Ming had been worried that using Nourishing Origin Pills and Qingxuan Incense to catalyze his cultivation would have side effects.
But as it turned out, there were no side effects. Instead, most of the Qingxuan Incense had been consumed, and he had run out of Nourishing Origin Pills.
The results of using a large amount of elixirs and Qingxuan Incense were clear, as Yuan Ming's cultivation had advanced and he was now at Qi Refining 11th Level.
However, he also found that in the later stages, the benefits brought by the Nourishing Origin Pills and Qingxuan Incense had significantly diminished.
In addition, the previous incense trials had used many materials but the outcomes were not very satisfactory, with no progress in replicating Black Incense or creating special Spirit Incense.
But today, Yuan Ming came to a secluded valley in the Ten Thousand Mountains, using materials he had high hopes for.
These were three black fruits he had purchased at the Ghost Market in the workshop, which, according to the stall owner, could attract nearby Fierce Beasts with just a whiff of their scent.
If there were any spiritual materials in Yuan Ming's possession capable of creating an exceptionally effective incense, they were these black fruits.
After some busy work, he used one fruit and other spiritual materials to make three sticks of dark black incense.
Yuan Ming also chose to conduct this experiment using the incense burner before the Tai Chi Pattern lit up.
The moment the black incense was lit, a wisp of faint fragrance immediately wafted out.
When Yuan Ming smelled this odor, he was slightly taken aback.
This fragrance was indeed unique; it was different from any other fragrance he had smelled in the past, emitting a distinct fluctuation of spiritual power within it.
At first, Yuan Ming didn't feel anything too strange, but after a short while, he sensed something off.Check My Virtual Library Empire (*) for the latest updates.
He felt a surge of heat on his body and, subconsciously, wanted to move closer to the incense and deeply inhale its unique fragrance.
"This effect?" Yuan Ming was greatly surprised.
He immediately circulated the "Moonlight Technique," summoned his Divine Soul Power, and suppressed this thought.
Fortunately, this desire was not strong; as long as his will was firm, a slight adjustment of his Divine Soul Power could fend it off.
But just then, a series of loud "boom" sounds began coming from all directions.
Yuan Ming leaped up, climbing to the top of the nearby ancient tree, and looked around.
From within the surrounding forests, there was a dust storm, and thundering hoofbeats; through the gaps in the forest canopy, he could see herds of various forest Fierce Beasts of all shapes and sizes converging towards him.
"This incense made from the black fruit is too powerful," Yuan Ming thought to himself in shock.
At first glance, their numbers were already in the hundreds, if not thousands. Aside from various Fierce Beasts, there were even more ordinary wild beasts, all with red eyes and drooling mouths, as if they had gone mad.
"What are you experimenting with now? The wild beasts have gone mad," a pleasant voice suddenly came from beneath the tree.
Yuan Ming looked down and saw Xi Ying, who had arrived at some point, and he promptly jumped down.
"Extinguish the incense... take the incense burner..."
Before Xi Ying could finish speaking, Yuan Ming had already put out the flame and done as she said the moment he landed.
By now, he was certain that the fragrance from the new incense made with black fruit was hugely tempting to wild beasts.
"We need to leave this place first," Xi Ying said, seeing the situation.
"It's too late, the Fierce Beasts have already surrounded us," said Yuan Ming, shaking his head.
"What did you use to make this? It's so powerful, tell me! So magical," Xi Ying said with excitement and curiosity.
"Don't worry, don't worry, let's deal with these wild beasts first," Yuan Ming replied with a smile, showing no sign of panic on his face.
As he spoke, he took out the incense burner again, placed another stick of black incense into it, pinched the head of the incense, and lit it. Guided by Yuan Ming, the rising smoke quickly formed a ring and expanded outwards.
Right after, he took out two Detoxification Pills, consumed one himself, and handed the other to Xi Ying to swallow.
At this point, the noise around them grew louder, and the Fierce Beasts and ordinary wild animals had all revealed themselves, their red eyes and drooling mouths charging towards them wildly.

chapters.title: Chapter 201 - 181: Floating Shadow
chapters.content:
However, as these Fierce Beasts charged into a range close to a hundred feet, without exception, they had only taken a few steps before they stumbled and fell to the ground, one by one, all unconscious.
Soon, they had piled up in a circle, blocking the Fierce Beasts behind them.
"When did you get such a strong seductive scent? It really is a good thing! What was that incense that attracted the beasts made of?" Seeing another miraculously effective seductive scent appear, Silver Cat Xi Ying grew even more curious.
Yuan Ming didn't answer directly but took out the remaining two pigeon-egg-sized black fruits and said, "Here, it's made from this fruit. There were originally three; I bought them at the Ghost Market in Black Rock City. According to the stall owner, they come from a unique tree of a certain family in the Southern Domain, which bears these strange fruits once every few hundred years. Exotic Beasts that eat them can rapidly increase their fertility rates. If these fruits are placed in the mountains and forests, even a trace of their scent can attract Fierce Beasts from hundreds of feet around to fight over them."
"So that's it, don't waste these strange fruits carelessly, they might be of great use in the future. This Ghost Market really seems interesting; I must visit it sometime," said Xi Ying, her curiosity fully ignited.
"Next time, we'll go together. With your keen eye, not a single good item will slip by. How about going now?" Yuan Ming said seductively.
"Forget about the Ghost Market for now; the commotion earlier was huge. If the Sect finds any clues, they'll definitely investigate, and your incense-making secret won't be safe," said Xi Ying.
"Then let's hurry and leave this place," Yuan Ming said soberly.
...
The two changed their location to a far distant spot and settled down again.
As night fell, at the mid-point of the month, a round moon hung high in the sky, bursting with radiant brightness.
Yuan Ming lit a campfire at the new campsite and roasted some beast meat, which he shared with the Silver Cat.
Speaking of which, he had never seen Xi Ying eat before.
With curiosity in his heart, Yuan Ming took a freshly roasted piece of beast meat, laid it on a clean, broad leaf, and tentatively brought it over to the Silver Cat.
Xi Ying merely glanced at it and disdainfully turned her head away.
"I don't eat," she said.
"How is it? Have you no need to eat anymore?" Yuan Ming asked, surprised.
"I stopped eating ordinary food long ago. Why don't you give me a Demon Core?" Xi Ying glanced at Yuan Ming and spoke.
"Once I can handle a Core Formation Stage demon beast, I'll definitely find one for you!" Yuan Ming's probing intent was seen through by Xi Ying, who chuckled dryly, swearing earnestly,
"It's a promise! I'll be waiting," Xi Ying said.
To hide his embarrassment, Yuan Ming chewed and tore at his food louder than usual, juice spilling from the corners of his mouth, adding to the natural aroma and making it seem even more delicious.
Xi Ying raised her head, glanced at the sky, and said, "It's getting late." She then leaped up and jumped onto a nearby large tree.
After looking back at Yuan Ming, she leapt toward another large tree.
"Xi Ying, where are you going?" Yuan Ming asked.
"I'm going to cultivate. Do you want to come and see?" Xi Ying's figure flashed, and she disappeared into the night.
Yuan Ming stopped chewing the delicious food in his mouth, hesitating whether to follow Xi Ying and see how she cultivated, but he restrained his curiosity and did not follow.
Just as he was about to eat his last bite, he suddenly felt a strange fluctuation drawing him in from afar.
He felt that the disturbance was mostly caused by Xi Ying's cultivation. After hesitating, he decided to go and protect her, quickly using the Wind Swift Skill to hurry over.
Yuan Ming had not yet come close when from afar, he could see a decades-old tree at the top, glowing with a dim white light, facing the round moon from afar.
As he got slightly closer, Yuan Ming finally saw clearly that it was none other than Silver Cat Xi Ying standing atop the tree.
By this moment, Yuan Ming could feel the distinct fluctuations of Divine Soul Power emanating from that figure and the light around it, gently crashing against his Divine Thought like the tide.
The Silver Cat had also noticed Yuan Ming but was in a critical moment of her cultivation and did not pay attention.
"Is Xi Ying cultivating?"
Yuan Ming was greatly touched in his heart, feeling this immense Divine Soul Power, which he had only seen in his life. Of course, he had no other references but to compare it with his own.
The result was, unsurprisingly, worlds apart.
Just then, his eyes narrowed as he gazed intently at the Silver Cat, only to see its eyes shining like stars, its body poised, and its head held high towards the sky, as if it were howling at the moon.
At the same time, the white glow over its body grew more intense, and a vague human figure suddenly floated out from it, no more than an inch away from the Silver Cat's body, resembling a young woman, transparent and exquisite, and stunningly beautiful.
Yuan Ming just took one look and was stunned.
Even though the figure was extremely blurred and its facial details could not be seen clearly, the blurry outline was much like a Nine Heavens Immortal, exuding an indescribable charm.
At this moment, atop the ancient tree facing deep into the space, matching the deep blue night sky, adorned with a myriad of twinkling stars, and accompanied by the bright round moon, the exquisite figure floated out, appearing even more ethereal and shockingly beautiful.
A moment later, in the high sky, a beam of moonlight, as if tangible, descended from above, enveloping both the silver cat and the silhouette of the woman completely within it.
Inch by inch, the moonlight was absorbed into the silhouette's body, and its glow became increasingly bright, while the fluctuations it previously emitted gradually shrank until they were completely converged.
Yuan Ming's gaze rested solely on that hazy silhouette, unable to be moved away.
A short while later, the silhouette of the woman slowly retracted, entering into the silver cat's body. The white light that enveloped it also gradually faded away.
Yuan Ming came back to his senses and saw the silver cat gracefully flying down, arriving in front of him.
"Xi Ying, is this what the advanced practice of the Moonlight Technique looks like?" Yuan Ming asked.
"Yes," the silver cat answered.
