Bai Lin's face was full of smiles, and after exchanging a few more pleasantries with Yuan Ming, he quickly left with everyone else in tow, looking rather downcast.
As Bai Lin and the others walked away, Immortal Xuanhua opened his mouth as if to say something but was stopped by Yuan Ming, who raised his hand and turned to enter the inner chamber.
He took out a Four Directions Sealing Spirit Talisman and opened a Barrier, then touched the silver Token to the Barrier's light screen. The Barrier immediately shimmered with a layer of silver light, completely isolating the inside from the outside. Only then did he relax.
"Fellow Daoist Yuan, are you truly a disciple of Chang Chun Temple?" Immortal Xuanhua asked eagerly.
"Of course, I am a disciple of Chang Chun Temple. My master and I came from Iron Tiger Town in the Southern Border to Yue Country on business," Yuan Ming said.
"Fortunate, truly fortunate." Immortal Xuanhua looked into Yuan Ming's profound eyes and suddenly felt uneasy, deciding not to inquire further.
He took out the storage magic tool given by Elder Bai Lin and, after infusing it with mana, he waved it towards the nearby ground.
A flash of white light later, there appeared a small pile of spirit stones—no fewer than two hundred; three pieces of spirit wood, two red and one white; and a white jade box.
"It's all thanks to Fellow Daoist Yuan that Bai Lin left these things behind. I only need this Heavenly Glue. The spirit stones are yours," Immortal Xuanhua said as he picked up the white jade box.
Yuan Ming only took away the three pieces of spirit wood.
He recognized these three pieces of spirit wood as Fire Pine Wood, Red Blood Branch, and White Yuan Bamboo. They all contained abundant spiritual power, and he planned to later incorporate them into Black Incense to see if it would prolong the possession time.
Immortal Xuanhua was both in awe and grateful towards Yuan Ming, and without saying much, he put away the spirit stones.
"I'll leave the matter of the Foundation Establishment Spirit Incense to you, Fellow Daoist Xuanhua," Yuan Ming said.
"Rest assured, I'll take care of it," Immortal Xuanhua said, patting his chest confidently.
With the crisis of Xuanhua Temple completely resolved and relying on Yuan Ming's previous words, neither White Dragon Island nor Blue Lizard Wanderer would dare to oppress them in the future. Immortal Xuanhua felt light-hearted and extremely confident about successfully creating the Foundation Establishment Spirit Incense.
...
Seven days later, Immortal Xuanhua successfully emerged from seclusion.
"Congratulations to Fellow Daoist on successfully coming out of seclusion," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
Immortal Xuanhua was half joyful and half worried as he said, "I am truly ashamed; despite using all those materials, in the end, I only barely managed to make two sticks of Spirit Incense."
"To succeed at all is no easy feat and certainly a cause for celebration," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"Now, we can only each take one stick. Whether we can successfully build our foundations is now up to fate," Immortal Xuanhua said, temporarily setting aside his worries as he passed one stick of Spirit Incense to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming took it and looked it over carefully, noticing that the aura it emitted was somewhat similar to that of a Foundation Establishment Pill, which immediately gave him a bit more confidence.
"Then let's each trust in fate and wish each other the best," Yuan Ming said with a laugh.
Immortal Xuanhua nodded silently.
Half a day later, both of them were prepared. Each chose a quiet room and went into seclusion to attempt their Foundation Establishment breakthroughs.
Immortal Xuanhua was oblivious to the fact that Yuan Ming was holding his breath and focusing intently, sitting cross-legged within the quiet room. He silently circulated the Nine Elements Technique, adjusting his state until late into the night.
At midnight, feeling that he had reached his peak condition, Yuan Ming immediately took out a Foundation Establishment Pill and swallowed it whole. He held the Stealing Heaven Tripod in front of his body, close to his Dantian.
As his mana began to circulate, the medicinal power of the Foundation Establishment Pill slowly started to take effect, and a sensation of heat gradually began to rise in the pit of Yuan Ming's stomach.
Feeling that burning sensation, Yuan Ming immediately circulated his mana to control the power and direct it toward his Dantian.
With the constant influx of this hot energy into his Dantian, Yuan Ming felt as if his Dantian had turned into a blazing furnace, relentlessly heating and burning his mana, causing it to rise in temperature.
This searing power was indeed difficult to endure, but it was the necessary path for his mana to transform from gas to liquid, becoming more condensed and pure.
Knowing this was a long and arduous process, Yuan Ming could not be too anxious. He had to remain steady, using the Foundation Establishment Pill's power to gradually refine the mana within his Dantian.
Time passed bit by bit, and Yuan Ming spent a hard twelve days in the quiet room.
In those twelve days, he refined the power of the Foundation Establishment Pill completely, transferring it to his Dantian.
The hot power within his Dantian tormented him constantly, strengthening him; his mana boiled yet he still couldn't get over the final hurdle to achieve the qualitative change from gas to liquid.
At that moment, an incense stick with a unique fragrance was inserted in an incense burner.
It had been burning for over half its length, its crimson flame still flickering at the top, emitting tendrils of thick white smoke.
The smoke enveloped Yuan Ming from all sides, remaining concentrated and not dissipating, as if he were wrapped in a layer of white cotton.
Yuan Ming had his eyes tightly shut, but his brows were knotted; sweat streamed down his cheeks and his expression was one of pain.
Just this morning, he felt that the power of the Foundation Establishment Pill within him had peaked and then started to wane, a sign that was not at all promising. His previous experience told him that this meant his Foundation Establishment was likely to end in failure once again.
At this critical juncture, without hesitation, he lit the Foundation Establishment Spirit Incense. Immediately, azure smoke twirled upward, filling the quiet room.
However, now half a day had passed, and the Foundation Establishment Spirit Incense had burned down significantly. Apart from maintaining the gradually fading power of the Foundation Establishment Pill within him, Yuan Ming did not feel anything special; the mana in his Dantian was still in a state of boiling.
Could it be that even the Foundation Establishment Incense was struggling to compensate for his Spirit Root's deficiencies?

chapters.title: Chapter 255 - 232 Foundation Establishment
chapters.content:
Finally, as the last moments drew near, the Foundation Establishment Incense gradually burned down to its end.
"After so many preparations, is it ultimately still going to end in failure?" Yuan Ming slowly opened his eyes, murmuring with an unwilling tone.
No sooner had he spoken than he couldn't help but take a deep breath.
At that moment, as the flame on the Foundation Establishment Incense extinguished, the yin and yang pattern on the Stealing Heaven Tripod suddenly lit up with brilliance. The thick white mist surrounding Yuan Ming immediately parted into two streams, curling backward and flowing into his nostrils.
Yuan Ming felt a searing sensation travel down his throat and into his chest and abdomen before finally settling into his Dantian.
The next instant, as if thunder had ignited Earth Fire, the mana bubbling within Yuan Ming's Dantian finally broke through the restraints and underwent a qualitative change.
Masses of mana began to condense and shrink continuously, as if completing some miraculous extraction, until they coalesced into droplets of gleaming transparent liquid, accumulating in the Dantian.
"Drip, drip"
Yuan Ming first heard the sound of two water droplets, followed by the overwhelming roar of a strong wind that engulfed his ears.
All he felt was his eardrums swelling, as his entire body became enveloped in powerful strands of nature's Primordial Qi; every pore in his body seemed to expand, greedily sucking in the converging Spiritual Energy.
"Is this the sensation of Condensed Liquid Foundation Establishment?"
Yuan Ming felt his entire being dazed, as if he had drunk a large jar of rich wine, basking in a feeling of bliss.
At this moment, his body was like a self-operating Puppet, almost managing on its own to complete the absorption of nature's spiritual energy, channeling it into the Dantian, refining and extracting it into liquid, and gathering it into that small pond.
After an indeterminable amount of time, Yuan Ming's Dantian finally conveyed a feeling of fullness and saturation. The state of automatically absorbing nature's spiritual energy gradually ceased, and Yuan Ming's Divine Sense returned to normal.
Reluctantly waking from that transcendent state, he eagerly checked his Dantian and found that all stored mana had condensed into a liquid state, forming a lake shimmering with rippling water.
In terms of the total volume of mana, it had increased more than threefold compared to his Qi Refinement period, and as for the purity of the mana, it was even more incomparable.
In fact, having completed the Foundation Establishment with the Qi Refining Thirteen Layers of Cultivation, Yuan Ming's mana was not only purer than that of a common cultivator at the same level, but the quantity was also at least half more.
This gave him an inherent advantage when facing other cultivators at the early stage of Foundation Establishment.
Meanwhile, Yuan Ming felt that his Divine Power, just as Xi Ying had said, had increased by almost half.
By the time he finished his Breathing Control and emerged from seclusion, it was already the morning of the third day.
Yuan Ming, feeling refreshed, pushed open the door to the quiet room to see Immortal Xuanhua sitting on a stone bench in the courtyard with his back toward him.
His shoulders were slightly slouched, looking somewhat dispirited.
Yuan Ming had an idea of what had happened and guessed that the other had likely failed at Foundation Establishment.
The Foundation Establishment was a major barrier on the path of Cultivation and it was common for most people to fail. If not for the Stealing Heaven Tripod bolstering the effects of the Foundation Establishment Incense, whether he could have succeeded remained an uncertainty.
Perceiving footsteps from behind, Immortal Xuanhua turned his head to look.
Seeing that Yuan Ming's face was composed, without any discernible joy or sorrow, he instinctively thought Yuan Ming had failed as well.
"Fellow Daoist Yuan, Foundation Establishment is never easy. Although I managed to refine the Foundation Establishment Incense, I couldn't guarantee a foolproof outcome. Don't take it too hard. We can find more materials in the future and continue refining," Immortal Xuanhua consoled him first.
"About that... Fellow Daoist Xuanhua, I succeeded in Foundation Establishment," Yuan Ming coughed lightly and said.
Immortal Xuanhua was taken aback, staring at Yuan Ming with eyes wide in disbelief.
Seeing him fall silent, Yuan Ming had to take the initiative to say, "Not to hide it from you, it was after three attempts that I finally succeeded."
He purposefully added an extra attempt to emphasize the difficulty of his Foundation Establishment.
To his surprise, Immortal Xuanhua's face took on a bitter expression, "This was my third time as well."
"Your third time? What about the previous two?" Yuan Ming asked, puzzled.
"The Foundation Establishment Pills obtained by spending all my wealth ended in failure. My talents are simply too poor, and my luck... even worse," Immortal Xuanhua said helplessly.
After saying that, he forced a smile and added, "At least you, Fellow Daoist Yuan, have succeeded. That alone proves the Foundation Establishment Incense I refined is not flawed. With this skill, I won't have to worry about going hungry in the future."
"Indeed, that's true," Yuan Ming responded, only able to reply with an embarrassed smile.
"Fellow Daoist Yuan... I should call you Senior Yuan now. What plans do you have for the future?" Immortal Xuanhua asked.
"There's no need for that between us," Yuan Ming said with a chuckle.
"On the path of Cultivation, the mighty are revered. Being one level higher in Cultivation makes one a senior, that's the common sense," Immortal Xuanhua was unusually serious.
"No, we should still address each other as Fellow Daoists. I'm planning to begin my journey soon and will travel alone." Yuan Ming said.
"That's good. I also plan to leave Xuanhua Temple and go on a travel to seek my fortune." Immortal Xuanhua nodded.
"Fellow Daoist Xuanhua, where do you plan to go?" Yuan Ming asked.
"I will visit the Southern Border, Southern Domain, and perhaps I will also go to the South Sea Islands. It is said that many overseas Loose Cultivators reside there, along with a production of unique spiritual materials not found in the Southern Border or Central Plains. Among them are many ores that are useful for incense making," said Immortal Xuanhua, his eyes shining with longing.
"Take care on your travels. I wouldn't have succeeded in Foundation Establishment without your help, Fellow Daoist Xuanhua. Even with my Four Spirit Roots, I managed to succeed, so do not lose heart."
Had Yuan Ming not procured the materials, it would have been impossible for him to make the Foundation Establishment Spirit Incense and to have helped him out of trouble. Speaking of gratitude, it was actually Yuan Ming who was owed more.
After a long moment of contemplation, he took out a blue-colored book and handed it to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming looked intently and realized it was the very secret book of Incense Making treasured by Immortal Xuanhua, which surprised him greatly.
"Fellow Daoist Xuanhua, what is this for?" Yuan Ming blurted out.
"Senior Yuan, you have better aptitudes than I do and enough talent for making Spirit Incense. Now that you've succeeded in Foundation Establishment, you also have a longer lifespan than me, and hence, more time to delve into this skill. I don't want the day to come when I perish, and have this secret technique lost to the world. Therefore, I hope you can make good use of this book and truly bring the art of making Spirit Incense to greater heights," said Immortal Xuanhua earnestly.
For a moment, Yuan Ming was at a loss for words.
"Take it, don't let my hopes go to waste," Immortal Xuanhua urged, as he pushed the book into Yuan Ming's hands.
"I will certainly live up to your expectations," said Yuan Ming, holding his fist in a salute, and responded gravely.
After that, Immortal Xuanhua seemed to have unraveled some knot in his heart, insisting that Yuan Ming treat him to a good meal, vowing not to return until drunk.
Thus, Yuan Ming summoned his Green Cloud Crane, and together with the old Immortal Xuanhua, they headed to a nearby State City. There they found an ordinary restaurant and even booked a private room…
Two days later, Yuan Ming bid his farewell and continued on his journey home, heading northwards.
As he had said, Immortal Xuanhua left Xuanhua Temple and went south.
Seven to eight days later,
Riding his crane and soaring through the sky, Yuan Ming, now after his Foundation Establishment, had a completely different mindset from when he first came to Yue Country. He leisurely held the secret book gifted by Immortal Xuanhua, perusing it without pause.
The record of various Spirit Incense with different effects within the book dazzled him, and he couldn't help itching to try his hand at refining some himself.
As he passed through a small workshop on his journey, Yuan Ming also took the opportunity to purchase some materials. Afterward, he proceeded unhurriedly down the road, refining some uniquely effective Spirit Incense along the way, stopping at scenic spots to stay for a few days.Lоvе this stоry? Shоw yоur suppоrt оn М9VLЕМРYR.
In addition to the seductive scent, Fog Incense, and Beast Attraction Incense that he accidentally made before, he also refined some Qingxuan Incense and Soul Calming Incense to aid in meditative cultivation, as well as Nourishing Body Incense with certain healing properties.
The book also contained incense recipes with special effects, like the Foundation Establishment Incense, but they required more exacting materials and craftsmanship, which Yuan Ming couldn't manage at the time.
Two months later.
In the middle of Yue Country, a small city built near the intersection of two rivers.
Wearing a green robe and holding the edge of his hat, Yuan Ming looked up at the not-so-tall city gate and read the name on the plaque: "Hekou Town."
"It seems the source of the epidemic is right here," Yuan Ming sighed softly, looking towards the gate.
He saw that the two large vermilion gates were half-open, with no soldiers at guard, and only spotted a dirty, emaciated old man, barely alive, leaning against the base of the wall.
Yuan Ming approached to check on the old man, who was already at death's door.
He shook his head, took out an elixir, and tried to put it into the old man's mouth to revive him, but the other party lacked even the strength to open his mouth. Even forcing it open, Yuan Ming feared the old man didn't have the power to chew.
The old man's eyes were lifeless, his expression indifferent, clearly having lost all desire to live.
Helpless, Yuan Ming put the elixir away and walked past the man, entering the city.
He had arrived near Hekou Town three days earlier and discovered that a widespread epidemic had broken out in several nearby market towns and villages.
Yuan Ming didn't ignore the situation, instead, he took action and helped clear the surrounding epidemic.
But after inquiring, he learned that the epidemic first broke out in the now-abandoned "Hekou Town," with the earliest and most severe cases.
The other market towns had initially offered help, but upon realizing they could not contain it, they eventually had to give up, reluctantly.
The unassisted Hekou Town was left to deteriorate, leading to the death of the majority of its population, with the survivors merely waiting for death, devoid of hope.
The local officials were powerless to intervene, and no Cultivation Sect had offered assistance. Yuan Ming, unable to bear it, decided to visit.
Had he not seen it, it might have been different, but having seen it, he wanted to help these mortals; otherwise, he might have struggled to overcome his conscience.

chapters.title: Chapter 256 - 233: Meeting an Old Friend in a Foreign Land
chapters.content:
Upon entering the city, Yuan Ming discovered that the situation inside was even more severe than he had imagined: corpses lay everywhere along the streets and alleyways, some already decaying and emitting a foul stench.
Along the way, he encountered two medical halls and a government office, all piled high with corpses, a horrifying sight.
In the city, the dead outnumbered the living.
Yuan Ming had brought medicine to eradicate the epidemic, originally intending to pour it into the well water for the townspeople to drink and be cured. However, given the current situation, that was naturally impossible.
With his power alone, it was also impossible to go around administering the medicine for treatment.
Therefore, Yuan Ming found a residence, briefly cleaned up the corpses inside, and then took out the incense-making materials he had bought earlier and began to busy himself.
By the time evening came, he had already produced several sticks of pale yellow incense.
The basic material for these incense sticks was the same as that used for the Fog Incense, but he had added some epidemic-eradicating medicinal powder and combined it with some special refining techniques written in the Spiritual Incense Secret Manual.
After the Epidemic Eradication Incense was made, Yuan Ming took it to an open space in the center of Hekou Town and pointed at his forehead.
Four soul crows flew out, three of which landed on the bodies of three recently deceased corpses nearby, while the remaining one flew high above to keep watch for him.
The three corpses, after being entered by the soul crows, lit up with a faint green glow in their eyes and staggered to their feet, approaching Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming gave each of them a stick of Epidemic Eradication Incense to carry and sent them in three different directions around the town, while he himself sat in the center with the Stealing Heaven Tripod and a stick of incense inserted into it.
When the four corpses reached the appropriate positions, Yuan Ming controlled them and himself to ignite the long incense together.
Once the Epidemic Eradication Incense was lit, in just a short moment, large plumes of yellow smoke began to rise from various parts of Hekou Town and soon enveloped the entire town in thick smoke.
In the midst of the dense smoke, the townspeople, already on their last breath, believed they had succumbed to the underworld.
Given their current physical state, they had no strength to avoid it and simply ignored it.
But quite the contrary, upon inhaling the thick smoke, each of them felt revitalized, shedding their previous state of dejection, uncertain if this was merely a dying flash of vitality or if they were truly healed.
After a long time, as the thick smoke gradually dissipated, those who were still alive found themselves free of the epidemic's influence. When they could once again see their surroundings clearly and realized they were still in the town, they burst into tears of joy, and their crying echoed throughout the town.
By then, Yuan Ming had already put away the Stealing Heaven Tripod, and all four soul crows had returned to his body.
Since advancing to the Foundation Establishment, his Soul Power had greatly increased; now, even releasing all six soul crows did not burden his Soul Power too much.
After a brief period of Breathing Control, Yuan Ming recovered as usual.
As he opened his eyes, he saw that some of the recovered townspeople had started to gather around.
These people were still very weak, some needing to support each other just to stand up.
But they, having heard from a child who witnessed the entire process of Yuan Ming casting, gathered around, calling him their savior.T@hi%s# cha-p&t@er* was o@ri^g%i.na.l%l$y p$osted* on *.+
"Kneel in gratitude for the Immortal Master saving our lives."
It was unclear who spoke first, but immediately others followed suit.
Soon, people started shouting, "Kneel in gratitude for the Immortal Master saving our lives," and one after another, they knelt down, performing a grand gesture of kowtow towards Yuan Ming.
"You are all just recovering from a great epidemic and are still weak; do not exhaust yourselves with such gestures, but go back quickly, eat, and recuperate. You still need to take proper care of the funeral affairs of your deceased relatives—please, go back," Yuan Ming urged, albeit reluctantly.
However, more survivors began to approach and continued to bow and give thanks.
Knowing persuasion was futile, Yuan Ming swiftly slapped his Spiritual Beast Bag, released the Green Cloud Crane, and swiftly mounted it to ascend into the sky.
"He is an Immortal, truly an Immortal…"
"Thanks to the Immortal Master for saving our lives."
"We are saved!"
The excitement grew among the people on the open ground in the town.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming had no choice but to leave first.
As they watched Yuan Ming leave, the townspeople who had walked on the brink of death at Ghost Gate finally got up.
A clan elder, who had once been quite influential, suddenly spoke up to the crowd, "The Immortal asks for nothing in return and leaves after bestowing his grace. We are not an ungrateful people; we should build a shrine for the Immortal and offer incense."
"Yes, we must build a shrine for the Immortal Master! Erect a monument with his deeds!" someone immediately responded.
"Scholar Luu, are you still alive?" the clan elder, gathering his strength, called out.
"Uncle, I am still alive, still alive indeed," a scholar in the crowd immediately answered.
"Have you gotten a clear look at the appearance of the Immortal Master? When you return, draw a portrait so we can sculpt a divine statue based on it," the elder shouted.
Hearing this, Scholar Luu had some difficulty, as the Immortal Master wore a conical hat that obscured his features, but he had no choice but to agree reluctantly.
In later generations, a temple named "Epidemic Eradication Temple" appeared in Hekou Town, featuring a statue wearing a conical hat, standing atop an immortal crane. Although it wasn't officially sanctioned by the officials, it always attracted bustling crowds, with people traveling from afar and keeping the temple popular for centuries without interruption.
But that is a story for another time. Let's return to Yuan Ming, who, after this minor episode, mounted his Green Cloud Crane and left Hekou Town, continuing northward.
Along the way, he delved into the Spiritual Incense Secret Manual and found that it contained numerous formulas for incenses that could heal diseases and preserve health. Most were of mild effect to cultivators but were precious spiritual elixirs for the common folk.
Since the materials needed were very common, Yuan Ming refined some in his spare time from cultivation, improving his incense-making skills and serendipitously healing the sick and distressed he met along his journey, giving him a sense of peace and satisfaction.
During his journey, Yuan Ming finally arrived at Haiyan City, located in the northeast of Yue Country near the East Sea.
When they parted in Black Rock City, Wu Lu had mentioned he would be resting here for a while and had invited Yuan Ming to join him.
However, at that time, Yuan Ming was eager to return to Da Jin and had other plans, so he did not agree.
Now that he was in Haiyan City, he thought of visiting Wu Lu again, as he also had a favor to ask of him.
Haiyan City, named for the clear and calm 'Hai River' at its mouth, is known not only for its famous landmark, the "Wave-Struck Cliffs," but also for the grand tide seen every fifteenth day of the eighth month.
The season wasn't right, so he couldn't witness the magnificent tide.
But Yuan Ming's interest lay not in sightseeing; meeting Wu Lu would be enough.
Upon entering Haiyan City, Yuan Ming found that, despite being smaller, the city was no less prosperous than the Da Jin Capital.
Branches and tributaries of the Hai River ran through the city, enriching its water system and creating a network that formed a distinctive landscape with streets and buildings along the river.
While the customs and architectural styles of the southern parts of Yue Country still resembled those of the Southern Border, and some traces remained in the central region, Haiyan City in the north fully embraced the style of the Central Plains.
Its bustling streets were lined with architecture and tile-roofed shops, creating a lively and festively earthy atmosphere.
Upon entering the city, Yuan Ming did not immediately seek out Wu Lu but instead stopped at a pavilion to drink tea and listen to music, thoroughly relaxing himself.
When he was in Da Jin Capital, he often visited pavilions to enjoy music, sometimes even composing his own poetry and music. Though not as prolific as his paintings and tales, his compositions were still circulated in Da Jin.
In the afternoon, after a pleasant bath in the inn and changing into fresh clothes, he left to head towards the famous Sea View Cliff in the eastern part of the city.
Yuan Ming had already determined Wu Lu's whereabouts before arriving in Haiyan City, through the use of the Stealing Heaven Tripod and incense possession.
Wu Lu was residing in a cliffside inn next to Sea View Cliff, overlooking the East Sea, where the entire Haiyan City's view of the sea waves crashing against the cliffs and stirring thousands of layers of surf could be seen.
When Yuan Ming found Wu Lu, the latter was sitting on the second floor of the Sea View Tower Inn, by a window facing the sea, with a few dishes and pouring his own drinks, clearly enjoying his time immensely.
Seeing Yuan Ming seat himself opposite, Wu Lu visibly froze, evidently in disbelief.
"Brother Yuan..."
"Brother Wu Lu, you are well, I hope," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"Brother Yuan, it's really you! What a coincidence!" Wu Lu, holding his cup, paused for a moment, suddenly filled with inexplicable joy.
This joy of "reunion after a long separation" combined with the surprise of "meeting an old friend in a foreign land" made him momentarily feel an uncanny sense of surrealness upon seeing Yuan Ming.
His emotional surge was not solely due to these feelings.
In fact, ever since deciding to visit Wu Lu, Yuan Ming had already used the Stealing Heaven Tripod to possess him three times with Black Incense, each time subtly suggesting to Wu Lu that he regarded him as a lifelong close friend.
As a result, Wu Lu sometimes thought his own spirit was troubled as he often found himself unexpectedly thinking of Yuan Ming.
However, the Black Incense made using Xuanhua Temple's incense ashes seemed somehow less effective in mental suggestion than those obtained from Liu Xin Sect, unfortunately, the incense ashes from Liu Xin Sect had already run out.
"How did you end up here?" Wu Lu asked in surprise.
"I was traveling north back to Da Jin when I encountered unexpected changes, so I detoured through Yue Country. Knowing you were here, Brother Wu Lu, how could I not meet up with you?" Yuan Ming replied with a smile.
"How did you know I was eating here?" Wu Lu asked.
"It was merely by chance. I saw this place had a nice scene, and unexpectedly found you here," Yuan Ming said.
"What happened to you on the road?" Wu Lu asked, frowning.
"Near Iron Tiger Town, I ran into some old debtors and managed to collect some interest on their debts," Yuan Ming nodded and stated.
Wu Lu closely observed Yuan Ming, his pupils suddenly shrinking in surprise, "Brother Yuan, you have completed your Foundation Establishment?"

chapters.title: Chapter 257 - 234: Stealing Techniques
chapters.content:
"Yes, this time Dawn gave me a Foundation Establishment Pill, and with nothing better to do during my journey, I passed through a quiet valley and couldn't resist taking it. Against all odds, someone with my modest talent successfully established their foundation with just one pill, truly a stroke of luck," Yuan Ming said with a chuckle.
"Congratulations, congratulations! How can you call this luck? This is a perfect example of accumulating experience until it pays off. With this leap across a great divide, you've effectively added a hundred years to your lifespan, and grand prospects await you," Wulu hurriedly congratulated him with a clasped fist.
"With this, we can still enjoy wine and laughter a hundred years from now," Yuan Ming responded.
The two burst into hearty laughter together.
"It's also after establishing my foundation that I remembered something. Back when we were in Biluo Cave, Brother Wu Lu, you must have been at the Foundation Establishment Stage already, right? How did you conceal your cultivation and still manage to deceive so many elders?" Yuan Ming asked.
Upon hearing this, a flicker of pride passed through Wulu's eyes, but he quickly concealed it, waved his hand, and said:
"Ah, it's just a trivial trick, not worth mentioning, not worth mentioning."
"Brother Wulu, did you create this method of hiding your cultivation yourself?" Yuan Ming asked.
"I don't have such talents. My origins are complicated, please forgive me," Wulu said after glancing at Yuan Ming.
"Brother Wulu, Biluo Cave has been destroyed, and now I am but a lost spirit. If I could learn your method, I could masquerade as a Qi Refining cultivator and manage to enter a reputable sect," Yuan Ming sighed and said.
Upon hearing this, Wulu remained silent, his face showing a mix of contemplation and hesitation, but he still shook his head and sighed, "Brother Yuan, if it were anything else, I might have agreed, but I really can't share this skill with others."
"Brother Wulu, I own multiple magic artifacts, have Spirit Stones, even spirit beasts! If you would impart this secret skill to me, whatever you ask for in return, I will do everything in my power to fulfill," Yuan Ming said.
"To be honest, this method of concealing cultivation is, is... really not something I can disclose. If it wasn't for a mission arranged by my family that compelled me to break an array out of necessity, I normally keep this technique secret. Please keep this confidential, Brother Yuan," Wulu said with a troubled expression, though he was tempted by Yuan Ming's various elusive vines, he still refused.
"Since that's the case, Brother Wulu, don't trouble yourself. I was too presumptuous. How about this—should I have any secret techniques in the future, we could exchange them fairly," Yuan Ming said, testing the waters since he knew his own bargaining chips were not sufficient.
"Alright, let's talk about it when the time comes. Now that we've reunited after so long, let's drink well and not let this meeting go to waste," Wulu said with a smile.
Having said this, he called for the inn's servant to set up the tableware, added more dishes and wine, and started chatting with Yuan Ming over drinks.
In the evening, after watching the sunset together, Yuan Ming bid his farewell with a fist salute and returned to his lodging.
At night, Yuan Ming once again took out the Stealing Heaven Tripod and lit the Black Incense.
With the smoke spiraling upwards, Yuan Ming quickly completed the possession and descended upon Wulu once again.
At that moment, Wulu was standing by the room's window, listening to the sound of the surging waves outside and gazing into the dark ocean in the distance.
Yuan Ming's request during the day was something he absolutely could not agree to.
Just then, in the distant sky, a snow-white bird with a red mark on its brow flew towards them.
The bird swept past the shadows of the trees outside and landed at Wulu's window.
Wulu quickly grabbed the bird, and from its ankle, he removed a delicately crafted Jade Scroll threaded with golden silk.
"A Jade Scroll message?" Yuan Ming thought to himself.
When Wulu saw the Jade Scroll, he instinctively frowned, evidently somewhat resistant to it.
At the same time, Yuan Ming faintly sensed his thoughts: "Another mission, those ambitious old men in the family are truly greedy."
While speaking, he removed the mini Jade Scroll and pressed it against his forehead.
In the next instant, the contents of the Jade Scroll appeared in Wulu's Sea of Consciousness, and Yuan Ming also reviewed them.
The content of the Jade Scroll was straightforward, instructing him to infiltrate a sect known as 'Fire Origin Sect' as a new disciple, climb the ranks to become a core disciple, and learn the sect's core Cultivation Technique, the 'Red Fire Heart Method,'
The Jade Scroll recorded the location of the Fire Origin Sect and an overview of the sect, mentioning the next disciple recruitment event and providing some advice.
Besides that, the Jade Scroll also praised Wulu's previous undercover work in the Biluo Cave, stating that he had not only accomplished the mission set by his family but also cooperated with the Dawn Alliance's task, killing two birds with one stone, which was highly commendable.
The family recorded his achievements and promised that a tenth of the profits from the sale of the skills and secret techniques from Biluo Cave would be allocated to him.
Upon reading this, Wulu didn't exhibit much joy but couldn't help but curse, "Such great risk for this mission, and they only give me a tenth of the profits? All the old folks do is order others around; why don't they do it themselves."
After cursing, he couldn't help but think that friends like Yuan Ming, whom he'd met by chance without any complicated interests involved, felt more precious and genuine.
Yuan Ming, sensing his thoughts, couldn't help but reflect: was his psychological manipulation going too far?
He gathered his doubts and only then remembered the real purpose of his visit, silently thinking, "Brother Wulu, sorry," and then began discreetly cultivating the Moonlight Technique to strengthen his Divine Thought, firmly locking onto Wulu.
Then, he began to repeatedly say in his mind: "It's been a long time since I practiced the secret technique, let's practice it again…"
At first, it had no effect.
It wasn't until Yuan Ming repeated it for the thirteenth time that Wulu, as if possessed, echoed the sentiment.
"Next, he was to embark on a mission again, and he knew he must revise the secret technique again."
After speaking, he was taken aback himself, unable to understand why such a thought had occurred, but then he remembered Yuan Ming's request and felt that it was because Yuan Ming had mentioned it today that he had thought of it.
In fact, this was the third time Yuan Ming had hinted at practicing the technique of concealing his cultivation during possession.
The effectiveness of his mental suggestions was actually quite limited. Trying to guide the actions of the possessed, the more complex the action or the more it deviated from the current situation, the lesser the chances of success.
Yuan Ming had thought he would definitely fail, which was why he had probed earlier during the day.
Unexpectedly, whether it was because of Yuan Ming's mention during the day or because Wulu had accepted a new covert mission and needed to prepare, he really did respond to Yuan Ming's psychological suggestion.
He closed the windows, set up an array, released a spider that quickly span a large web around the room. Then Wulu sat down on his bed, crossed-legged, and began to regulate his breathing.
Yuan Ming knew he was about to practice the secret technique, and he got excited, focusing intently on the movements of Wulu's mana.
Soon, Wulu finished his breathing exercise and began to silently recite the mnemonic of the secret technique in his mind.
Only then did Yuan Ming understand that the secret technique was called "Hidden Element Technique," a technique that reverses the flow of mana to sequester some of the Dantian power, similar to a Sealing Skill.
As Wulu's mana reversed, his brow suddenly furrowed, his face turned red, and his breathing became rapid.
When mana flows naturally in the meridians, it's like a river flowing smoothly, but reversing it is like a wave surging backward, painfully scraping the ground.
Even though Yuan Ming was just possessing Wulu, he could clearly feel his pain, even hearing his heart pounding several times faster than a normal person.
This made him recall the scene he had witnessed when he had rescued Wulu as a Fur Beast Slave in the Ten Thousand Mountains, making his scalp tingle for a moment.
It seemed that practicing Hidden Element Technique carried certain risks; he would have to be more cautious in his future cultivation.
Fortunately, the process was not too long. After only about two dozen breaths, the pain of the mana reversal subsided, and the dispersed mana in the veins reversed back into Wulu's Dantian, constrained by a Sealing force and dormant within.
Simultaneously, his breathing and heartbeat gradually returned to normal.
Apparently, because it was only a practice, Wulu's aura had fallen from the Foundation Establishment Stage back to the Qi Refining Seventh Level, and not completely sealed to that of a normal mortal.
That would mean sealing all his mana, and the process of mana reversal and meridian reversal would probably be longer, incurring even more pain.
After finishing the practice, Wulu checked his body, found nothing abnormal, placed a hand on his Dantian, and silently recited the unlocking mnemonic. Mana flowed from his palm into his Dantian, immediately releasing the seal.
The sealed mana awakened abruptly, bursting out of the Dantian, causing Wulu's face to flush and his head to spin.
Before he could fully recover, the time for Yuan Ming's possession had already reached its end.
When he woke up in his own room, he immediately closed his eyes and sat cross-legged, recalling every line of the mnemonic Wulu had recited and every detail of his mana circulation.
This text was acquired from *.
With the enhancement of his powerful Divine Soul, this was not difficult.
After he was clear on every detail, Yuan Ming immediately closed his eyes and began his first attempt.
An hour later, his face flushed, his body aching, he collapsed onto the bed, his chest heaving.
The first attempt had failed as expected. While possessing Wulu, he hadn't felt it much, but now, facing the pain of the meridian reversal alone, he realized it was truly bone-deep. Everything has a price.
Yuan Ming grimaced and struggled on the bed for a long time before gradually calming down.
Throughout the process, his mind never stopped thinking about what he might have overlooked. Once he had recovered, he immediately started the second attempt.
Then the third, the fourth...
By dawn, when the east was already pale with the light of early dawn.
Yuan Ming was sitting cross-legged on the bed, calm, his aura now clearly at the Qi Refining Seventh Level—he had succeeded.
The "Hidden Element Technique" was indeed against the natural order.
He took a moment to regulate his breathing, allowing his body to adjust to the state of having his mana sealed and suppressed, then he got up and moved around the yard, before using the unlocking method to restore the Dantian power.
At noon, Wulu actively sought out Yuan Ming.
Without asking, Yuan Ming knew he was coming to say goodbye, ready to head off to his next mission.
Seeing Yuan Ming looking listless, Wulu felt an inexplicable guilt.
In fact, Yuan Ming also felt guilty. Regardless, he had stolen Wulu's secret technique, even though he had taken it using his own skills, it was somewhat unfair to him.
Both harboring their thoughts, they bid farewell but both told each other to take great care.
Indeed, the challenges they both were about to face were far from easy, each carrying its own risks, yet neither sufficient to discuss with others.

chapters.title: Chapter 258 - 235: Guoguo Did a Great Job
chapters.content:
Half a month later, in a humble inn room within a small border town of Da Jin.
Dawn, at the crack of dawn.
Yuan Ming, after a night of cultivating the Moonlight Technique, slowly opened his eyes.
After entering the Fourth Level of the cultivation technique, the speed of his cultivation noticeably slowed down, but this was within expectations and not something to be overly concerned about.
He glanced outside the window and saw the shadows of the trees swaying, which reminded him somewhat of his house in the Fire Refining Hall.
"I wonder where Xi Ying is now?" Yuan Ming couldn't help but think.
The next moment, a thought arose in his heart: check on what Xi Ying was doing now.
Given that it was just after daybreak, and considering that Xi Ying was likely still in bed, Yuan Ming sat cross-legged again and meditated for quite some time, all the way until nearly noon, before he took out the Stealing Heaven Tripod.
Yuan Ming twirled a stick of Black Incense between his fingers, pondering in silence.
He obviously couldn't just possess Xi Ying, or rather, Xiao Ying directly; and possessing Xiao Yao might not guarantee seeing Xi Ying either, presenting a bit of a dilemma for him.
"Guoguo, it's up to you," Yuan Ming said with a focused gaze and a smile.
Having said that, he inserted the Black Incense and flicked the incense tip with his fingertip, lighting it immediately.
A flash of red light appeared on the head of the incense. As the smoke curled up, Yuan Ming's vision blurred, with only the figure of the silver cat coming to mind.
Time passed indeterminably, and Yuan Ming's vision cleared to see only a white embroidered shoe covered by gauzy skirts, beautifully stitched with a bright orchid flower.
"A foot?" Yuan Ming was taken aback.
"Guoguo, why have you run down to the ground again? Your feet are dirty, come here for a hug," a pleasant female voice said at that moment.
Then, Yuan Ming saw the embroidered shoe step back as a pretty young woman stooped down, cupping the silver cat under its arms and lifted it up.
Through Guoguo's eyes, Yuan Ming saw the woman's beautiful face, and though he knew the soul inside her was Xi Ying, he still felt unaccustomed to it for a moment.
In particular, witnessing the gentle peaks of Xiao Ying's chest from the strange high angle through Guoguo's eyes was a unique experience Yuan Ming had never had before.
He instinctively wanted to turn his head away to avert his gaze.
Xi Ying, seeing Guoguo suddenly turn its head to the side, thought something on that side attracted it and followed its gaze, but only saw the plum tree outside the pavilion with nothing there.
"What are you looking at?"
She forced Guoguo's head back around, facing her chest once again.
Yuan Ming, left with no choice, turned his head away again. His mind flooded with distracting thoughts, barely noticing that Guoguo's movements were almost entirely influenced by him at the moment.
Seeing Guoguo struggling a bit, Xi Ying didn't force the matter and then placed it on the stone table in front of her before sitting down herself.
On the stone table, a pot of tea was brewing, with six tea cups, one of which was already filled with tea, the aroma mingling with spiritual energy, wafting through the air.
"Guoguo, it's so boring staying here. In a few days, we'll go out and have fun," Xi Ying said, resting her head on her snow-white arm like a lotus root, staring at the silver cat in front of her.
Yuan Ming, looking into her bright eyes, felt as if he could see through the pupils to the shadow within, and his mood lightened considerably.
Just as Yuan Ming was silently delighted, the silver cat's ears suddenly perked up, hearing footsteps in the distance and looking toward the outside of the pavilion.
He saw two figures, one after another, walking this way along a winding path leading from the pavilion.
Xi Ying had also turned her gaze in that direction by this time, but her expression turned slightly somber, and her brows furrowed as she said, "How annoying, they're here again."
Soon after, a man and a woman entered the pavilion in succession.
The one in the lead was a young man dressed in a white Cloud Brocade Robe, wearing a carved jade crown, with striking features and a handsome appearance. Only the slightly upturned corners of his eyes gave him a somewhat wicked charm.
The woman following him was wearing a water-green blouse; her figure was slender and elegant with promise in her apricot eyes, glances occasionally landing on the man ahead of her.
"Ying'er!" As soon as the man entered the pavilion, he affectionately called out.
The woman behind him frowned upon hearing this, her gaze shifting to Xi Ying with a clearly jealous expression in her eyes.
The silver cat, upon hearing this shout, involuntarily turned around, unwilling to see the person.
"Stop it, Guan Chen. I've said many times, don't call me that, we're not that familiar," Xi Ying looked at the man in the brocade robe and hastily raised her hand to stop him.
The brocade-robed man looked puzzled but showed no displeasure, instead expressing confusion as he said,
"Ying'er, after a trip to the North Territory, you have changed your attitude towards me so much? But we've met several times, haven't we?"
As he said this, he poured himself a cup of tea.
"We have met only three times. If you continue calling me that, I'll ask you to leave immediately," Xi Ying coldly replied.
"Alright, alright, then I'll call you Miss Xiao. I fell in love with you at first sight. I believe there will come a day when you will accept me. No matter how late that day is, I will wait for you, even if it means waiting until the end of time," Guan Chen declared his feelings with passion. Hearing this, Xi Ying rolled her eyes, Yuan Ming felt a chill in his heart, and Guoguo wriggled uncomfortably, while the woman with the yearning gaze watched the man wistfully.
"Are you done or not? If you have nothing else, please leave," Xi Ying said with a look of disgust.
"Xiao Ying, don't go too far," the previously silent woman finally couldn't hold back and snapped angrily.
Xi Ying turned her head to look at her, her eyes not hiding her sympathy.
"My cousin is fond of you; he has made advances many times. You could just refuse him, so why treat my cousin like this?" the woman said furiously.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming couldn't help but find it amusing, and Guoguo also stood up from the table.
"Fu Yao, don't be so impolite to Miss Xiao," said Guan Chen before Xi Ying could speak.
"Cousin, I just can't stand it..." Fu Yao immediately looked teary-eyed and aggrieved.
"Miss Xiao, my little cousin is ignorant, don't mind her. I came to you because I know you are preparing a birthday gift for the Xiao Family's Ancestor. I have recently collected a Dragon Saliva Pearl from the South Sea; it's the size of a chicken egg and extremely precious, perfect as a birthday gift," Guan Chen said to Xi Ying, again with an adoring and peachy-eyed expression.
"There's no need, I have already prepared the birthday gift myself. The Dragon Saliva Pearl is a fine item; you should keep it for yourself," Xi Ying refused without a second thought.
"Miss Xiao, why must there be a distance between us..."
Guan Chen hadn't finished speaking when "smack," Xi Ying set her teacup down on the table with force. She had grown weary of Guan Chen's annoyance and her anger was starting to get the better of her.
Just as she was about to land a slap, someone else couldn't take it anymore.
"Get out of here," Yuan Ming's Divine Soul issued a silent growl within the silver cat.
The next instant, Guoguo suddenly leaped up from the stone table, raising a paw and swiping at the teacup in Guan Chen's hand.
After all, Guan Chen was a Cultivator and immediately noticed the silver cat's abnormality.
But by the time he reacted, it was too late.
With a "bang," the silver cat's paw struck Guan Chen's teacup, and he felt it fly out of his hand, not knowing where it disappeared to.
Silence descended upon the pavilion; everyone was somewhat stunned.
Both Xi Ying and Fu Yao turned to look directly at the silver cat, faces full of disbelief.
Yuan Ming, within the silver cat, was also taken aback: Why are you all looking at me? It was just a thought; how did Guoguo act so swiftly?
He then realized that humans and beasts are different after all. The Black Incense he replicated couldn't control human actions. Even when enhanced, it could only influence simple movements of the possessed person by continuous suggestion.
But Guoguo was after all just a cat, a spirit beast with undeveloped consciousness, and its Divine Soul was not as sophisticated as that of humans with Innate intelligence and was thus more easily influenced by his thoughts.
"Ah, cousin, are you alright?" Fu Yao was ultimately concerned about her cousin and was the first to shout out in concern.
"Ah, I'm sorry, but look, even Guoguo doesn't like you. I think you and your little cousin make a great match. Cherish the one before you," Xi Ying said, cuddling the silver cat affectionately.
After all, she was currently in Xiao Ying's body and had to act a bit more reserved.
A hint of hesitation flashed in Guan Chen's eyes but he concealed it well.
Still maintaining his noble demeanor, he said, "It's no trouble, why would I mind a cat, let alone a spirit pet that I would like very much!"
"This is not a spirit pet; it's my good friend. The one who understands my intentions the best," said Xi Ying with a light smile.
Yuan Ming felt Guoguo purr contentedly, rubbing its head affectionately against Xiao Ying.
"Ha ha, no wonder it's so perceptive; only such a perceptive Guoguo is worthy of you," Guan Chen laughed heartily.
Xi Ying could no longer endure this man's pestering, so she excused herself and left in a hurry, cuddling the silver cat and not bothering with the tea utensils.Your support on * keeps this series going.
"Guoguo, well done!" It wasn't until they were far away that she kissed the silver cat on the mouth, praising it.
And Guoguo, touched by the affectionate gesture, was even happier.
Yuan Ming had yet to savor Xiao Ying's kiss when suddenly everything went dark, and his vision from the silver cat was lost.
Back in the pavilion, Guan Chen's gaze dimmed as he watched Xiao Ying's retreating figure.
Fu Yao wanted to say something several times but felt there was nothing to say, feeling unspeakably bitter.
...
Yuan Ming returned to his own body, his mood greatly lifted, and he couldn't help but hum a tune.
"A fair maiden travels south as I head north, their traces hard to find across the world.
Mists and smoke waver between heaven and earth, Divine Thought connects with spiritual awareness.
Where does the future lie? Only shadows rush on endlessly."
He soon left the inn, leaving behind the small town. Riding on his Green Cloud Crane, he headed straight for Da Jin Capital.

chapters.title: Chapter 259 - 236: Gaining Fame Through Misfortune
chapters.content:
Time had reached past noon.
Underneath the tall city tower with its blue-grey roof tiles, soldiers clad in armor stood between battlements holding long spears, their postures straight and imposing.
Below the city tower, the grey wall stretched endlessly, and right in its center, a grand entrance with one high and two lower archways stood wide open. The stream of people and horses coming and going was ceaseless, a portrait of prosperity.
The fierce sun hung in the sky as the gigantic shadow of the city gate enveloped the crowd entering and leaving, crossing the drawbridge and the moat, stretching all the way to Yuan Ming's feet.
Gazing at the familiar gates, Yuan Ming lifted his head slightly, his gaze finally landing on the grey stone plaque above the archway.
In the plaque were only two bold and vigorous characters: "Qu Jiang."
It was under this plaque, years ago, that Yuan Ming bid farewell to the crowd seeing him off, leaving the capital of Da Jin. He and Lin Junsheng, carrying the titles of main and deputy emissaries, led the mission to the Southern Border, brimming with ambition and radiating vigor.
But now, things were no longer the same.
He fell silent for a moment, collecting his scattered thoughts, and stepped towards the city.
"Make way, make way!"
Just as he crossed the drawbridge, the sound of horsewhips and shouts came from behind Yuan Ming.
He turned his head to look, and saw three or four soldiers in full armor, riding tall horses, wielding whips, they were driving away the carriages and the common folk in front of the city gate.
They were rough, but their horsewhips didn't actually strike anyone; they were only to intimidate.
Further away, a large convoy of vehicles moved slowly, their banners unfurling in the wind revealing the character "Zhao."
Yuan Ming's brows furrowed slightly, but he said nothing and, like the frightened commoners beside him, stepped aside.
Soon, a path wide enough for two horse-drawn carriages to pass side by side was cleared before the gates, and the convoy bearing the Zhao banners made its way through.
The convoy was sizable, its horses and men plenty, with soldiers on warhorses guarding both the front and rear. The carriages in the middle, though not luxurious, bore woodwork and carvings that were simple yet majestic—clearly not meant for ordinary folks.
However, upon seeing the carriage decorations and the Zhao banners, a thoughtful look crossed Yuan Ming's face.
As the convoy drew near, the city guards at the gate seemed to grow tense, and a soldier clad in the Gate Captain's armor hurried out from the tower, making it down to the entrance just before the arrival of the convoy.
The convoy stopped before the gate, and from the leading carriage, a servant lifted the curtain to reveal an old man inside with white hair and a severe expression.
"Greetings, Marquis Zhao," the Gate Captain said with a smile, stepping forward to bow to the old man.
Meanwhile, beside Yuan Ming, a man dressed as a merchant whispered to his companion, "Brother Lu, whose convoy is this? Why such grandeur?"
His companion glanced around and lowered his voice: "Keep it down. This is General Jingbei's convoy. If we disturb them, our lives wouldn't be enough to make amends."
"That domineering? I've come from the south. Can you fill me in?" The merchant was taken aback. Brought to you by *.
"You haven't been to the north; you wouldn't know. General Zhao has been stationed at the borders for many years, and he's known to be domineering with an imposing reputation," his companion said with a face full of awe.
On the side, Yuan Ming chuckled without a sound. Whether General Jingbei was domineering, he did not know, but he remembered that in his youth, General Zhao was a regular visitor at his home and had watched him grow up.
On the other side, General Zhao merely nodded slightly to the Gate Captain. The servant dropped the curtain, and the convoy resumed its slow progress, with the scene in front of the gate quickly returning to its previous state.
But beside Yuan Ming, the two men were still chatting: "But still, General Zhao is usually stationed in the North Territory and rarely returns to the Capital unless something big happens. The year is far from over, so why would he suddenly enter the Capital with troops?"
"How would I know? Probably some big development with the court," said the merchant as he walked and talked with his companion.
By then, Yuan Ming had reached the gate entrance, where the city guard asked, "Name?"
"Yuan Ming," Yuan Ming replied.
"Yuan Ming? Young Master Yuan of the Yuan Mansion?" the city guard said in surprise.
"Yes, that's me," Yuan Ming responded.
To his surprise, once the guard saw Yuan Ming's face clearly, he exclaimed and excitedly reached for Yuan Ming's hand.
Someone beside them said, "Yuan Ming? Young Master Yuan, is it really you? I heard you went missing on your mission to the Southern Border and feared something had happened to you. To think you're still alive!" Suddenly, as if remembering something, the man patted his clothes and pulled out a roll of silk.
Wrapped in the silk was an exquisitely made book with four embossed golden characters on the cover— "Young Master Sheng's Southern Journey."
"I'm a true fan of yours, Young Master Yuan. I came here today specifically to buy this deluxe edition of Young Master Sheng's Southern Journey, but to think I'd actually meet you by the gate," the man said, his eyes shining bright with anticipation as he presented the deluxe book to Yuan Ming: "Could I trouble you for an autograph? I will treasure it!"
Unable to withstand his enthusiasm, Yuan Ming took the book but then said, "I'm sorry, I don't have a pen," and tried to leave.
"Ah, my oversight, please wait a moment," the man said in annoyance, slapping his forehead and turning to grab someone nearby, "Excuse me, could you lend me a pen and ink?"
"Pen and ink? Why would I carry those things on me when I'm out handling business?" The passerby was perplexed at the request, glancing between him and Yuan Ming, then his eyes suddenly lit up. "Hey, aren't you Young Master Yuan Ming?"
"Indeed, I've just returned from the Southern Border," Yuan Ming said with a smile.
"'Young Master Sheng's Southern Journey' is truly a riveting read, your experiences are absolutely thrilling," the man said.
Before Yuan Ming could respond, the passerby realized he had no writing brush and, just like the man before, turned to seek a writing brush from others on the road.
Word spread quickly, one telling ten, ten telling a hundred, and in no time at all, a large crowd had gathered around Yuan Ming.
The commotion near the city gate soon caught the Gate Captain's attention.
"Make way, make way, don't crowd around, what's happened here... Young Master Yuan?" he directed the city guards to push through the crowd, and when he caught a clear glimpse of Yuan Ming, he too exclaimed in surprise.
Yuan Ming was puzzled: "You recognize me as well?"
"Of course! Young Master Yuan, when you set out from the city with the delegation in military splendor years ago, it was my shift! Even though you look different now, taller, I still recognize you. After all, since your disappearance, the books you've written have sold out, with some editions being extremely hard to find!" the Gate Captain immediately said with a smile on his face while commanding his subordinates to part the crowd.
Yuan Ming listened and couldn't help but let out an embarrassed chuckle, remembering how it was said that an artist's works soar in value after their death, and now it seemed it was his turn.
At that moment, someone in the crowd was desperately trying to squeeze forward, yelling, "Young Master Yuan, I've found a writing brush!"
The Gate Captain's face darkened, about to scold, but Yuan Ming stopped him: "Let him through, I promised to sign for him."
"Young Master Yuan is still so kind-hearted," the Gate Captain complimented, ordering his men to clear some space.
Yuan Ming took the book, wrote a sentence of encouragement for the man's daughter, and added his signature, and the man retreated with a goofy smile.
Seeing this, the crowd grew even more excited, and numerous people also fished out copies of the same book from who knows where, all crying out to receive Yuan Ming's autograph.
"Young Master Yuan, is your 'Southern Travel Chronicles' a true story?"
"Young Master Yuan, please wait."
The pressure on the city guards increased greatly for a time.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming said loudly, "Gentlemen, I understand your feelings, but I have been away for many years and have just returned to the Capital today. My heart longs for my parents in the family home, and I really cannot linger long. Please understand. After resting for a few days, I will visit Tianming Bookstore and catch up with everyone."
Upon hearing this, various shouts of understanding burst from the crowd.
The Gate Captain wiped off a bead of sweat and hurriedly had his men escort Yuan Ming into the city.
But as soon as he passed through the city gate, Yuan Ming heard a roar like the tide from the crowd.
In the bustling streets, heads were packed tightly together, the surging throng at the gateway made it impassable. Whether scholars or peddlers, everyone squeezed into the masses, stretching their necks, desperate to catch a glimpse of Yuan Ming's demeanor.
Yuan Ming too was taken aback at the sight before him, thinking he had not been so famous before his disappearance, and couldn't help but turn with a wry smile, "It seems I'll have to trouble you to send someone to notify the General Mansion to come and clear a way."
"No need to bother the folks at General Mansion for such a trivial matter, I happen to have some extra men at hand, let them escort Young Master Yuan home," said the Gate Captain, thumping his chest.
Soon, he called over several idle city guards to accompany Yuan Ming on his way to General Mansion.
City guards, armed to the teeth, intimidated the crowd, finally carving out a passable path for Yuan Ming.
Even so, there were still many people crowding both sides of the route, and the windows of the taverns and tea houses along the street flew open, with patrons flocking to the windows, eagerly peering out at the scene unfolding, their excitement palpable as they watched Yuan Ming being escorted through.
Soon, news that Yuan Ming, the bestselling author in the Capital and the sole descendant of General Yuan Zuochong from General of the South, had returned safely from the Southern Border after being missing for years, spread throughout the entire Capital.
In General Jingbei's Mansion, Duke Jingbei - General Zhao Jisheng was being assisted off his carriage by servants, preparing to enter his home, when he heard the noise from the main street.
He frowned slightly, and a guard clad in armor immediately went to investigate.
In a short while, the guard returned with news. After hearing his report, surprise flitted across Zhao Jisheng's face, followed swiftly by a smile of genuine delight.
"Hey, Yuan, I always said the boy was lucky and blessed!"
He signaled to his attendants, "Send a gift to Yuan Mansion on my behalf, and a visiting card with it, informing them that I shall pay a visit shortly."
Meanwhile, at Tianming Book Society, the Shopkeeper was arranging for his employees to restock the sold-out shelves with leather-bound editions of 'Young Master Sheng's Southern Journey', when a clerk suddenly stumbled in, breathless.
"Shopkeeper, big news, huge news!"
"What news could possibly justify such a racket, and what if it disturbs the customers?" scolded the Shopkeeper of the Book Society.
Panting heavily, the clerk paused to catch his breath before managing to say, "Great news, Shopkeeper, it's Young Master Yuan, Young Master Yuan has returned!"
"Young Master Yuan? Which Yuan..."
The Shopkeeper of the Book Society paused, then quickly stepped forward, grabbing the clerk's arm: "You mean Yuan Ming, Young Master Yuan?"
"Exactly him, the streets are buzzing with it, saying Young Master Yuan has endured great hardships and returned from the Southern Border!" the clerk nodded immediately.
The Shopkeeper of the Book Society burst into laughter: "Excellent, excellent! Quick, arrange for someone to go out and spread the word, say that to celebrate Young Master Yuan's return, all books in the shop are being sold at a discount... no, at eighty percent of the original price!"
As he commanded, the clerks in the shop quickly dispersed to spread the news, with the Shopkeeper's eyes sparkling with excitement.
Your Majesty, Young Master Yuan has finally returned!
...

chapters.title: Chapter 260 - 237: Going Home
chapters.content:
General Zhen Nan Mansion was located in the north of Qujiang City, near the Imperial Palace.
Yuan Ming, escorted by the city guards, proceeded through the streets where the crowd of common folks gradually dispersed. The wide road was flanked by luxurious, sparse residences, everything appeared just as Yuan Ming had seen during Wang Shun's possession.
From afar, the sight of a five-story tall Eight Treasures Pointed Gray Tower entered Yuan Ming's view, stirring an impatient excitement inside him.
Suddenly, the city guard leading the way paused; Yuan Ming instinctively looked up and saw many people standing in front of the mansion gate.
Leading the group were a man and a woman. The man had a tall, robust frame, standing motionless like a mountain stele, though his temples were grey and his eyes misty.
The woman was graceful and majestic, her face as lovely as a lotus flower emerging from water, though her silk clothes were wet with tears. On seeing Yuan Ming, she was already sobbing uncontrollably.
Yuan Ming felt a lump in his throat and his vision suddenly blurred; his lips moved without sound for a moment before a somewhat raspy voice emerged.
"Dad, Mom, your child has returned..."
Hearing Yuan Ming's voice, his mother could no longer hold back her emotions and rushed forward to embrace him tightly, "Ming'er, my Ming'er, you've finally returned. Let Mom take a good look at you."
Yuan Ming felt the warm embrace he had missed for so long and looked towards his father.
The father he remembered, who rarely smiled or spoke much, now seemed to brush away a tear and walked up to Yuan Ming, expressing his relief, "It's good that you've returned, it's good."
Witnessing this scene, the stationed guards and soldiers including Fu Qing sighed continuously, while the mother's personal maids cried even harder.
"Enough, my lady. Ming'er has just returned. Let's not keep him standing outside any longer." Yuan Zuochong patted the shoulder of Yuan Ming's mother.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming's mother finally stopped her tears. Yuan Zuochong then gave a signal to the maids, indicating they should take her and Yuan Ming inside the mansion.
Next, he called over Fu Qing and turned to the guards who had escorted Yuan Ming, "Thank you, brothers, for escorting my son home. Fu Qing, give each of them ten taels of silver, and prepare some more for those at the city gate."
Hearing they would receive silver, the guards expressed their immense gratitude.
Meanwhile, Yuan Ming, led by his mother, entered the General Mansion and saw a spacious courtyard just beyond the gate.
At that moment, almost all the servants and maids of the mansion were gathered there, watching their Young Master with a mix of curiosity and anticipation they could hardly hide.
Yuan Ming scanned the crowd and saw many familiar faces, including Wang Shun.
Feeling Yuan Ming's gaze, Wang Shun looked over instinctively.
Yuan Ming smiled internally, recalled how Wang Shun had cared for his horse, their good relationship, and the time he had borrowed Wang Shun's eyes to observe the Mansion. He winked and nodded at him as a gesture.
Wang Shun seemed startled at first but then displayed a flattered expression. Yuan Ming approached and gently clapped Wang Shun on the shoulder, reminiscent of his time during the possession, chuckled, and continued walking forward with his mother.
The two walked to the northern building in the courtyard where they stopped. Yuan Zuochong also followed and joined Yuan Ming, gesturing for him to face the many servants below.
Father and son shared an understanding. Yuan Ming realized what was expected, stepped forward and cleared his throat.
Looking at those familiar and unfamiliar servants, Yuan Ming declared loudly, "Lift your heads. You must all know, over three years ago, I unfortunately went missing at the Southern Border. Now, by the grace of Heaven, I have luckily returned to see my parents, which is indeed a joyous occasion."
"To celebrate, I announce that from today, whether high or low, every servant in the mansion will receive one tael of silver, and this year's salary will increase by thirty percent!"
Instantly, the servants of the courtyard erupted in cheers, their hearts already overjoyed by Yuan Ming's return, now thrilled even more, their gazes filled with undisguised enthusiasm.
"Thank you, General, and congratulations, Young Master!"
Firstseenon*.
Amidst the chorus of voices from servants and maids, Yuan Ming smiled and waved his hand, then entered the house with his parents, leaving the excited crowd to turn the entire General Mansion into a place of celebration.
...
Inside the house, his mother pulled Yuan Ming down to sit and caressed his face, tears falling anew, "Ming'er, you look so strong, yet so dark. I barely recognize you. How much did you suffer in the Southern Border?"
Yuan Ming felt a choking sensation but didn't want his mother to worry, "It's alright, Mom. I'm well. Besides, I'm back now, aren't I?"
His mother wiped her tears, still heartbroken, "Your hair is such a mess. When I was there to look after you, it was never like this."
As she spoke, she suddenly ordered the servants to bring a copper mirror and started to redo Yuan Ming's hairstyle herself.
Yuan Ming could not resist her, so he obediently sat in front of the copper mirror, letting his mother fuss over him.
The reflection of his mother's face appeared in the mirror. He quietly observed her, noting that she had become much thinner compared to three years ago, with fine lines on her forehead and at the corners of her eyes. Her temples had more white hair than when he last used possession on his father, and the tear stains on her cheeks were still fresh. However, her lips curved in a smile, as if combing her son's hair was a joyous occasion.
His father also silently approached. He watched Yuan Ming with a highly complex expression, mingling relief, heartache, perhaps guilt, and worry.
Soon enough, his mother finished combing Yuan Ming's hair. Standing awkwardly, he got up and, under his mother's urging, reluctantly turned left and right to show her his current appearance.
"Ming'er has grown up," Yuan Zuochong said.
His mother nodded, but her gaze suddenly fell on Yuan Ming's clothes.
She stepped forward a few paces and touched the hem of Yuan Ming's garment, suddenly exclaiming, "Did you buy this clothing in Southern Border? This inferior material, you've never worn such clothes before! No, the new clothes are ready; I will get someone to fetch them immediately."
Yuan Ming gave a wry smile and stopped her, "Mother, please don't bother, I've gotten used to these clothes."
"My child, how can you wear these clothes out to meet people? Listen to your mother, don't be stubborn."
As she spoke, she started to scold him again, "I advised you not to go on that diplomatic mission, but you insisted on going out to achieve something. As a result, you encountered disaster in Southern Border. I've always said, not only Chang Chun Temple exists in the world, your grandmother's Sect is also not bad. I told you to take the White Jade Ring from your grandmother, but you refused. If you had taken it, you wouldn't have suffered this disaster."
Listening to his mother's nagging, Yuan Ming usually would have retorted, but today her nagging felt exceptionally affectionate.
Suddenly, Yuan Zuochong coughed twice, "Let's discuss these matters later. Wife, you've still not fully recovered from your illness the past few days, go rest for now, and let me have a word with Ming'er alone."
"Mother, how is your health?" Although Yuan Ming had learned of his mother's illness during his last possession of his father, he hadn't expected that she had still not fully recovered.
"Don't listen to your father's nonsense, I'm fine," she replied.
Yuan Zuochong's interruption finally put a stop to her scolding. Although she wished to talk more with Yuan Ming, she knew her husband needed to discuss important matters with him, so she didn't stay much longer. After giving a few simple instructions to Yuan Ming, she left the room.
Seeing this, Yuan Zuochong glanced around and said, "You all may leave as well. Fu Qing, stay outside with the others, don't let anyone in."
Seeing him treat the matter with such confidentiality made Yuan Ming nervous, wondering what had happened in the Capital during this time.
Once the others had left the room, Yuan Ming released his soul crow to monitor the entire Prince Manor, causing Yuan Zuochong to look mildly surprised.
"Fu Qing mentioned that Ming'er, your strength has far surpassed his already?" Yuan Zuochong asked.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming gave a slight smile, and with a flip of his hand, he took out the Cold Star Sword, activating the Frost Rune upon it. Instantly, a chilling cold filled the space, and the room's temperature dropped significantly.
He also summoned the Green Cloud Crane, making it stand still in the room.
"Father, please look, these are the Magic Artifact and the flying spirit pet I acquired in Southern Border. It is with their help that I could return to Da Jin," Yuan Ming said. His current level of Cultivation was masked by Hidden Element Technique, showing only about mid-stage Qi Refinement Realm.
Yuan Zuochong, knowing valuable items when he saw them, his eyes lit up upon seeing the two items, "Good, it seems Ming'er has indeed gained some fortune in Southern Border, relying just on this sword and this crane, even I am no match for you. Well done, well done!"
As the General of the South of Da Jin, Yuan Zuochong was also a cultivator, his Cultivation being significantly higher than that of Fu Qing, yet only around Qi Cultivation Seventh Level.
"The secret letter you had Fu Qing bring back, I have read it. You have truly suffered these past three years, it's just a pity that with the current political situation at court, I can't even take revenge for you," Yuan Zuochong sighed.
Yuan Ming puzzled, "Father, why do you say this?"
Yuan Zuochong shook his head, "Lin Junsheng is now a disciple of Chang Chun Temple, and with the Lin Family now favored by Eighth Imperial Uncle, they have gained influence and gradually taken control over the court. The situation has solidified, and I can't touch him now."
"I remember, Lin Junsheng's talents were no better than mine, why would Chang Chun Temple accept him? How is the Emperor now?" Yuan Ming inquired further.
Yuan Zuochong explained, "It all started with the diplomatic mission. After your disappearance, Lin Junsheng took it upon himself to continue the mission in Southern Border on your behalf. Upon his return, he used his achievements from the mission, and somehow found a connection to directly join Chang Chun Temple. As for the Emperor, he has been engrossed in Cultivation in recent years and gradually neglected state affairs, handing them over to Eighth Imperial Uncle, which gave the Lin Family their chance."
Yuan Ming recalled, the young Emperor, Liu Tianming, ventured into the Immortal Path, originally because the incense used for his first possession was that initial Black Incense, which probably contributed not only to controlling his actions but also affecting his thoughts considerably.
Looking at the current political situation at court, ultimately, it still somewhat related to him.
Yuan Zuochong, unaware of Yuan Ming's thoughts, continued with a sigh, "Speaking of which, it was also due to the late Emperor's wishes that I chose to assist the Emperor initially. Seeing the Emperor focusing entirely on Cultivation and ignoring the government, I gradually handed over my powers, thinking of improving my own Cultivation, possibly even attempting Foundation Establishment if fate allowed..."
He paused, then continued, "But then I received your secret letter, learning that it was Lin Junsheng who had harmed you. I thought of dealing with him, but since he's now a disciple of Chang Chun Temple, and he rarely comes out, alas... the opportunity is hard to find."

chapters.title: Chapter 261 - 238: Father and Son, Sovereign and Minister, Friends
chapters.content:
"Father need not blame himself; Lin Junsheng ambushed me, and I will repay the debt. Even if I enter Chang Chun Temple, I will have ways to deal with him. It would be counterproductive if you were to disturb your mind and hinder your cultivation because of this." Seeing his father's guilt-ridden face, Yuan Ming spoke to comfort him.
Yuan Zuochong looked at Yuan Ming with relief, "Heh heh, who would've thought that there would come a day when I would be comforted by Ming'er. A gentleman's revenge is not too late even after ten years. You mustn't act rashly."
"Father, don't worry, I have my methods. I have already waited for three years; what's another ten?"
Upon hearing this, Yuan Zuochong exhaled in relief.
Suddenly, Yuan Ming took out a wooden box and handed it to his father.
Yuan Zuochong instinctively took the wooden box, somewhat puzzled, he looked up at Yuan Ming. Seeing that Yuan Ming was smiling without speaking, he opened the lid of the box.
A faint aroma of elixir wafted out immediately, and in the center of the box, there lay a pill radiating star-like blue light.
"This, this is a Foundation Establishment Pill! Where did you get this from?" Yuan Zuochong abruptly stood up, his eyes widened in disbelief as he looked at Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming nodded calmly, "The Southern Border has its risks, but it also has many opportunities. This Foundation Establishment Pill was acquired through a fortunate coincidence. Since father has the heart to cultivate, this item will surely lend you a helping hand."
