chapters.title: Chapter 300 - 277 Counting the Harvest
chapters.content:
"Senior Hagon, we have a request. Earlier in the valley, three of our fellow sect members were poisoned by He Wendao's lethal toxin, and our detoxification elixirs had no effect. We thought they would be saved once we returned to the sect, but with such a delay, their lives are now hanging by a thread. I wonder if you could lend a hand in their treatment?" Luo Shan hesitated for a moment, then gave a fist and palm salute, pleading for help.
"I'm not skilled at detoxifying, but I can try. Where are they?" Yuan Ming asked.
The three Shengye Sect disciples lay unconscious, carried over by others. Their cheeks were marked with several patches of dark green poison spots, similar to those Shengye Sect disciples who had been killed by poison, weak breathing, clearly unable to hold on much longer.
After a brief examination, Yuan Ming sighed internally; the various detoxification elixirs he carried were quite ordinary and incapable of curing such a strange toxin.
Just as he was about to refuse, he suddenly thought of Hua Zhi and transmitted a message, "Hua Zhi, after absorbing Black Toad, do you still possess the ability to draw out fierce toxins?"
"Is master asking me to save these Shengye Sect disciples? That's a trifle," Hua Zhi replied telepathically.
"Alright, take them to the room inside," Yuan Ming said, standing up and speaking to Luo Shan.
Overjoyed, Luo Shan promptly took action personally, along with several other disciples, to move the three Shengye Sect disciples into a room.
Yuan Ming ushered everyone out, closed the door, and set up a Concealment Barrier.
Then, he slapped his Spiritual Beast Bag at his waist, and Hua Zhi extended three vine tendrils from within the bag, each piercing into the body of the poisoned individuals.
The trio merely twitched briefly, then the poison spots on their skin began to fade at a rate visible to the naked eye, quickly dissipating a great deal until they nearly matched the surrounding healthy skin.
But at that moment, an unexpected change occurred!
The spots, which had almost vanished, suddenly darkened once more, and in a moment, they returned to their original state.
"Eh! How strange, very strange indeed."
Hua Zhi let out a surprised murmur, wriggling out of the Spiritual Beast Bag with several vines extending from both arms, piercing into various parts of the three bodies as she muttered incantations and activated her full demonic power. A faint green light emanated from the many vines.
This time, the poison spots disappeared at an exceptionally rapid pace without any pause in between, and Hua Zhi continued to cast and maintain for a quarter of an hour after the spots had faded to match the healthy skin color.
Now, the three Shengye Sect disciples no longer had any poison spots on their bodies; their cheeks regained a healthy flush, and their breathing stabilized.
"This poison inside these three is quite strange, isn't it? Tell me about it," Yuan Ming approached Hua Zhi and asked after she had finished.
"The fierce toxin in these people is not particularly strong. However, it's as if the poison is a living thing; it has taken root in their flesh and feeds on their Qi-Blood power. If it's not entirely removed at once, it can regenerate continuously, and it greatly depletes the already weak life force of the poisoned individuals," Hua Zhi transmitted back.
"A toxin like a living thing?" Yuan Ming murmured in surprise, stroking his chin.
In his years of refining Poisonous Incense, he had studied intense toxins quite extensively, yet he had never encountered such a peculiar one that could swallow Qi-Blood and grow stronger.
"Master, if you're interested, you might as well examine He Wendao's storage magic tool; perhaps you could find some clues," Hua Zhi suggested telepathically.
Yuan Ming had this in mind. He immediately instructed Luo Shan and others waiting outside the door to come in and carry the three disciples who were out of danger away.
After Yuan Ming sat down cross-legged inside the room again, he used the Silver Token to open a silver light screen before taking out the storage magic tools of Bai Ye, Lu Shen, He Wendao, and Shi Dian.
He took out all the items inside and started to check them carefully.
He was on a mission at his grandmother's behest, which he thought would be a leisurely task aside from strenuous cultivation to relax the mind and body, but it almost cost him his life. Fortunately, the outcome was unexpectedly rewarding. Not only did he save his cousin, but he also found a windfall.
All four people were Foundation Establishment Cultivators rich in assets. Just the Spirit Stones alone amounted to over four thousand, not to mention the bountiful spiritual materials, magical artifacts, and elixirs.
Yuan Ming picked out the items useful to him first: five bottles of Harmonization Liquid Pills that would advance his Foundation Establishment cultivation, one large piece of spiritual material, three top-grade magical tools, and one set of an array.
The Harmonization Liquid Pill goes without saying; he would have been continuously purchasing them had he wished to carry on with his cultivation. This sudden windfall had saved him a considerable expense.
The spiritual material was a gold scale as big as a grinding stone, with wave-shaped spiritual patterns across it, seemingly from some giant beast. When he probed it with his Divine Sense, he could distinctly feel the strong Spiritual Power fluctuations radiating from it, which far surpassed that of a Second-level Demon Beast.
"Could it be the scale of a third-level Demon Beast? So large, I wonder what kind of demon beast it is?" Yuan Ming examined the item closely.
The golden scale was quite heavy, weighing about fifty pounds.
Being familiar with various demon beasts, Yuan Ming conjectured from the patterns that this scale might be that of the mythical Flood Dragon, which was inherently powerful and typically at least a Third-level Demon Beast once it reached adulthood.
After a moment's thought, Yuan Ming took out the Black Needle Magical Artifact, channeling thirty percent of his Mana to test it on the edge of the golden scale.
With a slight sound, the golden scale trembled, but there was not even a mark on the surface.
Yuan Ming nodded slightly, then increased his Mana to fifty percent and even seventy percent. The golden scale remained unscathed under the Black Needle's assault.
Determined, Yuan Ming pushed his Mana to its full capacity, turning the Black Needle into a subtle shadow that fiercely pierced the golden scale.
"Clang!" A great sound rang out as the golden scale was struck and sent flying. The struck area showed only a shallow white spot, far from being penetrated.
"A fine piece!"
Yuan Ming was inwardly delighted. This golden scale was exceptionally hard and durable, probably the toughest spiritual material he had come across since stepping foot into the Cultivation World. It was suitable for refining a top-grade defensive magical artifact.
He picked up the scale, then turned his attention to the three top-grade magical artifacts, which were Lu Shen's Earth Burying Mallet, a blue ring, and a green flying sword.
He picked up the Earth Burying Mallet to examine it. It was a top-grade Earth Attribute magical artifact, extremely heavy at four to five hundred pounds, and possessed exceptionally strong offensive power.
Yuan Ming held the mallet, but with his strength, he could only swing it a few times with difficulty; it was not handy for him, and its attribute also did not match his own.
Yuan Ming considered selling it, but then thought of Vajra.This copy comes from content on *.
This mutated White Ape had plenty of strength. The Earth Burying Mallet seemed perfectly suited for it, so he immediately tossed it into the Spiritual Beast Bag where Vajra was and gave a command.
Yuan Ming then picked up the blue ring. His Divine Sense entered it, and quickly, the artifact's details were clear to him.
He had obtained this blue ring from Shi Dian's storage magic tool, and it was inscribed with a name: "True Water Ring," a Water Attribute auxiliary magical artifact with no offensive effects. When worn, it had the effects of nourishing the body, fire resistance, and protection against the cold, making it quite a fine top-grade magical tool.
Yuan Ming had initially planned to wear it himself, but considering that Hua Zhi had suffered serious injuries and that he had just given Vajra a magical artifact, it wouldn't be fair to favor one over the other, so he granted the ring to Hua Zhi.
Top-grade magical tools were quite precious; with Vajra and Hua Zhi each receiving one, they both played with the tools joyfully.
Finally, Yuan Ming carefully picked up the green flying sword, which was obtained from He Wendao and was a poisonous sword.
Previously, He Wendao had used this sword to attack the Shengye Sect disciples, killing several of them. The three poisoned and unconscious Shengye Sect disciples were also wounded by this sword.
Yuan Ming carefully inspected the green flying sword. The entire sword was emerald green, seemingly refined from some type of Green Jade, with three runes inscribed on its body, all of which were Poison Incubation Runes.
Yuan Ming's eyes lit up. Master Hei Mu's Artifact Refining Manual had notes on the Poison Incubation Rune, which, as the name implies, helped preserve and gently cultivate the deadly poison within the materials, preventing it from dissipating.
A typical poisonous magical artifact with one Poison Incubation Rune would be sufficient, but this flying sword was inscribed with three such runes, indicating that the materials used to refine this sword were alarmingly toxic, something one rune could not contain.
Yuan Ming closely examined every part of the flying sword, which contained a strong and highly active potent poison, as if countless tiny insects were fighting to free themselves from the sword's hold and poison people to death.
"What is this sword made from that its poison is so intense?"
He couldn't figure it out, but he took care as he stored it away and turned his attention to the last artifact, the Bronze Thunder Pattern Array.
This array set, unlike the ordinary array tools such as Yuan Ming's Thousand Knot Water Rope Array, had its Array Patterns carved on seven bronze pillars, making installation much easier and less prone to damage.
However, crafting such specialized array tools set high demands on the Array Master, indicating that the creator of this Bronze Thunder Pattern Array was particularly skilled.
Yuan Ming carefully checked the seven bronze pillars and found the signature of the Array Master on the bottom of one pillar: Xiao Jiu.
"Xiao Jiu? It seems this Bronze Thunder Pattern Array comes from the Xiao Family of Red Lotus Island," Yuan Ming thought to himself.
The might of the Bronze Thunder Pattern Array was astonishing, almost causing his downfall when he was trapped in it. This adventure's greatest gain might just be this array set.
To bring out the full power of this array, Thunder Attribute Spirit Stones were needed. He just happened to have three high-grade Thunder Attribute Spirit Stones, which might prove to be very useful in the future.
He estimated in his mind and packed away the array set.
Yuan Ming sorted through the remaining items, each neatly stored away, and the ground soon cleared up, leaving behind only a giant sword broken in two, the very same Bronze Giant Sword of Shi Dian.
This sword was refined from Thunder Attribute spiritual materials and, although broken, retained much of the power of thunder and lightning within it.
Yuan Ming was somewhat troubled by what to do with this sword. The Bronze Giant Sword was damaged, and to repair it, aside from a very high level of Artifact Refining skills, similar types of spiritual materials were necessary for the restoration – a feat nearly impossible to achieve within Little Lake City's Square Market.
But abandoning or selling it seemed too wasteful.
"Could Lei Yu, being a Thunder Attribute spirit beast, possibly absorb the power of thunder and lightning from this giant sword?" Yuan Ming suddenly had an idea.
So he threw the two broken pieces into Lei Yu's Spiritual Beast Bag. Sensing the thunder and lightning power within the giant sword, Lei Yu immediately pounced on it, beginning to absorb the Green Thunder within.
Yuan Ming saw this and nodded his head, then closed his eyes and immersed himself in cultivation.
Just as he had anticipated, the journey back was smooth sailing. After several days, the group arrived at the gates of the Shengye Sect.

chapters.title: Chapter 301 - 278: Return to the City
chapters.content:
Shengye Sect.
High mountains and deep valleys adorned its landscape, with countless herbal medicine fields on its terrain, rich in spiritual energy. The fields were planted with various plants, brimming with lively, thriving scenery.
Near the summit, nestled against a bamboo forest, a majestic hall perched atop a cliff. Stepping out from the main entrance, one faced a long, steep staircase; from the top of the staircase, looking down, one could take in the panoramic view of the surrounding mountains.
This place was none other than the assembly hall of the Shengye Sect, where, on ordinary days, only the sect leader and the hall masters could enter. But today was an exception, as an outsider was welcomed in.
It was said that, within the Shengye Sect, there were over ten thousand disciples, more than ninety percent of whom were at the Qi Refinement Realm. The Foundation Establishment Realm had roughly a hundred people, primarily including the sect leader, the hall masters, and some direct disciples. As for the Core Formation Stage elders, mere handful in number, they generally spent years in seclusion, unconcerned with sect affairs.
The rumored elderly ancestor at the Nascent Soul Stage was like a pillar to the sect. Unless there was a significant event within the sect, it was nigh impossible to witness their divine presence.
Heavy bell tolls wandered through the valley. Inside the hall, the hall masters stood on both sides with grim expressions, while in front of the ancestral statue, the leader of the Shengye Sect also wore a face of sorrow.
"... That's how it is. I am truly ashamed that I wasn't able to detain Pu Zhengqing, to avenge Fellow Daoist Lu and Fellow Daoist Bai."
Under their watchful eyes, Yuan Ming narrated the events that transpired in the Yunluo Mountain Range, concluding with a face full of shame.
"Pu Zhengqing is cunning, Fellow Daoist Hagon. To have driven him off and saved our sect's disciples was no easy feat; please don't blame yourself," said Wang Xinghe, the leader of the Shengye Sect, shaking his head.
Then, he continued, "Fellow Daoist Hagon has made a great contribution to our Shengye Sect this time, and we will certainly reward you generously. If there's anything you need, please speak up, and I will arrange for it immediately."
Yuan Ming did not hesitate: "If that's the case, I wonder if your esteemed sect possesses any elixirs that can aid with breaking through the bottlenecks of the Early-stage Foundation Establishment."
Seeing that he did not make an outrageous request, Wang Xinghe looked at Yuan Ming with renewed esteem and immediately nodded in agreement.
"Please wait outside for a little while, Fellow Daoist Hagon. Once our assembly concludes, Master Yu will personally refine a batch for you."
A beautiful woman in palace attire immediately stood up and bowed to Wang Xinghe, saying, "Rest assured, Sect Leader Brother. I will select top-grade spirit grasses, and the elixirs I refine will surely be thirty percent better than those on the market."
"Moreover, if Fellow Daoist Hagon has no pressing matters, you may also stay in our sect for a few more days so that we may extend our hospitality," Wang Xinghe added.
Yuan Ming nodded, and then followed a disciple of Wang Xinghe out of the assembly hall to another elegant pavilion to sit for a while, where attendants served him spiritual tea.
The Shengye Sect leaders' assembly didn't last long. Soon after, Master Yu hurried over, bringing Yuan Ming to the Alchemy Hall to start alchemy.
On the way, Master Yu scrutinized Yuan Ming with undisguised admiration in her eyes.
"Fellow Daoist Hagon is truly accomplished despite his youth."
"You flatter me, Fellow Daoist," Yuan Ming said with a nod. Suddenly, he spotted someone riding a magic artifact approaching them, stopping right before them.
The person was Yuan Ming's grandmother. Yuan Ming smiled, knowing that in the presence of others, his grandmother would not acknowledge their relationship.
"Hehe, Junior Sister Wang, what brings you here in such a rush?"
"Naturally, I came to thank Fellow Daoist Hagon," Yuan Ming's grandmother responded with a smile.
"The Sect Leader Brother instructed me to personally refine a batch of elixirs for Fellow Daoist Hagon. Junior Sister Wang oversees the medicinal fields, your arrival is timely. The sect wants to thank Fellow Daoist Hagon with Origin Transformation Pills, and I am about to start the refinement process. Does the medicine storehouse have suitable aged materials?" asked Master Yu.
Although Yuan Ming's grandmother was a Foundation Establishment Cultivator, she was not among the hall masters and hence had not attended the assembly in the hall.
The palace-attired beauty expected Yuan Ming's grandmother to, as usual, exchange formalities with her, but to her surprise, Yuan Ming's grandmother simply nodded.
"Of course. I have a four-hundred-year-old Moon Returning Flower; you can take it and use it directly," said Yuan Ming's grandmother.
Check for the latest updates on My Virtual Library Empire (*).
Master Yu looked at Yuan Ming's grandmother in surprise, impressed by her generosity.
"My two disciples were also part of the trials this time. It is fortunate that Fellow Daoist Hagon made a move, otherwise the loss of so many disciples would be something the sect couldn't bear," said Yuan Ming's grandmother.
"Indeed, I too had several disciples who nearly perished in the ordeal. Senior Mo's nephew was also harmed this time, and the Sect Master is considering forming an alliance with all the sects of the Thunder Continent to hunt down this Pu Zhengqing," said Master Yu.
"No wonder Senior Mo looked so upset today," said the grandmother.
"Fellow Daoist Hagon, is this Pu Zhengqing's illusion technique really so unfathomably mysterious?" asked Master Yu.
Yuan Ming described Sha Hao's illusion technique once again.
"Indeed, it has been many years since a Soul Cultivator appeared. Their methods are tricky and hard to guard against. Law Practitioners and Body Cultivators at the same level have no absolute countermeasures against Soul Cultivators. Each time they appear, it's a bloodbath. Our sect also has records of Soul Cultivators causing chaos a hundred years ago. Battles often require several times their number in the same realm just to suppress them," said the grandmother.
"May I borrow these records for perusal?" Yuan Ming inquired.
After receiving a negative response, Yuan Ming didn't mind and then the three of them discussed how to break through the illusion technique…
As he watched his junior sister walk away, Master Yu said, "It's thanks to you that her disciple was saved; otherwise, she would never have been willing to part with the Moon Returning Flower that took four hundred years to cultivate."
…
Several days later.
Yuan Ming received several bottles of Origin Transformation Pills, which were even more effective than Harmonization Liquid Pills, as well as other elixirs gifted by the Shengye Sect.
The Origin Transformation Pills, personally refined by Master Yu using spiritual materials that were four hundred years old, were even more effective than expected.
Yuan Ming was in no rush to take them. He stayed in the Shengye Sect for a few more days, met with his grandmother in private, and got acquainted with quite a few Foundation Establishment Cultivators within the sect before returning to Little Lake City.
When passing the Rain Ruins Swamp, he placed Hua Zhi into the swamp and instructed it to hunt demon beasts on its own and absorb Qi-Blood to recover from its injuries.
As soon as he entered his own shop, he was greeted by a faint scent that was refreshing to the mind and spirit. Hu Tu and Mu Yang were chatting with customers, but their faces lit up with joy upon seeing Yuan Ming arrive.
Yuan Ming went straight to the back room of the shop, and soon after, Hu Tu followed him in.
"Has anything important happened in the shop during my absence?" Yuan Ming asked.
Before leaving Little Lake City, Yuan Ming had specifically left a Communication Talisman for Hu Tu and Mu Yang, telling them to contact him only if something truly unmanageable occurred.
Yet, just a few days ago, he suddenly received a message from Hu Tu stating that there was an urgent matter requiring his decision.
"Speaking of which, it's good news. A few days ago, a big customer came to the shop and wanted to buy up all our incense. Mu Yang and I didn't dare make such a decision on our own, so we immediately contacted you," said Hu Tu.
"Didn't I set a rule before that there's a limited purchase standard for the incenses in the shop? If someone wanted to buy them all, you should have just refused. Why did you need me to return to make a decision?" Yuan Ming frowned, his tone displeased.
"Of course I told the customer according to the boss's wishes, but that customer claimed to be from the City Lord Mansion and still wouldn't take no for an answer. I didn't dare offend them. After much persuasion, I managed to reduce their demand by half and slightly raised the price. Even then, we dared not sell without your consent, so we explained that we didn't have enough incense in stock and asked them to temporarily leave until you could make a decision," Hu Tu said with a hint of grievance.
The prestige of the Little Lake City Lord Mansion had to be respected, and in all the years Yuan Ming had been in the city, he hadn't heard of the City Lord engaging in bullying or unfair practices. The City Lord was known for handling matters fairly, enjoying unanimous approval among the Loose Cultivators. The City Lord Mansion's bulk purchase indicated that his incense had gained recognition from the City Lord Mansion.
Yuan Ming pondered for a moment and then said, "It's not your fault. But we can't just change the rules on the fly. Do this, separate out the incense requested by the City Lord Mansion and tell them we'll supply it on the first day of every month. Reduce the purchase limits of the Qingxuan Incense and Purple Mysterious Incense slightly, but keep the prices the same."
"Yes, I will convey this to the City Lord Mansion immediately," Hu Tu promptly replied.
"List the estimated sales for the next half a year now. I might not be able to attend to the business in the shop for some time. If something similar happens again, we can discuss it. We can provide extra supplies to powerful sects. Which incenses does the City Lord Mansion want?" Yuan Ming instructed further.
The list Hu Tu prepared for the City Lord Mansion included incenses for cultivation purposes as well as others meant for calming the mind and focusing, intended for supply to a shop known as the Four Symbols Tea House.
"What's the situation with this shop?" Yuan Ming asked, pointing to the Four Symbols Tea House.
"Back to the boss, that's also an establishment owned by the City Lord. It's quite famous in the city, and apparently, it's a place where high-level cultivators often visit," Hu Tu explained.
Yuan Ming nodded, no longer inquiring. He silently calculated the quantity of spiritual materials he needed and then turned and left the shop.
A few days later, after he had finished purchasing the spiritual materials needed for incense making at several of his regular shops in the city, he just happened to pass by the Red Refining Hall. After pondering for a moment, he walked in.
"Do you have any top-grade magical tools for sale?" he asked the approaching attendant as soon as he entered.
In the battle at Yunluo Mountain Range, Sha Hao, with the top-grade magical tool, the Silver Orb, destroyed most of his magic artifacts. Ordinary magic artifacts were extremely fragile in front of a top-grade magical tool, leaving him defenseless. The spirit stones he had earned from selling incense were all used to buy elixirs to enhance his cultivation, and now he needed to find a suitable top-grade magical tool for himself.
On hearing Yuan Ming's question, the attendant respectfully ushered him upstairs. Shortly after, the shopkeeper of Red Refining Hall hurried over.
"Senior, our shop currently has just two top-grade magical tools on offer. If you are truly interested, I will go get them right away. However, both tools are priced at over five thousand spirit stones," the shopkeeper said with a bowed hand.
"Besides the runes, what makes top-grade magical tools special compared to high-grade ones? What's different about their power?" Yuan Ming asked.
"To answer senior's question, the quantity of runes is secondary. What makes the top-grade magical tools special is that almost each one is made of extraordinary, rare materials, all unique. Each top-grade magical tool exists as a single piece, and they all have the potential to advance to become a Magic Treasure. Naturally, their prices are several times higher than those of high-grade magical tools," the shopkeeper explained, gauging Yuan Ming's wealth.
Yuan Ming nodded, and seeing the shopkeeper still standing there unmoving, he understood the implication of the shopkeeper's words. He then took out the Green Wood Token and flashed it.
Seeing this, the shopkeeper immediately understood and exited the room. He quickly returned carrying two jade boxes.

chapters.title: Chapter 302 - 279: Four Symbols Tea House
chapters.content:
"Senior, thank you for your patience. These are two top-grade magical tools from our collection, one named 'Molten Fire Refinement' and the other named 'Confusion Bell'. Please have a look,"
said the shopkeeper, opening the first jade box. Inside lay a copper pot, blood-red all over, from which flames occasionally burst forth, exploding into small fireworks in the air.
"This Molten Fire Refinement was crafted by our sect's predecessor, using millennium Fire Essence and engraved with the runes 'Burning', 'Endless', 'Bone Attachment', 'Everlasting Flame'. It can emit flames that cannot be extinguished, and once they attach, they can never be removed,"
the shopkeeper finished explaining, then opened the second jade box. This time, inside lay a small bell, tied up with pink silk ribbons.
"This Confusion Bell is a top-grade magical tool that our store purchased at a high price years ago. It bears the runes 'Illusion Sound', 'Dizziness', 'Mihuan', 'Blinding'. When used, it can emit an extremely harsh bell sound, causing the opponent to temporarily lose vision and fall into dizziness,"
Yuan Ming listened to the shopkeeper's introduction, his brow slightly furrowing.
Although these two top-grade magical tools were not lacking in power, the former indiscriminately affected friend and foe, likely causing accidental harm, while the effects of the latter could be completely replicated by his illusion techniques, essentially making it a useless appendage.
Seeing Yuan Ming frown, the shopkeeper forced a smile and said, "It seems neither of these magical tools meet the senior's expectations. Unfortunately, our shop has no other top-grade magical tools. If you wish to purchase a suitable magical tool, your best chance might be to try your luck at an auction."
Yuan Ming sighed. Auctions tended to mark items up significantly, and even if he found a magical tool to his liking, it likely wouldn't be affordable with just five thousand spirit stones.
But just then, Yuan Ming suddenly asked, "What about having a top-grade magical tool crafted here? What would be the price for that?"
"Crafting a top-grade magical tool is quite difficult, and ordinary spiritual materials simply cannot bear four runes. If we force the imprinting, it might damage the material beyond use, and in such cases, our shop cannot be held responsible. Please consider this carefully," the shopkeeper warned.
"If I provide suitable spiritual materials, what's the success rate of the crafting?" asked Yuan Ming.
"Only about ten to twenty percent," the shopkeeper stated.
Yuan Ming immediately shook his head. Such a low success rate was akin to throwing the spiritual materials into a lake.
If that was the case, rather than letting others gamble, he preferred to try refining them himself.
Yuan Ming did not discuss the matter of crafting magical tools any further. He turned and bought several books related to artifact refining and runes, then left the Red Refining Hall.
Upon returning to his residence, he spent some time creating the list of spirit incense.
After resting for a while and regaining some energy, he suddenly took out the Stealing Heaven Tripod, lit a piece of Black Incense, and inserted it.
Incense smoke spiraled up; Yuan Ming concentrated on the image of Sha Hao. Swirling around him blurred his surroundings, but when they came into focus again, he found himself in a stone house.
At that moment, Sha Hao appeared to be healing, surrounded by ordinary stone furniture with no peculiar features.
The stone house had no windows, and even the door was tightly closed. Eager to discover Sha Hao's location, Yuan Ming immediately employed a Soul Seal, coercing Sha Hao to leave the stone house.
However, no matter how he deployed the Soul Seal, until the Black Incense burned out and the possession ended, Sha Hao showed no response.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming furrowed his brow.
He had specifically created a higher quality Black Incense using incense ashes obtained from Zhenling Sect and applied the Soul Seal targeting Sha Hao, a Foundation Establishment cultivator, but it had no effect?
Was it possible that Soul Seals had no effect on Soul Cultivators?
Yuan Ming pondered briefly, deciding to try again in seven days. If the Soul Seal still had no effect, he would have to hope to catch Sha Hao leaving on his own during a possession.
After all, Sha Hao knew of his identity as a Soul Cultivator. The longer he lived, the more likely Yuan Ming's cover would be blown.
Besides possessing him every seven days, he'd need to think of another way to locate Sha Hao's whereabouts.
…
The Four Symbols Tea House was located on the east side of the lake in the city.
The five Zhang tall building was a pale blue, decorated with water wave patterns painting. Its entrance faced the lake, with eight window panes to the sides from bottom to top. They were interlaced with carved spirit wood and set with glazed tiles, reflecting the lake under the illumination of bright pearls. From afar, the building seemed to ripple like water, not standing on land, but floating-like a fairy pavilion in the lake.
Yuan Ming walked through the main entrance and immediately saw several coral rockeries and columns of jade and sea shells decorated around, blue light unveiled in every corner of the building. Moreover, many spectral fish darted within the coral, making it seem as if he had arrived at a Dragon's underwater palace.
Amazed by the scenery, Yuan Ming was appreciating the view when he saw a beautiful woman wearing Dragon Horns approaching.
"Greetings, superior immortal," the woman bowed slightly, her white dress with hints of blue flowing slightly with her movement, as if she were swimming underwater.
"Your decorations are indeed exquisite," Yuan Ming immediately noticed that the horns on the woman's head were merely accessories, yet even the maids were so deeply into their roles, which he found quite astonishing.
"Thank you for the praise, superior immortal. This month, the theme of the Illusion Array is the Dragon Palace in the sea. If you like, you can go to the counter and cast a vote with one spirit stone," the maid said with a smile.
"Oh? What exactly is chosen in this voting?" Yuan Ming asked curiously.
"Our shop changes the theme every month, and the specific arrangements are determined by the number of votes from the superior immortals," the maid explained calmly.
After hearing this, Yuan Ming smiled slightly, realizing that casting a vote seemed to require only one spirit stone, but in reality, the costs would skyrocket as people competed with each other. Moreover, if the scene one liked became the theme, with only one month's time, the voters would surely visit more often.
"Superior immortal, please follow me, I will take you upstairs for some tea and rest," the maid turned and gestured invitingly.
Under her lead, Yuan Ming entered a small room, four feet square.
The room's structure was entirely made of wood, with only three walls. Painted on the two side walls were scenes of fish playing in water, while the wall facing the entrance displayed an unknown formation with five indentations, seemingly fitted for placing spirit stones.
The maid led Yuan Ming into the room, then pulled shut a wooden lattice door hidden at the entrance.
"Superior immortal, this is a spirit ladder specially crafted by a master hired by our building. You only need to place the corresponding number of spirit stones in the formation, and you will be able to go to different floors on your own."
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming grew curious—it must be a transmission array, he presumed, and casually placed two spirit stones into the indentations.
Then, he heard a "click" sound, and the entire formation suddenly lit up, with the spirit ladder starting to ascend, reaching the second floor in no time.
However, during the operation of the spirit ladder, Yuan Ming noticed that the wall formation seemed to have only a symbolic role. The spirit stones placed inside were not consumed. Something else must be driving the spirit ladder.This copy comes from content on *.
Yuan Ming looked outside and scanned the second floor, seeing that the occupants were Qi refining cultivators, and the utensils and decorations were not luxurious, which made him understand immediately.
The so-called ability to reach the corresponding floor by placing spirit stones was just a fancy way to collect an entry fee. The treatment received for two spirit stones would be vastly different from that for five.
Having figured out the trick, Yuan Ming then took out three more spirit stones and placed them in various parts of the formation.
The spirit ladder slowly ascended, and the scenery at the entrance changed along with it. Soon, Yuan Ming reached the fifth floor. Before he could step out, the calming music of drums and zithers along with the aroma of spirit incense entered the spirit ladder.
The maid opened the wooden gate of the spirit ladder for Yuan Ming. He stepped out and looked left, seeing a raised platform at the southeast corner, where several young girls in pearl-white long skirts danced to the music, while others, dressed similarly, played drums, zither, or blew into reed instruments beside the platform, all elegant in demeanor and harmonious in sound, rendering a sight and sound too refined to interrupt.
In addition, several maids holding jade bottles moved between the tea tables, serving tea and water to the guests, each with a gentle smile, their movements exuding grace.
Whether it was the maids, the musicians, or the dancing girls, all had cultivation, with the lowest being at the Qi refining second level.
In the room, calming spiritual incense bought from Yuan Ming's shop was burning. Whenever the incense burnt down to a quarter of its size, a maid would immediately come forward to replace it, ensuring the aroma remained constant.
Some maids also held trays filled with various types of melons and fruits. Although Yuan Ming couldn't identify them all, he could tell from the fluctuations of spiritual energy that these were no ordinary fruits.
Yuan Ming looked around and saw that the occupants here were all foundation establishment cultivators. Some were alone, others in groups of two or three, dressed differently, including cultivators from Da Jin and Zhao Country, disciples from sects, and independent practitioners.
He observed for a moment, then approached a round table near the platform, greeting the five cultivators seated there with a smile.
"Would my fellow Daoists mind if I join for a cup of tea?"
"Not at all, not at all, please make yourself comfortable," one male cultivator said with a gesture and smile.
Yuan Ming nodded, seeing no objections from the others, and took a seat.
Just as he sat down, a maid immediately came over and placed a cup of tea in front of him.
Yuan Ming lifted the lid of the cup and was instantly struck by a refreshing aroma. He took a sip and felt a warm flow throughout his body, invigorating him.
Meanwhile, the maid who served the tea was about to leave when suddenly a frivolous male cultivator stopped her.
"Xiao Yun, did you like the painting I gave you last time?"
"I cherish the gift from my senior, but alas, I am not well-versed in the art of painting and cannot grasp the profound meanings of the senior's masterpiece. I have kept it high on a shelf to avoid any damage, please forgive my ignorance," maid Xiao Yun said with a graceful bow and then spoke softly.
"It's just a painting, it has no deep meanings. As long as you like it, any form of disposition is acceptable. But about the matter of us becoming Daoist companions that I mentioned last time, have you considered it?" The male cultivator said, smiling, unconcerned.
"Senior, as a foundation establishment cultivator, how can I possibly aspire to such a status? Please, no more jokes," the maid shook her head gently, bowed slightly towards the frivolous man, and then turned and left.
Seeing this, the man's expression revealed a hint of disappointment, while a middle-aged cultivator sitting beside him chuckled,
"Could it be Yu Qingli, who has been so successful in romantic pursuits for so long, also meets his match occasionally?"

chapters.title: Chapter 303 - 280: Anecdotes and Trivia
chapters.content:
"Zhang Zhi, what nonsense are you talking about? I've never been a player, and I truly care for Xiao Yun," Yu Qingli said annoyed, glaring at the middle-aged male cultivator. Then, he quickly turned to look at the maid Xiao Yun who hadn't walked far and swiftly tried to make amends.
Seeing his reaction, Zhang Zhi immediately broke into laughter, and the other two male cultivators at the table also showed smiles, while the only female cultivator's face displayed displeasure.
"You have the nerve to talk about true feelings, pah."
A cultivator dressed as a scholar immediately chimed in, "Fairy Hua is right, Yu Qingli, how many female cultivators have you truly cared for? Can you even count them all?"
Yu Qingli, both angry and anxious, could only fling his sleeve and say dryly, "If you don't believe me, forget it."
Everyone laughed and joked for a while, but seeing Yu Qingli dejected and no longer retorting, they lost interest.
At that moment, one of the five, an elderly man with white hair, turned to Yuan Ming and asked, "This fellow Daoist looks unfamiliar; have you just arrived in Little Lake City?"
"I've been in the city for a while now, but I've mostly been in seclusion for cultivation and seldom go out," Yuan Ming shook his head.
"Oh? It seems like you are a diligent cultivator. But in my opinion, it's still important to go out and about. Otherwise, it's easy to encounter mental stagnation, which isn't beneficial for one's cultivation," Yu Qingli perked up again.
"Daoist Yu is quite right, we cultivators must not confine ourselves and work in isolation; otherwise, even if our cultivation improves, it's like a castle in the sky, collapsing at the slightest touch," the white-haired elder nodded.
"Daoist Lu speaks the truth. Without looking far, isn't Shengye Sect a prime example? The disciples rarely go out for tempering; they spend their days either conducting alchemy, medicine cultivation, or in secluded cultivation. Their cultivation might seem strong, but in actual combat, they fall short. If not for the Nascent Soul ancestor overseeing the sect, they might have been wiped out long ago," Zhang Zhi nodded.
"Zhang Zhi, look at what you're saying; isn't that contradictory? In the end, didn't Shengye Sect manage to secure a foothold in Thunder Continent because of their ancestor's grueling secluded cultivation and Nascent Soul achievement? Doesn't this further prove that cultivation is more important than anything else?" Yu Qingli chuckled softly.
"That's a Nascent Soul, can it be compared? And come to think of it, when you list all the Sects in the Central Plains that have a Nascent Soul, Shengye Sect still ranks at the bottom. Isn't that because their Nascent Soul ancestor isn't as strong as other Nascent Soul cultivators?" Zhang Zhi countered.
"Indeed, Nascent Soul cultivators are not on the same level as ordinary cultivators; one can't generalize," Cultivator Lu also nodded.
"Speaking of Shengye Sect, have you heard about the recent attack on their disciples during an outing?" the scholar-clad cultivator suddenly interjected.
"Of course, we've heard about it. The attacker is none other than the Soul Cultivator Pu Zhengqing, who appeared in Little Lake City a few years ago. It's the talk of the town, and Shengye Sect has put up a hefty bounty, raising his price. Now many are looking to find him for a big reward," Yu Qingli said.
"You know what, don't let spirit stones blind you. A friend of mine told me that the murder of a Foundation Establishment cultivator from Zhenling Sect was also his doing. Counting the Shengye Sect trial, there have already been three Foundation Establishment cultivators who have died at his hands recently," said the scholar-clad cultivator.
"It's actually four; there's also a cultivator from Chang Chun Temple, named Xu Changqing, who died by his hand," Fairy Hua suddenly said.
Upon hearing this, everyone was startled.
"Is that true, Fairy Hua?" Zhang Zhi asked.
"A while ago, you all knew about the reward posted by Chang Chun Temple at the Loose Cultivation Association. I have a good friend from Zhenling Sect who mentioned this matter to me. It seems Xu Changqing's body was discovered alongside another from their sect named Gu Qiulong. There were also many signs at the scene that they had fought side by side against the same opponent, so it should be true," Fairy Hua expressed.
Hearing this, Yuan Ming was puzzled. He had clearly disguised the scene to look like Xu Changqing and Gu Qiulong had perished in a fire, and later, when he possessed a Zhenling Sect cultivator, they had confirmed this. How had it now turned into them fighting alongside one another?
Could it be that Zhenling Sect feared blame from Chang Chun Temple and deliberately fabricated the scene?
"Tsk, if that's the case, Soul Cultivators are truly terrifying. Two Foundation Establishment cultivators from reputable sects joined forces and still couldn't defeat one of them," Yu Qingli shook his head.
"What did you expect? Why do you think Soul Cultivation is taboo? It's because they possess the power to overwhelm their peers and have such unfathomable methods," Zhang Zhi said.
"That may be true, but Soul Cultivators aren't invincible. Isn't the recent incident with Shengye Sect a case in point? That Hagon, he not only killed two of the Soul Cultivator's subordinates by himself but also successfully repelled him and saved the Shengye Sect members. It's said that he's just a cultivator at the early-stage of Foundation Establishment. It's a wonder how he cultivated to achieve that," Cultivator Lu remarked with emotion.
"Indeed, I've also inquired about him. He seems to be a Loose Cultivator, and both his strength and character are exceptional. His future is immeasurable," Fairy Hua said, her eyes revealing a hint of admiration.
The scholar-clad cultivator beside her heard this and immediately commented bitterly, "He's just lucky that he made a name for himself with a single fight. There's no reason other Loose cultivators couldn't match him."
"Heh, if Fellow Daoist Cui thinks so, then why don't you name someone else as impressive as him?" Fairy Hua glared at him.
The Cultivator Cui, provoked by her, flushed red, his gaze darting around wildly. But for a moment, he couldn't recall another famous Loose Cultivator.
"Alas, I do recall someone who could rival Hagon, not sure if you all have heard about him?" Yu Qingli suddenly said with a smile.
Curious, everyone turned their gazes toward him, but he leisurely took a sip of tea before continuing.
"This person was once abandoned by the Chang Chun Temple and later plunged into the Southern Border alone. He lived through trials and tribulations, a slim chance of survival, and it took him three years just to return to the Da Jin Capital. Yet, when he did, he had already become a Foundation Establishment cultivator and even publicly challenged the State Preceptor at the abdication ceremony, killing him."
Hua Xianzi suddenly realized, "You're talking about Yuan Ming, the author of the 'Southern Travel Chronicles,' Young Master Yuan, right? Indeed, he's comparable to Hagon, but it seems we haven't heard much about him in recent years."
"Sigh, after all, he offended the Chang Chun Temple, even with his talent, his current life can't be easy," Cultivator Lu sighed, clasping his wrist.
Just then, Zhang Zhi looked at everyone with a peculiar expression and said, "In fact, I happened to encounter Yuan Ming not long ago."
"Really?" Everyone was immediately surprised.
Yuan Ming was startled and looked up at Zhang Zhi but couldn't remember where he had seen him.
"I remember it was near Tongdu City, I was being harried by a few cultivators at the time, and suddenly one erupted to rescue me, taking care of the enemies. When I asked for his name, he told me it was Yuan Ming. He not only declined the gift I offered in return but instead gave me a signed copy of 'Young Master Sheng's Southern Journey' which he claimed to have written. Let me show it to you," Zhang Zhi said as he took out a book and placed it on the table.
Everyone immediately crowded around, taking turns to hold the book and flip through it, all expressing admiration.
After making its rounds, the book reached Yuan Ming. As he opened it, he instantly recognized that, although the handwriting was somewhat similar to his, it wasn't written by his hand.
Why would someone impersonate me?
Contemplating in his heart, Yuan Ming passed the book back.
"In recent years, our Da Jin really has an abundance of talents. Not to mention Yuan Ming and Hagon among the young generation of cultivators. Even the abdicated Jin Country Emperor is said to have risen from Qi Refinement to Foundation Establishment in just three years, his path entirely unobstructed—such talent is truly enviable," Daoist Lu remarked wistfully.
"Isn't that the case? And what about the likes of Gao Qian from the Chang Chun Temple, Immortal Hai Xiang from the Water Spirit Palace, Bai Chengnan from the Bailuo Manor? Which one isn't invincible among their peers, known far and wide?" Zhang Zhi nodded in agreement.Thе оriginаl sоurсе is М|V|L5ЕМРYR.
"Sigh, who do you say is the strongest among these people?" Yu Qingli inquired.
"That would certainly be Gao Qian. He is the prodigy of the Chang Chun Temple. There's a rumor that not too long ago, he began secluding himself in preparation for Core Formation; it won't be long before he's on a different level from the others," Zhang Zhi responded.
"I don't see it that way; Fairy Hai Xiang had sparred with Gao Qian before and neither emerged superior. Moreover, she has also kept out of the public eye in recent years—she may be preparing for Core Formation as well," Cultivator Lu suggested, stroking his beard.
"So you're saying, among the three, Bai Chengnan is the weakest? And I wonder how Yuan Ming and Hagon compare to him," Yu Qingli said with a laugh.
"No matter how strong Yuan Ming and Hagon are, they are still Loose Cultivators. Bai Chengnan has the entire Bailuo Manor behind him; they couldn't possibly best him," Zhang Zhi shook his head.
"Speaking of the Bailuo Manor, I heard that their Foreign Affairs Elder was assassinated not long ago, I wonder if any clues have been found," Cultivator Lu mentioned.
"Who knows, the Bailuo Manor keeps a tight seal on its lips, even if there are clues they wouldn't speak out. Probably only after they catch the murderer and seek vengeance will we hear any news," Zhang Zhi said, spreading his hands.
While they were chatting, at the table next to them, a male cultivator suddenly stood up and walked over.
"Fellow Daoists, I am Jiang Xiong, and I apologize for the interruption. I have a few questions I'd like to consult with you, could you please enlighten me?" the male cultivator asked, cupping his fists.
"Fellow Daoist, please speak your mind," Cultivator Lu nodded.
"It's like this: I come from the Northern Desert and have a son who has cultivated with me for some time. He has now reached the Qi Refining Third Level, but as you know, the road of a Loose Cultivator is difficult to travel. I do not wish for my son to follow in my footsteps. Having long heard of the Central Plains as a holy land for cultivation, I brought him with me so he could be accepted into a sect here. However, I'm new to the Central Plains and unfamiliar with the details of the various sects. I happened to hear that you Fellow Daoists seem to be rather knowledgeable about the sects of the Central Plains, so I wanted to ask for some advice," explained Jiang Xiong.
"If Fellow Daoist has the means, then send your child to the Chang Chun Temple, after all, it's the foremost sect in the Central Plains, you can hardly go wrong," Zhang Zhi suggested.
"I have heard of the great name of the Chang Chun Temple, but my son has only three spirit roots, I'm afraid the Temple might not regard him highly," Jiang Xiong sighed lightly, smiling bitterly.

chapters.title: Chapter 304 - 304: 281
chapters.content:
"There's no need to worry about that, with three spirit roots, he has already met the criteria for discipleship at Chang Chun Temple. However, the temple doesn't only consider aptitude; character and temperament are also part of their evaluation. Regardless, come May next year, your son can go to Yuhua City to participate in the Initiation Ceremony. As long as he passes the preliminary selection, becoming an outer disciple shouldn't pose a problem," said Zhang Zhi.
On the side, Cultivator Lu shook his head, "That's not ideal. As the saying goes, it's better to be a head of a chicken than the tail of a phoenix. There are too many people wanting to join Chang Chun Temple, and with three spirit roots, I'm afraid he may forever be stuck at the Qi Refinement Realm. It might be wiser to choose a slightly inferior sect where he can receive more attention. Cultivation is not only about aptitude; the resources invested are also very important."
"Those slightly inferior would then be Water Spirit Palace and Bailuo Manor, both sects have Nascent Soul Middle Stage ancestors presiding over them," Yu Qingli said.
"Bailuo Manor is a cultivation family; they rarely recruit disciples outside of their surname, so they don't really count as a proper sect. As for Water Spirit Palace, it used to recruit only female disciples. Although they have started to accept male disciples in recent years, the Sect's disciples all practice Water Magic. I wonder, does your son possess a Water Spirit Root?" Zhang Zhi asked thoughtfully.
"No," Jiang Xiong replied, shaking his head in disappointment.
"Then neither of these options will work. Your only choice may be to look for a sect with just a Nascent Soul Early Stage ancestor in residence," Zhang Zhi added somewhat regretfully.
"Among the sects of this caliber, the one closest to Little Lake City is Shengye Sect. Their disciples are skilled in alchemy and medicine cultivation, and these are the main areas they test for in their entry examinations," Cultivator Lu explained.
"Apart from Shengye Sect, there's the Fire Sparrow Sect in the eastern part of Da Jin. Although they are not as powerful as Water Spirit Palace, they maintain a good relationship with it. It is said that the annual sect competition is jointly organized between the two, with much exchange and learning between them. However, their entry exam mainly assesses the disciples' proficiency in mana control, so if your son wishes to join, he'll need to put in extra effort in this area," said Zhang Zhi emphatically.
"There is also Thousand Sword Pavilion, located in the western part of Da Jin. Everyone in the pavilion practices sword cultivation, specializing in the Gold Element Magic and offense techniques. It is said that within the grounds there is a Sword Cliff where successive generations of ancestors have left their legacies. Any disciple may go there to gain insight. If one is lucky enough to inherit a powerful legacy, it's like ascending to the heavens in a single step. However, their entry examinations have stringent requirements on comprehension, and the participants must have a solid foundation in swordsmanship; this is something to consider," Cultivator Lu added.
Fellow Daoist Jiang nodded repeatedly as he listened, and just then, Fairy Hua furrowed her brows.
"You all have been discussing Da Jin sects; where do you place our Zhao Country sects?"
Cultivator Cui chimed in, "Indeed, our Zhao Country has the Five Thunder Sect, known for its unparalleled Thunder Skill, and the Spirit Talisman Sect, which looks down upon the rest of Central Plains with its talisman making technique. Though smaller in scale compared to Chang Chun Temple, they are both still among the top in Central Plains."
Anxious, Jiang Xiong quickly asked, "What are the requirements to join these two sects?"
"To join Five Thunder Sect, one must pass their Three Thunder Formation, which demands a lot in terms of comprehension, observation, and courage. Joining Spirit Talisman Sect is relatively easier; as long as the disciple has a good memory, can memorize the runes within the stipulated time, and can replicate them from memory, that would suffice," said Fairy Hua.
"I see, thank you for the insight," said Jiang Xiong as he bowed slightly. He then sat back down, seemingly pondering which sect he should have his son attempt to join.
Content presented by *.
Seeing him leave, Zhang Zhi turned to Fairy Hua, "Fellow Daoist Jiang is currently living in Da Jin. What's wrong with us recommending Da Jin sects to him? But Fairy Hua, you seem impatient, only keen to recommend Zhao Country sects. If not, why don't you recommend some from Wu Country and Chu Country too?"
Fairy Hua snorted coldly but did not reply. Yu Qingli, witnessing the situation, stepped forward and attempted to smooth things over.
"Let's not dwell over such a trivial matter, shall we? By the way, I heard some disciples fled from Five Thunder Sect; is that true?"
"Fellow Daoist Yu is well-informed, indeed. The incident caused quite a stir in Zhao Country's Immortal Cultivation World. It is said that they took several Heart-splitting Bombs from the sect, which are now commanding a price of two thousand spirit stones each on the black market. Whether they still have them is uncertain," Fairy Hua affirmed with a nod.
"Two thousand spirit stones? That's enough to buy two cheaper top-grade magical tools. Isn't the Heart-splitting Bomb just a one-time use magic artifact? Is it really that valuable?" Yu Qingli expressed his surprise.
"That's actually quite cheap. The Heart-splitting Bomb is a unique magic artifact of Five Thunder Sect and only a few ever make it to the market. Besides, its power is comparable to the full force of a peak Foundation Establishment cultivator's attack. If your life hangs in the balance, wouldn't you trade two thousand spirit stones for it?" Fairy Hua asked in return.
"Of course, I would. Maybe one day I'll come across it in the black market," Yu Qingli chuckled.
"Dream on. So far, I haven't heard of anyone actually getting their hands on one. For all we know, the deserters from Five Thunder Sect might have used it up while fleeing," said Fairy Hua, shaking her head.
Yuan Ming, an onlooker seated at the side, sipped his tea with an unperturbed expression, seemingly uninvolved. Yet, inside, he was beaming with delight. It seemed his purchase of those Heart-splitting Bombs had indeed been perspicacious!
With his glib tongue, he had only paid a thousand Spirit Stones for three bombs at the time, which was quite a bargain compared to the prices here.
"Alas, Fellow Daoist Zhang, you just mentioned that the Water Spirit Palace has now started recruiting male disciples too. What's that all about?" Cultivator Cui suddenly asked.
"What else could it be? The number of disciples they can attract has been decreasing yearly. If they don't lower the bar a bit and remove some of the insignificant restrictions, how would they continue to attract top talents?" Zhang Zhi took a sip from his own cup of tea.
"How could that be? Of the Four Major Countries of the Central Plains, Da Jin is the largest by far, with a population in the hundreds of millions—when did it ever lack talented disciples?" Cultivator Cui exclaimed in surprise.
"Heh, let me ask you, why do people say Da Jin's Cultivation World is the strongest in the Central Plains?" Zhang Zhi said with a smile.
"It's obviously because of Chang Chun Temple! It's the only place in the entire Central Plains with a Late-stage Nascent Soul Cultivator presiding. How could it not be strong?" replied Cultivator Cui without hesitation.
"Exactly. If Chang Chun Temple is so powerful, where do you think those talented disciples will be heading when selecting a sect to join?" Zhang Zhi shrugged his shoulders.
"In fact, it's not just what Fellow Daoist Zhang mentioned. Chang Chun Temple has been controlling the imperial governance for hundreds of years. Each Emperor who steps onto the Immortal Path joins Chang Chun Temple. Eventually, Da Jin has almost become their territory. When a prodigy appears, before local sects even become aware, Chang Chun Temple already receives the news and sends someone to recruit them. With this in mind, how can other sects compete with Chang Chun Temple in acquiring disciples?" sighed Cultivator Lu.
"I heard that not long ago, a cultivator from Chang Chun Temple proposed integrating selections of other sects into Chang Chun Temple's own Disciple Induction Ceremony. They claimed it would be more convenient for those who want to join a sect, saving them the trouble of running around. But in truth, it's for them to hoard all the talents from Da Jin for themselves. After all, given the choice, who wouldn't want to join Chang Chun Temple?" said Zhang Zhi, shaking his head helplessly.
"With Chang Chun Temple's domineering behavior, don't other sects have any complaints?" Cultivator Cui frowned.
"Complaints, of course, there are! But what can dissatisfaction do? For years, Chang Chun Temple has been arrogant and oppressive. Who dares to openly show their teeth and snarl at them? Loose Cultivators fear their power, sects fear their strength. Only someone as fearless as Yuan Ming would dare provoke them publicly," Zhang Zhi said with a sense of helplessness.
"The State Preceptor, under the guise of guiding the Emperor's early Cultivation, murdered Yuan Ming in secrecy. While Chang Chun Temple, under the pretense of considering the interests of Da Jin's Cultivation World, suppress other sects—is there any difference? Ultimately, it's still for their own sake! The words 'On what basis?' uttered by Yuan Ming at the abdication ceremony spoke for the hearts of many cultivators in Da Jin, truly exhilarating," Cultivator Lu exclaimed with a sigh, applauding the sentiment.
"Indeed, Yuan Ming's action won the hearts of many. Countless young disciples secretly idolize him," laughed Zhang Zhi, finishing off his cup of tea in a gulp.
Yuan Ming, still sitting quietly on the side with a calm gaze as placid as the water in his teacup, mentally reviewed everything he knew about Chang Chun Temple again and warned himself. While it was right to seek justice and revenge, without absolute strength, such impulses should be curbed.
These onlookers were unconcerned, treating the tales as mere stories to satisfy their vanity. However, should the day come when Chang Chun Temple came knocking at his door, or worse, sent a high-level cultivator to kill him, their casual conversation would probably take on a different tone, potentially saying, "Offending Chang Chun Temple is asking for trouble."
"Alright, let's not talk about this anymore. This matter doesn't concern us. Speaking of which, the Tianxiang Auction is going to be held soon. Has anyone managed to get an invitation?" Yu Qingli looked around and quickly changed the subject.
"How could that be easy? We Loose Cultivators wouldn't even know where to begin trying to buy an invitation to the Tianxiang Auction," complained Zhang Zhi.
Yu Qingli chuckled and pulled out a purple invitation from his chest, "Look, what is this?"
"An auction invitation? Where did you get that?" Zhang Zhi asked, surprised.
"Heh, a friend of mine recently came into possession of an invitation due to a fortuitous encounter. However, he unexpectedly had urgent matters to attend to and couldn't make it to the auction, so he transferred the invitation to me. Even so, it cost me over a hundred Spirit Stones to get my hands on it," Yu Qingli admitted, somewhat pained by the expense.
"Over a hundred Spirit Stones just for an invitation? I've heard of the grand reputation of the Tianxiang Auction, but is it really worth that much?" Cultivator Cui questioned.
"Of course. Keep in mind that the Tianxiang Auction isn't merely a high-end auction. When the event officially begins, many sects from Da Jin and Zhao Country will set up booths inside the Tianyu Building at the center of the lake. Often, some novel items will be on display. Even if one doesn't have the means to purchase anything, just browsing through and gaining experience and knowledge is worth the price," explained Zhang Zhi with a smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 305 - 282 Plotting
chapters.content:
"Although that's true, I didn't just buy this invitation to broaden my horizons. I've already inquired about it, and this time at the auction, Shengye Sect is going to offer an elixir called the Origin Transformation Pill. It can help break through the bottleneck at the Foundation Establishment stage. Its efficacy is said to be better than anything currently on the market, and it's extremely rare, with production so limited that only a few bottles are refined each year. Aside from the one bottle auctioned, they only accept orders from other Sects and don't sell to Loose Cultivators," said Yu Qingli.
"Eh? If I remember correctly, the last time we met, Qingli, weren't you still complaining about how slowly your Cultivation at the Foundation Establishment stage was progressing, unsure when you'd even reach the initial bottleneck? Now you're already planning to buy an elixir to help with the breakthrough; isn't it too early?" Zhang Zhi asked, puzzled.
"Hehe, Brother Zhang, what you don't know is that the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop in the city, I think it was the year before last, released a new product called Purple Mysterious Incense. Its effect is much better than Qingxuan Incense. I've been buying it frequently for the past two years. Combined with elixirs, my cultivation speed has indeed increased quite a bit. Now, my cultivation has already reached the peak standard of the early stages of Foundation Establishment," said Yu Qingli with a smile.
"Oh, really? I bought a stick of Qingxuan Incense before and felt it was too weak, only suitable for those in the Qi Refinement Realm. I didn't expect there to be something now that's also suitable for those in the Foundation Establishment stage. It looks like I have to buy a few sticks to use after I get back," said Zhang Zhi, quite pleasantly surprised.
"Wait until you get back? They sell their incense in limited quantities. If you go now, I'm afraid even the Qingxuan Incense will be sold out, let alone thinking of buying the Purple Mysterious Incense. Dream on!" Yu Qingli shook his head.
"It's that popular? Then when does their shop open? I can still go early," Zhang Zhi frowned.
"Their shop opens at 5 A.M., but since there are so many buyers, if you really want to line up, you should go at 3 A.M. to grab a few sticks. However, I have a way that doesn't require lining up, although I'm not sure if Brother Zhang would be willing," Yu Qingli said.
Zhang Zhi, seeing the sly grin on Yu Qingli's face, felt somewhat uneasy, but couldn't resist the temptation of the Purple Mysterious Incense.
"Brother Yu, don't beat around the bush; just tell me."
"Well, I've been a patron of their shop for quite some time now and have accumulated some points, which allow me to place an order a day in advance. However, there's a limit to how much Purple Mysterious Incense one person can buy in a day. If I give some to you, I'll have less for myself," Yu Qingli said meaningfully.
After hesitating for a moment, Zhang Zhi gritted his teeth and said, "Brother Yu, with the relationship we've had for so long, I naturally won't let you suffer any loss. In that case, for each stick of incense, I'll pay ten percent more. How about that?"
Yu Qingli nodded and agreed with a laugh.
However, just at this moment, Yuan Ming suddenly said, "Fellow Daoist Yu, I've heard that if the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop discovers someone selling incense by taking advantage of their points, they'll put that person on the shop's blacklist and never sell incense to them again. You should be more careful."
Upon hearing this, Yu Qingli was taken aback, and Zhang Zhi, catching on, immediately burst into laughter.
"Brother Yu, with our many years of friendship, how could I bear to see you suffer a loss? To be safe, I'll just buy them from you at market price. Otherwise, it would be bad if someone reported us."
A look of embarrassment and annoyance flashed across Yu Qingli's face; he glared fiercely at Yuan Ming but could only grudgingly agree to Zhang Zhi's proposal.
Yuan Ming didn't mind, knowing that regular customers with points get discounts when buying incense—it turned out that Yu Qingli was still making a profit.
The reselling business couldn't be banned, and Yuan Ming didn't have the time to meddle in everyone's affairs, but since it was happening right in front of him, he felt obliged to give a word of caution.
"Fellow Daoist Yu, since you're placing an order, could you also reserve a few sticks of Beauty Incense for me? You probably won't need that, will you? I'll pay you the market price," Hua Xianzi also said.
Seeing this, Daoist Lu stroked his beard and couldn't help but sigh, "Even Foundation Establishment cultivators have to reserve their purchase of incense. The business at the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop must be booming; the owner behind the scenes must be making a fortune, right?"
"Indeed, considering the prices of their incense and that they sell out every day, just sitting at home, there would be several thousand Spirit Stones coming into the account each month," said Cultivator Cui, nodding, with evident envy in his voice.This chapter was first seen on *.
"How wonderful that would be! Even the top disciples of Chang Chun Temple don't get such treatment. If I could open a shop like that in my lifetime, I would be perfectly content," Zhang Zhi sighed.
"Come off it, you? You'd better stick to carrying out Scatter Alliance tasks honestly—with no unique business of your own, where would you get such profits?" Yu Qingli laughed.
"Making simple trades like those, how could it be so easy to lose money? Besides, compared to opening a shop, Scatter Alliance tasks are more dangerous, right? Not to mention the usual exploring Secret Realms and guarding against criminals—have you heard? Recently, some decayed Scatter Alliances have started dealing in the slave trade, specifically luring local cultivators to unfamiliar places, poisoning and entrapping them. Those who are somewhat lucky just get their cultivation sealed and are sent to mine Spirit Stones, but the unlucky ones are sold directly to Evil Cultivators as Blood Sacrifice materials," said Zhang Zhi.
"Really? That's terrifying!" Yu Qingli was surprised.
"I have a friend who encountered a similar situation. He was told the mission was to go to a forest in the northern part of Zhao Country. But the farther he went, the closer he got to the Northern Desert. Fortunately, he reacted quickly and realized something was wrong, so he immediately fled, barely escaping with his life," said Cultivator Cui.
Everyone looked shocked upon hearing this, and then Jiang Xiong, who was sitting at another table, leaned over.
"Fellow Daoists, I hail from the Northern Desert, and there are some things I really shouldn't mention. But just now, as several of you kindly offered your assistance, I would feel remiss if I didn't offer a word of caution. In recent years, the situation in the Northern Desert Cultivation World has been rather strange. Many cultivators have disappeared without explanation, and numerous individuals with little potential have suddenly risen to power. In the black market of Wangyue City's workshop, Qi Refinement slaves occasionally appear. If possible, it is best for you all to stay away from the Northern Desert, or if you must go, be sure to take every precaution," he said.
This pronouncement tightened everyone's expressions. It was only when Yu Qingli forced a few chuckles and changed the subject that the atmosphere lightened slightly.
After that incident, they no longer discussed other odd rumors and instead chatted about trivial matters. Yuan Ming joined in from time to time, staying for over half an hour longer before getting up to leave.
However, as he was leaving, he suddenly saw Hu Tu driving a horse cart rushing over and stopping in the alley behind the tea house.
Yuan Ming, noticing that Hu Tu seemed not to have seen him, became curious and quietly positioned himself at the entrance of the alley.
In the alley, Hu Tu jumped off the horse carriage and knocked on the back door of the Four Symbols Tea House.
"Who is it?" inquired a server clad in light blue, poking his head out.
"Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop. I've arranged it with your steward, bringing the incense over," Hu Tu said, rubbing his hands together.
The server looked at him twice: "Wait a moment, I'll go call the steward."
Before long, a middle-aged male cultivator came out. Seeing it was Hu Tu, he gave a smile and a polite bow of his hands.
"Ah, Brother Hu Tu, for such matters you could have simply sent someone on my behalf, why trouble yourself to make a trip here?"
"Can't help it. The boss ordered me personally to come and notify you all. From now on, we'll provide a centralized supply of incense to you, with delivery on the first of every month. Also, don't forget to help us promote our shop when using it," Hu Tu explained.
"Of course, of course," the steward nodded, checking each item one by one, confirming the quantity. Then, he turned to enter the building and quickly came back out with a storage bag.
"Here's the payment for your shop's incense. Could Brother Hu Tu count it?"
Hu Tu took the storage bag, counted the spirit stones inside, and suddenly looked up: "Steward Xu, it seems you have given me too many spirit stones, haven't you?"
"Hehe, this is a small token I've specially prepared for Brother Hu Tu, a little extra for your troubles—it's the rule of the City Lord Mansion," Steward Xu said with a smile.
Hu Tu's eyes flickered, then without changing his expression, he pocketed the storage bag: "Given the friendship between you and me, for such a small favor, even if Steward Xu hadn't mentioned it, I would not have forgotten it."
After chatting a bit more, both men burst out laughing.
Outside the alley, Yuan Ming turned away and left.
...
After Yuan Ming returned home, he sat down cross-legged and pondered over the information he had gathered from his trip to the tea house.
News of Sha Hao's deeds was already well-known throughout the city, with even the deaths of Gu Qiulong and Xu Changqing attributed to him. Now, Yuan Ming had no idea how many people wanted him dead.
Yet, if they simply wanted to kill him that was one thing, but he dreaded the thought of someone coveting Sha Hao's Soul Cultivation Method, deliberately sparing his life, giving him an opportunity to reveal his identity as a Soul Cultivator.
Associating this with the reward for Pu Zhengqing on the Evil Cultivation list, and the words "alive" inscribed behind it, Yuan Ming's face darkened, and his desire to kill Sha Hao intensified.
Finding Sha Hao wasn't difficult for him; if necessary, he could use his Soul Seal a few more times, which should reveal some information regarding Sha Hao's whereabouts.
However, most of his magical tools were damaged, and considering Sha Hao's skill in illusion, if he didn't fully prepare, it would be hard to capture him.
Over the past few days, he had visited various shops in Little Lake City and hadn't found any top-grade magical tool to his liking. His only chance to acquire one would probably be at the Tianxiang Auction.
But a newly obtained magical tool might not perform as well as the one he was accustomed to using. Instead of buying a new one, he preferred upgrading his Black Needle to a top-grade magical tool.
After pondering for a moment, he took out the artifact refining books he had bought over the last few days and started to read them carefully.
These books, purchased at high prices, contained quite a bit about top-grade magical tools.
He had already learned the basic content in Biluo Cave, so he quickly skipped over it and focused his attention on the explanations and analysis of top-grade magical tools.
For Core Formation Stage cultivators, top-grade magical tools can also be referred to as "treasure embryos," considered as magic treasures that are not yet fully refined.
Unlike magic treasures, however, the runes on top-grade magical tools cannot be connected into a rune formation; they still exist independently.
Not all magical tools can withstand the inscription of a fourth rune to become a top-grade magical tool. Ultimately, this is due to differences in the spiritual materials used.
Most spiritual materials can bear only up to three runes. When attempting to add another, it conflicts with the existing balance of runes, leading to their shattering and the deterioration of the magical tool as the material cannot withstand the power.
Only a magical tool that has incorporated top-grade spiritual materials during the refining process can endure the engraving and enriching of a fourth rune. Even if it fails, the magical tool will drop only one quality level and will not be completely destroyed.

chapters.title: Chapter 306 - 283: Seeking Help
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming nodded silently as he read this segment; he gained a deeper understanding of top-grade magical tools. After steadying his mind, he continued reading.
The book also mentioned two methods for forcibly upgrading ordinary magical tools to top-grade magical tools.
One method was the Refining Method, which involved mixing top-grade spiritual materials into an already refined magical tool through special means, allowing it to withstand the Enriching of a fourth rune.
The other was the Strong Injection Method, which, simply put, was to choose the fourth rune as a derivative of the runes already on the magical tool. For example, if the magical tool had a "Frost" rune, then the fourth rune could be the derivative "White Frost" rune or the lower level "Cold" rune.
The advantage of this method was that it could bypass the limitation that ordinary spiritual materials could only bear three runes, and any magical tool could be elevated to a top-grade magical tool using this method. The downside was that the success rate of this technique was extremely low; if one in ten attempts was successful, that would be considered very lucky.
Moreover, if the Strong Injection Method failed, it would result in the destruction of the magical tool, rendering it unusable.
Even if the creation was successful, top-grade magical tools enriched by this method would not qualify for advancement to a Magic Treasure. Compared with top-grade magical tools crafted through normal methods, their power was also weaker, but still far superior to high-grade magical tools.
Yuan Ming read the content of the book carefully and took note of the methods for crafting top-grade magical tools.
Naturally, the methods for advancing top-grade magical tools couldn't be limited to these two, but other methods with higher success rates were privately held by Artifact Refiners and would not be casually available on the market.
In order to find Sha Hao's whereabouts, Yuan Ming now had to use his possession ability on this person every seven days. He couldn't spare any time to seek out and learn Artifact Refining techniques from other Artifact Refiners.
Therefore, he could only start by trying out these two methods described in the book. If these proved to be ineffective, he would then consider other options.
However, he currently had no top-grade spiritual materials on hand, so the Refining Method was out of the question. He could only try his luck with the Strong Injection Method.
Of course, with such a low success rate, he dared not apply it directly to the Black Needle; after all, it was the only high-grade magical tool he was quite comfortable using. If something went wrong, he would really be in tears.
Yuan Ming thought for a moment and suddenly took out a yellow short halberd and a green feather fan from his Storage Bag.
Though he had acquired these two magical tools from Gu Qiulong, it was inconvenient to use them openly. Now was the perfect time to practice with them.
First, he picked up the yellow short halberd and identified the three runes inscribed on it as "Earth Element," "Hard," and "Sharp." When he tried to identify the runes on the green feather fan, though, he encountered difficulties.
The runes he was familiar with were almost all from Master Hei Mu's notes, and the rest of the Artifact Refining books he bought only covered basic runes.
Out of the three runes on the green feather fan, he could only recognize "Wind Blade," and the other two were unfamiliar to him.
However, if it was just for practice, one was enough.
After pondering for a while, he decided to inscribe the fourth rune on the yellow short halberd as "Heavy," and the fourth rune on the feather fan as "Wind Roll."
These were derivatives of the "Hard" rune and the "Wind Blade" rune, respectively, with significant relevance.
Yuan Ming's residence lacked the tools for Artifact Refining, but fortunately, there were several shops in Little Lake City that rented out Artifact Refining Rooms. After briefly recalling their locations, he quickly packed up his things and left his residence.
One and a half months later, inside a certain Artifact Refining Room, steam billowed.
Inside the massive casting furnace, red spirit fog firmly enveloped the short halberd as Spiritual Power flowed unceasingly into the fourth rune at the handle of the short halberd, slowly filling the lines.
