Everything seemed to be going smoothly, but just as the fourth rune was halfway lit up, the short halberd suddenly shook, and the previous three runes on it also lit up, bursting out with extremely dazzling light.
A muffled "bang" sounded, the spirit fog in the furnace instantly swelled, then dispersed rapidly, and soon, there was no light left inside the furnace.
Yuan Ming opened the Sealing Door with a darkened expression and took out the fragments of the yellow short halberd.
As he looked at a high-grade magical tool turn to nothing, he couldn't help sighing deeply, feeling melancholic.
Since leaving the Southern Border, Yuan Ming had scarcely touched Artifact Refining. Although he still remembered a fair amount of the basics, his skills were indeed quite rusty.
Therefore, after renting an Artifact Refining Room, he did not directly use the Strong Injection Method, as it also fell under the scope of Artifact Refining.
He spent a month practicing forging, ruining who knows how many spiritual materials, before he stumbled his way to crafting his first Mid Grade Magical Artifact.
Although the quality of the magical tool he crafted wasn't great, it greatly bolstered his morale.
After numerous attempts and feeling sure that he had grasped the knack for crafting Mid Grade Magical Tools, he began to try crafting high-grade magical tools.
However, despite the difference of just one rune, the difficulty of crafting high-grade magical tools was many times greater.
Yuan Ming, aiming to make the crafting easier, almost exclusively chose simple runes with fewer strokes for Enriching. Yet every attempt would go awry midway through. After half a month, not one magical tool was successfully endowed.
If he couldn't even craft high-grade magical tools, let alone top-grade ones.
Yuan Ming still harbored a sliver of hope before giving up completely, thinking of giving the Strong Injection Method a final try, hoping it might be simpler than starting from scratch.
The current result, however, completely dispelled his thoughts of crafting a top-grade magical tool using the Strong Injection Method.
He quickly tidied up and then rose to leave the rented Artifact Refining Room.
...
Two hours later.
Yuan Ming returned to the secret chamber of residence number eighty-six, placing the books he had purchased on his way back on the table,
For him, Sha Hao's trickiest assets were two-fold, one being the top-grade magical tool, the silver sphere in his possession, and the other, his Soul Cultivation Illusion Technique.
Since the path to refining top-grade magical tools was impassable, Yuan Ming momentarily had no better strategy to contend with the silver sphere and could only consider how to deal with Sha Hao's illusions.
As a disciple of Xi Cangqiong, Sha Hao's mastery in the art of Soul Cultivation Illusion Techniques had received the true teachings of the Great Elder and showed signs of even surpassing his master.
On the other hand, Yuan Ming could only grope his way across the river, deducing the usage of illusion techniques on his own.
For this reason, he had specifically visited a shop in the city that sold various classics and purchased some of them.
These classics contained more or less some basic knowledge of illusion techniques and described some combat related to such techniques. Yuan Ming's choice to learn from the fragmentary knowledge within these books was an act of desperation since his soul cultivation master, Xi Ying, was currently in the Southern Border, a distance from Little Lake City that far exceeded ten thousand miles. Even using the Sound Transmission Talisman she had left him wouldn't reach her.
Previously, when he encountered Sha Hao, due to the urgency of the situation, his emotions erupted suddenly, and he had forgotten this, using one of the talismans.
The books he had purchased were very rudimentary, and the authors' analyses of illusion techniques were not profound—some even held biased views. However, for ordinary cultivators to understand illusion techniques and fill in foundational knowledge, these could still just barely suffice.
One of the books mentioned that the essence of illusion techniques is, in fact, to use one's Divine Sense to influence the opponent's perception.
Whether through magic or runes, the use of illusion techniques would inevitably consume the cultivator's own Divine Power.
Therefore, the stronger one's Divine Power, the more lifelike the illusion techniques cast and the harder they were to break.
By the same token, to counter illusion techniques, one either needed to possess Divine Power far surpassing that of the caster or utilize rare talismans, magical artifacts, and other means to dispel them.
After reading this, Yuan Ming thought of the range his illusion techniques could cover, which was comparable to the reach of his Divine Sense, and he nodded to himself, believing quite a bit in the contents of the book.
However, he then recalled something else.
After all, illusion techniques were merely a means every Soul Cultivator could master. The unique and bizarre abilities that came with Divine Soul Transformation were what truly differentiated one Soul Cultivator from another.
Yuan Ming's transformed Soul Crow possessed abilities such as Far Travel, leaning more towards assistance. Then what kind of abilities would Sha Hao's Blood Bat have?
Yuan Ming carefully recalled the details of his encounters with Sha Hao, particularly how, no matter how Yuan Ming fled, Sha Hao always managed to find him.
This сhаptеr wаs оriginаlly pоstеd оn М^VLЕМРYR.
Yet, this ability felt to Yuan Ming more like Sha Hao had mastered some secret technique or magic artifact rather than an intrinsic ability of his Divine Soul Transformation into a Blood Bat.
After racking his brain to no avail, Yuan Ming switched tracks and began to consider what he possessed that could restrain the exertion of Divine Power.
Quickly, he thought of the Fog Incense.
The dense fog created by the Fog Incense was something even the Great Elder couldn't see through directly, so it certainly would have a restraining effect on Sha Hao as well.
After pondering for a moment, Yuan Ming stood up and left his residence. He exited Little Lake City and, riding a magical tool, arrived at the Rain Ruins Swamp. Finding a secluded spot, he voluntarily descended, brought out the Stealing Heaven Tripod, took a stick of Fog Incense, lit it, and also released Vajra.
Soon, the thick white fog swallowed up the figures of Yuan Ming and Vajra, shrouding an entire area.
"I want to test if the Fog Incense can counteract illusion techniques. In a moment, no matter what you see, stand still and do not move," Yuan Ming instructed before moving five steps away from Vajra.
Seeing Vajra nod in preparation, he gathered his focus, intent on casting an illusion technique.
However, under the cover of the white fog, his Divine Sense could hardly leave his body, let alone reach Vajra to trap him in an illusion.
Yuan Ming tried several times, each time slightly decreasing the distance between himself and Vajra. Yet, even when he walked up to Vajra and pressed his hand on Vajra's shoulder, he was still unable to successfully cast an illusion.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming felt a surge of excitement.
Indeed, the Fog Incense had a countering effect on illusion techniques. With this card up his sleeve, he would likely have a much easier time dealing with Sha Hao in the future.
With the experiment yielding results, Yuan Ming did not linger. He extinguished the Fog Incense, gathered up Vajra and the Stealing Heaven Tripod, and then mounted the Jade Shuttle, ready to return to Little Lake City.
But suddenly, his expression changed, and he halted in his tracks.
"What's going on?"
Just now, he had unexpectedly received a distress signal from Hua Zhi, sent through the connection with the spirit beast.
Without a second thought, Yuan Ming hastily changed direction, flying towards the location of Hua Zhi.

chapters.title: Chapter 307 - 284: Siblings
chapters.content:
Meanwhile,
In the northern part of Rain Ruins Swamp, Hua Zhi was engaged in a fierce battle.
In midair, a large red bird with wingspan of about ten feet fluttered its wings vigorously, shaking off numerous crimson feathers like flames. The feathers ignited in midair, transforming into fist-sized fireballs and plummeting towards Hua Zhi below.
Realizing there was nowhere to hide, Hua Zhi suddenly plunged his hands into the ground. Instantly, dozens of vines shot out from the soil, intertwining and coiling around him, forming a dark purple vine cage above and around him.
The next instant, the fireballs collided with the vine cage, each bursting upon impact. The scattering flames landed on the vines, instantly turning them into a fiery inferno.
However, thanks to the "True Water Ring" given by Yuan Ming, a protective artifact on Hua Zhi, the flames did not actually ignite the vines. Even so, Hua Zhi dared not let the flames crawl back onto his body. He quickly flung the vine cage aside, withdrew his hands, and severed the connection with the vines.
Once detached from Hua Zhi, the vine cage, lacking the fire resistance effect of the "True Water Ring," burst violently under the blaze. The flaming fragments of vines shattered across the ground, and a plume of white smoke arose—swamp water vaporized into mist by the intense heat of the flames.
Amid the rising steam, Hua Zhi heard a sharp phoenix cry. Looking up, he saw the red bird circling half a round in the sky before it sharply dove towards him.
Hua Zhi immediately dodged backwards, swinging his hands forward at the same time. Instantly, a burst of blue light flickered, and dozens of wooden flying swords materialized, shooting simultaneously at the red bird.
However, the red bird did not dodge or evade, but instead charged straight into the flying swords.
The flying swords pierced the body of the red bird, as if entering an illusion, passing through without any hindrance, only carrying away sparks, and turning the flying swords to ashes.
Seeing no escape, Hua Zhi immediately tried to burrow into the ground, but as he moved, he saw a talisman shot from afar and land not far from him.
In an instant, the ground within several meters around Hua Zhi, originally soft and moist, became as hard as rock, making it impossible for him to dig in.
Left with no other choice, at the last moment, Hua Zhi crossed his arms in front of him, forming a wooden shield, hoping to withstand the charge of the red bird.
But just at the moment of impact, the red bird completely dispersed from head to tail, transforming into several crimson chains of flames that tightly bound Hua Zhi.
Hua Zhi immediately struggled, but the more he did, the tighter the chains bound him. However, for some unknown reason, although the chains were made of flames, they did not spread onto his body.
"I didn't expect you, a demon beast, to have some tricks. If I hadn't had an Earth Binding Talisman on me, you might have actually escaped," a voice said.
From the nearby woods, a young man clad in a long robe with red flame patterns and a gold-trimmed warm jade belt appeared.
The man was quite handsome, with a high nose bridge and pale skin, and his eyes shone as bright as dancing flames. Especially striking was his hair—black with hints of red, adding a somewhat bewitching charm to his appearance.
"Today, you're in luck. I happen to need a spirit pet by my side. From now on, you will follow me," the man said with a smile.
"I already have a master!" Hua Zhi cried inwardly, his body twisting incessantly.
However, the man couldn't hear Hua Zhi's voice and continued, "Heh, look at you, you must be thrilled, right? After all, to follow me, Di Chen, is the fortune of eight lifetimes for you."
Just then, a White Jade Shuttle suddenly flew from afar and landed nearby.
Yuan Ming stepped down from the shuttle, seeing Hua Zhi bound by the chains of flames, his brow furrowed. But upon realizing Hua Zhi seemed unharmed, he breathed a sigh of relief.
"Fellow Daoist, this is the spirit beast I raise here. I do not know what has upset you, but I kindly ask you to show mercy and let him go," Yuan Ming bowed slightly and spoke courteously to Di Chen.
"Your spirit beast? Do you have proof?" Di Chen looked at Yuan Ming and frowned.
"Have you noticed the Jade Ring on his body? That's the fire resistance magical tool I left with him," Yuan Ming explained.
Hearing this, Di Chen performed a series of Magic Formulas. The chains of flames coiled around Hua Zhi like snakes, quickly removing the True Water Ring from his body.
"Tsk, to give a spirit beast a top-grade magical tool for protection, it seems you truly care for this spirit beast. However, I've quite taken a liking to him as well. How about this, name a price in spirit stones for selling him to me?" Di Chen looked at the True Water Ring and proposed.
Yuan Ming shook his head: "I'm sorry, for me, Hua Zhi is not just a spirit beast, but also a partner, not something to be priced in spirit stones."
"Heh, no hurry. Think it over—are you sure you won't sell?" Di Chen narrowed his eyes, his aura surging with Spiritual Power.Visit Мy Virtuаl Librаry Еmpirе (МV-LЕМР-YR) fоr mоrе.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming sighed. He raised his right hand, and a green Flying Sword manifested out of thin air, its tip pointing directly at Di Chen.
A glint flashed in Di Chen's eyes. With a single hand gesture, he suddenly spat out a small red bird from his mouth. With a flap of its wings, it swelled to about ten feet in length.
Without hesitation, Yuan Ming silently controlled the green Flying Sword with one hand to stab at Di Chen, while his other hand also performed a spell, pointing towards Di Chen's feet.
In an instant, four or five green wooden dragons burst from the ground, lunging towards Di Chen.
Yet, Di Chen showed no fear. With a change of hand gestures, the large red bird in the sky suddenly exploded, transforming into dozens of flaming long swords that whistled down from the sky, pinning the wooden dragons to the ground.
At the same time, another red long saber appeared in Di Chen's other hand, tangling with the flying sword in combat.
Yuan Ming saw his attack easily blocked and his face instantly darkened. Seeing this, Di Chen's face showed a hint of smugness. Just as he was about to mock Yuan Ming, he suddenly felt alarmed.
A chill inexplicably crept up Di Chen's back. Without thinking, he flipped his right hand and slapped a talisman onto his body.
The next instant, a red light suddenly flared up around him, and a wave of scorching heat spread out like ripples, blowing away the Black Needle that was attacking him from behind.
If his reaction had been a step slower, he would have been pierced by that Black Needle.
Di Chen, still shaken, looked towards Yuan Ming and said, "Nice move."
Yuan Ming didn't respond but raised his hand to release Vajra and was about to use another magic.
At that moment, Di Chen's expression drastically changed. He immediately recalled his crimson long sword and unlocked the chain that bound Hua Zhi.
"Consider yourself lucky today. We'll fight another day." Di Chen dropped a harsh line and then pulled out a Flying Artifact, fleeing towards the east.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming suspected a trick and did not pursue. He remained on alert.
However, after a long while, he saw no sign of Di Chen returning or launching a surprise attack.
As Yuan Ming puzzled over this, he was about to ask Hua Zhi about the situation, but suddenly, another red light descended from the sky, landing in front of Yuan Ming.
From the red light, a woman in a gold-edged, fire-patterned long robe, with a ponytail, stepped forward.
Her skin was as flawless and white as jade. Her slender willow eyebrows sat above deep eyes sparkling like stars, and her red lips seemed as vibrant as blooming lotuses.
Her hair color, similar to Di Chen's—black with hints of red—didn't appear flamboyant but added an aura of brisk valor.
She scanned her surroundings, noticed the traces of the fight between Di Chen and Yuan Ming, and lightly knitted her brows. She then clasped her hands towards Yuan Ming.
"May I ask you, Fellow Daoist, were you just now in combat with a man whose hair resembles mine?"
"Indeed. He abruptly ran off to the east in the middle of our battle," Yuan Ming nodded and replied.
"As I thought. My younger brother has caused you trouble. If you hold any grudges, you may leave a message at the Five Elements Inn in Little Lake City, saying you're looking for Di Yue from the Fire Sparrow Sect. Once I catch him, I will surely bring him to apologize." Before Di Yue could finish speaking, she had already boarded a Flying Artifact and, as the word "apologize" dropped, she had flown dozens of feet towards the direction Di Chen had escaped.
Yuan Ming watched as the red light quickly disappeared, inwardly cursing.
Fighting senselessly with someone—which did not genuinely vent any anger—felt absurdly stifling, especially how this 'sister' acted as though in a rush, speaking as if running a relay.
It was only that the Fire Sparrow Sect was located to the east of Da Jin. What were they doing near Little Lake City now?
As thoughts flickered through Yuan Ming's mind, he turned to Hua Zhi and said, "It seems your injuries have mostly healed. You'd better stay close to me for now to avoid being caught by other cultivators thinking you're a demon beast."
Hua Zhi wanted to object that she wasn't that weak, but having been nearly captured recently, she found no words to argue and could only nod sullenly in agreement.
At that moment, from a nearby tree, Vajra leaped down, patted his chest towards Hua Zhi, and unashamedly let out a laugh:
"Dou Ya, you almost turned into kindling this time."
"Monkey, if you're so capable, come fight me!" Hua Zhi burst into rage, flailing her teeth and claws.
"Alright, alright, let's head back," Yuan Ming said, and without waiting for their responses, he slapped his Storage Bag, collecting Hua Zhi and Vajra inside.
He then shook his head, boarded his Magic Artifact, and flew towards Little Lake City.
...
Several months later.
Outside Little Lake City, a constant drizzle soaked the earth, and thunder rumbled across the sky like waves.
As ever, the weather was gloomy. However, today, apart from the dark clouds, Magic Artifacts streaked through the sky, landing at the city gates like falling stars, each transforming into one cultivator after another in various garments.
Under the azure protective shield, Little Lake City appeared exceptionally lively today.
The streets were bustling with more cultivators than usual. Amidst the crowds, many cultivators in light blue robes with high towers painted on the back regulated the flow of people, maintaining order within the city.
They were the City Lord's personal guards, usually only responsible for guarding the City Lord Mansion and seldom seen by the residents. However, on such important days they would appear on the streets to fill in for the city guards and to display the majesty and order of the City Lord Mansion.
Along the streets, various shops decorated their fronts with blooming flowers and simultaneously issued discount signs—half price here, forty percent off there—with each appearing exceptionally generous. However, few noticed that the original price listed above their discounted rates seemed significantly higher than usual.

chapters.title: Chapter 308 - 285: Recruitment
chapters.content:
In Little Lake City on such a bustling day, the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop naturally opened its doors early, and hung a sign outside for rewarding customers. Not only were the prices significantly discounted, but even the normally limited quantities of Spirit Incense had doubled. Still, by the time noon had not yet arrived, those limited-purchase incense sticks had all sold out.
However, the stream of customers attracted by reputation did not cease, keeping Hu Tu and Mu Yang busy for quite a while until around the start of noon, when visitor numbers finally began to dwindle, allowing them some time to tally the accounts and rest.
After seeing a customer out, Hu Tu turned to see there weren't many customers left in the shop, thus not requiring his attention. He decided to lean against the doorpost to take a brief respite.
As he looked at the lively scene on the street, along with the incoming and outgoing patrons, his eyes couldn't help but reveal a tinge of envy.
"What's the matter, do you also want to go out for a stroll?" Suddenly, Yuan Ming's voice entered Hu Tu's ears, startling him.
"The shop is busiest right now; how dare I neglect it," Hu Tu quickly waved his hands in dismissal.
"Heh heh, you all work hard day and night around the year; now that the city is celebrating a grand event, it's time you got some time off. Here's what we'll do: for the next couple of days, you and Mu Yang will take turns on duty each afternoon, leaving just one person in the shop. I'll also give you this month's wage in advance, go buy whatever you wish," Yuan Ming said.
Hu Tu was overjoyed, and he quickly gave thanks with his hands clasped, but then his expression became concerned, and he spoke in a low voice:
"Boss, I've heard from the customers who come to the shop recently that Chang Chun Temple seems to have sent Core Formation Elders to hunt down Pu Zhengqing."
Having dealt with cultivators in the shop over the years, his familiarity with the Cultivation World had grown, so he had also heard about Yuan Ming's enmity with the Chang Chun Temple.
Now that Core Formation Cultivators from Chang Chun Temple had come to Little Lake City, Hu Tu couldn't help but worry for Yuan Ming.
"You needn't worry about this matter. No one in the city knows I am the hidden owner of the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop; Chang Chun Temple won't trace it back to you," Yuan Ming said.
"You misunderstand, boss; I'm concerned for your safety," Hu Tu quickly demonstrated his loyalty.
His current position, even his first steps on the Immortal Path, could be said to be entirely thanks to Yuan Ming's support. Only if Yuan Ming was well, would he be well too.
"I am well aware of what I am doing; if you manage the shop well, that is a great help to me," Yuan Ming nodded.
He then instructed Hu Tu on a few more things before turning around and leaving the shop.
The Tianxiang Auction, as a triennial grand event, always attracts a large number of cultivators from different countries each time it is held.
Not everyone can acquire their desired items at the auction, so at this time each year, some customers come with loads of Spirit Stones and leave with an abundance of magic treasures and elixirs.
This coming and going has enabled other shops in the city to spot business opportunities, throwing out discount signs time after time. Those unable to find their desired items at the auction can't resist buying one or two things when they see this.
Even some cultivators without invitations to the Tianxiang Auction come to the city during the event, just to catch this rare discount festival.
Yuan Ming weaved through the crowd and quickly stepped onto the bridge spanning the city's lake, arriving at the central White Jade Square on the lake's heart.
The crystal tower in the center of the square shone brightly as usual. Yuan Ming looked up at it for a moment before walking towards it.
In front of the tower, two cultivators in trusted aide uniforms stood guard at the main door, one on the left and one on the right. The spiritual energy fluctuated around their bodies, revealing they were both at the early stages of Foundation Establishment.
Yuan Ming approached them and took out an invitation from his bosom, handing it over.
The trusted aides didn't inspect it and simply stepped aside to clear the way.
"Fellow Daoist, please enter. Before the auction officially starts, you can browse freely inside the building, except for the main auction venue. If you need assistance or have any questions, you can consult other patrolling trusted aides within the building," one of the trusted aides advised.
Hearing the reminder from the Foundation Establishment trusted aide, Yuan Ming put away his invitation, nodded, and passed through the doors into the tower.
His view broadened instantly, revealing an extremely grand hall with a massive column standing in the center, stretching all the way to the ceiling.
Dozens of suspended walkways branched out from the colossal column, connecting it with various floors. Standing at the entrance and looking up, it was like a giant ancient tree without leaves, its branches supporting the whole structure.
Yuan Ming then surveyed his surroundings and noticed that on the first floor, besides the giant column, there were neatly arranged wooden stalls. Some already had owners displaying items for sale, while others were still vacant.
He stopped a passing trusted aide and after inquiring, he learned that the first floor was specifically reserved for cultivators who had the need to set up their own stalls. However, the cultivators were not required to hawk their wares themselves; the Tianxiang Auction had arranged for professionals to sell on their behalf. If there were any incidents of lost items, the losses would be fully compensated.
Walking among the stalls, Yuan Ming noticed that the goods for sale varied in quality, and most of the stalls were mainly buying rather than selling. He soon lost interest and approached the giant column.
Only when he approached did he realize that at the very bottom of the pillar, there were many small doors, each with a spirit ladder installed within them, just like the ones he had seen in the teahouse. However, the spirits here were already prefitted with spirit stones in the formations painted on the walls, and they were also inscribed with numbers to indicate the floors.
Yuan Ming entered the spirit ladder and pressed the spirit stone labeled with the number 'two'. Soon, the spirit ladder began to slowly ascend within the huge pillar, bringing him to an aerial walkway that led to the second floor.
It was only at this moment that Yuan Ming discovered that, aside from the first floor, the other levels of the high building seemed to be constructed in a circular shape, allowing one to choose between using the spirit ladder or walking on the aerial walkways to move between them.
Unlike the first floor, the second floor was lined with large display stands against the walls, each styled in a distinct fashion that seemed to carry a strong sense of regional and Sect identity.
To the left of Yuan Ming was a display stand themed with lush flowers and greenery, with tender green vines climbing every corner of the platform. On the walls, blossoms the size of a human head flourished in pink, their centers covered by round glass shields. Suspended within these shields were various elixirs emitting a faint glow, appearing quite novel.
Curious, Yuan Ming walked over and discovered that the display stand belonged to Shengye Sect. There were many Shengye Sect disciples milling about, and Luo Xing'er was among them.For a smoother reading experience, visit MV&LEMPYR.
At that moment, she was not dressed in the attire of a Shengye Sect disciple but was wearing a carefully tailored light green dress. The dress flared out like lotus leaves in a pond, while a gauzy ribbon wound around her slender waist. From the end of the ribbon hung a piece of turquoise jade, partially concealed within the folds of her dress, creating an impression of a small boat in a lotus pond.
Upon hearing someone approach, Luo Xing'er quickly looked up, and upon seeing Yuan Ming, a look of joy spread across her face. She trotted over and leaned in close to Yuan Ming,
"Cous... Oh, it's Senior Hagon! Are you here to attend the Tianxiang Auction too?"
Yuan Ming nodded and glanced around the stand, "I happen to have an invitation and thought I'd take a look. What are you selling at this stand?"
"These are elixirs developed by the uncles in our Sect through the study of ancient formulas. If Senior Hagon is interested, let me introduce them to you," Luo Xing'er said.
Just as Yuan Ming was about to decline, he suddenly heard someone behind him ask,
"Are you Hagon?"
Turning around, he saw a kindly old man standing there, with white hair and beard, and a face beaming with smiles, his eyes crinkled into lines.
Behind the old man followed several Foundation Establishment cultivators, all wearing the same clothing. Yuan Ming even recognized a few of them; they were the Chang Chun Temple cultivators he had seen at the meeting with Lu Shen in the Loose Cultivation Association.
Luo Xing'er also recognized these people, and her whole body stiffened instantaneously, her hand clutching Yuan Ming's arm tense with nerves.
Yuan Ming smiled and patted the back of Luo Xing'er's hand, pulling his arm away and giving her a reassuring look, before he cupped his hands and inquired,
"Indeed, I am Hagon. May I ask who the senior before me is?"
The old man, a Core Formation cultivator, responded with a smile,
"I am Zuo Qinghui, an elder of Chang Chun Temple. I'm here to eradicate the Evil Path Soul Cultivator Pu Zhengqing. Our Sect disciples here have mentioned your name before, and we planned to contact you through Shengye Sect, but I didn't expect to encounter you here."
"Senior Zuo is too kind. What brings you looking for me?" Yuan Ming asked.
"It's nothing serious, I just wanted to ask you about the details of your encounter with Pu Zhengqing. But now that I've met you, you appear much younger than I imagined, and to be capable of defeating the strong while at the early stages of Foundation Establishment, such talent is wasted on a Loose Cultivator. Would you consider joining Chang Chun Temple to help eradicate Pu Zhengqing?" Zuo Qinghui said.
"Senior flatters me with his generous offer, and I'm greatly honored. However, I'm used to being undisciplined and do not wish to join any Sect for the time being, I hope Senior understands," Yuan Ming said.
As soon as these words were spoken, Zuo Qinghui had not yet responded, but someone behind him immediately showed anger.
"Hagon, think it through. So many people wish to join our Chang Chun Temple but find no doorway in, even if they plead. If you refuse today, don't regret it later."
Yuan Ming remained unmoved, not even casting a glance at the speaker, his gaze still lingering on Zuo Qinghui.
Despite the disciples behind him showing different reactions, Zuo Qinghui did not display any annoyance, still smiling warmly,
"Perhaps you, as a Loose Cultivator, think that joining our Sect might lead to being ostracized. You don't have to worry about that. I invite you not just to recruit talent, but more importantly because I see potential in you, and I wish to find a Closed-door Disciple for myself. Should you agree to this, you will be my disciple, Zuo Qinghui, from now on, and no one within the Sect will dare to trouble you."
Hearing Zuo Qinghui's words, his disciples were all surprised, while the Shengye Sect disciples nearby also murmured in shock and envy.
However, Yuan Ming's stance remained firm, "I already have a master and have no intention of switching allegiances, please forgive me, Senior."
At this, even the smile on Zuo Qinghui's face slightly faded, and the disciples of Chang Chun Temple behind him looked somewhat angry.

chapters.title: Chapter 309 - 286 Heavy Armor
chapters.content:
"Since that's the case, I won't press the matter any further. However, should you change your mind before the auction ends, you can still seek me out. If you leave the auction, I will offer no further opportunities. Please bear this in mind," Zuo Qinghui said. Having finished, he turned and led the disgruntled disciples of Chang Chun Temple away.
As soon as he had left, Luo Xing'er again grabbed Yuan Ming's arm, pouting as she said, "Senior, Chang Chun Temple is really overbearing. Won't they target you?"
Yuan Ming shook his head with a smile and said, "Don't worry, I just have to stay inside Little Lake City, and they can do nothing to me. They just want to use me to capture Pu Zhengqing, especially since I survived an encounter with him."
"What you say is true, but publicly refusing an elder of Chang Chun Temple and causing them to lose face will inevitably lead to trouble."
Hearing this voice, Luo Xing'er quickly turned around with delight, "Grandmaster Song."
Yuan Ming looked up to see a young female cultivator in a simple long dress with hairpins, her beauty delicate and emanating a natural fragrance. Even in plain clothes, her radiance was undeniable.
The title "Grandmaster" from Luo Xing'er immediately made Yuan Ming remember who she was: his grandmother's master, Song Huichong, the Core Formation elder of Shengye Sect. She was actually at least two to three hundred years old, yet somehow, she managed to keep her appearance so well preserved.
Yuan Ming immediately greeted her with a bow, but Song Huichong just waved her hand and asked, "I've heard from Fen Yun that you are a man of plans. Now that you've refused Fellow Daoist Zuo, you must already have a strategy in mind, right? You saved Xing'er and Xu Tian and have a deep connection with Fen Yun. It's only right that I help you. If there's anything you need, feel free to tell me."
"Thank you for your kind offer, Senior," Yuan Ming replied without hesitation. "Actually, there's something I'd like to ask for your assistance with. In my last fight with Pu Zhengqing, my magical tool was nearly destroyed, and now I wish to upgrade a high-grade magical tool of mine to top-grade. I wonder if you know any Artifact Refiners who could be recommended to me?"
Song Huichong pondered for a moment and nodded, "This is not particularly difficult, yet it's not easy either. The person I know has quite an eccentric personality. Even with my recommendation, it is up to you to persuade him to refine your tool."
"If you could give me a recommendation, Senior, I would be immensely grateful. Whether it is successful or not, I will remember your kindness," Yuan Ming said with excitement.
After making arrangements with Yuan Ming, Song Huichong floated away on her own, and Yuan Ming browsed the Shengye Sect's booth for a little longer before leaving the area as well.
Apart from the Shengye Sect, there were many booths set up by sects Yuan Ming had never heard of. He visited each one and was greatly enlightened by the experience.
When passing by a booth decorated with the image of a blazing Fire Phoenix, Yuan Ming happened to see two cultivators with whom he'd had a previous encounter.
Inside the booth, Di Chen was still wearing his red-patterned dragon robe. However, at that moment, he looked dejected, with his head hung low, resigned to his fate.
In front of him, Di Yue, with bright red lips and white teeth, hands on her hips, seemed to be scolding her brother.
Perhaps sensing Yuan Ming's gaze, Di Yue suddenly looked up in his direction and, recognizing him, her face momentarily lit up with joy.
"Fellow Daoist, over here!"
Di Yue motioned to Yuan Ming. Her black and red ponytail swayed slightly, giving off a spirited air. Hearing his sister's call, Di Chen stealthily raised his head to steal a glance at Yuan Ming.
Unlike his sister, Di Chen chose to ignore Yuan Ming outright. However, upon seeing the joy on his sister's face, his eyes shifted from confusion to wariness.
Seeing Di Yue's enthusiastic demeanor, Yuan Ming felt it would be rude to ignore her, so he approached the booth to stand before the Di siblings.
"Fellow Daoist, didn't I tell you to leave a message at the Five Elements Inn when you were in the city? Why haven't I heard from you for so long? I was worried you'd already left Thunder Continent. By the way, may I know your name?" Di Yue asked.
"Hagon," Yuan Ming responded with his usual alias.
"You are that Hagon? The one who repelled Pu Zhengqing?" Di Chen suddenly realized and asked.
Yuan Ming nodded, and Di Yue, surprised, said, "I never imagined it was Fellow Daoist Hagon. Then I must thank you for showing mercy before and leaving some face for my brother."
"Sister, why are you bringing up that again? You've mentioned it several times," Di Chen said, growing impatient.
Di Yue's eyebrows raised slightly in irritation, "I need to remind you because of your attitude. I don't know how many more people you will offend in the future!"
"It was just a spar. I didn't know at the time that you were the Hagon who had defeated Pu Zhengqing. I was thinking your demon was quite powerful. Last time I didn't use my full strength. Once things settle down here, let's spar outside the city. I want to see just how strong you really are, being someone who can defeat a Soul Cultivator!" Di Chen suddenly understood and excitedly readied himself as if itching to have a match with Yuan Ming.
But in the next moment, with a soft "slap," Di Yue gently smacked Di Chen on the head. She then turned to Yuan Ming, her face expressing an apology.
"I apologize, Fellow Daoist Hagon. My brother has been spoiled and loves to get into trouble, always eager for fights and sparring. Please, don't take his words to heart," she said.
Yuan Ming nodded, looking at Di Chen as he was reminded of Xiao Yao whom he had encountered in the Southern Border.
Di Yue apologized to Yuan Ming, then quickly switched back to a fierce demeanor, fiercely scolding Di Chen.
Di Chen seemed somewhat wronged, but under his sister's coercion, he reluctantly offered an apology to Yuan Ming.
Yuan Ming laughed it off generously, not really minding, however Di Yue then said, "Fellow Daoist Hagon, to show our sincerity, if you fancy anything at our Fire Sparrow Sect's booth today, I can offer you a 20% discount. Please don't refuse."
Upon hearing this, Di Chen was not pleased, yet he seemed to dare not refute Di Yue's offer. After a moment of hesitation, his eyes suddenly lit up.
"Sister, there's no need to trouble yourself. I happen to have a Protective Magical Device here that I don't need at the moment. I'd like to sell it, and offering it to Fellow Daoist Hagon as compensation would suffice."
With these words, he took out a wooden box as tall as a person from his Storage Ring and placed it onto the ground with a "thud," opening the door.
Seeing this, a hint of surprise flashed in Di Yue's eyes, while Yuan Ming curiously stepped forward to examine the magical artifact that Di Chen had brought out.
It was a full-body suit of armor crafted from fine steel, shiny as a mirror to the extend that it could reflect someone's image, and the joints appeared to have been specially treated to ensure flexibility without sacrificing much defensive capability.
This suit of armor was also a High-Grade Magical Artifact, engraved with three different runes. Yuan Ming recognized only one, which was the Complete Rune, even more prized than the Solid Rune.
With just this one rune, the armor's defensive capabilities could be increased by more than fifty percent. That such a precious item was being sold so readily, Yuan Ming couldn't help but feel sentimental about Di Chen's squandering.
The armor seemed overly heavy, however, and if one were to wear it during combat, it would be quite inconvenient for movement.
"How much for this thing?" Yuan Ming asked.
"Hehe, if Fellow Daoist Hagon likes it, then 2,000 Spirit Stones. Let's not become strangers over a transaction. Our Fire Sparrow Sect has some expertise in Artifact Refining, and the materials for this magical artifact were obtained with great effort by me personally. It's a pity I don't have much use for it myself, and I can't bear to let a treasure collect dust. If you like it, it's 2,000 Spirit Stones, no, 1,800." For some reason, Di Chen suddenly became rather polite.
Yuan Ming hesitated for a moment but, seeing the sincere look on Di Chen's face, and since he was in need of a top-grade defensive magical artifact, he decided to buy the armor, although it was a bit expensive at 1,800 Spirit Stones.
Just then, Di Yue abruptly interjected, "Wait, Ah Chen, which three runes did you use in refining this armor?"
"Naturally, the Solid, the Complete, and Avoiding Arrows," Di Chen replied with a slightly guilty smile.
Di Yue's brows furrowed sharply: "Are you sure it's the Solid Rune and not the Thousand Catties Rune? Is this armor supposed to be worn by people? With this weight pressing down, one will exhaust themselves first during a magical duel!"
Hearing this, Yuan Ming had an epiphany and smiled at Di Chen.
"Sister can't speak like that, but indeed, its defense is very strong, I've already tested it," Di Chen pretended to be aggrieved.

"You're clearly trying to deceive someone," said Di Yue, annoyed, as she glared at Di Chen, then turned to talk to Yuan Ming, "I apologize, Fellow Daoist Hagon. If you're in need of a high-grade defensive magical artifact, I can also refine a custom one just for you. This suit of armor is not suitable for you."
To her surprise, Yuan Ming shook his head, satisfied, patting the wooden box, "No need for that, I really like Brother Di Chen's magical artifact. Let's settle for 1,000 Spirit Stones, and let Di Chen take a bit more of a loss."
"Deal!" Di Chen immediately accepted, amazed that this Hagon was not only blind in appraising artifacts but also a spendthrift.
Yuan Ming didn't buy the armor to test his own strength but rather because his spirit pet Vajra could truly bear the title of Innate Divine Strength.
As Vajra was a practitioner of Body Cultivation, its physical strength was far superior to an ordinary person's. Now, with this suit of armor, there were probably very few who could break through its defenses.
The only regrettable point was that the design of the armor was based on a normal human structure, with only two arm guards. Before handing it over to Vajra, it would probably require some modifications to fit more appropriately.
Not wanting to bother with two tasks, Yuan Ming contemplated for a moment before suggesting, "Could this armor have two additional armholes added?"
Before Di Chen could reply, Di Yue took the initiative, "This is a simple task, leave it to me."
"That would be excellent, Fellow Daoist Di Yue. With such enthusiasm, I wouldn't dare to decline," Yuan Ming said.
"I won't hide the fact from you, there is another matter I wish to ask of you. My brother and I came to Little Lake City for two reasons: firstly, to attend the Tianxiang Auction, and secondly, to hire someone from the Scatter Alliance to travel through Zhao Country to the Northern Desert and investigate the case of missing disciples from our sect," said Di Yue.

chapters.title: Chapter 310 - 287: Puppet Master
chapters.content:
"Disconnected in the Northern Desert... Can Fellow Daoist Di Yue elaborate on that?" Yuan Ming inquired upon hearing this.
"About a year ago, the life plates of three Foundation Establishment disciples from our sect shattered simultaneously. The sect immediately dispatched people to investigate, but the leads they discovered were complex and convoluted. In the end, the only relatively clear conclusion they came to was that all three had been seen in Little Lake City. As the Tianxiang Auction was about to convene at that time, the sect dispatched a Core Formation elder along with some disciples, including myself, to come here and continue the investigation." Di Yue explained.
"Considering they were Foundation Establishment disciples, I don't think Pu Zhengqing should be too involved. Since you only found out that they'd been in Little Lake City, why did you go on to investigate the Northern Desert?" Yuan Ming thought of Sha Hao unconsciously but immediately dismissed it himself.
"After our thorough investigation, those three disciples only stayed in Little Lake City for a few days before heading to Zhao Country. Based on some other clues we discovered, we deduced that they most likely went to the Northern Desert in the end. I think Fellow Daoist Hagon is very suitable, could you help us investigate this matter? We will surely not treat you unfairly after the matter is resolved," Di Yue said.
"Since your sect has already dispatched a Core Formation elder to lead the investigation, why then recruit me, a Foundation Establishment cultivator, to participate?" Yuan Ming tilted his head and considered for a moment before posing a non-committal question.
"The journey to the Northern Desert may involve many uncertainties. It is better to have fewer but more capable companions. Fellow Daoist Hagon, having defeated Pu Zhengqing, is already a rare adversary amongst your peers. If you could lend us your aid, it would be adding wings to a tiger," Di Yue said.
"To be frank, for the time being, I am unable to make myself available and fear that I can't be of assistance to Fellow Daoist Di Yue," Yuan Ming pondered for a moment and then shook his head.
Di Yue's expression showed disappointment, but her attitude towards Yuan Ming remained unchanged, "No matter, I will have the armor improved in the next few days. Please leave a contact method, so I can have someone deliver it when it's ready."
"Then please send it to Qingmu Building, say it's for Hagon to pick up temporarily," Yuan Ming nodded and provided a location.
With Hagon's identity currently being quite conspicuous, to avoid trouble, it was best not to get involved with the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop.
Di Yue didn't seem to mind and mentioned that Yuan Ming could retrieve the armor in no more than seven days.
Afterwards, Yuan Ming exchanged pleasantries for a bit longer before turning to leave.
Initially, after hearing that the Fire Sparrow Sect was adept at Artifact Refining, he had intended to ask for their help in refining a top-grade magical tool. However, first, Song Huichong had already agreed to introduce someone for that purpose, and second, he had declined Di Yue's invitation, and she had agreed to optimize his Heavy Armor for him; he did not want to owe any more favors.
...
After leaving the Fire Sparrow Sect's booth, Yuan Ming continued to casually stroll around the building.
Soon, time quickly passed, and a clear bell began to toll suddenly within the building.
This was closely followed by a powerful voice, echoing within the tall structure.
"The time has come. The Tianxiang Auction is about to begin. Please ride the spirit ladder to the main auction venue," it announced.
Upon hearing this, Yuan Ming quickly made his way to the spirit ladder along with the crowd, and before long, he was transported to an open hall.
In the hall, several of the City Lord's personal guards were stationed at the exit of the spirit ladder, politely requesting invitation cards from each cultivator who arrived.
Yuan Ming handed his invitation card to one of the guards, who briefly examined it and then handed back a token to Yuan Ming.
"This token will be needed later for bidding. Please keep it safe and remember to return it when you leave. Next, please walk north and take the spirit ladder there to the venue," the guard instructed.
Yuan Ming pocketed the token and followed the guard's directions, boarding another spirit ladder.
As the ladder ascended, Yuan Ming lost track of time, and before he knew it, twinkling stars began to appear before his eyes.
Soon after, a massive domed hall suddenly revealed itself before him.
The floor of the hall was irregular, generally resembling a large bowl, towering on the sides with a depression in the middle.
Currently standing at the very edge and thus the highest point of the hall, Yuan Ming looked down a long flight of steps leading to the deepest point at the center of the hall.
There, another elevated platform stood, though it was empty and bare at the moment.
Along the corridor, elaborately carved wooden chairs were arranged in a stepped configuration from top to bottom. The chairs were not too close to each other, with a gap between each one.
Yuan Ming glanced around and casually picked a seat with a good view to sit down.
Just after he settled in, Yuan Ming looked up inadvertently and suddenly noticed that above the numerous seats, there were quite a few separate platforms. Not only were there seats on these platforms, but there was also a small table with fruits on it. Beside the table, maids in plain long gowns holding teacups were attending to guests. The treatment was several times better than the seats below.
"Tsk tsk tsk, if only one day, I could also sit over there, how nice that would be."
When Yuan Ming heard the voice and turned around, he saw a rotund cultivator with a figure so chubby he seemed to have no neck, taking a seat next to him.
The plump cultivator, noticing Yuan Ming looking over, immediately grinned and gave Yuan Ming a polite hand gesture: "I am Wang Chongshan, the Alliance Hierarch of the Mountain Flipping Alliance. May I ask how Fellow Daoist is called?"
"Hagon," Yuan Ming nodded, returning the gesture.
Wang Chongshan's eyes sparkled: "So it is Fellow Daoist Hagon, I've heard much about you. With your status, you should qualify for a private booth. Why are you sitting here?"
"This is my first time attending the Tianxiang Auction and I was not sure how to enter a private booth," Yuan Ming admitted candidly.
"Oh, I see now. Haven't you joined a Scatter Alliance yet, Fellow Daoist Hagon? The private booth seats at the Tianxiang Auction, besides those reserved for the big sects, the rest are given to well-known Scatter Alliance Hierarchs and Core Formation Cultivators. I assumed that with your strength, you must have already been recruited by some Alliance and would accompany its Hierarch to sit in a private booth at the auction. I did not expect you to be unaffiliated," Wang Chongshan said with sudden realization.
"I do not like being constrained, which is why I haven't considered joining any forces," Yuan Ming replied.
"I must say something about that, for you seem to misunderstand Scatter Alliances. They're quite different from sects and cultivation forces. Although a Scatter Alliance is a power in its own right, it doesn't impose constraints on its members. They are only called together for missions. Once a task is complete and rewards are distributed, members are free to leave. You can even be part of several Scatter Alliances simultaneously," Wang Chongshan explained.
"If that's so lax, then what is the point of forming a Scatter Alliance?" Yuan Ming asked.
"Heh, think about it, Fellow Daoist Hagon. When a bunch of strangers come together for a mission, there's no cooperation and one must be cautious of stabs in the back. But with a Scatter Alliance, the longer it has been established, the more familiar members become with each other. Not only does this improve their coordination, but resource distribution and rewards are also fair and just. Most importantly, an Alliance has a reputation to uphold; they won't take money and not complete the job. Hence, most cultivators and sects prefer to entrust tasks to reliable Alliances directly, rather than posting them. Only tasks with low rewards or ones that don't require many people are posted publicly," Wang Chongshan elaborated.This content is presented by *.
"There's also the situation where an Alliance accepts a task but doesn't have enough manpower to mobilize immediately. They will post tasks externally to recruit other Loose Cultivators, but the rewards for such tasks, set by the Alliance, are generally lower than what the Alliance was originally offered," Wang Chongshan added.
Yuan Ming, having roughly understood this during his time in the Southern Border, felt reassured by the explanation from a cultivator of the Central Plains, showing his acknowledgment with a salute to Wang Chongshan.
While he engaged in conversation with Wang Chongshan, other cultivators also entered the venue, and the seats gradually filled up, with many also taking places in the booths above.
Soon, the melodious sound of strings started playing, and the noisy venue gradually quieted down.
Under the gaze of many cultivators, a young woman wearing a goose-yellow long robe with fair skin and beautiful looks ascended from the platform at the center of the venue.
Yuan Ming widened his eyes at the sight of the woman, not because he recognized her identity, but due to the obvious joints and seams on her body.
Though she appeared lifelike and seemed like a real person, the cultivators present could tell that she was merely a puppet powered by Spirit Stones.
"First and foremost, I thank all the seniors for attending this Tianxiang Auction. My name is Gui Jiu, and I am the host of this auction. As you can see, I am a Spirit Stone Puppet. I assure you there will be no mistakes during the auction, a guarantee personally upheld by City Lord Lü, without any falsehood."
Having said this, Gui Jiu bowed to the audience with clear and logical speech. If not for her joints, no one would ever think that such a lively woman was just a puppet powered by Spirit Stones.
On the platform, Gui Jiu continued to introduce the auction rules.
"This auction will be conducted in an anonymous bidding format. If Fellow Daoists are interested in an item, you may make an offer using the Token distributed upon entrance. After receiving a signal, I will announce the highest bid to you all. If there are identical bids, I will clarify accordingly. Without further delay, please have a look at the first item."
As soon as Gui Jiu finished speaking, a square stone platform slowly rose behind her.
She took a camphor wood box from a stone stand padded with gold goosedown, opened it, and displayed the Jade Scroll inside to everyone.
"This Jade Scroll contains the Core Technique of Zhao Country's Fire Origin Sect, the 'Red Fire Heart Method.' As you all may be aware, the Fire Origin Sect was once as renowned as the Five Thunder Sect in Zhao Country. Regrettably, after the passing of their founding master, no one ascended to the Nascent Soul stage, and the sect ceased to be part of the first-class hierarchy. Nevertheless, the 'Red Fire Heart Method,' being the core cultivation method once practiced by the founding master, has not diminished in value. This piece offered by our shop is the complete 'Red Fire Heart Method,' intact in every word, even including the Core Formation stage method. Possessing such a technique could completely transform a small sect, allowing disciples with a Fire Spiritual Root to save at least fifty years of detours, dramatically cutting down on cultivation time and resources. The starting bid is merely twenty thousand Spirit Stones. Fellow Daoists, please place your bids freely."

chapters.title: Chapter 311 - 288 Water Crown Tree
chapters.content:
Yuan Ming was astonished after hearing Gui Jiu's introduction. He had not expected that the auction had just begun and the "Red Fire Heart Method," a core cultivation technique of a sect, was already up for bid.
Yuan Ming recalled that when he had possessed Wulu, he had seen him accept a mission from his clan to steal the "Red Fire Heart Method."
And Wulu had succeeded!
At the same time, he began to worry for Wulu. Although he did not know much about the Fire Origin Sect, it was at least a sect with a prestigious heritage. Now, one of its core techniques was being openly auctioned off at the Tianxiang Auction. Wasn't Wulu's family afraid of bringing disaster upon themselves?
As he was thinking this, suddenly, within the private box, an elderly man in brocaded clothes with a ruddy complexion stood up, bowed to the entire audience, and announced loudly,
"I am Luo Tian, an elder of the Fire Origin Sect. Unfortunately, not long ago, a traitor emerged from our sect and stole our sect's technique to sell at auction. I beg my fellow daoists to do me the honor of not bidding. Our sect will offer a token of appreciation afterward."
"Heh heh, no wonder the Tianxiang Auction decided to use anonymous bidding this time. They were preparing to trap the Fire Origin Sect. This is going to be quite the spectacle," Wang Chongshan chuckled mischievously, looking delighted by the trouble brewing, and turned to Yuan Ming to say,
"I have heard that the lord of Little Lake City, before advancing to the Nascent Soul Stage, had some grievances with this Fire Origin Sect. The specifics are now unclear, but it is said that he was instrumental in the rapid decline of the Fire Origin Sect. It is also him behind the scenes of the Tianxiang Auction. He purposely placed Fire Origin Sect's technique as the first item to stir up the atmosphere and to spite the Fire Origin Sect. However, I estimate that in the end, it will simply cost the Fire Origin Sect a lot of money, but the technique probably won't end up in others' hands. If other sects were harmed in a similar way, the city lord's days would not be pleasant."
"Based on what Fellow Daoist Wang said, it seems likely that it was the city lord who sent someone to steal the technique," Yuan Ming intentionally asked.
"Most likely. But if it really came to an investigation, it would definitely have nothing to do with the city lord," Wang Chongshan said. "Fellow Daoist Hagon, you might not see this often, but whether in the Central Plains or elsewhere, there is never a shortage of people willing to do the dirty work. It all trickles down through layers of outsourcing until the person who actually did the job probably doesn't even know what they were handling. Even if they were caught, they couldn't reveal who masterminded it."
On the other hand, Luo Tian's declaration seemed to have little effect. The price called by Gui Jiu kept climbing almost without pause, and Luo Tian's expression grew darker and more unpleasant, even as he continued to bid.
"…Twenty-one thousand four hundred spirit stones, is there anyone willing to bid higher?" After Gui Jiu called out another price, she surveyed the room and, after waiting for a moment, nodded her head, closed the wooden box, and placed it back on the stone platform.
Seeing this, Luo Tian let out a sigh of relief, immediately turned, and left the private box, clearly unable to bear staying any longer.
Twenty-one thousand four hundred spirit stones for a technique that could be cultivated up to the Core Formation Stage, Yuan Ming did not know whether this price was expensive or not, but for the Fire Origin Sect, no amount of spirit stones would justify letting their technique spread outside.
However, once the sect bought their own technique at a price far beyond normal, and the Tianxiang Auction ended and this news got out, surely many would laugh aloud.
City Lord Luu of Little Lake City, with this move, orchestrated a blatant scheme, trampling both the prestige and substance of the Fire Origin Sect underfoot, while his Nascent Soul Stage strength made the Fire Origin Sect dare not speak out.
In the Cultivation World, everything still ultimately depended on strength.
Yuan Ming sighed about the situation and turned his attention back to the auction.
"Next up is the second item of this auction, three pieces of Moon Cold Iron, taken from…"
On stage, Gui Jiu presented one distinctive item after another, including both spiritual materials and elixirs as well as Magic Tools Talismans. Regardless of the item, she promoted them extravagantly, as if not buying would be a regret in one's life.
Under her leadership, many items sold for at least twenty percent higher than usual prices. Although it was an anonymous auction with no open call for bids, the atmosphere grew increasingly heated, surprising Yuan Ming.
Suddenly, Yuan Ming began to notice something.
Every time Gui Jiu quoted a price, the tone of her voice slightly varied, sounding as if different people were bidding. Moreover, it seemed that special magic artifacts were installed in the auction hall, continuously playing string music, connecting Gui Jiu's voice seamlessly, leaving no gaps and clearly interfering with normal thinking, making the atmosphere even more intense.This chapter was originally posted on *.
However, Yuan Ming was not swept away by impulse. He occasionally bid on a few items of interest, but only up to a point. Once the price exceeded his expectations, he would immediately abstain.
By that point in the auction, he had not purchased a single item.
However, as Gui Jiu picked up another item from the rising stone platform, Yuan Ming suddenly sat up straight.
"The next item up for bid comes from the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop in Little Lake City."
"These three sticks of incense I hold are the seductive scents secretly produced by the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop. The materials are extremely rare, and most notably, once lit, there are no fluctuations of Spiritual Energy at all, completely silent and traceless."
As he said this, there was a light gasp from the audience, and some began to whisper among themselves.
"Just by inhaling the smoke of this incense, even a Foundation Establishment Cultivator will fall into unconsciousness in a short time, completely at the mercy of others. The only drawback of this incense is that it performs poorly in open areas. How to use it specifically will depend on everyone's innovation. At the request of the owner of the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop, this auction will sell only three sticks, with a starting bid of one hundred Spirit Stones for each. Due to limited materials, this seductive scent is not available for sale in the shop."
No sooner had Gui Jiu finished explaining, his expression shifted and he immediately said, "Good, a Fellow Daoist has already bid one hundred and ten Spirit Stones, I wonder... It seems many Fellow Daoists are interested in this incense. The price has now gone up to one hundred and twenty Spirit Stones, no, one hundred and fifty Spirit Stones. Any more bids?"
Listening to the constantly changing prices mentioned by Gui Jiu, a smile gradually appeared on Yuan Ming's face.
Soon, the three sticks of seductive scent Yuan Ming offered were all sold at a price higher than expected. After deducting the commission, he netted nearly six hundred Spirit Stones in income.
The seductive incense Yuan Ming offered for auction had been tried and tested in real combat; now, by putting it up for auction, he was also testing the value of his product. Earning an extra batch of Spirit Stones was secondary; more importantly, he aimed to establish a strong reputation for the Xuanhua Spirit Incense Shop while cultivators from all around were gathered in the city.
After the auction of Yuan Ming's Spirit Incense, Gui Jiu, without missing a beat, presented the next item up for auction.
"The next item for auction is perhaps the most unique one of this auction."
As he spoke, Gui Jiu opened the wooden box storing the item and displayed its contents.
Lying in the box was a green wooden post. Although it had been cut, it showed no signs of decay or wilting. On one side of the stump, several small tender buds of varying sizes were growing, emitting a faint glow and appearing quite magical.
"This piece of spirit wood was once parasitized by five Yimu Purple Mushrooms, which co-exist with the spirit wood. Not only are these mushrooms exceptionally medicinal on their own, but the spirit wood that hosts them also undergoes special changes, imbued with vigorous life force. The Yimu Purple Mushrooms have been removed, and after special treatment, this piece of wood is an excellent top-grade spiritual material, especially suitable for refining Wood Magic Tools. Most notably, after appraisal, this is a piece of thousand-year level spirit wood," Gui Jiu elaborated non-stop.
This was the first appearance of thousand-year level spiritual material in this auction, and at this point, all the cultivators in the hall turned their eyes to the item Gui Jiu held, their eager gazes almost wanting to swallow the wooden post whole.
Just then, from a private room, an old man's hoarse voice rang out, "I'm afraid that the introduction to this item is not complete, is it? If I'm not mistaken, this piece of spirit wood comes from a thousand-year-old Water Crown Tree, containing conflicting Water and Wood Spiritual Energies, making it impossible to serve as the main material for refining magic tools!"
"Senior Song indeed has sharp eyes. However, this spirit wood, having endured a millennium, even if it cannot serve as the main material for refining, if treated specially, as an auxiliary material during the upgrade of top-grade magical tools, it still holds certain value. And with everyone here being elites from various fields, perhaps there could be more ingenious uses yet to be discovered. Hence, the starting bid for this item is set at three thousand Spirit Stones, which is quite fair," Gui Jiu frankly admitted and then quickly announced the starting bid after an explanation.
After hearing her words, the cultivators in the hall regained their calm and began to discuss among themselves.
Through the discussions of the people, Yuan Ming learned that the Water Crown Tree was an extremely special type of spirit wood, just as the old man with the surname Song in the private room had described it. It possessed both Water and Wood Spiritual Energies, constantly in conflict with each other, making it unsuitable as the main material for refining tools no matter its thousand-year cultivation; the refining process often resulted in easy failure, and its medicinal value wasn't high either. Using thousand-year-old spirit wood as an auxiliary material was too luxurious when other substitutes were available.
As the chatter in the crowd gradually dwindled, Gui Jiu began the auction, but this time unexpectedly met with a cold response, with no bids for a long time.
"It seems that the Fellow Daoists here aren't very interested in this piece of spirit wood, no matter, there are still more treasures waiting for everyone. So I declare this auction... wait a moment, someone has bid three thousand Spirit Stones! Three thousand Spirit Stones for the first time, are there any other bids? Three thousand Spirit Stones for the second time..." Just as Gui Jiu was about to declare the auction a failure, she suddenly paused, then spoke.
However, Gui Jiu's last efforts were in vain. Except for the unknown cultivator who bid at the last moment, everyone else watched indifferently, with no further bids.
Eventually, this thousand-year-old Water Crown Tree spirit wood was sold for the base price of three thousand Spirit Stones.

chapters.title: Chapter 312 - 289: Auctioning Oneself
chapters.content:
When Yuan Ming heard the final price of the auction item, a faint smile appeared on his face as he shifted his palm away slightly from the bidding token he had just used.
This bidding token was a specially refined magic artifact. By infusing it with a bit of mana, one could trigger a bid without any visible sign on its surface, thus protecting the bidder's privacy.
To many, 3,000 spirit stones might not be considered high for a thousand-year-old spirit wood, but it was no small sum either—almost the entire fortune of an ordinary Foundation Establishment cultivator, enough to exchange for at least two top-grade magical tools.
To most people, the Water Crown Tree spirit wood seemed quite superfluous. Most cultivators, after some consideration, would not make a bid.
For Yuan Ming, however, he did not mind whether the spiritual energy contained in the Water Crown Tree spirit wood conflicted with others. As long as the wood was old enough, he could use it for incense making, which would significantly increase the duration of spirit incense attachment.
Yuan Ming estimated that if this spirit wood were of another wood attribute spirit material, it would be among the best choices for a Core Formation cultivator to refine a magic treasure embryo. If it were auctioned, he might have to spend over ten thousand spirit stones to secure it, and it might even be priceless in the outside world.
The price now was merely a month or so of profits from his Spiritual Incense Shop, so purchasing it was clearly a gain for him.
Finally having acquired something, Yuan Ming felt excited and started looking forward to the upcoming auction items with renewed anticipation.
As the auction gradually neared its end, Gui Jiu finally brought out the first item of the auction that could truly be considered the finale.
"Speaking of formations, do you think of the Chen Kun Sect of Chu Country first, or Red Lotus Island of the Southern Border? The debate over who is the top in formations has been ongoing without a clear conclusion. However, if we talk about which formation shines the most against Foundation Establishment cultivators, there's no other answer than Master Xiao Zhang from Red Lotus Island with his Gentle Wind Illusion Demon Formation."
"Today, our shop is fortunate to have received a consignment from Master Xiao Zhang to auction, and I am proud to introduce his latest creation—the Melt Gold Break Water Array."
"This array integrates offense and defense. Once deployed, anyone approaching with a magic artifact will trigger a fire that incinerates, and any spell cast will summon a flood of weak water. The fire melts the artifact, and the water absorbs spiritual power, hence the name 'Melt Gold Break Water.'"
"After testing by our shop, once trapped inside this formation, even a Core Formation cultivator would find themselves hindered and need to expend some effort to escape, let alone an ordinary Foundation Establishment cultivator. The value of this item is self-evident. Now, let the bidding for this formation start at 3,000 spirit stones."
Before Gui Jiu could finish speaking, some eager cultivators began to bid immediately, driving the price sharply upward. It quickly surpassed five thousand and was heading straight for eight thousand.
Listening to the introduction, Yuan Ming felt somewhat tempted. However, after a second thought, considering he already possessed two sets of formations and was wealthy, focusing on acquiring a top-grade magical tool without securing one yet could potentially affect his ability to purchase a top-grade magical tool later.
Eventually, the Melt Gold Break Water Array was successfully auctioned off for 11,000 spirit stones, heating up the atmosphere of the venue even further.
Capitalizing on this excitement, Gui Jiu swiftly brought out another major work.
"The next item up for auction is personally refined by Master Xu Xinyang of Zhao Country — the top-grade magical tool called Flowing Cloud Ruler. It is engraved with the four runes: Rapid, Concealment, indestructibility, and immense force. Once activated, it moves incredibly fast, appearing without a trace, and its attack is powerful. It can easily destroy any magical tool below top-grade and even hold its own against other top-grade magical tools."
"You should all be aware of Master Xu Xinyang's caliber. To date, he has crafted a total of eleven top-grade magical tools, each of exceptional quality, eight of which have even been upgraded to magic treasures. The starting bid for this Flowing Cloud Ruler is six thousand."
Below, Yuan Ming glanced at the immaculate jade ruler in Gui Jiu's hands, his eyes reflecting a conflicted expression.
This magical tool greatly suited his tastes, yet in actual use, its effects were quite similar to those of the Black Needle, both emphasizing stealth and surprise.
Therefore, if he purchased this top-grade magical tool, his own Black Needle, if continued to be refined, would result in possessing two top-grade magic treasures upon success.
While he contemplated this, the bidding announced by Gui Jiu had already soared to ten thousand spirit stones and looked to increase further. Suddenly, a brawny middle-aged man with a rugged appearance stood up in one of the boxes overhead. Without even using mana, his voice projected to every corner of the venue.
"Among those coveting this treasure, if anyone has thousand-year-old spirit wood and is willing to trade, based on the current bid of 8,600 spirit stones, we'll calculate the exchange rate by deducting the value of the thousand-year-old spirit wood; refund the excess spirit stones and make up any shortfall. This magic tool will be yours."
Yuan Ming looked up to see this man with a tiger-like face, his round eyes as wide as bells and a mouth as broad as a palm. His black hair stood erect, blending with the bushy sideburns on his cheeks, giving him a fierce appearance.
From his words, it seemed this was Xu Xinyang as mentioned by Gui Jiu.
At that moment, Xu Xinyang's ears flickered as if someone was transmitting a message to him. Soon after, a satisfied smile spread across his face.
"Indeed, Fellow Daoist's bid is very reasonable. What was his name, Gui Jiu right? There's no need to auction this item anymore, quickly bring out the next item for auction," he said.
On the stage, Gui Jiu looked completely bewildered, frozen on the spot as if such a sudden interruption to her auctioning process was not part of her plan, causing a stir among the cultivators present.
This chapter was uploaded by the team at *.
Gui Jiu remained motionless there until after seven or eight breaths, when she seemed to receive instructions from the host of the venue, and regained her composure. She then said, "As Senior Xu has instructed, we will naturally follow. Let us continue with the next item."
As Gui Jiu spoke, she suddenly stepped down from the podium and stood in the center of the stage, and beside her, eight figures slowly rose.
Just as everyone present was somewhat confused, not knowing what this final item was, Gui Jiu continued:
"This second to last item for auction, as you all can see, consists of spirit stone puppets. My siblings and I are all produced by the Hundred Machine Sect, totaling nine units, all made from superior materials and each possessing the strength comparable to the Qi Refining Early Stage."
"Importantly, each of us possesses basic spiritual intelligence. As long as supplied with enough spirit stones, we can perform various tasks under the control of our master," she added.
"Nine spirit stone puppets, the starting bid is four thousand five hundred spirit stones. With us, you can assist the master in related work, and also have some self-protection capabilities while ensuring the master's secrets are kept," said Gui Jiu, suddenly giving a playful smile and winking spiritedly at the audience, adding, "In the Southern Border, even a Qi Refinement stage slave costs three thousand spirit stones, we are indeed a bargain."
This speech of Gui Jiu "auctioning herself" caught everyone by surprise, and the atmosphere in the venue took on a strange vibe. While those present knew these were puppets from the Hundred Machine Sect, there was still a sensation as if cultivators were being auctioned as slaves.
Seeing this, Yuan Ming's interest was also piqued; these puppets had such initial spiritual intelligence, and if he could buy them back and teach them the Incense Making Skill, he wouldn't have to worry about producing incense in his shop anymore.
However, he soon abandoned this idea, mainly because the security of his rented cottage wasn't guaranteed. If someone seized the puppets, his incense-making secrets would also become known to others, and that would be a loss not worth the gain.
If necessary in the future, he could directly purchase them from the Hundred Machine Sect. For now, his spirit stones were better spent on top-grade magical tools.
In the end, the nine spirit stone puppets were sold for prices ranging from five thousand to around six thousand spirit stones each.
After the auction was complete, the other eight spirit stone puppets descended back down, leaving only Gui Jiu alone on the stage to continue her duties as the auctioneer.
"Next, the final item for auction has arrived. It is a magic treasure gathered by our auction with considerable expense—the Purple Star Nine Dragon Spear. This treasure was the lifebound magical treasure of the Core Formation Cultivator Long Xinghe, who made a name for himself with it in the East Sea. Unfortunately, a genius met an early demise; he fell suddenly in a conflict, leaving only this treasure behind," she announced.
"There are rumors that before his demise, Long Xinghe told his disciples that he had discovered an ancient secret hidden by this treasure. It is a clue to a secret treasure in the East Sea. However, many years have passed by, and the Purple Star Nine Dragon Spear has changed numerous ownerships, his major cultivation technique 'Star Picking Technique' also fell into obscurity. His mentioned secret has not been revealed to the world."
"After our shop's verification, this spear is indeed a relic left by Long Xinghe. The runes on it are intact and the body of the treasure is undamaged; it only requires some minor refining before it can be used again. The starting bid is twenty thousand," she concluded.
The appearance of a famous Core Formation Cultivator's magical treasure in this auction excited many cultivators in the venue, who gazed at the purple spear behind Gui Jiu with great eagerness.
Yet, with a starting bid of twenty thousand, this was not something most cultivators could afford; only the wealthy guests sitting in the private boxes were truly capable of bidding.
By this stage, those Core Formation Cultivators or representatives from major sects didn't bother using bid tokens anymore; each started shouting their bids out loud, unwilling to let anyone outdo them.
For a time, the Five Thunder Sect, Shengye Sect, all joined the bidding war.
"Our Chang Chun Temple bids thirty-one thousand spirit stones. Are there any others who wish to raise the price?" After a fierce bidding session, Zuo Qinghui suddenly stood up, stroked his beard, and cast a cold glance around.
Wang Chongshan whispered to Yuan Ming, "I knew it would turn out like this; Chang Chun Temple always tries to dominate others with their power."
After Zuo Qinghui stood up, Gui Jiu waited briefly, but seeing no other increase in bids, she bowed to him, "Congratulations, Senior Zuo on obtaining this treasure. With that, all items in this auction have now been sold. Please exit in an orderly manner. Those who won items, please wait briefly in the downstairs lobby; someone will guide you shortly to collect your items."
As the auction ended, the crowd gradually dispersed.
By a large window overlooking a small lake, Zuo Qinghui looked into the waters and instructed one of his disciples, "Go check, find out where this Hagon originated, whom he studied under, what magical artifact he uses, especially the details of his confrontation with Pu Zhengqing."
"Yes," someone responded.

chapters.title: Chapter 313 - 290: Give an Inch, Take a Mile
chapters.content:
That night,
Yuan Ming returned to his dwelling and immediately took out the piece of Water Crown Tree spirit wood he had acquired that day. He carefully cut approximately one-tenth of it, ground it into a fine powder, mixed it with other incense-making materials, and added the incense ashes from the Zhenling Sect to quickly create a new stick of Black Incense.
Then, he took out the Stealing Heaven Tripod and inserted the finished Black Incense into it. Calming his mind, he attempted to possess Sha Hao.
Soon, Yuan Ming's vision shifted, and he once again found himself inhabiting Sha Hao's body.
However, the scenery around him remained unchanged from his previous possessions; Sha Hao seemed rooted to the spot as usual, still sitting in silence within the stone house, diligently cultivating.
Yuan Ming was quite accustomed to such scenes and did not grow impatient. Instead, as always, he quietly began to sense the flow of spiritual power within Sha Hao's body.
Half a quarter of an hour later, just when Yuan Ming thought that this attempt would also be fruitless, Sha Hao suddenly opened his eyes, reached into his storage bag, turned a porcelain bottle over in his palm, but nothing came out.
